author: vkuttyp
body:
The §68 report for two adjacent inventory §3 rows, taken together because they are one subject: **a checker is worth what it checks *and* what its reports are known to do.** Report only — no behaviour changes.

## Three invariants the checker does not verify

`design.md` states the extent invariant as a property of the format:

> Runs are sorted by `lblk` and never overlap; a logical block that no run covers is a **hole** and reads as zeros.

`cosmofs_check` verifies neither half, nor that a name appears once in a directory. **To its credit it says so** — there is a "What it does not check" section naming all three — so this is a documented gap, not a false claim, and the report is careful about that distinction because it changes what the unit is for.

| invariant | what a violation does | caught today? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| no two runs cover the same `lblk` | two extents claim one logical block; which one a read gets depends on walk order | **only** when they also share a *pool* block, where `block_seen` sees two claims. Distinct pool blocks: invisible |
| runs sorted by `lblk` | a lookup assuming order stops early and reads a hole where data exists | no |
| no name twice in one directory | two entries resolve to different inodes; unlink removes one and the name survives | no |

## Five classes that have never been reported

`dir_bad` is reported from six sites and `chain_cycle` from five. Two `dir_bad` sites have tests; **the other four and every `chain_cycle` site have none** — a block pointer outside the pool, a snapshot member table that doesn't fit its block, an over-long `namelen`, a directory reached from two parents, and any cycle at all. `CFS_CHECK_MAX_CHAIN` (4096) is a bound nothing has ever reached.

Five reporting paths that have never executed is five chances to be wrong. The plan puts them **before** the harder work and predicts at least one will be.

## Why it matters

`cosmofs-replay` runs the checker over **410 replayed images every boot**, so the suite's silence about extent ordering means nothing at all. Four of ten classes are auto-repaired under `COSMOFS_CHECK_REPAIR`, and `/dev/fsctl` (#146) put "no findings" in front of an operator as an answer they act on.

## Design

**The two extent checks need no memory** — one `prev` per inode as the extents stream past. That matters: the pass allocates everything up front so it can answer `-ENOMEM` honestly rather than half-finishing, and every addition has to live inside that discipline.

**Duplicate names are the real obstacle**, and the design document names it exactly: the pass "keeps maps of numbers and that needs a set of strings". Three options weighed — sort each directory (exact, unbounded memory), a per-directory hash set (bounded by the largest directory), or a fixed bitmap with a re-scan on a hit. **Bitmap plus re-scan**, because it keeps the fixed-budget property and pays only on collisions, with the hash set named as the fallback rather than pretending the choice is obvious.

Overlap and ordering are **two classes, not one**, because they are different repairs: an ordering fault may be repairable by sorting, an overlap is data loss.

## Tests

Nine, each with a bug-proof, each new check getting a `COSMOFS_CORRUPT_*` kind — the tree already made that the way to fire a class.

**The vacuity risk is named in advance**: `block_seen` already catches an overlap that *shares* a pool block, so a careless test would be caught by the **old** code and prove nothing. The corruption therefore points the second run at a different pool block — precisely the case the document says is invisible.

## The best possible outcome, stated as such

Three new checks are three new questions asked of each of those 410 replayed images. **If one trips, that is a finding about cosmofs, not a bug in this unit** — and the plan treats it that way rather than as an obstacle.

body:
## Summary

On the new RoboLedger MCP resource (`/v1/mcp/roboledger`, RoboFinSystems/robosystems#1416), the consent page offers only the graphs that resource can grant. The API refuses anything else; without this change the picker would still list the SEC repository and other graphs, and choosing one would end on a misleading "You don't have access to that graph."

## Changes

- **`/oauth/consent` page** (`src/app/(consent)/oauth/consent/content.tsx`)
  - When the pending authorization names a `product`, the picker lists only graphs that serve it. That excludes shared repositories (the SEC repository declares the `roboledger` extension too), subgraphs (which inherit their parent's extensions), and graphs without the extension. The "Shared repositories" group therefore never appears for a RoboLedger request.
  - The heading reads "Choose the RoboLedger graph to connect" and the client line "wants to use RoboLedger on your behalf".
  - The default selection only picks a graph that can be granted: the user's current graph if eligible, otherwise their first eligible graph.
  - An account with graphs but no RoboLedger graph sees "This connection is for RoboLedger graphs, and you don't have one yet", and approve stays disabled.
  - Requests without a product (`/v1/mcp`, per-graph URLs) behave exactly as before.
- **`src/lib/oauth-consent.ts`**: `PendingAuthorization.product` (optional), plus `graphServesProduct` and `productLabel`. The predicate mirrors the API's check and reads fields already on the SDK's `GraphInfo`.

## Deploy Notes

Needs RoboFinSystems/robosystems#1416 deployed for `product` to appear on the pending authorization. The field is optional, so deploying this first is harmless: without it the page behaves as today.

## Testing

- `npm run test:all` (via the pre-commit hook): 410 tests passed; format, lint and typecheck clean.
- New tests: a RoboLedger request lists only the RoboLedger tenant graph among a repository, a subgraph and a RoboInvestor graph; a current graph that cannot be granted is not preselected, and approve posts the eligible graph; no eligible graph shows the product message with approve disabled. Unit tests for `graphServesProduct` and `productLabel`.
- `npm run build`: not run (no routing, layout or config change). A stale `.next/types` from another branch failed the local typecheck first; `next typegen` regenerated it, and nothing in `src/` was affected.
- Not yet run: the live consent flow against a deployed API.

body:
## Summary

- Yahoo `get_free_agents` and `get_players` never requested the rate they reported: both built `league/{key}/players;…/ownership`, and Yahoo's `ownership` sub-resource carries league owner/waiver state only. The platform-wide rostered rate is the sibling `percent_owned` sub-resource. Both handlers now request `;out=ownership,percent_owned`.
- The extractor read a path that does not exist in Yahoo's payload (`playerData[1].ownership.percent_owned`) and only accepted a scalar. It now finds `percent_owned` by key at any sub-resource position and reads `value` from Yahoo's array-of-single-key-objects form, the flattened object form, and the numeric-keyed container form. `0` preserved; absent → `null`.
- With every rate `null`, the comparator's name tiebreak re-ranked the whole list alphabetically, discarding the `sort=OR` order Yahoo had applied. Rate-less entries now compare equal so the stable sort keeps provider order (they still sort after rated entries).
- Gateway: `capabilities.rosteredRate` for Yahoo is derived from the returned entries instead of a static `true`. No tool description, annotation, or declared schema changed; `ordering` stays the declared two-value enum.
- Fixtures replaced with Yahoo-shaped ones; regression test that an all-null response preserves provider order and reports `rosteredRate: false`. `docs/CHANGELOG.md` updated.

## Evidence of the defect (production, eval identity)

- Baseball: flaim-eval `free-agent-yahoo-live --target prod` run `2026-09-17T00-27-30Z` — 5/5 `percentOwned: null`, `capabilities.rosteredRate: true`.
- Football: manual run `2026-09-17T00-31-58Z` — 25/25 null, names strictly A→Z.

Linear: FLA-9 (this was also FLA-132's original May finding).

## Verification

- [x] `workers/yahoo-client`: type-check clean, 311/311
- [x] `workers/fantasy-mcp`: type-check clean, 255 unit + 134 integration
- [ ] Codex audit
- [ ] CI
- **Prod-only live verification** (Yahoo cannot be exercised on preview): after merge, `free-agent-yahoo-live --target prod` must pass acceptance, and a manual Yahoo football prompt must show non-null rates, non-alphabetical order, `rosteredRate: true`. If rates are still null, `wrangler rollback` on `yahoo-client` restores the previous URL and parser; the gateway change is inert without it.

The `;out=` request form is confirmed against Yahoo's `out` filter documentation and two production clients (uberfastman/yfpy; khaney64/yahoo-fantasy-baseball), not against a live call from this worker — that is what the post-merge check is for.

## Summary

- `auto_continue`'s dispatch lane pick (`_grid_lane_for` in `cli/src/fno/backlog/advance.py`) judged lane account capacity from a cache-only read that never refreshed a stale or never-probed account. A reading older than the 300s usage TTL read as `unknown`, and `on_unknown=skip` dropped that lane, so every worker fell through the declared `lanes[0]` (`codex-luna`) to `claude-sonnet-5` even when the codex account had real headroom.
- Fix: `route_resolve.runtime_capacity()` gained a keyword-only `probe_stale` flag. When set (and quota observation is on), it refreshes each lane account through the existing probe-on-stale `refresh_usage` before `headrooms()` is read. `_grid_lane_for`, the autonomous dispatch seam, now passes `probe_stale=True`. Every other caller of `runtime_capacity` (`explain.py`, `route_cli.py`, `spawn_defaults.py`, `config_cli.py`) keeps the cache-only default.
- Self-review cleanup: added `QuotaConfig.observes` (`cli/src/fno/adapters/providers/model.py`) as the one shared home for the `observe or defer_dispatch` check, used by both the new probe gate and the existing `evaluate_quota_signal`. Removed a duplicated boolean expression and hoisted the check out of the per-harness loop.

## Changes

- `cli/src/fno/route_resolve.py` - `runtime_capacity(probe_stale=...)` + `_quota_observes()` helper
- `cli/src/fno/backlog/advance.py` - `_grid_lane_for` passes `probe_stale=True`
- `cli/src/fno/adapters/providers/model.py` - `QuotaConfig.observes` property
- `cli/src/fno/adapters/providers/runtime_state.py` - `evaluate_quota_signal` reuses `quota.observes`
- `cli/tests/unit/test_route_resolve.py`, `cli/tests/unit/test_advance.py` - AC1-AC5 coverage

## Test Plan

- [x] `cd cli && uv run pytest tests/unit/test_route_resolve.py tests/unit/test_advance.py -q` - 241 passed
- [x] `bash scripts/ci/check-python-static.sh` - ruff + mypy clean across 631 files
- [x] `bash scripts/ci/check-file-budget.sh` - `cli/src/fno` net +27, allowance 100
- [ ] Live check after merge: with a codex snapshot older than 300s, run one `auto_continue` tick; `fno agents feed` or the spawn receipt names `codex-luna`, and `fno config accounts list` shows the codex usage row fresh.

body:
The saved-corpus review found ticker collisions in early rankings, collection concentrated at window boundaries, a follower-only profile cohort, and broken watcher timestamp handling.

Adds evidence-backed voice-role views for early discoverers, original-analysis candidates, amplifiers, configured project/platform sources and reporting feeds. Exact-contract anchors exclude older ambiguous meme-token chatter; Zcash accepts bare ZEC. Repeated analysis formats have capped credit, and distinct subsequent reply/quote accounts are visible with caveats. Fixes watcher native database timestamps.

Collection prioritizes one fresh sample and partial-window continuation, plus one-hour exact-contract focus windows around first saved identity evidence. Retires unfinished broad PONS/STANDARD rolling queries without deleting evidence. Adds daily bounded comparable-age engagement refresh and fixed weekly mixed profile cohorts.

Weekly cohorts and follower/posting baselines are immutable database snapshots. Seven-day evaluation retains inactive candidates and excludes later backfills. It measures sampled attention, not returns or causal influence. Existing credit ceilings, expiries, per-run limits and uncertain-request blocking remain unchanged.

Validation: 21 local role, identity, watcher and research tests plus TypeScript typecheck pass. Disposable Postgres safeguards cover budgets, continuation, focus windows, cohort immutability and pending evaluation before the first updated collection.

#### d719d23779c25d41ec347c2bfb200f3c88815561 
createImageBitmap-from-hdr
https://bugs.webkit.org/show_bug.cgi?id=324399
rdar://187632132

Reviewed by Mike Wyrzykowski.

createImageBitmap() always allocated a BGRA8 buffer, so an ImageBitmap
made from an HDR source clamped its extended-range values, and drawing
it into a float16 canvas could only produce SDR.

Derive the buffer's color space and pixel format from the source instead:
Keep the source's RGB-model color space, extending it when the source
draws HDR content, and use RGBA16F whenever that color space uses
extended range.

Video and WebCodecsVideoFrame sources still allocate BGRA8 buffers for
now.

author: zhiyangk
body:
## Summary

`coli_cuda_available_device_count()` is called by `qwen36_tier.c` **before** `coli_cuda_init()` —
the count decides which device indices are handed to init — but the wrapper gated on
`g_cuda.available`, a flag only init sets. On Windows that answered `0` on every host, so the tier
fell back to the CPU path unless `COLI_GPUS`/`COLI_GPU` was set by hand (#1577).

This is the fix #1577 proposed, plus the regression test that issue said it did not have.

## Changes

**`c/backend_loader.c`**
- `coli_cuda_available_device_count()` now calls `coli_cuda_load()` instead of reading
  `g_cuda.available`, exactly as `coli_cuda_attention_project_ragged()` already does. The
  optional-export fallback to `device_count()` is unchanged, so a DLL predating #1533's export
  still loads and still answers.
- The "no synchronisation here" note above `coli_cuda_load()`'s HIP branch named exactly two
  callers; it now names all three and records why the new one stays inside the single-threaded
  start-up window — the tier asks the count while it is still choosing the devices to hand to init,
  before it creates any thread of its own.

**`c/tests/test_backend_loader.py`**
- The generated stub backend answers the two device-count exports with **distinct** non-zero values
  (2 and 5) and can now be built without the optional export. `0` is both a legitimate device count
  and what the `g_cuda.available` gate returned without loading anything, so a test that cannot
  separate those two cases cannot see this bug.
- The generated harness prints the count with the backend-module state on **both sides** of the
  probe, then still runs init.
- New `LoaderPreInitAvailabilityTest`, four cases:
  1. backend present, no init, no `COLI_GPUS` → the count comes from the DLL (2), the harness
     observes the DLL being loaded **by the probe** (`0 → 2 → 1`), and init still succeeds after;
  2. no backend → `0` devices, nothing loaded, no crash, init still reached;
  3. DLL without the export (new `oldvariant` fixture) → falls back to `device_count()` (5);
  4. HIP control → a HIP host still refuses on `COLI_HIP_RUNTIME_DIR` before init and leaves the
     backend unmapped.

## Test plan

```
$ python c/tests/test_backend_loader.py
Ran 82 tests in 75.4s
OK
```

Reverting the one-line change in `coli_cuda_available_device_count()` makes cases 1 and 3 fail
(`0` instead of `2`/`5`) — which is what these tests exist for.

The build path from #1533 is exercised too:

```
$ make -C c qwen36.exe CUDA_DLL=1 ARCH=native
gcc ... -DCOLI_CUDA qwen36.c qwen36_tier.c backend_loader.o -o qwen36.exe -lm -fopenmp -static -lpsapi
```

— the tier is compiled in by the Makefile alone (no variable overrides) and links against the
patched loader with no missing symbol.

Environment: Windows 11, MinGW w64devkit 2.10.0, Python 3.11. The fixture skips honestly where
`gcc`/`objdump` are absent, and loads no real vendor runtime.

Fixes #1577

Decompose the zero-headroom (2666/2666) gated file src/physics/multi_node_solver/mod.rs into two child modules under src/physics/multi_node_solver/ — helpers.rs (free functions + SurfaceExteriorTemperatures) and tests.rs (extracted inline #[cfg(test)] mod tests) — per the PR #3688 coverage_tests precedent and the two-stage protocol in issue #3790. author: sandeep-agami
body:
Spec: ACE-136

## What went wrong

When agami's query is refused or fails, the execution tier writes nothing to stdout, but the redirect still leaves `rows/<n>/actual.csv` behind, zero bytes long. `reconcile.py record` read that file with `_csv_shape`, which turned an empty file into `{"columns": [], "row_count": 0}`, a result with no columns and no rows. Because that is not `None`, the branch that says `agami's statement did not run: <detail>` never ran. The row recorded a comparison sentence instead:

- A refused or failed run on a statement row said `the two results are tables, and they were not compared`.
- A question-only row with no run record was worse. It recorded `ungraded` with no error, so it waited for a person to judge an answer agami never gave.

The person's own side had the same problem. A refused statement leaves `statement.csv` empty. The record carried it as a result of no columns and no rows, and the page showed "0 rows" as your answer.

## Repro

```
rows/4/agami-answer.json  {"sql": "SELECT region, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY region", "error": null}
rows/4/agami-run.json     {"status": "refused", "exit": 2, "kind": null, "rule": "column_scope", "remediation": "..."}
rows/4/actual.csv         (zero bytes)
rows/4/statement.csv      region,n / EU,2 / US,5
```

`reconcile.py record --run-dir <run> --row 4` recorded `"error": "the two results are tables, and they were not compared"`. It now records `"error": "agami's statement did not run: refused"`.

## The fix

All in `plugins/agami/scripts/reconcile.py`:

- `_csv_shape` returns nothing for a file whose first row names no column. That covers a zero-byte file, a file holding only a blank line, and a header of nothing but spaces. A real result always has a header row that names its columns. This matches what `_read_csv`, `_probe_csv` and the comparator's `result_from_csv` already do for an empty file.
- A new helper, `_run_result`, returns nothing when the run record beside the CSV is there and does not say `ok`. A missing run record says nothing either way, so the CSV decides alone.
- A new helper, `_run_record`, reads a run record. A run file that is empty or not JSON is `_load_json`'s own error object, and says nothing about the run, so it counts as no record. Without this, it hid a real result beside it, and the row gave a JSON parser message as the reason the statement did not run.
- `record` reads `actual.csv` beside `agami-run.json`, and `statement.csv` beside `run.json`, through those helpers.

The "did not run" sentence and its format are unchanged. A run that says `ok` and returned a header with no rows is still a result, and is still compared.

### Telling the loader's error from the session's

`_run_record` first spotted `_load_json`'s error object by its shape: an `error` and no `status`. That matched too much. `agami-run.json` is written by the reconcile session, not by code (SKILL.md Phase 2b), so a run that failed can arrive as `{"error": "the client timed out"}` and nothing else. Read as a parser message, it was dropped, the leftover `actual.csv` beside it became the row's result, and a run that never finished was recorded as a verified match — the exact bug class this PR exists to remove. `{"error": "empty_file"}` collided with the loader's own word outright.

So `_load_json` now marks its own error objects with a private key, and `_run_record` looks for that mark. Nothing on disk carries it, because nothing but the loader writes it. A record holding only an error the session wrote is now what it is: a run that did not succeed, with no result. The row's sentence reads that error too (after the tier's own `detail`, `kind` and `status`), so it says `agami's statement did not run: the client timed out` instead of falling back to the plain sentence.

## Other paths of the same shape

I searched every reader of a result CSV. `record` was the only one that read an empty file as a result, for both `actual.csv` and `statement.csv`, and both are fixed here. `_sample` (via `_read_csv`), `_probe_csv` in the plugin and in `semantic_model/probes.py`, and `comparator.result_from_csv` already treat an empty file as "no result".

One path is left as it is. The card's Data section (`_sample`) reads the two CSVs without their run records. So if a run that did not succeed left rows in its CSV, the record says the statement did not run, but the Data section still shows those rows. The execution tier writes an empty CSV when a statement is refused or fails, so only a hand-made fixture reaches this today.

## Tests

New tests in `tests/test_reconcile_record.py`:

- A refused run with an empty `actual.csv` records `agami's statement did not run: refused`.
- A failed run with an empty `actual.csv` records `agami's statement did not run: column_not_found`.
- No `agami-run.json` and an empty `actual.csv` records the existing "was not run" sentence as an error, not `ungraded`.
- An `actual.csv` holding only a blank line, or a header of spaces, is no result either.
- A run file that is empty or not JSON, on both sides, leaves the result to its file: the row is a `match`, and with an empty `actual.csv` it records the "was not run" sentence, not a parser message.
- A run record holding only an error the session wrote is a record, not a parser message: the row is an `error` naming that error, and the CSV beside it is not its result. Run for `the client timed out` and for `empty_file`, the word the loader uses too.
- A run that says `ok` with a header-only `actual.csv` still records `{"columns": [...], "row_count": 0}` and is compared (`mismatch`).
- Your statement refused with an empty `statement.csv` records no `statement_recorded`, and the page item shows no "0 rows".
- A run record that says `failed` or `not_run` wins over a CSV with rows beside it, on both sides.

Each new rule fails its tests when it is reverted on its own.

- `uv run python dev.py check`: 6312 passed and 13 skipped, with the one flake below.
- `uv run python dev.py cover`: 100% of the changed lines covered (23 of 23).

One thing this PR does not change: `test_7` in `tests/test_reconcile_flawed_inputs_e2e.py` depends on earlier tests in the same module. It fails whenever xdist puts those tests on different workers. It failed that way on every local run of `dev.py check` here, and it fails the same way on this branch with these changes stashed, so it is not this PR's. The whole suite passes with `--dist loadfile` (6312 passed, 13 skipped), and the module passes on its own.

author: danielh2018
body:
## What changed, and why

The final whole-branch review of the landing-latency plan (#1769, #1770, #1773, #1796, #1806, #1810, #1842) found one seam no per-task review could see, plus nine smaller items. This PR is that fix round.

**A PR reaching service tags and a self-applied plane took the fast path and was graded on a tick it never awaited.** Since #1810 a tagged PR deploys from a snapshot of its merge commit and only kicks the tick. For a PR that also touches `roles/setup/gitops_deploy/` (or a remaining-setup host), the tick IS the apply for that half, and the health verdict reads the tick's markers, so the landing finished `needs-manual-apply` with a hand-apply command for work the kicked tick applies a minute later. Every mixed PR in the plan (#1773, #1796, #1806) was that shape; the fast path had not run live for one yet. `Landing.tick_is_the_apply` (`self_applied or remaining_setup`, deliberately not `plane`) now routes such a PR back to the tick-first path, on the derived-tags path and on `--tags` too — the `--tags` early return in `classify.py` used to skip the self-applied classification entirely. `# DECIDED:` at the branch in `land_lib/pipeline.py`.

**`--detach` service-lock contention exited 76 instead of 75.** `service_lock_status=$?` inside `if ! take_service_locks` read the negated status. The bash test failed on the old code (`assert 76 == 75`) and passes now.

**Docs and comments that still described pre-plan behaviour:** `CLAUDE.md` and the auto-mode-bridge hook enumerated "75/4/3/2, all four" against a `_DEPLOY_EXITS` that carries 77/76/75/4/3/2 and 20 (both now cite the dict); `docs/deploying.md`'s "the lock serialises; it does not queue fairly" (pre-ADR-0017); the pipeline design page's "a PR with service tags skips this step entirely"; raw line-number citations on the measured-floor page replaced by symbols; two dead test-path citations; a `# DECIDED:` at deploy.sh's `--detach` notifier stating the snapshot-render / caller-markers split.

## What it costs

A `--tags` landing makes two more step-1 reads (`gh pr view --json files` and the PR-head fetch) to classify the self-applied half. A mixed PR pays the tick wait it paid before #1810; a tags-only PR is unchanged.

## What still needs a live proof

Both routing fixes are traced statically and pinned by tests on the argv order. The first landing of a PR touching a service role and a setup role together, derived and with `--tags`, is the live confirmation — read it off the `VERDICT:` line (`settled`, not `needs-manual-apply`).

## Services touched

none — `scripts/deploy.sh`, `scripts/deploy_tools/`, `.claude/hooks/auto-mode-bridge.py`, `scripts/lib/deployer_park.py`, docs and skills.

## Deploy

- [ ] Deployed after merge
- [x] Deliberately deferred — reason: operator tooling and docs read from the checkout; nothing to apply on a host.

## Verification

- [ ] `probe.py health <svc>` — no workload
- [x] Exercised the changed behaviour itself — how: pipeline tests pin the argv order and the absence of `--at` for a mixed PR (derived and `--tags`, both red on the unfixed code), the fast path for a tags-only PR, and the bash `--detach` contention exit.

```
$ uv run pytest scripts/deploy_tools/tests ansible/tests/deploy -q
1392 passed, 1 skipped in 32.27s
$ prek run --all-files
(every hook passed — implementer's run at the final commit)
```

Reviewed under subagent-driven development: final whole-branch review (F1–F10, adjudication of every ledgered minor), one fix dispatch, one scoped re-review (R1–R9), round 2 verified against the diff. Filed from the review: #1843, #1844, #1845, #1846, #1847, #1848.

Host-side, value-preserving changes. Each is a substitution whose result is identical to what the code produced before; no kernel, template constant, grid, threadgroup shape or byte of traffic changes.

## 1. `downCombine`: bind `isFast` once

## 1. `downCombine`: bind `isFast` once


`TrackFastMoEKernels.downCombine` derives its shape values at the top of the
function and never rebinds them:

```swift
let BR = idx.dim(0), F = act.dim(1), H = wd.dim(1)
let S = BR / topK
```

It then called `isFast(k: F, n: H)` twice — once inside the precondition and
once, five lines later, as the `FAST` entry of the template list:

```swift
-        precondition(act.dim(0) == BR + S && gate.dim(0) == S && sharedDown.rows == H && !isFast(k: F, n: H))
+        let fast = isFast(k: F, n: H)
+        precondition(act.dim(0) == BR + S && gate.dim(0) == S && sharedDown.rows == H && !fast)
...
-            ("K", topK), ("FAST", isFast(k: F, n: H)), ("BR", BR), ("VPT", S), ("KSG", ksg), ("RPS", rps)],
+            ("K", topK), ("FAST", fast), ("BR", BR), ("VPT", S), ("KSG", ksg), ("RPS", rps)],
```

`isFast(k:n:)` is a pure integer predicate over its two arguments. `F` and `H`
are immutable between the two call sites, so the two evaluations return the
same `Bool` by construction and the bind is a substitution rather than a
behaviour change.

The predicate is in fact pinned: the precondition immediately above asserts
`!fast`, so any window that reaches the dispatch carries `FAST = false`. The
template therefore receives exactly the value it received before.

- **Kernel selection.** `S == 1 ? downCombineKernel1 : downCombineKernel` is
  unchanged, and both kernels keep their own `inputNames` / `outputNames` /
  `source` / `header` declarations.

  ("K", topK), ("FAST", ...), ("BR", BR), ("VPT", S), ("KSG", ksg),
  ("RPS", rps)` in that order, with `FAST` bound to the same `Bool`.
- **Launch geometry.** `grid: (32, (H / rps) * ksg, S)` and
  `threadGroup: (32, ksg, 1)` are unchanged, and so are the values feeding

  and `rps = S == 1 ? downRowsPerSimdgroup : 4`. `downRowsPerSimdgroup` and

  && w.dtype == .float32 && S >= 1 && S <= 8` check above it is unchanged, and
  the edited precondition still asserts the same three conjuncts plus the same

`downCombine` is the routed-expert down GEMV plus the expert-weighted combine
plus the shared-expert gate and add, in one launch. Its signature and its


author: markamccorkle
body:
Closes #1853.

## What the evidence actually shows

The issue diagnoses the lockfile as unsatisfiable. It is not. `package-lock.json`
already carried a nested SDK resolution:

```
packages/nightgauge-sdk/node_modules/js-yaml  5.4.2
node_modules/js-yaml                          4.3.2  (dev-only, transitive)
```

`npm ci` from a clean tree succeeds on `origin/main`, `npm run build` exits 0,
and `ComplexityModelService.test.ts` passes all 33 tests — verified with no
source change. The hoisted 4.3.2 is a transitive dev copy of eslint's and does
not serve the SDK.

## The real defect, in two parts

**1. A wrong-major types stub.** `@types/js-yaml: ^4.0.9` sat next to
`js-yaml: ^5.4.2` in three manifests. js-yaml 5 ships its own declarations
(`types: ./dist/js-yaml.d.ts`), so the stub is unnecessary *and* a major behind.
Whenever npm hoists a js-yaml 4 copy above the workspace — or a tree carries a
stale `node_modules` from before the nested 5.4.2 entry existed — TypeScript
resolves `js-yaml` through `node_modules/@types/js-yaml@4`, and `quoteStyle`, a
js-yaml 5 `DumpOptions` field used at `ComplexityModelService.ts:396` and
`KnowledgeService.ts:1289`, fails TS2353. That is the reported symptom, and the
`schema_version: "1.0"` quoting test fails with it.

So the tree is on js-yaml 5 and `quoteStyle` stays.

**2. Two undeclared importers.** Removing the stub turned the extension build
red with TS7016 — which is the correct signal. `packages/nightgauge-vscode`
(`estimateWorkTime.ts`, `workTimeFeedback.ts`, `DashboardState.ts`) and the root
tooling scripts (`audit-complexity-model.ts`, `backfill-complexity-model.ts`,
`evaluate-models.ts`) import js-yaml without declaring it, and were silently
type-checking against whatever major happened to be hoisted. Both now declare
`js-yaml: ^5.4.2`.

## Change

- Remove `@types/js-yaml` from `packages/nightgauge-sdk`,
  `skills/nightgauge-product-audit` and the generated plugin mirror.
- Add `js-yaml: ^5.4.2` to `packages/nightgauge-vscode` dependencies and the
  root devDependencies.
- Regenerate all three lockfiles, and the plugin mirror via
  `scripts/install-agent-skills.sh --generate-only`.
- `CHANGELOG.md` entry under `## [Unreleased]`.

No source change. Dependency-only, landing alone over settled `main`.

## Verification

- `rm -rf node_modules packages/*/node_modules packages/*/dist && npm ci &&
  npm run build` — exit 0, zero TS errors. (A stale `.tsbuildinfo` will mask
  this; the dist wipe is what makes the check honest, and is why the first push
  went red in CI and green locally.)
- `bash scripts/ci-local.sh` — one failure,
  `TestOpenCodeOperatorInstallRiskDoesNotMisclassifyAFastFailure`, the known
  concurrency flake tracked as #1836. The three opencodeAdapter SIGINT tests
  (#1693) pass here because this run had its own `node_modules`.

body:
## Contexto

Promocao de `develop` para `main`.

`FIX-0394` + `FIX-0395` + `FIX-0396`, os tres no mesmo diff.

O app tinha **TRES grafias do mesmo papel**, nao duas: a sidebar dizia **"Dono"**, e `invites` / `profile` / `invite-accept` diziam **"Proprietario"** e **"Gerente"**. Cada tela carregava o proprio mapa, e os mapas ja tinham divergido entre si. A sidebar ja esta em producao com "Gerenciador" desde o PR #262 — o resto do app e que ficou para tras.

## O que muda

Passa a existir **uma fonte unica**: `utils/role-labels.ts`, com `OWNER=Dono`, `MANAGER=Gerenciador`, `DRIVER=Motorista`. Acrescentar um papel amanha e editar esse arquivo **e mais nada**. Os cinco mapas locais foram removidos.

O `FIX-0396` esta **absorvido aqui**: `admin-company-detail.ts` e `admin-user-detail.ts` — os dois que ainda diziam "Gerente" — tiveram os mapas removidos junto. Nao ficou meio-termo; `'Gerente'` como rotulo de papel nao existe mais em `src/app`.

**A traducao e SO de exibicao.** O enum, o claim do token e todo payload de API continuam em ingles — nos selects, por exemplo, o `value` segue `'MANAGER'`/`'DRIVER'` e apenas o `label` e PT-BR. Nenhuma string traduzida entra em comparacao, request ou storage.

**Papel desconhecido cai no valor BRUTO**, mantendo a politica do `FIX-0371`: uma divergencia com o backend fica **visivel** na tela em vez de sumir em silencio.

`SystemRole` (`USER | PLATFORM_ADMIN`) e **outro eixo** e nao consome este mapa. Os dois se chamam "role" e significam coisas diferentes; o util registra isso por escrito para ninguem fundir os dois daqui a seis meses.

## As ancoras do tour foram MEDIDAS, nos dois lados

Uma tentativa anterior deste trabalho foi escrita sobre um checkout muito atrasado e **teria revertido as ancoras do tour guiado**. Por isso aqui a verificacao e explicita e nao por confianca:

- `TOUR_ANCHORS` em `sidebar.ts`: **12 nesta branch, 12 em `origin/develop`**;
- `data-tour` em `sidebar.html`: 4 — e o arquivo **nao foi tocado**;
- **zero** linhas removidas no diff contem `tourKey`, `TOUR_ANCHORS` ou `data-tour`;
- os specs do tour rodam e passam: `tour.service` 30, `tour-spotlight` 8.

## Achado conhecido, deliberadamente NAO corrigido nesta janela

`src/app/pages/invites/invites.ts:100-103` mantem um **segundo mapa de rotulos** — o array de options do select, no mesmo arquivo que ja importa e usa o util na linha 121.

Os textos **batem** com o mapa hoje, entao nao ha inconsistencia visivel e nao ha bug: e divida de manutencao, nao defeito. Escapou porque a forma e diferente (precisa do par `value`+`label`), entao nao casa com o padrao de substituicao dos outros cinco.

**Por que fica para depois, e nao agora:** sao tres linhas sem efeito visivel, e este lote e o **passo 1 de uma colisao de tres vias** (`sidebar.ts` com o `FEAT-0108`) cuja base envelhece a cada release promovida. O custo de segurar a janela por isso e maior que o ganho. Fica registrado aqui para nenhum revisor descobrir sozinho e achar que passou batido.

## Validacao

**85 testes, 9 arquivos, 0 falhas**, na base atual:

- `role-labels` 5 · `sidebar` 12 · `tour.service` 30 · `tour-spotlight` 8
- `invites` 10 · `invite-accept` 10 · `admin-company-detail` 5 · `profile` 3 · `admin-user-detail` 2

`tsc -p tsconfig.spec.json` limpo e build de desenvolvimento limpo.

## Nota sobre o historico de `develop`

`develop` carrega merges de diff vazio ("Merge main de volta em develop apos a promocao do PR #NNN"). Sao obrigatorios e **nao devem ser apagados**.

author: manuel-cosovschi
body:
Hace falta mandarle un mail a los 18 suscriptores del popup contando que los precios de la página bajaron. Queda como un bloque en **Admin → Marketing** en vez de un envío suelto, por dos razones.

La primera es práctica: **la clave de Resend vive en Vercel**, así que el mail sale del servidor de producción o no sale.

La segunda es que mandarle algo a toda la lista no se puede deshacer. Entonces:

- El mail se muestra **entero en pantalla, tal cual va a salir**, arriba del botón.
- Hay un botón aparte para **mandárselo uno primero a sí mismo** — en la casilla nunca se ve igual que en una vista previa.
- El botón de mandar a todos **pregunta antes**, con el número de personas adelante.

## Los precios "de antes" van escritos, no calculados

La baja se redondeó para abajo al múltiplo de $500, así que dividir el precio nuevo por 0,95 **no** devuelve el viejo: la Japón quedó en $61.500 y esa cuenta da $64.737, no los $65.000 que costaba. Un "antes" inventado en un mail es de las pocas cosas que un cliente puede verificar y no perdonar, así que los cuatro ejemplos llevan el número real, verificado contra la base.

## El mail no inventa un motivo

Dice que los precios bajaron y que es el precio nuevo, no una promoción con fecha. **No dice por qué** bajaron: esa razón no la tengo y no se inventa en nombre de la tienda.

## Cómo se manda

De a uno y no en copia oculta — cada persona recibe su mail con su nombre, y si uno rebota no se cae el resto — con una pausa de 600ms entre cada uno, porque Resend limita por segundo y sin eso la mitad vuelve con 429 y parece que no anduvo.

Al terminar dice cuántos salieron y cuáles fallaron, y queda asentado en el historial quién lo mandó y a cuántos.

author: probepark
body:
## Why

`packages/coding-agent/src/config/settings-schema.ts` declares `sdk.promptDeadlineMs` with
`default: 3_600_000` (1 hour), but both places that actually arm a lease hardcoded a *different*
miss-fallback of `1_800_000` (30 minutes):

- `src/sdk/bus/index.ts:5210` — `readFiniteSetting("sdk.promptDeadlineMs", 1_800_000)`
- `src/sdk/host/session-runtime.ts:5212` — `... Number.isFinite(v) ? v : 1_800_000`

So whenever a Settings lookup missed — no settings object, an unwritten key, or a non-finite stored
value — the armed deadline was half what the schema, the description and the generated
`schemas/config.schema.json` all promise, and a long prompt was terminalized as
`prompt_deadline_exceeded` at 30 minutes. That is #5583.

This is the uncontested half of #5623, resubmitted on a clean `dev` base. The deadline-triggered
worktree autosave from that PR is intentionally excluded and remains under discussion there.

## What

The declared default and the code fallback are now literally the same constant, so they cannot
drift apart again:

- New exported `DEFAULT_SDK_PROMPT_DEADLINE_MS` / `DEFAULT_SDK_PROMPT_MAX_RUNTIME_MS` constants and
  `resolveSdkPromptDeadlineMs()` / `resolveSdkPromptMaxRuntimeMs()` helpers in `settings-schema.ts`.
  The two schema entries now take their `default:` from those constants.
- Both lease call sites (`sdk/bus/index.ts`, `sdk/host/session-runtime.ts`) resolve through the
  helpers. The now-callerless `readFiniteSetting` helper in the bus is removed.
- Values are unchanged (3_600_000 / 21_600_000), as are `validate:` bounds, descriptions and types —
  so `schemas/config.schema.json` is byte-identical and needs no regeneration.

The resolvers are a **finiteness** fallback only; range enforcement stays with the schema's
`validate:`, so `0` and negative stored values still pass through exactly as before. Clamping to the
declared bounds would be a behaviour change beyond #5583 and would need its own issue.

Scope is deliberately 5 files; nothing in the autosave/flush design from #5623 is included.

## Local tests (command + result)

```
bun test packages/coding-agent/test/sdk-prompt-deadline-setting.test.ts \
         packages/coding-agent/test/sdk-prompt-deadline-lease.test.ts \
         packages/coding-agent/test/sdk-prompt-deadline-manager.test.ts
  -> 36 pass / 0 fail, 144 expect() calls (74.49s)

bun test packages/coding-agent/test/sdk-bus-prompt-deadline.test.ts
  -> 13 pass / 0 fail, 61 expect() calls (81.37s)

bun test packages/coding-agent/src/sdk/host/session-runtime.test.ts
  -> 133 pass / 0 fail, 489 expect() calls (133.99s)

bun run check:schemas        -> pass; `git status --short -- schemas/` prints nothing
bun run check:tools          -> biome 4127 files clean, tsc clean, check-unsafe-rmrf clean
bun --cwd=packages/coding-agent run check -> biome 3187 files clean, tsc --noEmit clean
bun scripts/changelog-fragments.ts check  -> 33 fragment(s) across 3 package(s) validated
```

### The new test is not vacuous (falsification)

The resolver body was surgically reverted to a literal `1_800_000` fallback while keeping
`DEFAULT_SDK_PROMPT_DEADLINE_MS` referenced by the schema entry, so the file still compiles:

```
bun --cwd=packages/coding-agent run check   -> tsc exit 0   (broken state still type-checks)
bun test .../sdk-prompt-deadline-setting.test.ts -> 7 pass / 2 fail
    Expected: 3600000  Received: 1800000     (x2, both assertion diffs — not compile errors)
```

Restored to head: 9 pass / 0 fail, `git status --short` empty. The two failures are exactly the
non-finite-fallback case and the Settings-parity case; the other two tests pass in **both** states,
which is what shows the suite pins the behavioural delta rather than merely the new export.

## Needs e2e

Low. No wire protocol, schema or persisted-state change; the only behavioural delta is the numeric
lease value chosen when a Settings lookup misses. Worth one ACP/SDK smoke confirming a prompt with
no `sdk.promptDeadlineMs` configured is not terminalized at the 30-minute mark.

## Acceptance

| AC | Implementation | Local test |
|----|----------------|-----------|
| AC-1 — branch off latest `dev`, base `dev`, non-draft | branch cut from `origin/dev` @ `e3855f974`; no rebase/cherry-pick of #5623 | `gh pr view` → base `dev`, `isDraft: false` |
| AC-2 — diff confined to `packages/coding-agent/src/`, no generated schema touched | 5 files; `git diff --name-only origin/dev...HEAD -- schemas/` = 0 | `bun run check:schemas` pass + `git status --short -- schemas/` empty |
| AC-3 — fallback unit test for `undefined`/non-finite/string | `test/sdk-prompt-deadline-setting.test.ts` → `describe("sdk prompt deadline resolvers")`, 9 cases incl. `undefined`, `null`, `NaN`, `±Infinity`, `"3600000"`, `{}`, `[]`, `true`, plus Settings-parity and constant-vs-schema identity | 36 pass / 0 fail; falsification 2 assertion failures with tsc exit 0 |
| AC-4 — affected-path CI green | see CI section below | pending CI; all local equivalents green |
| AC-5 — resubmission sentence in body | stated verbatim in **Why** above | — |

`PR contract bootstrap` / `Validate exact-head PR contract` are expected red: this is an
agent-authored PR, so the verdict is `needs-human` by design (see below) — that is the contract
working, not a broken build.

## Open questions

- Should the resolvers also clamp to the schema's declared bounds rather than only guarding
  finiteness? Out of scope for #5583; current behaviour is preserved deliberately.
- #5623 is left open and untouched; the autosave half still needs its own decision.

## Agent

gjc (primary) failed to start on home2 — `Failed to create agent: Timeout waiting for message
(60000ms)`, the open issue Yeachan-Heo/gajae-code#5565, aggravated by load average 31 on that host.
Evidence filed as https://github.com/Yeachan-Heo/gajae-code/issues/5565#issuecomment-5706650536.
Fell back to **claude/claude-opus-5** via paseo on studio (worktree `gjc-5583-deadline-default-cc`).
Diff, gates and the falsification above were re-run independently by the coordinator, not taken from
the agent's self-report.

`PORT_BASE=28120`, `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=gjc-5583-deadline-default`, leftover: none.

## Risk

- [x] `low-risk` — ordinary fix/maintenance; the repository owner may use the explicit `merge-self-approved` solo verdict (no independent human review; the verdict name itself records this) with a risk-record comment bound to the exact head.

## Verdict

```text
gajae.pr-review-verdict.v1 needs-human sha256:0bf7aeab20cea60bbd67b823c4c258243b9dc3cd01328772ae3b9f3e5516616a reviewer:human reviewer-id:probepark evidence:local-gates-green-plus-falsification-tsc0-2-assertion-diffs
```

body:
## Summary

`POST` and `DELETE /remote-support/sessions/:id/legal-hold` were open to any authenticated caller in the tenant: the group they mount on carries authentication and nothing else, and the handlers gate on session visibility, not on role. Neither opens a host nor reveals a credential, so the freshness gate the PAM launches carry was the wrong control — but **releasing a hold is what lets the retention sweep purge the recording it protected.**

This closes the question the step-up census had recorded as *undecided*: both writes now take `requireAdminRole()`. Under `STEPUP_GATE` that gate already asks an admin *write* for a fresh second factor, so release inherits it. The list (`GET .../legal-holds`) stays open — reading which holds exist grants nothing.

## Changes

- `RegisterRemoteSupportAdminRoutes(r, stepUp, admin)` takes two **named** gates and hands `admin` to `RegisterLegalHoldAdminRoutes`; the mount site in `service.go` supplies `requireFreshMFA(...)` and `requireAdminRole()`. `withGate` composes a chain and skips a nil gate.
- **The census learned to follow a parameter across frames, positionally.** Its gate resolution accepted a gate passed by name and looked at the enclosing function's callers — one level. `RegisterLegalHoldAdminRoutes(r, admin)` is called from inside `RegisterRemoteSupportAdminRoutes` with the *parameter*; the literal gate sits one frame further up. On the day the writes were gated, the census called them ungated. Resolution is now transitive (depth ≤ 3) and follows the **parameter position**: which parameter the chain names, which argument that is at each call site, and what sits there (a literal gate; another parameter → recurse; anything else → open mount). The two "undecided" register entries are gone; a gated route cannot sit in the register.
- A behavioural pair measures what the text-reading census cannot: `requireAdminRole` refuses `user`/no roles and admits `admin`/`super_admin`; the legal-hold registration puts a gate in front of both writes and not the read (sentinel gate, no database). `TestTheLegalHoldGateIsTheAdminGateNotTheFreshnessGate` pins the mount line to *which* gate goes *where*.

## Type of Change

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security

## Testing

- [x] Unit tests pass — `go test ./internal/access/` green
- [x] Lint passes — `golangci-lint` 0 issues; `gofmt`, `go vet`, `orgscope -fail`, `testmatrix`, `check-docs-drift.sh` clean; verified on this commit alone
- [x] Manual testing performed — mutation rounds below

**Eight mutations against a green no-op control — two stayed green on the first run, each exposing a census limit that was then closed:**

- the mount site passing `nil` for the admin gate stayed **green**: resolution accepted *any* literal gate anywhere on the caller's line, so the freshness gate going to a *different* parameter counted for the legal-hold writes. Now positional → red.
- the two gates **swapped** stayed **green by the census's own rule** (either gate is a classification) while letting any user with a fresh second factor release a litigation hold. Pinned → red.
- red first time: the registration ignoring the parameter; `withGate` dropping the gate (text unchanged, so only the behavioural test goes red — which is why it exists); `requireAdminRole` admitting everyone; non-transitive resolution; and the read gated too (positive-path control).

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows the project style guidelines
- [x] Self-reviewed the changes
- [x] Added tests for new functionality
- [x] Updated documentation if needed

author: brendanlong
body:
A review pass over the whole repo for duplication, special cases, dead code and UI consistency, in four commits:

**Web dashboard + CLI output layer.** One `act()` for the four job buttons; the host card drops `driver` (the backend never filled it), `pkg` (only its diff matters, and the error line already shows that) and `root`; a shared card's foreign usage sits in its state cell instead of a holder column that repeated the running table; the page ports the CLI's `shared N/M free, none owned`, `needs N gpus`, queue placement after a reorder and `(exit N)` fallback; registry errors draw in place instead of re-toasting every refresh; the updated ticker uses the document's own `gathered_at`. CLI: one `read_registry_warned()`, one `_answer()` tail for cancel/reorder/preempt/estimate, one `host_answer()` for the host-verdict commands, one `package_root()`, one not-a-repo error, one `job_uri()`; elapsed times and pod ages use `format_duration` like every other duration on the line; `status --json` goes through `jsonout.emit`; `version` renders its own document.

**Host side.** `dispatch` and `health` are ordinary subparsers, so the argv prelude goes, with `dispatch --once/--interval`, `enqueue --no-dispatch`, `runner.main`, the `list` subcommand and the bare `config` form (all test-only). The lock body uses the same tolerant readers as everything else; both Popen calls share one helper; the cleanup walkers share their finished-age preamble; the three upload commands share one binary lookup and one run-or-fail; `reorder` answers with its own refusal like `preempt` and `estimate`, so the control side stops inventing one. `util_sampled_at` and `progress_at` were written and never read.

**Control plumbing.** `forget_host_locked()`, `_terminate_and_forget()`, `env_prefix()` in `remote`, `parse_timestamp()`, one `Reporter`, one disk default, one pod prefix, one Python floor, one ssh timeout. Gone: the transport's never-set `extra_options`/`state_dir`, `DesiredHost.image`/`idle_minutes` (the pod's config is the record), unread `BootstrapResult`/`Connection`/`RemoteError` attributes, RunPod's unreachable rate-limit raise and never-passed kwargs, and `scripts/runpod_day_one.py` (superseded by `tests/test_runpod_e2e.py`).

**Docs.** `requirements-review.md` deleted (its live reasoning is in the wiki; the rest described a different program). ARCHITECTURE.md keeps the contract and points at usage.md instead of carrying a second copy of the priority, estimate, preempt, shared-GPU, cleanup and reconcile stories (1374 → 1041 lines); its package tree matches the tree. usage.md and setup.md stop repeating each other and `--help`; stale bits fixed (the #36 caveat, `OLDER`, 0.83 GiB → 0.34, a troubleshooting row for a refusal that is now a usage error). `job.example.yaml` says what each key is and points at the doc. `gpuc host probe` names a card the way `host list` does.

Behaviour changes worth knowing: `python -m gpuc.host reorder` prints `{job_id, status, priority}` / `{job_id, error}` (was `{reordered}`); `python -m gpuc.host resume` prints JSON; `status --json` jobs carry `exit_code`; elapsed shows as `1h36m` rather than `96.2m`.

`./check.sh --fast`: 1287 passed, 3 skipped (no local GPU on CI), 2 deselected (billable).

body:
# CRI-191: PARAPET: navigation & info architecture (agent detail, deep links, breadcrumbs)

**Repository: `brokenbots/castle`** (parapet/)

## Feature request

Navigation and information-architecture improvements for the parapet UI, as requested in the Linear ticket:

1. An agent detail route (`/agents/:criteriaId`) backed by the existing, currently unused `GetAgent` RPC. The detail view shows the agent's identity, labels, status, and registered/last-seen information, plus the agent's runs via `ListRuns` filtered by `criteria_id` (the request supports this filter).
2. Run-list filter state reflected in URL query params, so filtered views are shareable and deep-linkable (e.g. `/runs?status=running`), and status chips on the run list are clickable into the corresponding filtered views.
3. Breadcrumbs plus a back affordance on run detail (browser back from deep in a run is currently the only exit), and a document title that reflects the current run/workflow name.
4. Agents list entries link into the agent detail pages.
5. Tests covering routing and URL param sync.

## Current behavior

Per the ticket:

- Only three routes exist: `/`, `/runs`, `/agents`.
- Agents have no detail view; the `GetAgent` RPC exists but is unused.
- Run detail has no breadcrumbs or back link; browser back from deep in a run is the only exit.
- No deep-linkable filtered views exist (e.g. `/runs?status=running` is not supported).
- The run ID is not shown in the document title.

## Required behavior

Observable behavior the implementation must provide — no implementation approach is prescribed beyond the RPCs the ticket names:

- Navigating to `/agents/:criteriaId` renders an agent detail view showing the agent's identity, labels, status, and registered/last-seen information, and lists that agent's runs (fetched with the `criteria_id` filter on `ListRuns`).
- Entries on the agents list are clickable and navigate to their agent detail views.
- Filter state on the run list is encoded in URL query params: changing filters updates the URL, and opening a URL carrying those params restores the corresponding filtered view, making filter state shareable/deep-linkable.
- Status chips on the run list are clickable and navigate to the run list filtered by that status.
- Run detail shows breadcrumbs and a back affordance so users can exit a run view without relying only on browser back.
- The document title reflects the current run/workflow name when viewing a run.

## Exit criteria

- Opening `/agents/:criteriaId` for a registered agent displays its identity, labels, status, registered/last-seen info, and its runs; agents-list entries navigate to these detail views.
- Applying run-list filters updates the URL query params; loading a shared URL (e.g. `/runs?status=running`) reproduces the same filtered view.
- Clicking a status chip on the run list lands on the corresponding filtered view.
- Run detail shows breadcrumbs and a working back affordance; the browser tab title shows the current run/workflow name.
- Tests for routing and URL param sync exist and pass.
- `npm run test:run` and `npm run typecheck` pass (ticket acceptance criteria).

author: jasonxudeveloper
body:
Four small things found while checking the tree after the refactor stack landed. No code changes.

## The licence never named anyone

`LICENSE` shipped with the Apache-2.0 appendix template unfilled — `Copyright [yyyy] [name of copyright owner]` — and grepping the tree turns up no copyright notice anywhere else: not in `Cargo.toml`, not in the README, no `NOTICE` file. So nothing in the repository said who holds the rights the licence grants. Now `Copyright 2026 Pamin Labs`.

Worth knowing that the appendix is a template Apache provides for applying the licence to *your own source files*, and shipping it verbatim is not a defect. The defect was the absence of a holder anywhere at all.

## The submodule pointer named a commit only a branch kept alive

It pointed at `9980ec8`, the branch commit, rather than `07becb1`, the merge that carried it onto the private repository's `main`. Reachable, so nothing was broken, but one commit behind and dependent on a branch that should be deleted.

## Four claims the code no longer backs

None of these had a test, which is why nothing failed when they went stale.

| where | said | actually |
|---|---|---|
| README `why` example | ends on `"modifier": "importance", "factor": 1.0` | the ranker stopped emitting modifiers that changed nothing |
| README Quickstart | `pamin stop` shuts the database down | it stops the resident server too |
| README "What It Does" | leads with page/tree structure | the same file lists it under "Not built yet" |
| `docs/cli.md` | lexical weight is `0.5`, in the table and the worked example | it has been `0.25` since the sweep across both corpora settled it |

The last one is the one that matters: the CLI reference documented the wrong value for a shipped default. The corrected `contribution` and `score` are recomputed from the `weight / (10 + rank)` that the same page defines, not re-run against a live index; the ordering of the three hits in the example is unchanged either way.

## The README said nothing about how well it works

It described the design at length and left a reader to open an ADR to learn whether any of it retrieves well. There is now a `## Measured` section:

- **Quality** — MIRACL Swahili dev (131,924 real passages, one language throughout) 0.7359 nDCG@10 / 0.9494 recall@50; XQuAD-R cross-language 0.6097 / 0.8864 and same-language 0.7971 / 0.9630.
- **Latency** — a write 32 ms, a search 32 ms on a small workspace and 204 ms over 13,014 documents with the reranker, 39 ms with `--rerank off`.

Two design choices about how these are stated, both reacting to how the earlier numbers here went wrong:

1. **Every figure is taken through `pamin search` and `pamin write` themselves**, and the section says so. The previous generation of numbers in this repository described a pipeline one stage shorter than the one that ships.
2. **What the figures are not is stated next to them** — a four-core result, and a write figure for short content — and the ADR is named as the source of truth if the two ever disagree.

A README carrying numbers is a README that can go stale, which is why the last round deliberately kept them out. The mitigation is labelling each with its corpus and pointing at the ADR, not omission; a project that measures this much and publishes none of it is the worse failure.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace` (19 suites green), `python3 ci/budget.py` — clean.
- The harness invocation the README now cites was run: `cargo test -p pamin-engine --test crosslingual -- --ignored --list` compiles and lists `search_reaches_across_languages` and `the_model_reaches_across_languages`.
- Every quality figure traces to the tables in `docs/adr/0001-tech-selection.md` and `crates/pamin-index/src/reranking.rs`; no figure here is new.

## Follow-up

`claude/scale-refactor-roadmap` is still on the `InternalDocs` remote — its history is already in `main` as the squash of #6, plus a duplicate of the commit #7 merged. Deleting a remote branch fails from this session (the proxy drops the send-pack), so it needs removing by hand.

author: philcunliffe
body:
## Feature or issue
`@hypaware/github` registered `github_events` with a `discoverPartitions` that returned exactly one hardcoded path, the `all` spool label. The rows carry no client identity and the plugin declares no `cachePartitioning`, so `appendChunk` commits every row under `github_events/source=unknown`, and the sink driver flushes the pending spool inside `discoverReadyPartitions` before re-running discovery. A dataset that answers the same single label both times hands the sink only the path that flush just emptied: the tick reported `status: 'exported'` with `partitionsExported: 1, bytesWritten: 0`, indistinguishable from an idle tick, and no blob sink, S3 sink, or central forward ever carried a GitHub row. Queries were unaffected, which is why nothing surfaced it: `createDataSource` re-discovers through `storage.discoverCachePartitions` and unions what it finds. Same defect as #1574, which #1586 fixed in two smoke fixtures; this is the same assumption in shipped product code.

## Solution
- `discoverParts` now lists the `PARTITION_LABEL` spool path first (so pending rows still get flushed) and then appends every committed partition `discoverCachePartitions` surfaces, deduped by path. This is `@hypaware/gascity`'s shape verbatim, the same one `@hypaware/otel` and `@hypaware/ai-gateway` use; no new idiom, no new dependency, no schema or config key.
- `test/core/github-events-sink-discovery.test.js` drives the real `githubEventsDatasetRegistration()` through the real `createSinkDriver` with two `github_events` rows and asserts the committed `source=unknown` partition reaches the sink in the same tick with bytes written. Driver level rather than dataset level, per the issue: the dataset-level call looks correct in isolation. Before the change it fails on `batches` (only the spool label is handed over); after, it passes.
- The stale paragraph on `createDataSource` that described `discoverParts` as hand-rolling a single path was corrected in the same commit; its `@ref LLP 0015` still applies unchanged.

**Code:** +37 / -11 lines

## Switches on a flow that is pending a maintainer decision
This fix makes the central forward sink actually carry `github_events`. Today an enrolled machine forwards no GitHub activity at all, because `discoverRolloutPartitions` (`hypaware-core/plugins-workspace/central/src/sink.js:603-625`) drops the emptied label the same way the blob and S3 sinks do. After this lands, it will forward.

That is exactly the open question on **#1805**, which neutral is holding with `neutral:stuck` for a maintainer. Its three findings:

1. On an enrolled machine, accepting the GitHub offer syncs `github_events` to the org server.
2. The flow is never named on any screen.
3. It is not opt-out-able: `@hypaware/github` owns no picker rows, and `source_withhold.js:243` never withholds the dataset.

Nothing here resolves that, and nothing here was meant to: no withholding, consent prompt, picker row, or opt-out plumbing is added or touched, and `src/core/cli/wizard/`, `source_withhold.js`, and `llp/` are untouched. The coupling is stated so the reviewer and the maintainer see it before either change lands. If the maintainer's answer on #1805 is that the forward needs a consent surface first, the sequencing question is whether this fix lands ahead of it or behind it.

## CPU and memory
`discoverParts` goes from returning a literal to one `discoverCachePartitions(cacheDir, { datasets: ['github_events'] })` call. 

**Corrected after review** ([F1](https://github.com/hyparam/hypaware/pull/1824#issuecomment-5706884442)): the scan is **not** confined to this dataset. `discoverCachePartitions` (`src/core/cache/partition.js:849`) walks the whole `<cacheDir>/datasets/` root and applies the `scope.datasets` filter at the leaf, *after* recursing - and it calls `readCursorSync` (a sync `readFileSync` plus `JSON.parse`) on every partition it reaches **before** that filter discards non-matching ones. So a `github_events` sink tick pays a sync cursor read per partition across every dataset in the cache, not only its own. It reads cursor files and directory entries, never row data, and allocates one `QueryPartition` per matching partition plus a `Set` of path strings. The sink driver calls it once per tick (`src/core/sinks/driver.js:204`) and a second time only when that tick flushed something (`:251`, guarded by `flushedAny`), which for a spool-backed dataset is the active case - so an exporting tick pays it twice. The conclusion is unchanged. Cost is O(total partitions) in CPU and O(matching partitions) in memory, and `github_events` declares no `cachePartitioning`, so the cache commits it under a single `source=` segment: the partition count is 1 in practice and does not grow with row count, repo count, or uptime. `createDataSource` already made this identical call on every query, so the per-tick work is not new to the process, just newly reachable from the sink path. The call sites are a sink tick (cron-scheduled, not a hot path) and query planning, neither per-record. No unbounded growth, no busy loop, no new allocation that scales with data volume.

## Noted, not landed
- The three `test/core/hyparquet-floor-pin.test.js` failures and the `src/core/otlp/server.js(85,51)` typecheck error are identical on `origin/master` and untouched here.
- `discoverParts` is now the sixth near-identical copy of list-the-label-then-scan across the plugin workspace (gascity, otel, ai-gateway, claude telemetry events, both graph plugins, github). A shared kernel helper would collapse them, but it is a cross-plugin refactor and not this fix.

Fixes #1593

author: acissejzhong
body:
The original optimization idea was inspired by this [MLA Ulysses CP proposal](https://gist.github.com/fegin/bd9bd9e9147ae1b11375dfb68815f78a).

For both CP backends, this PR keeps the head-shared `k_rope` headless during
communication and expands it across heads locally.

- **Ulysses CP**
  - Before: three input all-to-alls for materialized Q, K, and V. K included
    one repeated `k_rope` copy per head.
  - After: one all-to-all for packed Q and compact per-head K/V, plus one
    all-gather for headless `k_rope`. The output all-to-all is unchanged.
- **K/V all-gather CP**
  - Before: separate all-gathers for materialized K and V. K included repeated
    `k_rope`.
  - After: separate all-gathers for compact per-head K/V and headless `k_rope`,
    followed by local K materialization. Fusing them into one all-gather showed
    no benefit and slightly regressed performance.

## Summary

- Add Kimi K3 MLA Flex and Varlen backends that preserve compact K/V inputs
  through CP communication and materialize K locally.
- Wire model-specific CP backend selection, SPMD layouts, and focused tests.
- CP=8 benchmarks show a `4.03%` K/V all-gather throughput improvement; the
  Ulysses communication reduction does not produce a measurable speedup.

## Tests

Deterministic BF16 runs compared parent commit `5a30c8a1b` with PR commit
`0469340ff` at CP=2, using the same seed checkpoint (`seed=42`), 256 tokens per
step, and 100 training steps. Values come from full-precision TensorBoard
metrics; diffs are relative to the parent implementation.

The optimized collectives change backward reduction ordering, so the training
trajectories are not bitwise identical.

Performance was measured at CP=8 on 8 H100 GPUs with 2,048 tokens per step.
Each run averages steps 21-99 using full-precision TensorBoard throughput
metrics. All-gather results average three 100-step runs; Ulysses results
average five 100-step runs executed in balanced order.

### All-gather CP: before vs. after

| Step | Generic loss | MLA loss | Diff | Generic grad norm | MLA grad norm | Diff |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | `12.473673` | `12.473673` | `0.000%` | `27.2500` | `27.2500` | `0.000%` |
| 10 | `4.037894` | `4.083763` | `1.136%` | `6.3125` | `5.9062` | `6.436%` |
| 100 | `2.879660` | `2.914417` | `1.207%` | `5.8438` | `5.6562` | `3.209%` |

| Implementation | Mean TPS | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Before: `KVAllGatherCPFlexInnerAttention` | `574.3` | |
| After: `KVAllGatherCPMLAFlexInnerAttention` | `597.4` | **`+4.03%`** |

### Ulysses CP: before vs. after

| Step | Generic loss | MLA loss | Diff | Generic grad norm | MLA grad norm | Diff |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | `12.460487` | `12.460487` | `0.000%` | `27.2500` | `27.3750` | `0.459%` |
| 10 | `4.009133` | `4.295489` | `7.143%` | `7.1875` | `6.2188` | `13.478%` |
| 100 | `2.740203` | `2.837717` | `3.559%` | `5.4688` | `5.4062` | `1.143%` |

| Implementation | Mean TPS +/- run SD | Change |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Before: `UlyssesCPFlexInnerAttention` | `607.7 +/- 5.7` | |
| After: `UlyssesCPMLAFlexInnerAttention` | `593.9 +/- 30.9` | `-2.28%` |

### Performance analysis

- **K/V all-gather:** Both implementations use two input all-gathers, while
  the MLA path replaces per-head copies of `k_rope` with one headless tensor.
  Fusing compact K/V and headless `k_rope` into one all-gather showed no
  benefit and slightly regressed throughput, so the implementation keeps two
  all-gathers. Throughput improved by `4.03%`, consistent with the reduced
  communication volume.
- **Ulysses:** The complete path and controlled comparisons show:

  | Experiment | Before | After | TPS | Change |
  | --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | Full implementation comparison | No packing + repeated `k_rope` (3 all-to-alls) | Packed Q/KV + headless `k_rope` (1 all-to-all + 1 all-gather) | `607.7 +/- 5.7` -> `593.9 +/- 30.9` | `-2.28%` |
  | Q/KV packing ablation | Separate Q/KV + headless `k_rope` (2 all-to-alls + 1 all-gather) | Packed Q/KV + headless `k_rope` (1 all-to-all + 1 all-gather) | `599.3 +/- 9.5` -> `593.9 +/- 30.9` | `-0.91%` |
  | Headless `k_rope` ablation | Packed Q/KV + repeated `k_rope` (1 all-to-all) | Packed Q/KV + headless `k_rope` (1 all-to-all + 1 all-gather) | `609.5 +/- 3.5` -> `593.9 +/- 30.9` | `-2.56%` |
  | Headless `k_rope` without packing | No packing + repeated `k_rope` (3 all-to-alls) | No packing + headless `k_rope` (2 all-to-alls + 1 all-gather) | `607.7 +/- 5.7` -> `599.3 +/- 9.5` | `-1.38%` |

  Packed Q/KV with repeated `k_rope` matches the baseline, while both headless
  variants are slower on average. The additional all-gather offsets the lower
  `k_rope` payload, and the current packed, headless path also has high
  run-to-run variance. No conclusive Ulysses speedup was measured at this
  scale.

author: moshehbenavraham
body:
Closes #91.

## What changes

**Sanitizer matrix (`test.yml`, job `sanitizers`).** ASan+UBSan on GCC 13 and on Clang 18, and ThreadSanitizer on Clang 18. Each entry sets `CC`, proves the compiler family and version, and runs the new `scripts/ci/check_sanitizer_build.sh`, which prints the configured `CFLAGS`/`LDFLAGS` and the sanitizer runtime each binary links (`__asan_init`, `__ubsan_handle_*`, `__tsan_init`, libFuzzer entry points, static or via the shared runtime) and fails when any is missing. The syntax-check boot now runs inside the instrumented suite (the skip variable is gone from these jobs), the instrumented server is installed and booted through autorun against the isolated MariaDB, `scripts/ci/smoke_client.py` holds a pre-authentication conversation with it (a declined new account name, an invalid name, an over-long line, Telnet negotiation, an empty name that closes the connection), the health endpoint is checked again, and a graceful shutdown is required. `halt_on_error=1` is set for all three sanitizers and there is no suppression file. Logs are uploaded on failure.

**Production-linked fuzz targets (`luminari_fuzz`, job `fuzz`).** A libFuzzer executable that links the cutest objects, so every target drives the parser the server compiles and there is no mirror to drift:

| Target | Boundary |
| -- | -- |
| `dotenv` | `lib/.env` assignments |
| `config` | `lib/etc/config` (`load_config`) |
| `dg` | DG script expressions and `%variable%` substitution |
| `world` | world, mobile, object, zone, and trigger file records |
| `command` | socket line assembly (`process_input`, Telnet stripping) and the command tokenizers |
| `i3` | Intermud3 line framing and JSON-RPC decoding |
| `ai` | AI provider response decoders (OpenAI, Ollama) |
| `discord` | Discord bridge inbound JSON |
| `onboarding` | web onboarding envelopes, capability, and catalog controls |

The world loader and the config reader end the process on a rejected file, so those two run behind an exit guard (`exit()` is interposed and returns to the target) and without leak detection; every other target keeps leak detection on. Seeds, dictionaries, and regression inputs are checked in under `unittests/CuTest/`. `Test_fuzz_targets_replay_seed_and_regression_inputs` replays all of them deterministically in the ordinary production-linked suite in a forked child that fails on a signal, an unexpected exit status, or a sanitizer report. `scripts/ci/run_fuzz_targets.sh` runs each target with its dictionary, keeps and minimizes every reproducer under `fuzz-artifacts/`, and the job uploads that directory on failure. Pull requests get the replay plus 15 s per target and the existing protocol and binary-format fuzzers; `fuzz-campaign.yml` runs longer campaigns weekly and on demand.

**Defects the campaigns found**, each fixed at the root with its reproducer saved as a regression input:

- `asciiflag_conv_aff` shifted a 32-bit `int` past its width for uppercase affect letters from `F` on.
- A mob `Feat`/`MFeat` espec indexed the feat arrays with any number (out-of-bounds write at boot).
- `check_object` read a NULL short description.
- `parse_trigger` tokenized a NULL command list for an empty script.
- `flush_queues` left a live descriptor pointing at a pooled large output buffer, so a second `--` command linked the pool into a cycle and hung the server (player-triggerable).
- `var_subst` stepped past the terminator of an unterminated `%variable` and read beyond its stack buffer when the line filled it.
- Script arithmetic (`* / + -`) overflowed `int`; it now evaluates in `long long`.
- `load_default_config` leaked (and, after a rejected `menu` string, double-freed) its strings when the defaults were loaded again.
- The legacy 3/4-field record conversion indexed `zone_table[-1]` for a record outside every zone.
- `setup_dir` indexed `dir_option[]` with any `D<n>` exit direction; found by the fuzz job's first 15-second run on GitHub, whose uploaded, minimized reproducer became the regression input.
- `matching_quote` skipped the terminator after a trailing backslash in a quoted script token and read past the line (review finding).
- The `--` command discarded a player's pending output, including its own cancellation notice, whenever that output had grown past the small buffer; it now drops only the input queue (review finding).

**Review follow-up on the harness.** The config target now feeds `load_config_stream()` (split out of `load_config()`, which still opens the file) an in-memory stream it owns and closes after a guarded exit, replacing the helper that closed a range of descriptors and left the parser's `FILE` behind. The world target bounds its index tables by every `#` byte, because `get_line()` and `fread_string()` split a line longer than `READ_SIZE - 1` bytes and its tail can become a record header the newline-based count missed; the input that overflowed `parse_room()` through that path is a regression input.

**Documentation.** `docs/guides/TESTING_GUIDE.md` now has a "Sanitizers and Fuzzing" section with the job table, the reproduction commands, the supported compilers cited from the compiler policy, the no-suppression rule, the MemorySanitizer assessment (not enabled: the MariaDB client, json-c, libevent, libcurl, OpenSSL, libgd, and libcrypt are uninstrumented), and the OSS-Fuzz suitability note. The CMake guide documents `LUMINARI_FUZZ`.

## Acceptance criteria from the issue

- ASan+UBSan on both intended compilers, failing on the first unsuppressed finding: the `sanitizers` matrix with `halt_on_error=1` and `check_sanitizer_build.sh`.
- Syntax boot and a pre-auth client interaction under sanitizers: in all three matrix entries.
- TSan covers the threaded subsystems: the full production-linked suite (AI worker, Intermud3 client thread, logging, database handoff) plus boot and client smoke run under `-fsanitize=thread`; nothing is excluded.
- Each named trust boundary has a production-code fuzz target: the nine targets above plus the existing protocol and binary-format fuzzers.
- CI uploads minimized reproducers and logs on failure: `fuzz-artifacts/` and `sanitizer-logs/`.
- Fuzz findings become permanent deterministic tests: the regression replay test plus focused CuTest cases.
- Reproduction commands and supported platforms are documented.

## Verification

- `luminari_fuzz` (Clang 18, `-fsanitize=fuzzer-no-link,address,undefined`): four local campaigns of 6 to 10 minutes across all nine targets on this branch found the defects above; the final campaign on the fixed tree ran clean, and every seed and regression input replays clean.
- Full production-linked suite under ASan+UBSan with the syntax boot against a fresh isolated MariaDB: 1662 tests OK. Under ThreadSanitizer: 1662 tests OK, no reports.
- Every job of `test.yml`, `integration.yml`, `quality.yml`, `hygiene.yml`, and `security.yml` (33 jobs including the three sanitizer entries and the fuzz job) passed as local container replicas (`scripts/ci/local/run.py`) on the review follow-up commits; the two GCC Release jobs, the GCC 16 warning budget, the Debug Clang job, and the clang-tidy gate were rerun on the final commit after the follow-up fixes to the new test code.
- The review findings were reproduced before fixing: the old record count overflowed `parse_room()` under AddressSanitizer on the new world input, and the old `matching_quote` read past the substitution line on the new dg input; both new focused tests fail on the old code and pass on the fixed code.
- GitHub's own runs: all three sanitizer entries passed end to end (1660 tests, the client interaction, and the graceful shutdown), and the fuzz job proved its artifact path by finding the exit-direction defect above and uploading its minimized reproducer.

author: dnobj
body:
## Summary

Plan-first docs for the console's discovery widget (ADR-0072). The code follows in one PR once this merges.

**Why.** "Discover devices on my network" is one of the most common console requests.
- Today the model re-types the whole scan as a markdown table: about 70k input tokens for 31 devices, and nothing on it is clickable.
- Adding the new cameras means asking again, and then approving **one card per device**, because onboarding gates account creation per device (ADR-0059).

**What ADR-0072 decides**
- **Each scan is kept server-side for a day** (`discovery_scans`), because the browser's copy of a tool result stops at 50 items. The tool result names the scan and says which devices are already registered.
- **The console renders the scan as a widget,** built from the structured tool result only.
  - It shows Axis devices by default, with an All toggle, and nothing is pre-checked.
  - Rows that can't be added say why.
- **The widget's Add button is the approval: one click, two requests.**
  1. A same-origin, all-or-nothing POST builds one `add_discovered_devices` session from the scan row. It never trusts the request body.
  2. The existing `POST /api/chat/confirm/{token}` approves it.
  - So the approver check, confirmation password, per-token lockout, audit row and console note are all unchanged, and a retry reuses the token.
- **One executor handles the batch under that one approval.** It is added to **both** provisioning-authority lists, and for each device it:
  1. re-checks identity, fail-closed: the unauthenticated serial must match the MAC, which guards against DHCP handing the address to another box;
  2. registers the device;
  3. onboards it. No nested per-device card is raised.
  - It succeeds only when every device ends up credentialed; otherwise the error names each gap.
- **The model summarises the scan** instead of reprinting it. The prompt line is scoped to the text console.

**Out of scope:** the widget surviving a reload (KL-CB-008), a chat batch-add tool, and #404's periodic scan, dismissals and discovery page.

**Owner-overridable decisions:** see the table in the ADR (batch cap 20, scan freshness 60 min, onboarding concurrency 4, no API-key restriction, …).

## Files
- `docs/specification/decisions/0072-discovered-devices-are-added-from-the-chat-in-one-click.md` (new)
- `requirements/discovery.md`: FR-DISC-010 📋, FR-DISC-011 📋; FR-DISC-008 names the widget path
- `requirements/web-chatbot.md`: FR-CB-021 📋, KL-CB-008 ⚠️
- `user-stories/network-discovery.md`: US-ND-006 📋
- `INDEX.md`, `ui-deferred.md`

## Test plan
- [x] `pytest tests/test_doc_inventories.py tests/test_doc_links.py`: 181 passed
- [ ] CI

Refs #404
