author: israeltraigent
body:
## Summary

`epsilon_pareto_gate`'s objective parser silently coerced any non-`"maximize"`
`direction` value (or a missing one) to `"maximize"`. On paths that bypass
schema validation — the deprecated `tvl-ci-gate --policy` legacy branch and
the public `epsilon_pareto_gate` API — a typo'd `direction` (e.g.
`"maximise"`) silently inverted the non-inferiority/superiority test and
could flip a Promote/Reject verdict. `_parse_objectives` now raises
`ParseError` on a missing/empty `name` or an out-of-enum `direction` for
non-banded objectives, so the gate fails closed on its own input.

Closes #16

## Verification

- `PYTHONPATH=<worktree>/python pytest -q tests` → exit 0 (536 passed)
- tests added: `tests/test_promotion_objective_validation.py` (typo'd
  direction, missing direction, missing name all raise `ParseError`; a valid
  objective still parses and evaluates)
- re-verified on trunk (`origin/main` @ `4bc0df5`): before the fix, the same
  four assertions failed with `DID NOT RAISE ParseError` — the typo'd
  `"maximise"` direction was silently accepted and coerced, and a candidate
  that regressed hard on that objective produced no rejection from the
  parser. Red run captured, then reverted to green after the fix (see PR
  diff).

## Risk

Medium — this changes `_parse_objectives` from "always succeeds" to "raises
on invalid input" for two entrypoints that used to accept malformed
objectives silently (`tvl-ci-gate --policy` and the public
`epsilon_pareto_gate` API). Any caller currently passing an
absent/misspelled `direction` will now get a loud `ParseError` instead of a
silently-wrong verdict — that is the intended fix, but it is a behavior
change worth a reviewer's attention. Banded objectives (identified by a
`band` key) are exempt from the direction check since they are tested via
TOST equivalence, not a maximize/minimize direction; verified against the
existing banded-objective tests, which all still pass. No new dependency.

author: tokuhirom
body:
## Summary

`next()`, `last()`, and `redo()` — the explicit empty-argument-list call form of the loop-control
statements — used to make mutsu print a false-positive `Useless use of () in sink context` warning,
even though the program's output was already correct.

```
$ raku repro.raku
1
3

$ target/debug/mutsu repro.raku
Useless use of () in sink context
    at repro.raku:3
1
3
```

## Root cause

`next_stmt`/`last_stmt`/`redo_stmt` (`src/parser/stmt/simple/control_stmts.rs`) consumed the
keyword (and an optional label) but left a trailing empty argument list `()` entirely unconsumed.
The statement-list parser then re-entered at the leftover `();`, parsed it as a **separate**
statement — a bare empty-list literal (`Expr::ArrayLiteral([])`) — and appended it right after the
`Stmt::Next`/`Stmt::Last`/`Stmt::Redo` node:

```
Next(None),
Expr(Grouped(ArrayLiteral([]))),   // phantom statement from the un-consumed "()"
```

The sink-context warning pass walks every statement in a block statically, so it flagged that
phantom statement, even though `next()`'s control transfer means it never actually executes.

Found while investigating `mzef install`: the vendored zef's `Zef::Client.rakumod` writes `next();`
in sink position inside a `for` loop, so this warning fired on every `mzef` invocation going
through that code path.

## Fix

`next_stmt`/`last_stmt`/`redo_stmt` now consume a literal empty argument list (`()`, optionally
with inner whitespace/comments) right after the keyword/label, mirroring how `return_stmt` already
special-cases `return()`. A non-empty parenthesized form (e.g. `last(LABEL)`, a real call with a
`Label` argument) is left untouched.

## Test plan

- Added regression cases to `t/control/sink-warning.t` for `next()`/`last()`/`redo()` in sink
  position inside a `for` loop, asserting both the correct output and the absence of the warning.
- `cargo fmt --all`, `make lint` (all four configurations), `make test`, and `make roast` all run
  clean locally. The only `make roast` failures are the three documented container-only exceptions
  in `docs/agent-environments.md` (`roast/6.c/S32-io/file-tests.t`,
  `roast/S16-filehandles/filetest.t`, `roast/S32-io/IO-Socket-Async.t`, plus `eof.t`'s bad-plan
  shape) — unrelated to this change.

Closes #8610

author: pryancito
body:
## Deadlock (kernel, master since #1198)

Seen on QEMU with build `03a7b287da`:

```
[DEADLOCK: spinlock(s) stuck >8s] cpu=3 at zircon-object/src/object/mod.rs:375
HOLDER cpu=3 at zircon-object/src/object/mod.rs:394
```

Line 375 is `KObjectBase::name()`, line 394 is the lock in `signal_change()`. Same CPU on both sides: a self-deadlock.

Chain: `Process::exit` → `signal_set(PROCESS_TERMINATED)` holds the process's `KObjectBase` lock while it runs the callbacks → the fork-time callback drops the file table → dropping a pty master sends `SIGHUP` to the foreground group → the `[signal]` trace from #1198 calls `current_process_pid_name()` → `proc.name()` on the exiting process → spins forever on the lock its own CPU holds. Every exit of a terminal that still owned its pty wedged that CPU.

**Fix:** `KObjectBase::try_name()` (`try_lock`, `None` when held), exposed on the `KernelObject` trait (default `Some(self.name())`, the macro overrides it), and every `[signal]`/`[wait]` trace name goes through it, printing `?` instead of blocking in the contended case.

## CPU-exception report

`TrapReason::GernelFault` (#GP from a misaligned SSE access or a non-canonical pointer, #DE, ...) only logged at `warn!`, so at `LOG=error` such a death left just `[exit] killed by signal SIGSEGV` with no fault line at all. That is exactly what lunarbg's `SIGSEGV at pc=0x41d321` looked like in the same log: no "unhandled page fault" report because it was not a page fault. The path now reports at `error!` with `proc=`, `pc` as `lib+offset`, registers, code bytes and the user-stack backtrace, via a `dump_user_fault_context` helper shared with the page-fault path (no behaviour change there).

## Validation

- `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --all-features` (Build CI `workspace`): clean.
- `cargo test -p linux-object --lib` (81) and `cargo test -p zircon-object --lib --features libos,aspace-separate` (124): pass.
- Not runtime-tested here (this sandbox's QEMU cannot run user processes, see #1201 review).

## Summary
`tvl-check-operational` had no exception handling around module loading: a missing
or malformed module file raised straight out of `main()`, printing a raw Python
traceback and exiting 1 with no JSON emitted even under `--json`. `tvl-check-structural`
already handled this case gracefully. This PR gives `tvl-check-operational` the same
fail path: catch the loader's error types, emit a structured `PhaseResult` error
payload (or a plain `Error: ...` line without `--json`), and exit 2.

Closes #20

## Verification
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q tests` → exit 0, 536 passed (log: `gate-20-full.log`)
- tests added: `tests/test_cli_error_paths.py` (4 new parametrized cases covering both
  `tvl-check-structural` and `tvl-check-operational` on a missing file and on malformed
  YAML, with and without `--json`)
- re-verified on trunk: ran both CLIs against a missing file with `--json` before
  fixing — `tvl-check-structural` already emitted a JSON error payload and exited 2;
  `tvl-check-operational` dumped a raw traceback (`tvl.errors.ParseError`) and exited 1
  (log: `repro-20.log`)
- red-before-green: reverted `tvl_tools/tvl_check_operational/cli.py` to the trunk
  version and re-ran the new tests — the two operational-CLI cases failed with the
  pre-fix traceback, the two structural-CLI cases passed (log: `gate-20-red.log`)

## Risk
Low: the change only adds a caught-exception fallback path around an existing
`load()` call; the success path (`check_operational` result handling) is untouched.
No new dependency.

author: mustachemushroom
body:
## Why

`aio-agentic-sdlc` is a **public** repository with **no LICENSE file**, which means it defaults to all-rights-reserved. That is inconsistent in two directions:

- `pyproject.toml:11` already declares `license = { text = "PolyForm Noncommercial License 1.0.0" }`
- `agentic-backlog-kit` ships `LICENSE.md` + `COMMERCIAL.md` with exactly that posture

So the intent was never ambiguous — the file was just missing. GitHub's community health check scored this repo 37% against the kit's 75%, with the license as the main gap.

## What

- Add `LICENSE.md` — PolyForm Noncommercial 1.0.0, mirroring `agentic-backlog-kit`
- Add `COMMERCIAL.md` — dual-licensing terms, same wording, pointed at this project
- Rewrite the README `## Licensing Note` section, which still read as a pre-publication to-do ("When you publish this to GitHub, it is highly recommended to select a license...") despite the repo having been public for some time

No code or behavior changes.

## Review notes

The license wording is a deliberate copy of the backlog kit's, with only the project name and self-references adjusted, so that the three repositories state one consistent posture rather than three drifting variants.

author: mike-axiom-mir
hannahhoward
body:
## Summary

The demo shard has failed a different test on each of the last three `main` runs, always a `toBeVisible` timeout on the result of an interaction. Two causes:

- `next dev` compiles each route and server function on first use, and the cost lands on whichever expectation reaches it first. On CI the demo shard now runs `next build` into its shard dist directory and serves the build, so nothing compiles during the run. All four committed darwin baselines match the production build pixel for pixel across five runs.
- A click or fill issued between the server render and React attaching is silently lost, so the next expectation waits out its budget. Every document load followed by an interaction now waits on the shell's `data-hydrated` attribute: 15 sites in `demo.spec.ts` (first commit) and 27 across the ui shard's specs (second commit), through helpers in a shared `apps/web/e2e/shell-hydration.ts`. Loads followed only by assertions, the native form submission one search test exists to exercise, and the two pages outside the shell whose existing assertions already wait for their mount effects are left as they are, with the reasons in the code.

The `ui` shard keeps the dev server: Next inlines `NODE_ENV=production` into every bundle a build emits, so a built server refuses the `x-clockwork-persona` header those specs authenticate with.

Budgets: the demo shard's CI expectation budget drops from 20 s to 15 s, sized from the slowest measured expectation on the built server (1.33 s) at the runner's four-fold slowdown; the ui shard's budgets are unchanged.

## Verified

Run with the shards' exact commands and environment from `scripts/release-suites.mjs`: demo 21/21 four times (78 to 84 s including the build, against 99 s on the dev server), ui 113/113 four times (about 160 s, unchanged by the waits), `node --test scripts/release-artifacts.test.mjs` 37/37, traceability and release-test-inventory checks, Prettier, ESLint and `tsc` on the touched files. The first commit's CI run was fully green on `macos-15`, gate included.

author: uuriko
body: ## Problem Home `#dasha-digest` paints a Dexscreener tape line from the evening digest Worker snapshot (`/digest.json` `tick` / seed). UX hunt saw that line go stale (`$0.0001384 · -24.7%`) while same-origin `GET /price` was live (`~$0.0000897`). Evening digest tick stays a separate Worker job; this PR is the home client remount. ## Approach Digest remount already lives in `dasha-digest.mjs` (`digestRemountScript` → `#dasha-digest-remount`), injected by the Worker HTML transform. No Muse / Motley / Room / wrangler files. On `/` load (and every ~60s): 1. Still fetch `/digest.json` for news rows. 2. Overlay the Dexscreener price / 24h change / liq line from same-origin `GET /price` (`priceUsd`, `change.h24`, `liquidityUsd`, `pair` only). 3. Fail soft: keep last good `/price` this session; if none, hide stale Dex dollar numbers (`$dasha` only) rather than invent. 4. Do not invent mint/pair. Dex href is `https://dexscreener.com/solana/{pair}` from `/price.pair`. 5. `fetch(priceHref)` uses `var priceHref='/price'` so leftover Studio `#price-now` strip does not eat remount. `String.replace` injection now uses function replacers so `$` in the remount script cannot expand (`$'`). ## Prove (after merge / Worker ship) ```bash # live JSON curl -sS https://www.getdasha.com/price | jq '{ok,priceUsd,change,liquidityUsd,mint,pair,asOf,stale}' # home remount source now fetches /price (not evening tick as the number) curl -sS https://www.getdasha.com/ | grep -o "priceHref='/price'" curl -sS https://www.getdasha.com/ | grep -o 'id="dasha-digest-remount"' # first paint may still show the last digest snapshot; after JS remount # the visible Dexscreener row must match /price (or "$dasha" if /price failed) ``` Unit: ```bash node dasha-digest-tick.test.mjs node dasha-digest-home.test.mjs node dasha-home-crew-line.test.mjs ``` ## Stay-outs - No Muse product IA (#225) - No Motley leftover maps (#227) - No Instinct evaluator-start (#226) Telegram invite line - No Project Room - No wrangler deploy / Designer publish / `dasha-lobby-static-gen.mjs`

author: chad4545
body:
## Summary

Track C, PR 2 of 2 for #357. Rebased onto `main` after #359 and #362 merged; one feature commit plus one review-fix commit. Reviewed on Fable (integration-guardian, architect, code-critic, test-critic, doc-critic, ux-critic) with a tier-1 verification of the fixes.

`coral-cli backend provider-host list|inspect|evict` now reach a draining coordinator, and a coordinator that has released a proxy set's administration control answers with a typed torn-down disposition instead of a whole-inventory throw.

- **Admission.** Four operational-catalog entries (`provider_host.list`, `list.v2`, `inspect`, `evict`), each reusing its RPC spec's own `requires`, all `requiresRunningLifecycle: false`, all `onRefusal: 'report-refusal'`: a successor cannot discharge an eviction (it resolves no row for the exact ref and answers `provider_host_not_found` before reaching `evictHost`). `evict` joins `acceptedDrainingRecovery`; `drainingRecoveryIngress` stays a conjunct, so an accepted eviction wakes a retained shutdown only while draining. Capabilities are read, not widened: a nested child still lacks `system:shutdown`.
- **AC13, observed.** The local coordinator owner survives a drain (in-memory inventory, drain-built `evictHost`). The exposure is a proxy set whose control this coordinator released: the drain's final step settles every set's control close before the IPC socket, so a hold there leaves IPC serving with owners that can no longer be asked, and `captureInventory` / `discoverRetainedEvictionOwner` threw `provider_host_inventory_unavailable` for the whole inventory. The same release happens on a healthy coordinator for containment and succession.
- **The torn-down answer.** The fact is owned where it happens: `initiateControlClose` in the set authority raises `controlReleased`, and its four `providerHosts` wrappers refuse at call entry without sending (`ProviderHostOwnerTornDown`). A `control_client_closed` from a sent call (dead proxy, lost reply) keeps `provider_host_inventory_unavailable`, whose remediation is the right one for "may have run". The service partitions released owners out of the inventory; `inspect`/`evict` on a ref that no observed owner holds, or a work-dir selector while any owner is unasked, answer `provider_host_owner_torn_down` (503, exit 75) naming the owners, the ref or directory, and the exits: `backend status`, the successor once it serves, `shutdown-recovery abandon provider-control-and-ipc-authority-release` for a held drain, or the released set's own token for containment.
- **New address for the new field.** `coordinator.provider_host.list.v2` returns `{ hosts, tornDownOwnerIds }`; v1 stays exactly `{ hosts }` and answers `provider_host_inventory_unavailable` when any owner is torn down, as it always did, because the released v0.10.9 CLI parses it `.strict()`. The CLI calls v2 and falls back to v1 on method-not-found. `provider-host list` prints a `provider_host_owner_torn_down:` line ahead of the header naming the unlisted owners, with `command=coral-cli backend status`.
- **Nested-session authorization.** The IPC operational gate now answers `missing_capability` (exit 77, the nested-session message) for a present principal lacking the capability, and `unauthorized` only when no principal was presented. This also corrects the four pre-existing drain-admitted routes and is pinned per route.

Deferred with an argument on record (review consensus): expressing the owner-adapter's third answer in its return type rather than a thrown class; collapsing the transport copy of the provider-host error-code set into one owner (coordinator services may not import `transport/rpc/catalog`, so the new invariant pins the copy instead); an invariant that spawn-successor routes are issued only through the fallback helper; `KnownIpcMethod` typing for `ensure`.

## Acceptance criteria

- **AC3** `draining-recovery.test.ts`: authenticated `list`/`list.v2`/`inspect` return rows without waking the retained shutdown; `evict` answering `evicted` wakes it exactly once after the response is written; `provider_host_shutdown_held` (409) and `provider_host_owner_torn_down` (503) do not; `jobs.list` still refuses.
- **AC3b** a non-draining IPC fixture: successful `jobs.abort`, `provider_proxy_set.contain.v2` and `provider_host.evict` each leave `onShutdownRecoveryAccepted` uncalled, asserted after the listener is closed.
- **AC13** real `ProviderHostAdministrationService` over a real `StubbedContainmentProviderHostManager` driven to `shutdown-held`: `list` returns the held row; `evict` traverses owner resolution to the hold. Real `createProviderProxySetAuthority` over a real control client: after `initiateControlClose` all four calls refuse without sending; after a peer-side close they keep `control_client_closed`.
- **AC11** `principal-route-requires` updated deliberately; `process-observation-composition` and `liveness-is-never-a-boolean` run explicitly; new `provider-host-error-code-vocabulary` invariant pins the transport copy of the error-code set to its owner.
- **AC12** `docs/cli-errors.md`, `docs/architecture.md`.

## Verification

- `npm run build`, `lint`, `format:check`, `typecheck:tests`, `knip`: clean.
- `npm test` run alone: zero failures beyond the host-level set that fails on pristine `main` on this machine.
- Two tier-review rounds (integration-guardian, architect, code-critic, test-critic, doc-critic, ux-critic); all BLOCKING and STRONG findings resolved. The round-1 tier-1 reviews corrected the design: torn-down is decided at the release, not inferred from a control-channel error.

Source only: no version bump, no `clients/bridge/` rebuild.

author: obra
body:
Follow-up to the one review finding on #1620, which is now merged.

The chat listing tests that touch `context_window` also set `context_length`, so a regression that dropped the top-level spelling, or its use in `row()`, left every test green. A gateway publishing only `context_window` would then get no window at all, and `ApplyTokenBudget` would skip the total-context clamp and allocate output with no ceiling.

This adds that case. It was checked against exactly that mutation (`FirstPositiveInt` called without `m.ContextWindow`): the new test fails, while `TestListModelsPrefersContextLengthOverContextWindow` stays green, which is the distinction the old coverage could not make.

author: gogoalswo
body:
## 무엇

`server/src/combat.ts` 의 상태 기계를 옮겼다.

```
idle ──(사람이 어그로 안으로)──▶ chase ──(사거리 도달)──▶ attack
  ▲                                                        │
  └──────────── 집에서 leash 넘게 멀어지면 돌아간다 ◀───────┘
```

- **휘두르는 동안 몬스터도 묶인다** (`monsterRootMs`). 화면이 공격 클립을 보여 주는 창과 같은 길이라, 동작이 끝나는 순간에 발이 떨어진다
- 쫓는 놈끼리도 통과하지 않는다. 미는 쪽은 지금 움직인 그 놈이다 — 한 마리를 쫓아 여럿이 몰려도 사거리 언저리에 둥글게 선다
- 서 있는 80마리까지 매 프레임 밀지 않게 **움직인 놈만** 민다. 폰에서 버겁다

## 죽으면 저절로 살아나지 않는다

체력이 0 이 되면 `dead` 로 두고 가만히 둔다. **사람이 화면을 눌러야** 마을에서 되살아난다. 웹 클라에서 5초 뒤 제자리에서 일으켜 세웠더니 죽은 걸 읽기도 전에 화면이 사라져서 죽은 줄도 몰랐다 — `ZoneRoom` 에 같은 주석이 있다.

죽어 있는 동안 이동 입력은 순번만 갱신하고 위치는 안 옮긴다. 안 갱신하면 나중에 서버를 붙였을 때 클라 보정이 그 구간 내내 멈춘다.

## 확인

| | |
|---|---|
| 어그로 9.1m 밖 | 안 움직임, `idle` |
| 어그로 안 | 1초에 **8.00 → 4.40m** (이동속도 3.6 과 일치) |
| 사거리 1.9m 안 | **8 피해** — TS `computeDamage(9, 8)` 과 일치 |
| 공격 간격 안 | 한 번만 |
| 줄이 끊기면 | 쫓기 포기, 집 쪽으로 |
| 죽으면 | 120틱을 돌려도 안 살아나고, 움직이지도 못함 |
| 부활 | 마을에서 체력 가득 |

고도 테스트 6개(`movement`·`world`·`touch`·`monster`·`combat`·`aggro`), `npm test` 135개 전부 통과.

## 아직 없는 것

보스 범위 공격(`MonsterKind.aoe`)은 안 옮겼다. 예고 원을 그리는 화면이 필요해서 UI 단계와 같이 한다. 지금 보스는 평타만 친다.

## 합친 뒤 볼 것

초원에 들어가면 **몬스터가 다가와서 때린다.** 체력이 줄고, 0 이 되면 `YOU DIED - tap to revive in town` 이 뜬다. 아무 데나 누르면 마을에서 체력 가득 차 되살아난다. 멀리 도망가면 몬스터가 제자리로 돌아간다.

author: peytonfrankecode
body:
Asked for: select one, assign it, and be able to work one at a time **or** do them all at once.

The number keys **toggle** now instead of switching, so places can be picked in any combination. That matters because the places usually fall into groups rather than lining up one by one — the same phrase means one parallel in two products and something else in a third, and answering those singly would work and would be tedious.

```
1-9   pick or unpick a place
A     pick every place (again to clear)
0     clear
X / typed name    answers everything picked
```

One at a time is picking one. All at once is `A` then answer. Anything in between now works too.

## Nothing picked is not the same as everything picked

Both are wanted, and they say different things, so both are kept:

- **Nothing picked** — stored once, globally. Covers products that aren't on this list, and months not yet collected.
- **Every row picked** — one decision per place, saying nothing about anywhere else.

The screen states which it's about to do rather than leaving it to be inferred.

A phrase stays open until every one of its places is answered. Advancing while some are undecided would silently abandon them, and the sales counter would claim work that hadn't happened.

A refusal is no longer reported as a save. When the typed name is in no checklist every job fails, and the previous code would have flashed `+0 sales` — which reads as done.

## Verified by breaking it

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| number keys switch instead of toggle | the combination check fails |
| only the first picked place answered | the per-place check fails |
| a total failure flashes success | the refusal check fails |

The desk page is checked by **executing** its script, so a syntax error there is a failing test rather than a blank screen found by a person.

Full suite green, 34 suites, EXIT=0.

body:
## Summary

Implements one bounded slice of #461: the first public **bring-your-own-agent challenge**.

The challenge asks a human, AI agent, or human+agent pair to classify six candidate objects against IDKMesh's existing canonical `ResultManifest v0.1` contract. It adds a deterministic evaluator, regression tests, and a public outcome-table protocol without creating a second result format or granting any repository authority.

Files in scope:

- `examples/challenges/byo-agent-001/challenge.json` — six frozen candidate manifests, source revision, and exact canonical-schema Git blob pin;
- `scripts/byo_agent_challenge.py` — zero-network deterministic evaluator using JSON Schema Draft 2020-12;
- `tests/test_byo_agent_challenge.py` — schema binding, exact blob pin, scoring, strict/fail-closed input, deterministic JSON, authority, and CLI contract tests;
- `examples/challenges/byo-agent-001/README.md` — participant protocol, limits, public outcome table, verification instructions, and provenance/run record.

## Motivation / integration

Issue #461 explicitly asks for a first public BYO-agent challenge with a small task, reproducible evaluator, and visible outcome table. Rather than inventing a toy task disconnected from IDKMesh, this challenge exercises the repository's existing worker-to-verification evidence boundary: `schemas/result-manifest.schema.json`.

The evaluator loads that canonical schema directly and verifies its Git blob object ID (`e2cd2f55cff59bb306ba74bfc63ff8f4c6ffd934`) before scoring. If the schema later changes, the challenge fails closed until deliberately versioned or repinned; a historical challenge cannot silently change meaning.

During stewardship review, the JSON loader was additionally hardened to reject duplicate object keys and non-finite `NaN`/`Infinity` tokens rather than inheriting Python JSON parser extensions. Regression coverage now pins that fail-closed behavior for participant/challenge inputs.

This scope does not overlap the open swarm-policy, review-capacity, README, interop, or gate-audit PRs.

## Scientific / evidentiary discipline

This is deliberately an **open conformance/onboarding exercise**, not a hidden benchmark. Fixtures and evaluator are public. The only supported claim is that, for the frozen challenge and pinned schema, classifications are scored deterministically.

The report explicitly marks:

- `hidden_benchmark_evidence: false`;
- `independent_review: false`;
- `integration_authority: false`;
- timing/reviewer effort as `self_reported_unverified`.

The documentation states that results do not establish general coding capability, model superiority, causal multi-agent benefit, security, independent review, or comparative efficiency. Those require separate controlled evidence.

## Validation

The branch is based on current `main` after #456 merged. Focused regression coverage includes schema binding and blob drift, correct/wrong scoring, structural submission failures, non-finite measurements, duplicate/non-standard JSON rejection, deterministic strict JSON output, authority flags, and CLI exit codes.

Fresh GitHub checks on the exact current PR head are the merge authority. Required `gate (3.11)` and `gate (3.13)` plus relevant security/schema checks must pass before merge; no checks will be bypassed.

## Related

- Progresses #461; does not close the umbrella issue.
- Uses `schemas/result-manifest.schema.json` as the sole semantic source of truth.

## Community Impact

This creates a low-cost public contribution path that does not require private context, paid compute, external credentials, or a specific agent vendor. Human and agent submissions can be recorded using the same transparent evaluator, while owner-controlled agents must be identified and cannot be miscounted as external participation.

The outcome table accepts negative/incomplete outcomes as well as perfect ones to reduce selection bias.

## AI/tool provenance

Implemented by the owner-controlled IDKMesh hourly issue steward using the connected GitHub integration and independently reviewed/hardened by the PR Integration Steward. No hidden chain-of-thought, credentials, paid compute, or repository authority is included in the challenge result.

## Risks / limitations

- The task is intentionally small and public; it must not be cited as a model benchmark.
- Participant time/review-cost measurements are self-reported unless a later independent protocol verifies them.
- The challenge is pinned to one schema blob. Intentional schema evolution requires versioning or repinning this challenge instead of silently inheriting new semantics.
- A passing challenge result is not merge authority and does not replace independent code review.

## Checklist

- [x] Focused change; no unrelated files.
- [x] Canonical contract reused instead of duplicated.
- [x] Deterministic regression tests added.
- [x] Strict/fail-closed parser behavior covered.
- [x] Documentation and public outcome protocol included.
- [x] Scientific/benchmark limitations explicit.
- [x] No network, secrets, paid compute, or write authority added.
- [ ] Exact-head required GitHub checks pass.

author: adityashett
body:
## Automated Root Cause Analysis

### 1) Root Cause

The `transform_data` task failed because it attempted to access a column named `'user_id'` from a pandas DataFrame, but the DataFrame received from the upstream `load_dataset` task does not contain a column with that name. The column was renamed to `'uid'` in the upstream data source. This is a schema drift issue.

### 2) Evidence

*   **Log Line Indicating Failure:**
    ```
    [2026-09-10 03:12:41,812] {python.py:194} ERROR - Task failed with exception
    ```
*   **Specific Error Type and Message:**
    The traceback clearly shows a `KeyError: 'user_id'`. This error occurs when trying to access a non-existent key (in this case, a column name) in a dictionary-like object (a pandas DataFrame column selection).

*   **Code Line Causing the Error:**
    ```python
    File "/opt/airflow/dags/tests/dag1.py", line 30, in transform_data
        user_ids = df["user_id"].tolist()
    ```
    This line in the `transform_data` function explicitly tries to select the column `"user_id"`.

*   **Upstream Data Definition (Source of the Drift):**
    The `load_dataset` function, which provides the data to `transform_data`, defines the DataFrame with the column named `"uid"`, not `"user_id"`.
    ```python
    # From DAG CODE, lines 21-23:
    data = {
        "uid": [101, 102, 103],
        "event_type": ["click", "view", "purchase"],
        "amount": [0.0, 0.0, 49.99],
    }
    df = pd.DataFrame(data)
    context["ti"].xcom_push(key="raw_df", value=df.to_dict())
    ```
    The `raw_df` XCom pushed by `load_dataset` will therefore contain `uid` as a key, not `user_id`. When `transform_data` converts this back into a DataFrame `df = pd.DataFrame(raw)`, the resulting DataFrame `df` will have a column `uid`, but not `user_id`, leading to the `KeyError`.

### 3) Confidence

**High**

## Proposed Fix
```diff
--- a/dags/tests/dag1.py
+++ b/dags/tests/dag1.py
@@ -27,5 +27,5 @@
 def transform_data(**context):
     raw = context["ti"].xcom_pull(key="raw_df", task_ids="load_dataset")
     df = pd.DataFrame(raw)
-    user_ids = df["user_id"].tolist()
+    user_ids = df["uid"].tolist()
     print(f"Processed {len(user_ids)} user records")
```

**Confidence score:** 1.0 (high)

**Diff applied:** True

**Estimated LLM cost:** $0.00000 USD (~$0.00000 CAD) -- 0 input / 0 output tokens on gemini-2.5-flash. Rates and FX are estimates from config/pricing.json, not a billed invoice figure.

**This Pull Request was opened automatically. A human review is required before merging.**

author: mikemcdougall
body:
## Summary

`FeatureServerField.Nullable`/`Editable` collapsed an omitted source member to the same value as an explicit `false`, and `FeatureServerSpatialReference` dropped `wkt`/`latestWkt` entirely. Both are typed members, so the lost data never reached `AdditionalProperties`.

## Changes

- `FeatureServerField` gains `IsNullable`/`IsEditable` (`bool?`, `null` when the source omits the member), alongside the existing `Nullable`/`Editable` (`bool`) members, **kept unchanged** for binary compatibility with published 1.x releases.
- `FeatureServerSpatialReference` gains `Wkt`/`LatestWkt` (`string?`). `Wkid`/`LatestWkid` stay `int` (unchanged) — the issue calls their own absence-collapse "related, not blocking on its own", and a plain `int` → `int?` change is a binary break (see below), so it's out of scope here.
- A hand-written `FeatureServerFieldConverter` reads `name`/`type`/`alias`/`nullable`/`length`/`editable`/`defaultValue`/`domain` once per field and populates both the legacy and tri-state properties from it, because System.Text.Json rejects two properties bound to the same JSON member name (`nullable`/`editable`), which rules out binding `IsNullable`/`IsEditable` to those keys directly via attributes.

### Why additive, not a type change

`FeatureServerField.Nullable`/`Editable` (`bool`) and `FeatureServerSpatialReference.Wkid`/`LatestWkid` (`int`) already shipped in 1.8.0. I first tried changing their types directly to `bool?`/`int?` and confirmed with `apicompat` (the same tool `scripts/validate-api-compat.sh` runs in CI) that this is a binary-breaking change:

```
CP0002: Member 'bool Honua.Sdk.GeoServices.FeatureServer.Models.FeatureServerField.Nullable.get' exists on [Baseline] ... but not on ...
CP0002: Member 'int Honua.Sdk.GeoServices.FeatureServer.Models.FeatureServerSpatialReference.Wkid.get' exists on [Baseline] ... but not on ...
```

The PR Gate's API Compatibility job runs on every PR with no override available (the breaking-change bypass is restricted to the manually dispatched major-release workflow), so a straight type change would fail CI. This PR instead adds new members and leaves the old ones untouched; I re-ran `apicompat` against the final diff and it reports no breaking changes.

## Testing

- `dotnet test tests/Honua.Sdk.GeoServices.Tests` — 222/222 passed (includes 5 new tests: omitted-vs-explicit `nullable`/`editable`, a full round-trip of every other `FeatureServerField` member including `AdditionalProperties`, and WKT-only spatial references on both a layer extent and a query response, matching the certification's capturing-handler style).
- `dotnet build Honua.Sdk.sln --configuration Release /p:TreatWarningsAsErrors=true` — 0 warnings, 0 errors (solution-wide, confirms no downstream project regresses).
- `dotnet tool run apicompat` (baseline 1.8.0 from nuget.org vs. this branch) — no breaking changes.
- `dotnet format --verify-no-changes` on the changed files.

Refs honua-io/honua-server#4599 (this closes the last SDK gap blocking its layer-metadata-discovery and source-inventory-scan boxes).

Closes honua-io/honua-sdk-dotnet#381

author: realacco
body:
## 무엇을

내 정보 화면에 「이 폰」 카드를 만들고, 화면 모드를 **기기 설정 · 밝게 · 어둡게** 중에서 고르게 한다. 누르는 순간 앱 전체가 바뀌고, 고른 값은 이 폰에만 저장돼 앱을 다시 켜도 남는다.

- 선택값 해석은 순수 함수(`shared/config/theme-preference.ts`), 저장은 스토어(`shared/config/theme-preference-store.ts`) — 둘 다 1층 테스트가 있고 일부러 깨뜨려 빨개지는 것을 확인했다
- 저장은 `expo-secure-store`(새 네이티브 모듈 없음). 로그아웃해도 지우지 않는다
- 켤 때 반대 테마가 비치지 않게: 저장값을 읽은 뒤에 그리고, 스플래시는 앱 셸이 창 배경을 칠한 **뒤에** 내린다. 읽기는 1초 한도, 스플래시는 3초 상한. 세션(토큰) 읽기는 테마 읽기를 기다리지 않는다
- 저장 쓰기는 누른 순서대로 줄을 선다 — 연타해도 마지막에 누른 값이 마지막에 저장된다. 낡은 쓰기의 실패는 알리지 않고, 같은 칩을 다시 누르면 다시 저장한다(실패 뒤 재시도)
- 기능 정의서 페이지를 새로 만들고 인덱스에 행을 넣었다

## 기능 정의서와 다르게 간 것

없음. 정의서(F-SES-09)는 이 PR 과 함께 새로 썼고, 리뷰에서 더한 동작(스플래시 붙잡기 · 1초 읽기 한도 · 3초 스플래시 상한 · 연달아 누르기)도 정의서에 반영했다 — https://app.notion.com/p/3dea433436ef81249493e9164ece2656

`shared/config/theme-provider.tsx` 를 고쳤다(디자인 시스템 규칙상 허락이 필요한 영역). 사용자가 이 기능 작업을 직접 요청해 그것을 허락으로 보았다. 토큰 값은 안 바꿨고, 쓰는 곳이 없던 `override` prop 을 지웠다.

## 관련 이슈

- #54 — 세션 `hydrate()` 가 저장소 실패로 던지면 스플래시(게이트)에 갇힌다. **이 PR 이 고치지는 않는다.** 테마 쪽은 같은 실패 모양을 막았고(던져도 · 멈춰도 `ready`), 3초 상한은 네이티브 스플래시만 내린다 — 세션이 `ready` 가 안 되면 게이트 로딩에 그대로 남는다. 기능 ID 가 달라(F-SES-04) 따로 고친다

## 3층 확인 — 눌러본 화면

**아직 못 봤다.** 에뮬레이터에서 확인할 것:

- [ ] 내 정보 → 이 폰 → 밝게 · 어둡게 · 기기 설정을 누를 때마다 앱 전체가 바로 바뀐다
- [ ] 어둡게를 고르고 앱을 완전히 껐다 켜기를 **5번** 해도 밝은 판이 한 번도 비치지 않는다
- [ ] 칩을 **빠르게 여러 번 연타**하고 마지막에 고른 값을 확인한 뒤 앱을 껐다 켜면 그 값으로 뜬다
- [ ] 기기 설정을 고른 뒤 폰의 다크 모드를 바꾸면 앱도 따라 바뀐다
- [ ] 로그아웃 → 다시 로그인해도 고른 값이 남아 있다
- [ ] 시스템 글자 크기를 키웠을 때 칩 세 개가 잘리지 않고 줄바꿈된다
- [ ] 상태바 글자 색이 고른 테마에 맞는다

알려진 한계: 스플래시 이미지 · 시스템 Alert · 키보드는 기기 설정을 따른다 (정의서에 적었다).

body:
People can connect the DorkOS app to self-hosted communities, enroll local agents, and exchange messages and files with other members. Agents run on their owners' machines. Accounts, approval and participation work without DorkOS Cloud.

The app now includes community channels, threads, unread state, files and agent controls. Historical messages cannot start old agent turns. A durable delivery queue preserves one confirmed reply across reconnects, held receipts and retries. Stop and removal revoke local authority before remote cleanup; each delivery checks the agent's current local manifest. Community credentials stay on the local server.

This completes deployment and password-recovery documentation, operator account recovery without email, durable file-cleanup retries, and required packaged acceptance in the merge queue. The existing local server remains Express and single-owner.

## Validation

- Complete packaged journey: one pass in 85.050 seconds in the merge queue; zero skips, retries, unexpected failures or report errors. Runs installed production packages with deterministic agent inference on an isolated Docker network. PostgreSQL remains reachable; public-IP and DorkOS-host access fail.
- Covers two communities, human admission/pairing, agent Join/Leave, exact reply/file bytes, restarts, offline/retry, held receipts/reload, live and held Stop, ejection, human post/file transfer, unread/thread behavior and mobile keyboard navigation.
- Independent inspection of seven screenshots, the mobile accessibility snapshot and three recorded browser pages passed.
- Real PostgreSQL/native conformance: 100 passing tests, four declared capability exclusions. Standalone browser: three passing cases. Current focused participation suite: 54 passing tests. Combined typecheck/lint: 33 successful tasks with existing warnings.
- Production verification before the readiness-only follow-up, `pnpm verify`: all 35 tasks passed in 25m27.068s (26 cached). Server: 1,117 files / 19,070 tests passed, with two declared skipped files / 55 skipped tests. Client: all 1,240 files / 15,507 tests passed.
- Follow-up `pnpm verify` passed all 35 tasks (34 cached); the scripts suite separately passed all 597 tests.
- Combined test-stability follow-up `pnpm verify`: all 36 tasks passed (35 cached).
- Independent `REVIEW.md` review accepted the production composition and each subsequent fix. Boundary mutations demonstrate failure when dispatch, origin, recursive-output, ejection-order and attachment-wire guards are removed.

The packaged runner waits for PostgreSQL over TCP so the image’s temporary Unix-socket initialization server cannot pass readiness early. The 30-attempt bound and sealed network are unchanged. Two isolated runner regressions prove delayed readiness and failure without launching the app; all 597 scripts tests pass. A real PostgreSQL startup drill reproduced the Unix-ready/TCP-refused window before final TCP readiness. Independent review accepted the fix and the fresh packaged proof.

Two existing test families exposed unrelated timing assumptions in the merge queue. Session queue tests now wait for successor lifecycle events; a final witness message proves removed adopted entries cannot run after the assertion. Controlled delayed settlement fails the original test and passes the correction; broken handoff and cancellation mutations still fail. The mobile sidebar fixture now keeps visits inside Today’s 04:00 boundary and exercises that edge with a fixed browser clock. The original fixture reproduces both browser failures; the corrected full mobile spec passes all 11 cases without retries. Both changes received independent `REVIEW.md` acceptance and change test code only.

The clean production build is `sha256:3aa6dfe659958f65b7f7fb64fe56b31bb63844411a7d381adc970c3350458e9b`; the successful proof adds only the independently reviewed 180-second overall Playwright budget. Per-assertion deadlines remain unchanged. No live inference credentials are used. Evidence and limitations are recorded in `specs/community-server/04-implementation.md`.

Closes DOR-589.
Closes DOR-594.
Closes DOR-595.
Closes DOR-596.

The architecture documentation is reconciled with main commit `a203bad52e`. The merge changes only docs and diagram assets; production code is identical to the fully verified `f4d1e36db8`. MDX generation, site typecheck, documentation guards, and independent `REVIEW.md` review passed; the three changed diagrams were rendered and visually inspected.

body:
## Summary

- Phase/Sub-phase: N/A. Follow-up to #318, not a V1 implementation slice.
- Linked issue: none. Raised in review on #318, where the gap was documented rather than fixed.
- Scope statement: **one concern.** A custom endpoint that requires no authentication could not be declared. In: an `"auth": "none"` opt-in, the flag's path to the three providers and across the provider protocol, and treating an empty key as absent. Out: anything about which credential is chosen when one does exist, and the origin-binding work tracked separately.

## The problem

`~/.makai/providers.json` is meant to cover a self-hosted llama.cpp, vLLM or LM Studio server. Those usually accept anything, including nothing. But all three wire formats available to custom providers refuse before opening a connection when no key resolves:

- `anthropic_messages_api.zig`, `streamAnthropicMessages`
- `openai_completions_api.zig`, `streamOpenAICompletions`
- `openai_responses_api.zig`, `streamOpenAIResponses`

Each has the same `api_key` block ending in `return error.MissingApiKey`. So the documented workaround was to name an environment variable holding a value the server throws away. #318 shipped that wording as a known limitation.

## What changed

An entry can declare `"auth": "none"`:

```json
{ "id": "local", "api": "openai-completions", "base_url": "http://localhost:8000/v1", "auth": "none" }
```

**It is an opt-in, and nothing else implies it.** An absent `auth` block still means "a key is required and none was found", so forgetting to log in fails loudly rather than quietly sending an unauthenticated request. An `auth` block that is present must be one of the two valid shapes; anything else is now a load error (`InvalidAuthMode`) instead of being silently ignored. That covers an object with no `env`, a non-string or empty `env`, a misspelled key such as `{ "environment": "KEY" }`, any other string, and any non-object non-string value. Each of those previously parsed as "no key" and surfaced much later as a confusing `MissingApiKey`, which is the same failure mode this PR exists to remove.

A provider that declares it still prefers a real key when one resolves, from the keychain or from the request, and only falls back to sending nothing.

**Path.** `custom_providers.auth_none` → `model_catalog.customModel` → `Model.allows_anonymous` → the three providers, which omit `Authorization` (OpenAI formats) or `x-api-key` (Anthropic) when the resolved key is empty. Everything else about the request is unchanged, so `anthropic-version` and `content-type` still go out.

**Vendor paths cannot be dragged into it.** Each provider refuses to honour the flag for the vendor ids it serves: `anthropic` on the Anthropic format, and `openai`, `deepseek`, `kimi`, `github-copilot`, `openai-codex`, `azure` on the OpenAI ones. A declared provider can never hold one of those ids, because they are reserved at parse time, so this only bites on a crafted protocol request. Honouring it there would cost nothing worse than an unauthenticated request to a URL the caller already chose, and no credential would leak either way, but refusing keeps the vendor paths uniformly credentialed and makes the invariant checkable rather than argued.

**Empty is now absent.** Key resolution treats a zero-length key from request options or from the environment as "not found" rather than as a credential. Without this, a blank key from a misconfiguration would have taken the new no-credential path silently instead of failing.

## Spec Alignment

- Clauses implemented: N/A.
- `Model` gains `allows_anonymous`, serialized on the provider protocol only when true. An absent field deserializes to `false`, which is the previous behaviour, so an older peer is unaffected in both directions. `docs/custom-endpoints.md` is updated in this PR.

## Traceability Matrix

- N/A. Not a V1 implementation PR; per `docs/review-process.md` §2 the matrix requirement is scoped to phase work.

## Backward Compatibility

- [x] Backward-compatible
- Notes: the flag defaults false everywhere and is only set by a declaration that did not previously parse. Two changes touch existing paths. An empty key is now treated as absent, turning a request that would have gone out with an empty `Authorization: Bearer` into a clear `MissingApiKey`. And `auth` blocks that were previously tolerated are now load errors, which is stricter than before on a config that used to load: a parse error disables **every** custom provider until the file parses, which is pre-existing behaviour in `loadCustomModels`, and the TUI reports it as a startup row naming the file and the error rather than failing silently. `auth` only became a field in the unreleased #318, so a config in the wild carrying one of these shapes is unlikely.

## Tests

- [x] Unit tests added: the opt-in parses and stays off otherwise, and two new rows in the config error table (`"auth":"anonymous"`, `"auth":true`); the flag reaches the model through the catalog; `allowsAnonymous` is off by default, on when declared, and refused for every vendor id in all three providers; Anthropic header assembly carries no `x-api-key` or `authorization` when the key is empty but keeps `anthropic-version` and `content-type`; the flag round-trips over the provider protocol and defaults off when the field is absent.
- Commands run:
  - `zig build test` — full suite passed
  - `node scripts/check-no-comments.mjs --check` and `./scripts/check-zig-patterns.sh` — clean

**End-to-end**, through `makai --stdio` against a stub server that records request headers:

| Model | Reached the endpoint | `Authorization` | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allows_anonymous: true` | yes | not sent | streamed a reply, `result` |
| flag absent | no | n/a | `auth_required` nack, no connection opened |

Exactly one request reached the stub across both runs, which is what confirms the second never opened one.

Worth recording for whoever tries this next: `makai -p` is not a harness for custom providers. It hardcodes a Kimi model and uses `--model` only for the model id, so it cannot exercise a declared endpoint at all.

## External Review Rounds

| Round | Reviewer | P0 | P1 | P2 | P3 | Resolution commit(s) | Status |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| - | pending | - | - | - | - | - | awaiting first review |

- [ ] At least 2 external rounds completed — pending

- [x] No unresolved blocking review findings

author: clubanderson
body:
Closes #7260

## The problem

Convergence ships a rollout procedure: soak in shadow, read the evidence from your own fleet, then promote to enforce. The default was `off` — and `off` returns before computing anything, so the soak ring stayed **empty forever** on every hive whose owner had not already opted in. The evidence the documented promotion path depends on could never accumulate. That default was not conservative, just inert.

## Why shadow is safe to default to

Shadow is **dispatch-identical to off**. `applyConvergenceKickAdmission` returns the raw actionable population in shadow, so no kick is withheld and no queue row changes. I verified the cost too: the path is `ConvergenceKickProjectionDetailed` → `newAdmissionSweep` → `buildBeadDependencyIndex`, which reads **local bead stores only** — no LLM call, no extra GitHub fetch — and the telemetry goes into a bounded ring.

## The subtlety the issue glosses over

The old contract was *any* unrecognised value **including empty** resolves to off. Moving the default meant splitting a case the code deliberately collapsed:

| configured mode | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| unset / blank | off | **shadow** (never chose → default) |
| `garbage`, `shadowy`, `true` | off | **off** (chose something unhonourable → fail-safe) |
| explicit `off` | off | off (no migration) |

Collapsing the two either strands hives on the inert default or lets a typo silently select a posture nobody asked for. `config.ResolveConvergenceMode` is now the single source of truth — the dashboard open-coded the old fallback and would otherwise have painted **`off` selected in the settings UI while shadow was actually running**. That inconsistency is now its own guard.

`off` stays fully selectable as the rollback and as the control arm for #4263's fixed-commit A/B comparison. It never required `off` to be the *default*.

## UI

The Features-tab tooltips described the mode choice without ever saying what convergence *does*; rewritten as problem → modes → workflow. The soak summary now answers the promotion question directly (`Safe to enforce` only on a **full** ring with zero would-differ passes — a handful of clean passes is not evidence) instead of leaving the operator to infer it from raw counts.

## Verification

- Guards assert **both halves together** — nothing withheld AND evidence recorded — so they fail if someone makes the default inert again *or* makes it enforce.
- **5/5 mutations killed**, each verified as actually applied (not build-error artifacts): default→off, default→enforce, collapse unparseable into default, explicit-off ignored, dashboard reports off while shadow runs.
- Tests that were about *off* behaviour now select off explicitly instead of relying on an unset value. One needed the env override left unset instead, since it drives the flip through config and an env value would have made the crossing unobservable.
- `pkg/dashboard`, `cmd/hive`, `pkg/convergence/...` all green. The single `pkg/config` failure (`TestEntrypointHardensRuntimeConfigItRecreates`) is pre-existing on clean `v4` — confirmed by stashing.
- inline-JS/no-undef gate and api-reference citation check both pass.

## Summary
- Fix Windows PowerShell treating successful Worktrunk stderr output as a terminating error before Herdr worktree registration.
- Capture native JSON-command stderr as unformatted diagnostic records, separate from stdout, and report operation, exit status, and diagnostics on failure while preserving interactive merge/remove output.
- Persist bounded, best-effort error logs, keep interactive failures visible until acknowledged, and notify for launcher/background failures.
- Return failure status from failed operations, preserve the primary error during cleanup, and document diagnostics and recovery.

## Verification
- Native Windows PowerShell 5.1: **166 assertions passed** at `a8ca336`; both push and pull-request workflow runs passed.
- [PR workflow](https://github.com/giard-alexandre/herdr-worktrunk-windows/actions/runs/35178133278)
- [Push workflow](https://github.com/giard-alexandre/herdr-worktrunk-windows/actions/runs/35178129345)
- PowerShell 7.1.7 on macOS: `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -File tests/Run-Tests.ps1` passed **70 assertions**.
- Registration fix reproduced with real Git and Worktrunk, using stubbed fzf selection and Herdr calls: before, checkout created but no Herdr registration; after, `herdr worktree open` reached. Existing-branch recovery also exercised.
- Regression coverage includes raw stderr with success/nonzero status, invalid/empty JSON, persisted/bounded logs, redaction, logging failure isolation, noninteractive acknowledgement, and Windows entrypoint/notification failures.
- Live Windows desktop UI behavior has not been manually verified.

## CI correction
The initial Windows notification regression failed because stderr redirected to a file acquired PowerShell error-record formatting. The runner now separates typed error records from stdout and captures their diagnostic messages directly. The notification regression remains intact; additional assertions require unformatted native stderr on both successful and failing commands.

## Commits
- `5b9b637` Fix Windows worktree registration after successful creation
- `5b9aa35` Add persistent plugin error reporting and visible failures
- `a8ca336` Capture native stderr without PowerShell error formatting

author: alstonhuang
body:
## Summary

Implements the AgentOS-wide **Discovery Cost Reuse Floor** as executable behavior, not only governance prose.

Closes #340.

## Core behavior

Before broad repository/environment discovery, continuation resolution now hydrates:
- current continuation IR;
- canonical project/source state;
- project reusable-fact state;
- execution head;
- project-associated authoritative Resource Registry facts.

Stored facts are evaluated against requested scope, depth, freshness, and evidence strength. Equivalent discovery is skipped when facts are sufficient.

When rediscovery is justified, the result carries machine-readable reasons:
- `missing`
- `stale`
- `deeper`
- `expanded_scope`
- `conflict`
- `stronger_evidence`

## Promotion / persistence

- Adds `agent_core/project_knowledge.py` for stable reusable facts under the project data layer (`projects/<id>/knowledge/reusable-facts.json`).
- Promotion does not grant source or mutation authority.
- Discovery receipts distinguish reused vs rediscovered facts.
- Credential/bearer fields and credential-bearing repository remotes are sanitized before persisted project knowledge and resolve output.

## Regression coverage

The real `leopardcat-tarot` continuity regression is now a concrete fixture:
- canonical repo/branch/path/node are reused without broad rediscovery;
- Resource Registry runtime facts such as service/port/git state hydrate before discovery;
- stale runtime facts allow targeted revalidation with reason=`stale`;
- credential-bearing remotes are projected only in credential-free form.

Additional tests cover deeper exploration, scope expansion, conflicts, stronger evidence, promotion, and receipt semantics.

## Governance

The branch also retains GOV-2026-09-17-001 and the AGENTS.md hydration-before-rediscovery rule. Capability still does not imply mutation authority.

## Problem
`/ledger` showed a Net of \$4,541 with no visible source: Net is summed **all-time** (the `settled` column was dropped in migration `1aa83cc20783` and nothing replaced its scoping), while the itemized list was scoped to **this month**. Past real-life settlements were never recorded, so the running balance drifted upward with no way to reset.

## Fix
- **`/paid`** — new command, posts one balancing ledger entry so the running balance → 0.
- **`_get_ledger_itemized`** — now scopes to activity since the last `/paid`, so the listed items always sum to Net (verified with a reconciliation sim).
- Relabel the Net field + ledger title; drop the now-unused `datetime` import.

No schema change, no migration.

## Reconciliation (post-deploy, manual)
Run `/pay 2295.88 "backfill: paid Steph ~20d ago"` to record the untracked payment, then `/ledger` to eyeball the remaining breakdown, then `/paid` when settled.

body:
## 更新内容

メタグリラボ「農業AI通信」（https://metagri-labo.com/ai-guide/ ）の記事をもとに、スキルを2段階で更新しました。既存の比喩・説明は削除・変更しておらず、すべて追記です。

1. **比喩対応表に13件追加**＋モード①②の記述を補強
2. **活用事例ナレッジベースを新設**（`references/katsuyou-jirei.md`、244行）

---

## 1. 追加した農業×AI比喩（13件）

| AI概念 | 農業比喩 |
|--------|---------|
| フィジカルAI | 生成AIが「農業の教科書」なら、フィジカルAIは「教科書を読んで実際に畑に出て作業するロボット」 |
| エッジAI | 電波の届かない圃場で「その場で自分の頭で考えて動く」こと。クラウドAIは「JAに電話して指示をもらう」に近い |
| LiDAR | カメラが「目」なら、LiDARは「レーザー光で形を確かめる触覚」。両方そろって雑草と作物の高低差が分かる |
| ハルシネーション | AIが流暢に語る「もっともらしい嘘」。話は上手いが現物を見ていない指導員の助言と同じで、圃場で裏を取る必要がある |
| Grokking（突然の理解） | 何年も同じ作業を繰り返した人が、ある日ふっと「作物の気持ち」が分かるようになる、あの瞬間 |
| ブラックボックス問題 | AIは「理由を言わない名人」。ベテラン農家が「なんとなく分かる」としか説明できないのと同じ |
| AIのメモリ（農園カルテ） | 新しい研修生に毎回ゼロから説明せずに済むよう、農園の基本情報をカルテにまとめて渡しておくこと |
| スケジューラー（自動巡回） | 夜間の自動灌水タイマーと同じ発想で、情報収集そのものを決まった時刻に自動で見回らせる |
| 自律制御（自律栽培） | 決まった時刻に水を出すタイマーではなく、土の湿り具合を見てから水をやる農家の判断そのものをAIが担う |
| 画像診断AI | 葉の写真を撮るだけで病気を見分ける。ベテランの「目利き」を技術で再現したもの |
| デジタルツイン | 「牧場物語」のように、自分の畑と同条件のデータ上で試し運営してから本番で動かす |
| VLA（Vision-Language-Action） | 「赤い実だけ取って」という普段どおりの指示が、そのまま機械に通じるようになる技術 |
| RaaS（ロボット月額制） | 農機を買わずに月額で借りる。初期費用ほぼゼロで最新のロボットを試せる仕組み |

### モード①への追記
- **比喩選びの原則**：迷ったら「その技術は、ベテラン農家の"勘"や"目利き"の何を再現しているのか」に立ち返る
- **AIの限界を扱うときの補足**：確認5ステップ（公式裏取り → 出典確認 → 圃場検証 → 複数AI比較 → 最終判断は自分）。「AIは間違える」で止めず、付き合い方まで書き切る方針を明記

### モード②への追記
- **連載シリーズ型**：入門回／用語集回／実力比較回／課題回／未来予想回。特に「なぜ農業現場での導入は難しいのか」という課題回を必ず入れる
- **インタビュー型**：「きっかけ → 試行錯誤 → 変化」を追う構成と、到達点をタイトルに入れる作法

---

## 2. 活用事例ナレッジベース（新規ファイル）

`skills/nougyou-ai-guide/references/katsuyou-jirei.md`

モード①で「実際の活用シーン」を書くとき、モード②で記事を組み立てるとき、モード③で「5分でできること」を出すときに参照する事例集です。想像で事例を書かないための裏付けになります。

### 収録内容

**① 農園AIエージェントを育てる**
単発チャットから自律的な農園アシスタントまでの6段階（定時通知 → 自分ごと化 → 記憶を持たせる → 経験を貯める → 自動巡回 → どこからでも指示）。ChatGPT Tasksの毎朝6時通知、`my-farm/`＋`CLAUDE.md`での前提共有、Coworkスケジューラー、Dispatch、Project Sol（Claudeによるトマト100日自律栽培、Sense→Think→Act→Logループ）。

**② フィジカルAI**
国産3メーカーの現在地（クボタの水素FC無人トラクタ、ヤンマーの隅刈り自動化、井関の直進アシスト1,410万円〜）、John Deere「See & Spray」（36台のAIカメラ、除草剤50%削減）、AGRIST（宮崎、誤切断99.96%抑制）。**農業へのAI導入が難しい5つの壁**（天候・不整地・通信制約・個体差・安全規制）も収録。

**③ 農家の実践ストーリー**
- 冨安寛樹さん／WFPダチョウファーム（北海道、約100ha）：プログラミング未経験から100日チャレンジ。ハウス温度監視を**初期投資約7,000円・月額0円**でDIY
- 川上牧場（酪農・乳牛約80頭）：確定申告の伝票整理が**丸1日 → 20〜30分**。作業動画からGeminiで多言語マニュアル生成
- 樫村ふぁーむ：無料版＋AIボイスレコーダーで議事録化。「信頼するが、信用しない」
- トヤマミカン（静岡・三ヶ日）

さらに、記事化に使える**共通の型**を5つ抽出しました（入口は無料／有料化は具体的な不満がきっかけ／最初の成果は事務作業に出る／AIを信用しきらない姿勢／目的は人に向かう）。

**④ 農家の"普段の仕事"で使う**
経理（勘定科目プロンプト、8割正解・要検証の原則）、事業計画（骨子→肉付け→チェックの3ステップ、提出前15分の照合）、投資判断（買う/リース/中古の総コスト比較）、販促（直売所POP 約5分、お礼状1件10秒）、病害虫診断（写真＋役割設定で約3分）。

---

body:
## Summary
- **`lx.createVideoContext` always failed on iOS** with `E_INTERNAL` for videos inside a native island. The native bridge installs before the page's WebView learns its lxapp, so the component manager captured the `"app"` placeholder. Every island commit then failed the media URL policy check (`LxApp is not registered: app`), no video node was built, and the video id never reached the component router. The island now reads the WebView's lxapp when it is created (iOS and macOS).
- **Component router unregisters only what a manager owns.** A torn-down page's deferred `teardownAll()` could drop the registration a reloaded page had just made for the same id. Found while reading the teardown path, not reproduced on its own.
- **`NATIVE-ISLAND-001` on phones**: the video page fits one phone screen, so `window.scrollTo` did nothing and the island had no geometry change to follow. The spec pads the page for the check and removes the padding afterwards.

`NATIVE-VIDEO-001` claims `lx.createVideoContext`, but the video page swallows its exception, which is how the iOS failure stayed hidden.

## Test plan
- [x] iPhone 11: `lx.createVideoContext` returns a context on the island fixture (was `E_INTERNAL` on every call)
- [x] iPhone 11: full `ios.test.ts` 99 passed / 0 failed (was 97 / 2: `SHAPE-RUNTIME`, `NATIVE-ISLAND-001`)
- [x] macOS: `SHAPE-RUNTIME`, `NATIVE-ISLAND-001`, `NATIVE-VIDEO-001` pass
- [x] HarmonyOS device: `NATIVE-ISLAND-001` passes (was failing on the scroll check)
- [x] Android device: `NATIVE-ISLAND-001` fails with the main spec and passes twice with this spec

Note: in one full iOS run before the last, `DESKTOP-PREVIEW-HTTPS-VIDEO-001` failed three times in a row and then passed on fresh builds and in the final full run; it does not touch the changed code.

author: hugoqui
body:
## Qué trae

Fase 4 de `specs/002-identidad-de-iglesia/tasks.md` (T4.1–T4.11), que implementa [ADR 0016](docs/adr/0016-sesion-firmada-verificable-sin-internet.md).

Biblioteca nueva `libs/sesiones`, compartida por el nodo y la nube:

- **Contraseñas con Argon2id**, sal por usuario y parámetros guardados junto al hash en formato PHC (`$argon2id$v=19$m=…,t=…,p=…$sal$hash`). Eso es lo que permite subirlos mañana sin invalidar las contraseñas de hoy.
- **Sesiones firmadas con Ed25519**, con dos emisores: cada lado firma con su clave y verifica al otro con su mitad pública. El nodo emite y verifica **sin red**.
- **Dos duraciones**: acceso de una hora, renovación de 30 días atada a un dispositivo. De la renovación se guarda solo la huella, nunca el token.
- Las claves se leen del entorno y **ninguna privada entra al repositorio**. Se generan con `dotnet run -- generar-claves`, que las imprime y no escribe ningún archivo.

Se añadió el [ADR 0018](docs/adr/0018-criptografia-con-bouncycastle.md), porque .NET 10 no trae ninguna de las dos primitivas —comprobado en el SDK del proyecto, no supuesto— y había que elegir biblioteca. BouncyCastle: una sola dependencia, código administrado, sin binarios nativos que puedan no cargar en la PC de un templo.

## Verificación

`dotnet test` en verde: 87 pruebas, 23 de ellas de la biblioteca nueva.

Las pruebas están escritas para intentar colarse: firma alterada, cuerpo reescrito conservando la firma original, token caducado, token de otra iglesia, token de renovación usado como acceso, y tokens mal formados.

El comando `generar-claves` se probó de verdad contra el proceso de la nube.

## Tres decisiones que conviene revisar

- **El token no negocia algoritmo**: no dice con qué se firmó y el verificador no se lo pregunta, siempre es Ed25519. Es lo que evita el ataque clásico de pedir "algoritmo: ninguno" y que el servidor obedezca.
- **El identificador de clave se deriva de la clave pública** en lugar de ser otra variable de entorno: una cosa menos que se pueda configurar mal, y dos claves distintas nunca comparten identificador.
- **T4.2 queda a medias a propósito.** El criterio de calibración está escrito —que verificar una contraseña tarde entre 0,25 y 1 s en la PC más débil de las iglesias, que es la que además proyecta—, pero **la medición en esa PC real está pendiente**. Los parámetros por defecto (64 MiB, 3 pasadas) son el punto de partida del RFC 9106 para equipos con poca memoria.

author: dongss
body:
Closes #20.

Every frontend took a reasoning-effort parameter and none of them did anything with it. Two of the four backends have a knob.

| frontend | parameter | before |
|---|---|---|
| `/v1/chat/completions` | `reasoning_effort` | not decoded |
| `/v1/responses` | `reasoning.effort` | decoded, dropped |
| `/v1/messages` | `thinking` | decoded, dropped |

Same failure as #10 — a caller sets a constraint and gets a 200 with no sign it was ignored — and the comment justifying it (*"no CLI takes a knob for it"*) had gone the way of the schema comment before #11.

## Levels, not a boolean

`adapter.EffortSetter` follows #11's pattern with one difference: it reports **which levels** the backend takes rather than yes/no. The scales genuinely do not line up — Claude Code runs `low`…`max` and has no `minimal`; OpenAI's vocabulary has no `max`. Reporting the list lets the refusal name both sides:

```
minimal on claude-code  400 does not take reasoning effort "minimal"; it takes low, medium, high, xhigh, max
high on cursor          400 the cursor backend has no reasoning-effort setting; ask for a model whose CLI does
turbo on claude-code    400 unknown reasoning effort "turbo"; it must be one of minimal, low, medium, high, xhigh, max
```

The last one is refused **before any backend is consulted** — it is the caller's typo, not a capability question. `gate.Wrap` forwards the interface explicitly, as #14 learned it must.

## The Anthropic decision

That dialect measures thinking in tokens; the backends measure it in levels. Any threshold turning `budget_tokens` into a level would be invented here and defended nowhere, so a budget is refused and only `thinking.type` is carried. Nothing is fabricated on the way back either — a backend with no knob gets no effort echoed into its response.

## Verifying before building changed what gets claimed, twice

**`--effort` works, but what it does is the model's business.** On 2.1.274, `sonnet` spent no thinking tokens at `low` and ~130 at `max`. `haiku` showed no separation across three runs at each end (612–1073 vs 657–1310), and nothing in the CLI's output echoes the flag back, so there is no confirmation to assert on. The flag is passed on regardless — the same contract as `temperature` — and the measurement lives in the adapter comment rather than in a test that would be measuring the weather.

**codex validates nothing and delegates the meaning upstream.** It accepts any value (`nonsense` included) and turns the level into a `thinking_budget` for whatever endpoint sits behind it. Against the provider reachable here, `low` worked and `high` came back:

```
400 InternalError.Algo.InvalidParameter: The thinking_budget parameter
must be a positive integer and not greater than …
```

That surfaces as an honest upstream error rather than a silent downgrade, which is the behaviour to keep — but it means a level this adapter accepts can still be refused further up. Recorded where someone debugging it will look.

## Testing

9 new unit tests across the three frontends and the gate; 5 new conformance cases, suite now **52 passed, 0 failed**. Verified end to end against the real CLIs: the flag reaches argv (`--effort max` confirmed in the debug log), and all four refusal paths produce the messages above.

## Also in here

Re-verifies the fixtures against Claude Code `2.1.274`, cursor-agent `2026.09.15` and Qwen Code `0.24.0` (codex unmoved at `0.154.0`). No fixture needed re-recording. Claude Code's `result` line gained `result_index`, which the parser does not read; Qwen Code still reports `tools: []` under the generated settings, which is the check that adapter rests on.

The README gained three words, not a section: the refusal joins the existing `What is not supported` list. Which backend has which capability is deliberately not documented there — it goes stale, and `doctor` is where it belongs. It does not report capabilities yet, which is now worth fixing for schemas and effort together.

author: kunlunl
body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Add the opt-in `--moe-fused-router-chain` path, combining sigmoid group-limited top-k routing, normalization/scaling, sequence auxiliary loss, and their logits gradients in one autograd Function backed by Triton kernels.

The eager routing and auxiliary-loss branches otherwise meet through autograd accumulation. Owning both branches lets the fused backward accumulate their contributions inside one kernel. This draft is based directly on `dev` and is independent of #7416.

## Implementation

- Add `FusedSigmoidRouterChain`, a Torch mathematical reference, and CPU/CUDA tests.
- Compute sigmoid, expert bias, group/expert selection, normalized probabilities, and a routing map in the fused routing kernel. Compute auxiliary statistics and loss in separate kernels, preserving the required count reductions.
- Compute the joint logits gradient from routing-probability and auxiliary-loss gradients in one backward kernel.
- Use libdevice exponential and IEEE division; reduction order can still differ from eager Torch.
- Return a Boolean routing map through the integrated router path. Preserve auxiliary-loss attachment/logging and expert-bias count updates.
- Default the flag to false and fall back to the existing path outside the supported CUDA/Triton, sigmoid, sequence-auxiliary-loss, microbatch-one configuration. Padding, packed sequences, capacity limits, hash/replay/quantile routing, and z-loss are excluded from the fused path.

## Validation and performance

A same-node, same-source A/B at `e83b057` used BF16 DeepSeek-V3-style training on 8 H100 80GB GPUs, TP2/PP2/DP2/EP2, selective recompute (`moe,mlp,mla_up_proj,layernorm`), and attention CUDA Graphs. Each process ran 25 iterations, with the final 23 summarized using the slowest rank per iteration.

| Metric | Flag off | Flag on |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mean iteration time | 17.709 s | 16.166 s (-8.7%) |
| Median iteration time | 17.087 s | 15.820 s (-7.4%) |

Peak allocated memory was effectively unchanged; peak reserved memory decreased by 10 MiB. This is one same-node pair with substantial run-to-run variance, not a complete performance acceptance result.

The added CPU checks compare the closed-form gradient against eager autograd; existing local results report maximum absolute differences around 7e-11 and 2e-11 for the tested shapes. Isolated GPU comparisons reported routing-probability relative-L2 error about 5.3e-8, equal selected expert sets, and equal auxiliary loss on the tested inputs.

**This path is not bitwise equivalent to eager routing.** The first measured training loss differed by approximately 1.2e-4 absolute (1e-5 relative), and later training trajectories diverged. Changing the dispatcher-facing map and using IEEE division did not eliminate that difference. The observations are consistent with remaining reduction-order differences, but a complete same-input layer/gradient analysis has not been performed.

## Draft limitations

- Supported shapes/settings are deliberately narrow; edge cases, ties in top-k selection, and broader distributed auxiliary-loss configurations need additional coverage.
- Full training correctness and convergence validation, complete Megatron tests, repository formatting, DCO sign-off, and commit signing remain pending.
- The reported local mathematical and GPU comparisons do not establish whole-model gradient equivalence.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: none.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [x] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the autoformatter on my PR

author: adamsilverstein
body:
Task 6 of the Battlezone recreation: the enemies, their explosions and the scoring. This is the part where the game starts playing back, so faithfulness to the ROM's AI mattered more than tidiness, and the reference documents got read closely enough to catch two places where they contradict each other.

Stacked on top of #5 (`feat/world`), which has not merged yet, so this branch currently carries its commits too. The enemy work is the top six commits.

## What is in it

**The tank** (`src/game/enemies/tank.ts`) is `ROBOT` plus `FIREIT`: a goal heading and a decision timer rather than per-tick tracking, which is what produces the original's jerky drive-rotate-drive gait. It tries a shot after every single turn step, so it can fire mid-pivot, and the difficulty ladder (score minus the enemy's own kills) sets the decision interval, the aiming tolerance and the mood - approach, circle, wander - with the beginner handicap that only shoots a new player from in front and from close range.

**The supertank** (`supertank.ts`) is the same machine with the ROM's faster numbers, plus the one behaviour in this task that the original does not have: design spec 5.2 asks it to dodge, so it breaks off across the player's line of fire once per player shell. Flagged as a deviation in the file and in the constant.

**The missile** (`missile.ts`) follows `BUZBOM` in order: levitate over an obstacle, keep out of the cone behind the player, weave, fly at four times the player's step, ram. The two reference docs disagree about which side of the swoop threshold the weaving happens on; the code follows the self-consistent reading (straight in when close, weaving when far), which is what makes the first missile of a game fly straight and late ones swerve until the last moment.

**The saucer** (`saucer.ts`) owns its whole life in one system because it sits outside the one-unit rule: the random wait, the spin and drift, the 32-tick disintegration, and the visit timeout the spec asks for (the ROM's saucer never leaves).

**The spawner** (`spawn.ts`) keeps exactly one unit on the field, on the ROM's ladder - tanks, then a coin flip with missiles, supertanks by missile count rather than score - and places the replacement on the tick the previous unit's highest chunk lands, so there is no gap between enemies.

**Explosions and scoring** (`explosions.ts`, `score.ts`): six chunks on the ROM's fixed spray pattern, yawing only, the turret piece thrown highest; 1000/2000/3000/5000 points, a bonus tank at 15,000 and the 1812 Overture at 100,000.

Hit resolution (`enemies/index.ts`) follows `CheckProjColl`: the unit, then the saucer, then nothing - so shells cannot shoot each other down - and it tests the shell at each of its four sub-step positions, because a whole tick of flight is wider than any hit radius.

## Deviations from the ROM, all documented in the files

- The supertank's dodge, the saucer's visit timeout and hover height, and the smaller missile/saucer debris are spec requirements the ROM has no equivalent for; their constants are marked ESTIMATE.
- A missile that has climbed to `TOP` stops testing for obstacles, so it passes over the box it hopped instead of hovering beside it forever.
- `resolveShellHits` takes the `Rng` as a second argument, because a hit scatters debris and nothing in `src/game` may reach for `Math.random`.

## Testing

`npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test` and `npm run build` all pass on every commit. 411 tests, 33 files.

New test files: `tank`, `supertank`, `missile`, `saucer`, `spawn`, `explosions`, `score`, `enemies` (integration), plus additions to `collision`. Everything is seeded through `createRng`, so the AI is reproducible.

Worth a look from a reviewer:

- the tank turns toward the player and fires when it lines up, holds its fire for the first two seconds, and only shoots a beginner from in front and up close

body:
PR 1 de 5 (feature-branch-chain) de la feature **modo-cuidador** — rol de cuidador con cuenta propia y acceso de solo lectura a la adherencia del usuario mayor.

## Qué incluye este PR

- Migración `008_cuidadores.sql`:
  - `vinculos_cuidador` — invitación elder→cuidador con token de un solo uso; el claim solo ocurre dentro de la RPC `security definer`, nunca vía policy directa.
  - `alertas_dosis` — log/dedupe de alertas de dosis vencida (fase posterior de esta misma cadena de PRs).
  - RLS **aditiva** de solo lectura (`medicamentos_select_cuidador`, `medicamentos_tomas_select_cuidador`) — coexiste con las policies `_all_self` existentes, no las reemplaza.
  - Sin policy de `select` en `perfiles` — RLS es de fila, no de columna; el nombre del elder se expone solo vía `listar_elders_vinculados()`.
  - `reclamar_invitacion_cuidador()`: nunca recibe `cuidador_id` como parámetro, valida token+expiración+email antes de aceptar.
- `docs/data-model.md` actualizado.

## Encontrado en revisión manual (ya corregido en este PR)

La policy `vinculos_all_elder` (`for all`) dejaba que el propio elder actualizara `estado` a `'aceptado'` directo, saltándose el consentimiento del cuidador que la RPC está pensada para garantizar. Se agregó `with check (... and estado <> 'aceptado')` — esa transición ahora solo es posible dentro de la RPC.

## Verificación

Aplicado a la DB real (`supabase db push --linked`) y verificado con `psql` directo: RLS habilitada en ambas tablas nuevas, las policies `_all_self` existentes sin tocar, ambas RPCs con `security definer` confirmado.

Sin código de app en este PR (Fase 1 de 5 — schema/RLS/RPCs solamente). PRs siguientes de la cadena: invitación+claim (app), dashboard del cuidador, modo simple, alertas+cron.

author: alexjba
body:
Part of logos-fleet/logos-workspace#235.

A private send was 239 s on a physical iPad Air 4, of which 221 s was one opaque `provider.sync()`. This makes that leg fast, observable and interruptible.

- **`rust-lib/src/sync.rs` (new)** tunes `RpcSyncer` through its own public `with_batch_size` / `with_batch_delay` (1 000 blocks, no sleep) instead of the engine defaults (10 blocks, 1 000 ms) — 100 ms saved per tail block, unbounded. Measured twice against public Sepolia over a ~215-block tail: 32 006 ms → 8 333 ms. Proved RED as a unit test: the same 2 200-block range is 3 `eth_getLogs` calls here and 220 (plus 220 s of sleep) under the defaults.
- **`sync_step` / `sync_status` / `sync_cancel`** turn the sync into bounded windows (≤25 000 blocks, ≤20 000 ms), so no call takes minutes and the caller gets a real percentage and ETA. `UtxoIndexer::sync_to` persists `synced_block` before each window returns, so **cancel is simply stopping the calls** — nothing to roll back; a later step or a later launch resumes. Asserted with a test that stops three windows in, throws the engine away, and finishes over the same database with a second one.
- **The subsquid half is one window.** `sync::subsquid_frontier` reads `SubsquidSyncer::latest_block` — exactly where `ChainedSyncer` hands over — and `Plan::with_fast_forward` takes everything up to it in one go, stepping only the tail. A cold sync on device went from 469 windows / 195 s to one big window plus a handful of small ones.
- **Device evidence in `docs/specs.md`**: the second sync on the same device is 110 blocks, one window, 506 ms. Also corrects #222's conclusion ("a private send on iOS needs neither a background job nor a cancel path"), which was true of the parts it measured and false of the operation they belong to.
- **`plan_reply()`** assembles the progress reply in one place instead of six (no behaviour change).

Verified in the implementer and reviewer sandboxes; no builds were run in the landing phase.

Adds SQLiteLimitCoordinator as the durable local backend for context-owned admission. Independent coordinators and local processes share atomic grants, persisted request history, policy revisions, expiring wait tickets, and fenced leases. Short transactions run in a bounded I/O executor; queued coroutines hold no database connection or thread while waiting.

Contexts renew active leases and stop local execution on lease loss. Cancellation racing with a committed grant releases the resulting lease. A persisted clock floor prevents rollback from refunding rate quota. Backend failures and mixed policies fail closed. Documentation specifies recovery, storage schema, cross-process refresh, remote-work fencing limits, and the initial single-state-row scaling tradeoff.

Dependent on #272; base branch: work/183-context-limits. Rebased onto its reviewed core fixes in e07e858. No distributed-filesystem or exactly-once remote-execution claim is made. Live policy migration and a high-volume normalized store remain future backend work.

Validation with the rebased region-capacity stack: 1,531 passed, 1 existing expected failure; Ruff lint/format, Pyright, typecast diagram, and diff checks passed. Nine backend tests cover independent coordinator instances, reopen persistence, clock rollback, killed-owner recovery with increasing fencing generation, cancellation/grant races, backend/policy failure, heartbeat renewal, lease loss, and wait-hook cleanup.

Related to #183.
