body:
- [ ] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

Add the opt-in `--moe-cached-recompute-dispatch` flag. Keep a checkpointed forward's DeepEP routing handle, received routing data, and host expert counts, then use DeepEP's cached dispatch for its backward replay instead of rebuilding the dispatch layout and receiving counts again.

This is an experimental draft with **no demonstrated E2E speedup in the tested Megatron configuration**. It is based directly on `dev` and is independent of #7416. The branch name contains `hoist`, but this Megatron patch implements cached replay dispatch, not cross-layer dispatch hoisting.

## Implementation

- Give each `CheckpointFunction` call a token that pairs its forward and backward replay.
- Keep per-checkpoint/per-manager dispatch metadata in a process-wide, locked stash. The stash is shared across the model and autograd worker threads; scope tracking remains thread-local.
- Add `CachedFusedDispatch`: its forward redispatches the recomputed activations using the saved handle, and its backward retains the routing-probability gradient path through the corresponding combine.
- Consume cached metadata once and fall back to normal dispatch, with a diagnostic, when an entry is unavailable. Track retained metadata bytes.
- Require full recompute or selective recompute including `moe`, the flex dispatcher with DeepEP, and no FP8/FP4. The flag defaults to false.

## Validation and performance

A same-node, same-source comparison at `2fea7db` used BF16 DeepSeek-V3-style training on 8 H100 80GB GPUs, TP2/PP2/DP2/EP2, selective recompute, and attention CUDA Graphs. Each process ran 25 iterations, with the final 23 summarized using the slowest rank per iteration.

| Metric | Flag off | Flag on |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Mean iteration time | 18.294 s | 18.510 s (+1.2%) |
| Median iteration time | 17.974 s | 18.314 s (+1.9%) |

Peak allocated memory was effectively unchanged; peak reserved memory increased by 410 MiB. An additional same-node flag-off run at the preceding implementation revision averaged 18.062 s. These observations show no measured benefit; the run-to-run variation limits precise regression attribution.

Nsight confirms that the backward replay no longer launches its dispatch-layout and normal notify kernels: the rank-0 counts fall from 960 each to zero, while cached dispatch remains. That profile comparison uses a different-node flag-off capture, so it establishes the mechanism more directly than the size of a timing change. Backward GPU-idle time remained around 3.85 s, consistent with a host-submission bottleneck in this workload.

The final enabled run reported no fallback warnings; the first cached entry retained approximately 1.62 MB. Initial reported loss and gradient norm matched the disabled runs, with later production drift. No full-model bitwise or independent gradient validation has been completed.

## Draft limitations

- This is a mechanism experiment, not a performance improvement demonstrated on the measured configuration.
- Replay must reproduce the routing corresponding to the saved handle. Broader checkpoint combinations, stash cleanup when backward is abandoned, and cache lifetime require further validation.
- No dedicated automated tests are added yet. Distributed correctness tests, repeat performance measurements, repository formatting, DCO sign-off, and commit signing remain pending.

## Issue tracking

Linked issue: none.

## Contribution process

### Pre-checks

- [ ] I have added relevant unit tests
- [ ] I have added relevant functional tests
- [ ] I have added proper typing to my code
- [ ] I have added relevant documentation
- [ ] I have run the autoformatter on my PR

A node waiting for a narrower region previously retained its parallel scheduler slot, which could prevent unrelated work from running. Region admission now returns only that scheduler capacity and reacquires it atomically with the region quota. Whole-node provider ownership and rate history remain intact.

On region exit, scheduler capacity transfers back to the parent lease in one coordinator transaction, including nested regions. Ordinary admission errors restore the slot before returning to catchable node code; cancellation interrupts that restoration and safely releases ownership. Transfers and releases preserve the independently reviewed repeated-cancellation cleanup guarantees. The SQLite transaction waiter also uses the shared cleanup helper when cancellation repeats.

## 요약

#1389 중 색 대비를 뺀 **ARIA 위반**을 정리하고, 스토리북 접근성 검사를 경고(todo)에서 **color-contrast만 제외한 error**로 올립니다.

**원인**: react-native-web 0.21.2 `createDOMProps`는 개별 `aria-*` props는 DOM으로 옮기지만 `accessibilityState`·`accessibilityValue` **객체는 옮기지 않습니다**. 네이티브에선 멀쩡한 체크 상태·진행 값이 웹에서 사라졌습니다.

| 규칙 | 전 | 후 | 수정 |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| aria-prohibited-attr | 39 | 0 | 토큰 스토리 스와치에 role image |
| aria-required-attr | 5 | 0 | 곰 체크·토글 `aria-checked`, 휠 피커 `aria-value*` |
| aria-progressbar-name | 5 | 0 | 진행 바 이름(기본 '진행률')·`aria-value*`, 로딩 '불러오는 중' |
| aria-allowed-attr | 3 | 0 | 확인 다이얼로그 스토리가 `role=dialog`가 붙을 때까지 대기 |
| aria-dialog-name | 1 | 0 | 확인 다이얼로그(제목)·바텀시트(기본 '시트') Modal 이름 |
| nested-interactive | 1 | 예외 1 | 휠 피커(웹 한정, 아래) |

스토리 테스트: 실패 20 → 0 (82/82). 포트폴리오 사례 추가.

Part of #1389

## 리뷰 포인트

- **네이티브 접근성**: `aria-checked`·`aria-value*`·`aria-label`은 RN 0.83이 accessibilityState/Value/Label로 합쳐 VoiceOver·TalkBack 동작은 같습니다. 휠 피커는 `aria-valuetext`가 있어 종전처럼 라벨을 읽습니다. 바텀시트에 선택 prop `accessibilityLabel` 추가(호출부는 후속으로 구체 이름 지정 가능).
- **확인 다이얼로그 aria-allowed-attr**: RN Web Modal은 페이드 후 `onShow`에서야 `role=dialog`를 붙입니다(그 전엔 `aria-modal`만). 규칙 예외 대신 스토리가 열린 상태를 기다리게 했습니다.
- **예외 1건**: 휠 피커 nested-interactive — 네이티브는 부모 adjustable이 줄들을 하나로 합치지만 RN Web은 줄 버튼을 따로 포커스 가능하게 냅니다. 줄을 비활성화하면 마우스·터치 선택이 사라져 스토리 단위 예외(사유 주석).
- 스토리에서 a11y rules를 덮어쓸 땐 전역 color-contrast 제외도 같이 적어야 합니다(배열이 병합되지 않음, preview 주석).

## Scope

Follow-up audit of PRs updated on **2026-09-16 in America/New_York**. Initial inventory: #14–#23; #24/#25 appeared during the audit. The inventory, changed-file lists, review discussions and CI were checked, with deeper inspection of task/dependency lifecycle and execution/deployment boundaries. This is not an exhaustive line-by-line certification of all twelve PRs.

This PR repairs four confirmed follow-up findings in merged #21, including the analogous single-task interruption path. Other PRs are not claimed defect-free.

## Fixes

1. **Interrupted agents cannot be left falsely running after rejected completion.** Persist confirmed interruption recovery in a graph-locked transaction; cancel the exact operation/topic and pause only the matching current-topic + reservation snapshot. Recover partial family interruptions and single-task writes too. Never clear a successor run or silently swallow recovery failure.
2. **Private dependents remain automatically dispatchable.** Authenticate the visible completed source, discover same-workspace dependents internally, check readiness and run under each dependent creator, exclude trashed candidates, and redact private identifiers/errors from the completing member's response.
3. **Legacy dependency ownership survives account deletion.** Idempotent data migration `0169_task_dependency_ownership` reassigns old member-authored dependency rows to the dependent creator, so the writer's user FK cascade cannot erase someone else's blocker.
4. **Concurrent task-detail polling requests are deduplicated.** Use the polling wrapper with a 1-second dedupe window while preserving 10-second active/linked and 15-second idle cadence. A real-SWR regression mounts staggered page/drawer consumers on one cache.

author: philphauler
body:
Hey 👋

Fixes #632. In C++20, stateless lambdas are default-constructible ([P0624R2](https://www.open-std.org/jtc1/sc22/wg21/docs/papers/2017/p0624r2.pdf)), which makes a lambda with the correct call signature satisfy all `is_udbfe` requirements. The existing test expects the lambda NOT to be a valid UDBFE, but that was only true in C++17.

The fix guards the assertion with a `__cplusplus` version check:
- **C++20+:** `is_udbfe<decltype(fun)>` is `true` (lambda is default-constructible, so it IS a valid UDBFE)
- **C++17:** `is_udbfe<decltype(fun)>` is `false` (unchanged behavior)

Also adds a C++20 test that constructs a `bfe` from the bare lambda and exercises it, confirming the type trait result is correct for the standard in use.

This unblocks GCC 16, which defaults to C++20.

The MSVC check (`_MSVC_LANG`) is included because MSVC does not always set `__cplusplus` correctly without `/Zc:__cplusplus`.

Tested conceptually against the C++20 spec; no local Boost installation to compile-verify. CI should confirm 🙏

All the best ⚡

author: murdore
body:
The native generate path answers a `schema` request by appending a synthetic `final_result` tool and unwrapping its arguments back into text. That makes the vendor report `stop_reason: "tool_use"` on a turn where no tool call is surfaced, so the path substitutes a `"stop"` finish to stop the turn misreading as step-capped.

**The substitution applied to every stop reason, not just the one it was written for.** A turn can also end at `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` — the model was still writing the `final_result` arguments when the output ceiling hit, so the structured payload is cut mid-object. Reporting that as `"stop"` told the caller the response was complete: `neurolink.ts`'s `finishReason === "length"` check never fired, `jsonTruncated` stayed unset, and the truncation warning was never logged.

## Why this was silent from both directions

Whatever fragment arrived is *itself valid JSON*, so `coerceJsonToSchema` parses it and never sets its own `truncated` flag. The finish reason was the only remaining signal that the object was a fragment — and it had been overwritten. A caller following the documented contract (check `jsonTruncated` before trusting `structuredData`, per CLAUDE.md rule 3) was handed a half-written object as a whole one.

## Fix

Narrow the substitution to the reason it exists for: swap in `"stop"` only when the mapped reason would be `"tool-calls"`, and otherwise report what the vendor said.

This is the rule the **streaming path already applies** — it overrides only `finishReason === "tool-calls"` — so the two paths now agree instead of diverging. That divergence is what made this reachable on generate and not on stream.

## Coverage

`test:anthropic-silent-truncation` serves the exact non-streaming Messages API wire shape over `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL`, so the real provider, the real SDK and the real unwrapping code all run and only the vendor is substituted. No credentials, no network egress, deterministic in CI — the same local-stand-in pattern as `test:anthropic-streaming-retry` and `test:native-vendor-recovery`.

The determinism exception applies (CLAUDE.md rule 15): no reachable live endpoint produces "a `final_result` call cut off at the output ceiling" on demand, since it needs model, prompt and cap to land just so.

**Red on the unfixed build was `Passed: 1 / Failed: 2`.** The completed-turn control passing in that same red run is what shows the fixture and routing are sound and the two failures are the defect, not a broken harness. **Green is 3/3.**

Gates: `check` 0 errors · `lint` 0 errors · `build` exit 0 · `providers-mocked` 95 passed / 0 failed · `provider-structure` 3/3 · `anthropic-streaming-retry` pass.

* **Bug Fixes**
  * Corrected completion status reporting for Anthropic structured outputs that are cut off by the token limit.
  * Truncated JSON responses now report a length-based finish reason and are flagged as truncated, while preserving any recoverable content.
  * Completed tool-use responses continue to report a normal stop status.

* **Tests**
  * Added coverage for Anthropic structured-output truncation and completed responses.

* **Chores**

body:
Collect student-selected teacher log-probabilities in row tensors before assigning them to the evidence batch. The previous path made a PyTorch scalar write for each candidate at every selected response position. A live Open-MOPD step spent time on this CPU path after the teacher engines drained while the GPUs were idle.

A local 64×1,024×16 scoring benchmark fell from a median 1.278 seconds to 0.053 seconds. Candidate order, sparse masks, padding, and missing-token errors retain their existing contracts. The full-step effect is unmeasured: generation took 3,733 of step 3's 5,757 seconds in the current native run, which remains on its pinned revision.

author: hgopalan
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #2041. The multi-level `FieldPlaneAveraging` (from #1792) interpolates a coarse cell to the center of each fine bin using its closest neighbor. Next to a non-periodic domain boundary that neighbor is the ghost cell, which the code treats as a value located at the domain face. This PR verifies what those ghost cells actually hold during an ABL run and makes the averages independent of them.

## What the ghost cells hold

Checked with a temporary print in `ABLStats::calc_averages` on `abl_godunov_static_refinement` with the level-1 box covering half of the wall (`amr.n_error_buf = 0`), reading the level-0 velocity next to the wall in the coarse part of the domain:

| when | `u(k=-1)` | `u(k=0)` | `u(k=1)` |
|---|---|---|---|
| step 0 (physics `post_init_actions`, before the first fillpatch) | 0 | 6.67 | 6.95 |
| steps 1-3 (after the nodal projection's `fillpatch`) | 6.2 | 6.6 | 6.9 |

So in the time loop the wall-model gradient written by `apply_bc_funcs` does not reach the averages: the `fillpatch` at the end of the nodal projection replaces it with the `hoextrap` value of the `wall_model` BC, which is an extrapolation to the ghost-cell center, not a value at the face. At initialization the ghost is still the unfilled initial value (zero here), and the first-cell bins of the fine average read it: at step 0 the fine average at half a fine cell was 5.1 against 6.1 one step later. With the default `ABL.log_law_height` (level-0 half cell) the errors of the two bins cancel exactly in the interpolated mean, so the initial friction velocity is unaffected; with another log-law height or `ABL.stats_max_level = 1` it is not. Which value the ghost holds and where it sits therefore depends on the boundary condition (`ext_dir`: face value; `hoextrap`/`foextrap`: ghost center; wall models: a gradient until the next fill) and on the point in the step at which the average is taken.

## Change

Across a non-periodic domain boundary the interpolation now uses the interior neighbor instead of the ghost cell (one-sided linear interpolation). In the periodic direction and inside the domain nothing changes. Cells whose center coincides with the bin center still get zero interpolation weight, but only to roundoff: in the first and last cells next to a non-periodic boundary, the roundoff difference between the bin center and the cell center used to multiply the ghost value and now multiplies the interior neighbor. Single-level cases can therefore change at roundoff too (see *Regression tests* below; `abl_godunov` happens to be bit-identical). Multi-level cases with a coarse level at a non-periodic boundary change only in the first and last bins; `abl_godunov_static_refinement` with the level-1 box over half of the wall agrees with `main` to roundoff after 10 steps (1e-15 relative), because with the default log-law height the two wall bins cancel in the wall function and `ABLForcing` samples the profile well inside the domain.

## Regression tests

The CPU Release jobs compare against `main` with no tolerance, so they report these answer changes. On the macOS job the following tests differ from `main`, all at roundoff:

| test | levels | max. absolute difference (velocity, temperature, p) |
|---|---|---|
| `abl_godunov_mpl` | 1 | 2.3e-12 (relative 9e-14) |
| `abl_godunov_mpl_amr` | 2 | 2.2e-12 |
| `abl_sampling` | 2 | 7.7e-12 |
| `abl_subvolume` | 2 | 2.4e-13 |
| `box_refinement` | 2 | 4.5e-13 |
| `udf_refinement` | 2 | 2.8e-13 |

The relative differences are at most 1e-12, except for fields close to zero (e.g. the level-1 vertical velocity, 1e-9 relative). Running `abl_godunov_mpl` locally with and without this change gives the same size of difference.

## Test

`FieldPlaneAveragingFineTest.test_linear_ignores_domain_ghosts`: the linear-field test of #1792 with the ghost cells outside the domain set to 1e10. It fails on the current code and passes with this change. The existing tests, which fill the ghosts with the face value, still pass because the one-sided interpolation is exact for a linear field.

## Summary

`deno task test` fails type-checking on `main`. The webhooks feature added fields to `ExtensionPushSuccessData`, `ExtensionPushPrepareInput`, `ExtensionContentMetadata` and `PackageCacheHashInput` without updating the fixtures that construct them — 6 errors across two test files:

```
TS2741: Property 'webhookCount' is missing …        ExtensionPushSuccessData
TS2739: … missing webhooksDir, allWebhookFiles, webhookEntryPoints
TS2322: Property 'webhooks' is missing …            ExtensionContentMetadata
TS2345: Property 'webhookFilePaths' is missing …    PackageCacheHashInput
```

Fixture-only change: every added field takes its empty value, matching the sibling collections beside it.

## Why this reached main

`deno check main.ts` passes, because test files are not in `main.ts`'s dependency graph. The errors surface only in the test step — so the type-check gate and the test gate disagree about what is checked, and the change landed green.

Worth considering separately: whether the type-check step should cover test files too, which would catch this class of breakage at the cheaper gate.

## Test Plan

- `deno check` clean on both touched files
- `deno task test` — **12019 passed, 0 failed, 30 ignored**
- Full verification: build 9/9, reviews pass, skills skipped by guard

author: tgradea
body:
Turns the five-series FRED archive into a backtesting toolkit and a
self-contained dashboard, with the statistics needed to tell a real edge
from a lucky search.

## What is here

**Point-in-time discipline.** Two panels, not one: `raw` is observation-dated
and drives returns; `pit` applies publication lags and is the only thing
signals may read. NFCI is week-ending-Friday released the following
Wednesday, so it carries a 4-business-day lag.

**Par-bond repricing.** Duration and convexity are recomputed from each day's
own yield via a symmetric 1bp bump rather than held fixed, which matters over
a sample that starts at double-digit yields.

**Financed steepener.** A duration-neutral 10s2s has to be financed at the
front end. Without that leg the strategy quietly earned most of the yield
level for no duration risk (Sharpe 2.46); with it, the always-on version is
Sharpe -0.25. Verified against the textbook identity at rho = 0.999958.

**Learned regimes.** A Gaussian HMM over 5-day RMS yield changes, fit by
Baum-Welch on a rolling 5-year window and applied by *forward filtering* so
no future observation informs a past label. Three states at 2.79 / 4.17 /
6.25bp mean daily move. All four crisis windows land in the high state; 2017
is predominantly low.

**Significance testing.** Probabilistic Sharpe, Deflated Sharpe
(Bailey & Lopez de Prado), minimum track record length, and a stationary
block bootstrap (Politis & Romano) with geometric block lengths.

**Volatility forecast benchmark.** QLIKE loss, Diebold-Mariano with the
Harvey-Leybourne-Newbold correction, and a Model Confidence Set.

## The honest result

Ten of the eleven strategies are indistinguishable from a lucky search once
the Sharpe is deflated by the number and dispersion of trials. The dashboard
says so on its face rather than burying it.

`markov_risk_budget` clears the bar at DSR 0.976, and that number is recorded
as an **upper bound**: deflation counts strategies, not the model revisions
that preceded them.

## Caveat carried on the page

Sharpe ratios run against a zero cash rate because the archive holds no
short-rate series. Over this sample that materially overstates risk-adjusted
return on an unlevered bond position. Ingesting `DFF` corrects it, and it is
first on the dashboard's "pull these next" list.

## Provenance

`markov.py` is a clean-room implementation written from the primary
literature. Two QuantGuild repositories carry no LICENSE file, so nothing
derived from them may enter this repository, which is public.
`BACKTESTING.md` records the two-tier rule.

## Verification

- 57 tests pass, including 23 that specifically assert no lookahead
- Archive verified 5/5 against `manifest.json`
- Dashboard rendered headless at 390px and 1280px: standards mode,
  `scrollWidth == innerWidth` at both widths, no page errors

author: jorgeg94
body:
## Pin pic to v0.9.0

The `pic` dependency was tracking the moving `main` branch, so two builds of the same pic-blas commit could resolve different pic. This pins it to the `v0.9.0` tag in both build systems, so fpm and CMake agree:

- `fpm.toml` — `branch = "main"` → `tag = "v0.9.0"`
- `cmake/modules/Findpic.cmake` — `_rev` `"main"` → `"v0.9.0"`, flipping the tag/branch comment blocks so the tag is the active path and the branch form is the commented-out alternative

## Drop the standalone app, and fix what the pin uncovered

The pin surfaced a latent CMake bug: `app/main.f90` failed to compile with `Cannot open module file 'pic.mod'`.

This was **not** an API change — `module pic` and `pic_print_banner` both still exist in v0.9.0. It is a module-directory move, which pic's own `CMakeLists.txt` documents:

> `0.8.2 moved them from the top-level build tree into pic's own, which was right but broke every consumer that had hardcoded the old spelling, in a patch release.`

pic-blas was one of those consumers. The exe was given only `${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR}/modules` — pic-blas's own module directory — and pic was linked `PRIVATE`, so pic's module directory never reached it. It only ever worked because pic used to write `pic.mod` into that same top-level directory. `main` is green today only because its last run predates the move.

Two changes follow:

**The app is removed.** It only called `pic_print_banner`, exercising pic and nothing in pic-blas, so it tested nothing this library owns. With it go the `PBLAS_BUILD_STANDALONE` option that existed solely to build it, its status line in `demo_status.cmake`, and the CI flag that enabled it. `auto-executables` is turned off on the fpm side for the same reason.

**pic moves to the PUBLIC interface.** Removing the app alone would only have moved the failure: the test target has the identical shape and its sources `use pic_types`, so it was next in line — the build just stopped before reaching it. Since `pic_blas_interfaces` and `pic_lapack_interfaces` both `use pic_types`, pic is genuinely part of pic-blas's public interface, and anyone compiling against our `.mod` files needs pic's as well. pic-blas now also carries its own module directory as an `INTERFACE` include directory rather than having each consumer hardcode it — the exact spelling that just broke.

## Prep for the patch release

Both version fields had drifted from the release tags: `fpm.toml` still read `0.1.0` and the CMake project `VERSION` was `0.0`, neither touched since v0.1.0 even though the last release was v0.3.2. Both now read `0.3.3`.

The CMake one isn't cosmetic. `PROJECT_VERSION` feeds `write_basic_package_version_file`, so the installed `pic-blasConfigVersion.cmake` was advertising version 0.0 — with `AnyNewerVersion` compatibility, any consumer doing `find_package(pic-blas 0.3.x)` against an installed pic-blas was rejected.

Tagging `v0.3.3` is still a manual step after this merges; there is no release workflow in the repo.

## Testing

CI is green across all eight jobs: four CMake (gfortran, ifx, flang-new, nvfortran), three fpm (gfortran, ifx, flang-new), and Fortitude, plus pre-commit. Not built locally — no Fortran compiler or BLAS in the authoring environment.

Worth noting the fpm jobs passed at every stage, including with the broken app, because fpm puts all modules in one place. This was purely a CMake target-propagation bug, and the meaningful signal is that `pic-blas-blas-tester` now compiles at all — its sources `use pic_types`, so the build succeeding is what demonstrates pic's module directory reaching the test target.

## Left out on purpose

- `CMakeLists.txt` still carries the template placeholder `DESCRIPTION "ADD YOUR DESCRIPTION HERE"`, which ships in the installed package config. Worth fixing before cutting the tag.
- `cmake/pic-blasConfig.cmake.in` does not `find_package(pic)`, so an installed pic-blas exports a `pic::pic` target a consumer's CMake cannot resolve. The dangling reference predates this PR — `PRIVATE` already put it in the export set as `LINK_ONLY` — but making pic PUBLIC turns it into a hard requirement. CI never runs `install`, so nothing goes red; it surfaces for whoever first consumes an installed pic-blas.

author: romanize
body:
`--role=hub@1.3` was refused at the flag. AGX-195 accepted only exact pins,
because a pin names a release tag and `versions.json` described only what is
current -- there was nothing to resolve `1.3` against. The refusal was honest,
but `hub@1.3` is the shape a fleet operator wanting security patches without a
minor jump reaches for.

This gives the manifest history, which is what makes the question answerable:

```json
{ "hub": { "current": "1.3.7", "releases": { "1.3.7": 3, "1.3.6": 3, "1.2.9": 2 } } }
```

## Why not the GitHub releases API

`resolve_component_versions` runs before `ensure_node`, which is why
`versions.json` is read by a bash grammar and not by `node` or `jq`. A
`/releases` array is deeply nested JSON, which is a different class of problem
in shell. The endpoint is also rate limited to sixty unauthenticated requests an
hour per IP and needs pagination past a hundred releases, a number four
independent release trains reach quickly.

History in the manifest costs one file that already gets fetched, one grammar
that is already written, no new network call, no rate limit and no pagination.
A thousand releases is roughly thirty kilobytes.

## It deletes an artifact

The per-tag `<component>-v<version>.json` existed only because the manifest had
no line for anything but the current release, and a pinned component's protocol
has to be known *before* installing -- otherwise a hub and a server that cannot
pair are found out after both are installed and running. That answer is now in
the file the installer has already fetched, so the second artifact, its upload
step, its pre-check download and the `AGENTPLEX_VERSIONS` directory layout that
mirrored it are all gone. The release got smaller by giving one file more to
say.

## `hub@1` resolves, and here is why

The argument for refusing it is that a major-only pin is barely a pin. The
argument that won: it is the same resolver either way -- a prefix at a dot
boundary, and the newest release under it -- so refusing `1` would mean a second
grammar and a second refusal to explain, in exchange for withholding the pin
semver says is the one that constrains the breaking axis. An operator who wants
less movement than a minor jump types more digits.

## Prereleases

A series never selects one: `hub@1.3` will not take `1.3.8-rc1`. It falls out of
the candidate pattern, which fixes the field depth (`1.3` matches
`1.3.<patch>`, `1` matches `1.<minor>.<patch>`) and so rejects anything carrying
a `-` or a `+`. The same pattern is why `1.3` cannot match `1.30.0`. Naming
`1.3.8-rc1` exactly still installs it: that is a tag, and it exists.

## Three things verified at the origin

**`sort -V` works on both, and is still not used.** The ticket flagged it as the
one genuinely novel part. It is present on both machines this script runs on --
BSD sort 2.3-Apple on macOS 26, GNU coreutils 9.1 in the `debian:bookworm-slim`
the install tests use -- and they agree on the ordering this needs. The
comparison is written out anyway: the loop that filters candidates is already a
loop, and six lines of numeric compare inside it cost less than a claim about
every `sort` on every machine this script is piped into. Nothing is spawned per
candidate either way.

**`set -e` does not carry a `die` out of a nested command substitution** under
the bash macOS ships as `/bin/bash`, still 3.2. Caught by a test: a manifest
that was not a JSON object printed its refusal from two substitutions down and
the run carried on to a second, vaguer one about the same file. The manifest
readers now assign to globals rather than printing, so every refusal happens in
the process that has to stop. The pure readers are still called through `$(...)`
because they return a status rather than dying, and every caller writes the
`|| die` out.

**`${rest%%[{}]*}` silently matches nothing** -- the `}` inside the bracket
expression closes the parameter expansion before the pattern is ever read, so
the brace-counting loop never advanced. Two expansions and a length compare
instead.

## What this costs

Every install reads the manifest now, pinned or not, because the manifest is
what answers a pin. That is one fetch where a fully pinned install used to make
one per pin against the per-tag artifact, so it is fewer requests -- but it does
remove the old escape hatch of pinning everything to install without reaching
the `v1` branch. `AGENTPLEX_VERSIONS` is the replacement, and it is the one an
air-gapped fleet was going to need anyway; the refusal names it.

A pin the manifest does not list is refused rather than attempted. The file is
append-only and is the record of every release there has been, so a version
missing from it is a tag that was never published -- and finding that out before
the first download is a refusal, where finding it out later is a 404 partway
through an npm install.

## `agentplex update` still takes exact pins only

Deliberate rather than an oversight. A second resolver, in TypeScript, would be
a second thing to keep agreeing with the first, for a command an operator runs
by hand on one machine rather than points a fleet at. It does now read a pinned
release's protocol out of the history, so its protocol agreement check covers a
pinned component instead of having to leave it out.

## Checks

- `pnpm check` green: build, lint, typecheck, and every suite.
- `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME=agx-198 pnpm docker:test` green, which is where
  `install.sh.integration.test.ts` runs as root on Debian under bash 5 -- 122
  tests there, including the nine skipped locally.

## Summary
- Restrict org self-registration (/register-organization web + /api/v1/auth/register-organization mobile) to requests with valid invitation code
- Deployment-wide shared code via `AMLKIT_REGISTRATION_INVITE_CODE` env var
- Fail closed when not configured (registration disabled)
- Rate limit: 5/minute on both POST routes
- Denied attempts logged to `auth_log` (not `audit_log`) to avoid PII exposure via tenant isolation bug
- Parity: web and mobile API both gate the same way
- Test fixture autouse + limiter.reset() eliminates fixture churn

## Why
QA finding: partner officer self-registered via /register-organization and landed in a separate org (org_id mismatch). Invite-only prevents accidental org creation by unauthorized users.

## OPERATIONAL IMPACT
- **After deploy**: ALL org self-registration (web + mobile) is DISABLED until `AMLKIT_REGISTRATION_INVITE_CODE` is set in Cloud Run
- **Mobile app**: returns 403 until amlkit-mobile ships invite_code support (separate Kotlin PR needed)
- **How to set**: Set env var `AMLKIT_REGISTRATION_INVITE_CODE`, no app restart required

body:
## The bug

`validate_recipe_docker` accepted **HTTP 404** as proof that a recipe's
container is accessible:

```python
if status is not None and (200 <= status < 400 or status in (401, 403, 404)):
```

A 404 says only that *some process is speaking HTTP on the port*. It does not
say the ADK app mounted. An image whose web server boots but whose app never
starts answers 404 on **every** probe path — and this gate called that a PASS.
That is precisely the false green the check exists to prevent.

## The fix

404 is excluded. `401`/`403` are still accepted — refusing a request requires
the route to exist and the request to have been routed to it, which is the
signal we want. 2xx/3xx likewise.

**This tightens nothing that currently passes.** All six recipes with a root
Dockerfile answer `/list-apps` with HTTP 200 on the green `main` run
([35176298541](https://github.com/google/adk-samples/actions/runs/35176298541)),
so none was relying on the leniency.

Also realigns the probe timeout with `.github/policy.yml`, which declares
`deployability.verification` the source of truth and says
`ready_timeout_seconds: 120` where this module had drifted to `90`.

## ⚠️ One divergence I did NOT resolve — needs a maintainer decision

`policy.yml` defines `deployability.verification.run_allowlist`:

> Recipes whose containers are safe to RUN, not merely build. Some recipes
> create real GCP resources at import — for example
> `core/python/cross-session-memory` calls `client.agent_engines.create()` at
> module scope. [...] anything not listed here is BUILT ONLY.

**CI honours no such list.** It runs every recipe with a root Dockerfile, and
there is *zero overlap* between the two sets:

| | |
|---|---|
| policy allows running | `contrib/python/financial-advisor`, `core/python/rag-agent-search`, `core/python/rag-vector-search` |
| CI actually ran | `brand-search-optimization`, `multiformat-hybrid-rag`, `ambient-expense-agent`, **`cross-session-memory`**, `genmedia-for-commerce`, `long-horizon-harness` |

Including the one recipe the policy names as its example of the hazard.

It is harmless *today* only because the job holds no real credentials — the
container gets a placeholder project and no ADC, which is why the unguarded
telemetry bug surfaced as a crash rather than as a provisioned resource. That
is safety by accident, not by design. Wire real credentials into that job and
the policy's worst case becomes live.

Resolving it is a genuine choice between two costs:

- **Honour the allowlist** → all six recipes become build-only, losing the run
  verification that just caught the telemetry bug on two of them.
- **Rescope the allowlist** to credentialed contexts only, and say so in policy.

That is your call, not a bug-fix's, so it is documented in a comment in the
source and left alone.

## Verification

- 4 regression tests added, and I checked they earn their place: with the old
  behaviour restored, `test_all_paths_404_is_not_accessible` and
  `test_probe_timeout_default_matches_policy` **both fail**; with the fix both
  pass.
- `test_probe_timeout_default_matches_policy` reads `policy.yml` directly, so
  the next drift is a test failure rather than a silent difference.
- `uv run pytest -q` → **1995 passed** (up from 1991)
- ruff clean

author: sankarshanmukhopadhyay
sreedal
body:
Summary:

`zero_` on CUDA was moved off the `fill_` kernel and onto `cudaMemsetAsync` in
#195303 (`df69a036b4c2`, "[ATen] Zero CUDA tensors with cudaMemsetAsync instead
of a fill kernel"), which added `zero_cuda_` and repointed the `CUDA` dispatch
key for `zero_` in `native_functions.yaml`. On affected ROCm versions that path
silently returns wrong data: `hipMemsetAsync` captured into a HIP graph leaves
stale bytes behind, so a buffer `zero_` reports as zeroed reads back non-zero.
No error, no NaN, correct shape and dtype, so nothing downstream notices.

This is a ROCm runtime regression, not a PyTorch one, and it is bounded:

| ROCm  | memset under graph capture |
|---|---|
| 6.4.2 | clean |
| 7.0.0 | broken |
| 7.1.0 | clean |

The fix landed in ROCm/clr `3038c4c3777eeb55eabfddee56807c6f74b1b77c`, and
pdesupinski confirmed the bug does not reproduce on 7.1.0. So the window is
`[7.0.0, 7.1.0)`: `zero_cuda_` takes the memset fast path everywhere else, and
inside the window falls back to `self.fill_(0)` -- what `zero_` did before
#195303. CUDA is untouched.

Credit to pdesupinski for reducing this to `hipMemsetAsync` plus graph capture
and for pinning the fix commit. The original diff gated all of ROCm because the
mechanism was unclear at the time.

How it was found, for context on why the symptom looked stranger than the bug:
an LLM inference server on MI350X returned garbage completions. A decode step
zeroes a scratch buffer every iteration; when the zeroing does not take effect
the sampler reads stale logits and emits a long run of token id 0. The
production hit rate tracked concurrency -- 16% of responses at 64 concurrent
requests, 41% at 512, 6% at 8192 -- which is why light traffic looked clean.
Concurrency is not part of the trigger though; it only changes how often the
captured graph is replayed and how much stale data is sitting in the buffer.
Graph capture is the trigger, and disabling capture while leaving
`torch.compile` on was enough to make the corruption disappear:

| configuration | corrupt responses |
|---|---|
| memset, `torch.compile` on, graphs captured | 3.03% (174/5737) |
| memset, `torch.compile` on, graphs disabled | 0.00% (0/4656) |
| memset, `torch.compile` off, graphs disabled | 0.00% (0/5956) |
| `fill_` kernel, `torch.compile` on, graphs captured | 0.00% (0/5782) |

Authored with the assistance of an AI coding agent.

Test Plan:
Unit tests, `test/test_torch.py`:

* `test_zero_dense_emits_memset` asserts that dense `zero_` emits a `Memset`
  event. Which path `zero_` takes on ROCm is now version dependent, and the
  test-side ROCm version helper (`common_cuda.ROCM_VERSION`) is major/minor
  only, so rather than duplicate the version window in Python and have it rot
  against the C++, the test is skipped on ROCm and its original CUDA assertion
  is restored unchanged.
* `test_zero_dense_inside_graph_capture` is new, and is the one that actually
  covers this bug on ROCm. It captures `zero_` into a graph, replays it, and
  checks the buffer really is zero -- an assertion about behaviour rather than
  about which kernel ran, so it holds on every backend and every ROCm version.
  It is skipped where graph capture is unavailable.

```
python test/test_torch.py -k test_zero_
```

Honest status: these have not been run on a ROCm host. The MI350X capacity
reachable from here runs a packaged serving build, not a PyTorch source tree,
so `test_torch.py` cannot be invoked against it directly. The end-to-end runs
below exercise the same code path on the same hardware, but that is not a green
test run and is not claimed as one.

CUDA is unaffected by construction: `!defined(USE_ROCM)` makes the gate
unconditionally true on a CUDA build, so `zero_cuda_` compiles identically to
before this diff, and the profiler assertion on CUDA is the pre-existing one.

Minimal reproducer, pure PyTorch -- no serving stack, no model, no concurrency:

```python
import torch

buf = torch.empty(512, 151936, dtype=torch.float32, device="cuda")
sentinel = torch.full_like(buf, 7.0)
bad = torch.zeros((), dtype=torch.long, device="cuda")

def step():
    buf.copy_(sentinel)
    buf.zero_()
    bad.add_(buf.ne(0).sum())

side = torch.cuda.Stream()
side.wait_stream(torch.cuda.current_stream())
with torch.cuda.stream(side):
    for _ in range(3):
        step()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        step()
torch.cuda.current_stream().wait_stream(side)

bad.zero_()
for _ in range(20000):
    graph.replay()
torch.cuda.synchronize()
print("stale elements:", bad.item())   # expect 0
```

End-to-end evidence, collected before the mechanism was narrowed. A 0.6B
decoder-only model served with vLLM on one 8-GPU MI350X host, driven with a
fixed 200-token prompt and 100-token output, stop tokens disabled so every
request decodes the full 100 tokens. A response counts as corrupt if it
contains a run of token id 0. Each row is a separate run against a freshly
started server; checkpoint, sampling settings and every other flag held
constant, only the named column varied.

| concurrency | before (memset) | after (fill kernel) |
|---|---|---|
| 64 | 16.42% (33/201) | 0.00% (0/201) |
| 512 | 40.55% (339/836) | 0.00% (0/836) |
| 8192 | 6.31% (190/3012) | 0.00% (0/3000) |

Throughput and latency over the same runs, showing the fill kernel costs
nothing here:

| concurrency | | QPS | decode tok/s | avg latency | p50 TTFT | p99 TTFT |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 64 | before | 89.09 | 8857 | 0.715s | 712.4ms | 824.1ms |
| 64 | after | 91.18 | 9041 | 0.699s | 700.4ms | 812.4ms |
| 512 | before | 561.44 | 55958 | 0.845s | 752.5ms | 2142.9ms |
| 512 | after | 566.42 | 56164 | 0.837s | 744.4ms | 2252.7ms |

`arc lint` on all four changed files: no issues.

author: christopherthompson81
body:
The clash rule drops a `2°` whose syllable is adjacent to the `1°`, and its exception required a **true diphthong** (`AY`/`OY`/`AW`) in a **closed** syllable. Its own comment records how that shape was reached — rows changed, and tests not breaking. **The reference was never asked.** Run 17 put a number on the cost: the rule drops a dictionary `2°` gold keeps on **2,383 of the 4,162** gold-covered sites it fires on.

### What gold actually does at a clash site

Over 31,760 words:

```
final syllable, CLOSED    gold marks it  1,849 / 1,973   94%
final syllable, OPEN      gold marks it    167 /   330   51%
NOT the final syllable    gold marks it    918 / 1,973   47%
```

The open-final row is **two populations**, not a coin flip:

| marks it | | doesn't |
|---|---|---|
| `OY` 10/10 · `AW` 8/8 · `EY` 65/71 · `AY` 11/12 · `AO` 10/11 · `UW` 22/33 | | `OW` 22/104 · `IY` 9/55 · `AA` 5/15 |

That split **is** the distinction the original narrowing was reaching for and couldn't express: `airway` (`EH1 R W EY2`, gold `ˈɛɹwˌA`) against `zorro` (`Z AO1 R OW2`) — CMUdict writes `OW2` on an ordinary final `-o`, and marking it over-articulates.

So: exempt a `2°` on the **final** syllable when that syllable is **closed**, or when its vowel is one of `EY AY OY AW AO UW`.

| | exact vs gold |
|---|---|
| before | 39,160 (43.80%) |
| after | **41,767 (46.71%)** |

**+3,038 / −431, net +2,607** — the largest single gain of this series, larger than the syllabic-schwa import (+2,053).

### Two negative results, kept because they bound the change

- **Deleting nothing** scores 86.63% against the widened rule's 87.82%. The deletions the rule still makes are right; this is not a rule to remove.
- **Exempting non-final sites too** is *worse* — 86.88% — matching the 47% measured directly. Those keep being dropped.

And closed-final has **no sub-split**, which was checked rather than assumed: gold marks it 88–99% across every vowel and every syllable count.

### ⚠ The 431 regressions are irreducible

Lexicalized compounds gold declines to mark: `almost`, `ambush`, `backbeat`, `birdshot`, and the `-field`/`-board`/`-ville` place names. Capitalization is **not** the discriminator (19% of losses vs 4% of gains), and there's no vowel or length signal. Gold marks `aardvark` and not `birdshot` — the same shape. That's the hand lexicon's own inconsistency, not a rule we're failing to find.

### The probe's validity was established before any variant was scored

Scoring a stress rule needs per-nucleus alignment between ARPABET and IPA, which is the step most likely to produce a confident wrong answer. The probe reimplements the shipped rule as a control and reproduced the shipped mark sequence on **32,464 of 32,491 dict words (99.92%)** — the 27 exceptions are words resolved by other paths. Every word whose alignment couldn't be confirmed was discarded.

### Two tests changed meaning

- `a priori` moves. The test pinning it was titled *"an open final syllable is not marked"* and was recording a **design choice**, not a reported misreading. `priori` is `P R AY0 AO1 R AY2` — an open final `AY`, which gold marks 11 times out of 12. The test now records the vowel split.
- **#1323's pinned divergence is closed.** That PR found `airway`/`aircrew` losing their mark here while measuring something else, and pinned them rather than folding an unmeasured fix in. Both are inside the widened exception.

Gates: **`csharp/tools/parity` 189/189 byte-identical**, C# 6,687, vitest 5,943, goldens 0 stale (109 rows, every one machine-checked to have the signature — same phonemes, same primaries, more secondaries — before regenerating), tsc and package fence clean.

body:
## Resumen

**PR-2 — Contributor Mission-First UX:**
- ZOOM audit of the existing Knowledge Contributor Program (F1 slice, #627) against the Field Knowledge Control Center's PR-2 spec: backend workflow was already complete end-to-end, but the public `/contributors` UX was still terms/account-first, and a real financial-safety gap existed — demo/example missions had no server-side guard and could actually be accepted and paid out.
- API: `acceptMission` now rejects `isDemo` missions with `400 CONTRIBUTOR_PROGRAM_MISSION_IS_DEMO` before any acceptance/snapshot row is created.
- BFF: propagated a machine-readable error `code` end-to-end so the web layer can react to specific API errors, not just display a message string.
- Web `/contributors`: mission-first hero, primary CTA "Ver misiones disponibles" (was "Participar" → login), four-step explanation with the spec's exact copy, "tarea (misión de SEMSE)" terminology, demo missions shown as non-payable and non-acceptable, inline consent flow that keeps the contributor on the selected mission.
- Report: `docs/reportes/knowledge_contributor_program_pr2_2026-09-17.md`.

**PR-3 prerequisite — LiveKit webhook signature fix (new in this update):**
- ZOOM trace of the Prometeo Live / LiveKit backend found `livekit-webhook.controller.ts` verified its signature against `JSON.stringify(parsedBody)` instead of the exact raw bytes LiveKit signed — the same class of bug this codebase's own Stripe webhook already avoids via `@RawBody()`. Since `LIVEKIT_URL`/`LIVEKIT_API_KEY`/`LIVEKIT_API_SECRET` are configured on the production `semse-API` service (confirmed read-only via the Railway API), this meant real LiveKit `room_started`/`participant_joined`/`room_finished` webhooks would very likely fail signature verification in production — `LiveSession` status has effectively never been able to auto-advance from actual room state.
- Fixed to use `@RawBody()` matching the Stripe pattern; also hardened `verifyWebhook` against a length-mismatch crash (`timingSafeEqual` throws instead of returning `false` on a malformed/truncated signature — a real crash risk on this `@Public()` endpoint).
- Added `apps/api/test/livekit-webhook.test.ts` (10 tests): proves a real-raw-bytes signature verifies, the old `JSON.stringify` reconstruction does **not** (regression fixture), tampering/malformed/unconfigured cases fail closed without throwing, and the controller correctly dispatches `room_started → ACTIVE` / `room_finished → ENDED` only for a valid signature and recognized room.
- **Native mobile Prometeo Live media (camera/mic/video rendering) was not attempted** — genuinely absent at the dependency/permission/native-config level (no LiveKit RN SDK, no CAMERA/RECORD_AUDIO permission declared), and closing it requires a native dev-client build and a physical device/simulator, neither available in this sandbox. Documented as a real blocker with exact next steps for whoever has a device, not glossed over.
- **Also found and reported, not silently changed:** `LIVE_SESSION_SWEEP_ENABLED` is not set on the production `semse-worker` service, so expired LiveSessions aren't currently auto-swept — left alone per this repo's rule against an agent touching production Railway config; needs a maintainer decision.
- Report: `docs/reportes/prometeo_live_pr3_zoom_2026-09-17.md`.

These two changes are unrelated domains bundled onto one PR because this session is constrained to a single designated branch; happy to see them split into separate PRs at merge time if preferred — neither depends on the other.

## Tipo de cambio

- [x] Bugfix (demo-mission payout guard; LiveKit webhook signature verification)
- [x] Feature (mission-first UX)
- [ ] Refactor
- [ ] CI/CD
- [x] Documentación

## Checklist

- [x] Probado localmente — against a real local Postgres 16 (contributor-program) and real HMAC/JWT fixtures (LiveKit webhook), not mocked away
- [x] Tests actualizados o agregados — demo-guard integration test; 10 new LiveKit webhook tests; fixed a pre-existing test whose fixture incidentally set `isDemo: true`
- [x] Spec actualizado o confirmado como no aplicable — PR-2 implements `15_PR2_CONTRIBUTOR_MISSION_FIRST_UX.md`; the webhook fix is a correctness/security fix uncovered during PR-3's ZOOM trace, no spec change needed
- [ ] `pnpm spec:preflight` ejecutado — could not run; requires network access to Railway not available in this sandbox
- [x] Sin regresiones visibles — see evidence below
- [x] Documentación actualizada (si aplica) — both reports in `docs/reportes/`

## Evidencia

- `node --test apps/api/test/contributor-program.service.test.ts` → 5/5 pass against real Postgres.
- `node --test apps/api/test/livekit-webhook.test.ts` → 10/10 pass.
- `node --test apps/api/test/live-sessions.service.test.ts` → 20/20 pass (no regression from the webhook fix).

- `pnpm build:packages && pnpm build:api && pnpm build:web` → clean.

- `pnpm typecheck` → clean across api/web/worker/mobile.
- Mobile: `npx jest src/screens/LiveSessionScreen.test.tsx` → 5/5 pass (unaffected — native media path untouched).

author: joeqth
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

`ScoreEncoderCacheManager.reset()` clears `self.freeable`, an attribute inherited from upstream `EncoderCacheManager` (`vllm/v1/core/encoder_cache_manager.py`). In this subclass the inherited single-level `freeable` dict is never populated:

- every method that inserts into it (`check_and_update_cache`, `can_allocate`, `allocate`, `free_encoder_input`) is fully overridden, and
- evictable entries are tracked in the subclass's own `npu_freeable` / `cpu_freeable` dicts, which are already cleared later in the same method.

The cleared dict is therefore always empty and the line is a no-op. This PR removes it so the code no longer implies the inherited single-level bookkeeping is still live, and so future contributors don't build logic against a dead field.

No behavior change: the attribute still exists via `super().__init__()`, and nothing in this subclass or its tests reads it.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

None.

### How was this patch tested?

- Covered by existing unit tests: `tests/ut/core/test_score_encoder_cache_manager.py`, in particular `test_allocate_reuse_promote_free_and_reset_preserve_invariants` (calls `reset()` and then `_check_invariant()`). They are expected to pass unchanged; CI will confirm.
- Local check: `python -m py_compile vllm_ascend/ec_manager/score_ec_manager.py`.
- No new tests added: pure no-op line removal; the existing reset/invariant tests already exercise this path.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/84030bbe3d74d99bad477a3d2e37a973ccd8865c

That netlist is regenerated from `design/sar_adc_top.sch`, a file this repo
really does change (DR-004 Amendment A moved the comparator's device count;
DR-008/DR-009 changed sub-block interfaces), so a port added, renamed, or
dropped would have left §2 describing an interface this repo no longer builds.

Check 10 compares four things:

- **(a) the quoted `.subckt` line** — port for port and in order.
- **(b) coverage, both directions** — a netlist port with no table row, and a
  table row naming something that is not a port, are each a failure naming the
  signal. A port with no row is the cheapest way to make a slot budget fit.
- **(c) per-row counts** — each row's "Count used" against the ports its
  Signal cell names, ranges (`DOUT9..DOUT0`) expanded. The shared-rail row
  claims no count and is exempt, since it is charged against no slot.
- **(d) the Totals sentence** — each per-category total recomputed from the
  rows the table itself assigns to that category (read off the "Assumed
  Challenge slot" column, never a list in the checker), and the conditional
  dedicated-pad total from the dedicated pads plus the harness-supplied
  reference lines. A row charged against the budget while matching no category
  is reported too, so a new signal cannot slip past the totals by being
  uncategorised.

## No verdict moves, no spec row relaxed

**No live drift found**: the committed document passes unmodified. All 19
ports map, the quoted `.subckt` line is the netlist's own, and the four totals
(2 / 11 / 3 / 2, conditional 5) are the table's own sums. §4 is untouched —
"Post-layout PVT simulation" stays **UNMET** and "DRC/LVS-clean GDS" stays
**PARTIAL/UNMET-BLOCKED** at 98 mismatches. Criterion 3 remains gated on #103
(still open, still `loom:blocked`); criterion 4 remains not-yet-triggerable
(`rules-4.html` still unpublished). DR-007 re-checked this pass: still
`proposed`, so the two "Informational only" rows are correctly graded.

The Totals sentence is restated in the gated form (bolded counts; the
conditional phrased distinctly so the two dedicated-pad numbers cannot be
graded against each other). Its meaning, including the open slot-budget risk
that `VREFP`/`VREFN` may have to be dedicated pads, is unchanged.

## Verification

Mutation-probed against the live document rather than declared working —
dropping a port from the quote, reordering it, deleting a table row, adding a
signal that is not a port, miscounting a row, relaxing each of the four
totals, shrinking the conditional total, and uncategorising a counted row each
produce exactly the findings that name the defect, while the unmutated
document produces none. A simulated netlist-side port addition (`VSS`) fails
the document too.

11 fixture tests plus 2 real-document vacuity guards (the netlist parse and
the gated Totals form): an unparsed input would leave check 10 inert and still
exit 0, which is the trap checks 4, 6, 8 and 9 each needed a guard for.

`npm run lint`, `npm run test` (233 tests, OK), `npm run
check:proposal-citations`, `npm run check:spec-coverage` and `npm run
check:report` all pass.

body:
Performs `docs/backlog.md` 57 `set-staging-alertmanager-to-its-register-values`, and deletes the entry.

Appendix A's second table carried `main-staging-alertmanager` at 5 minutes / 2 minutes **from intent**: at `write-and-rehearse-the-rebuild-runbook`'s pre-destroy read that check did not exist — both hosts were feeding production's — so its row was written from production's observed values, and the paragraph beside it went on to infer from the table's own preamble that a check created by its first ping *must* be sitting on the vendor's default.

**The operator read it at the observer on 2026-09-17: period 5 minutes, grace 2 minutes, green and receiving pings.** That is the pair the row already recorded, so nothing was changed at the observer and neither table was wrong. The inference was — and how the check came to carry those values rather than the vendor's is not established, which the paragraph now says rather than guessing.

The correction the paragraph gains is the reusable part: the preamble licenses the *suspicion* that a check may be sitting on a default, which is why it says to read these back. It does not license writing down what the default would have made of it. That distinction is what turned a one-day-old record into a claim, and the row is a record now because someone looked.

**Taken as a fix rather than a change**, the same call `give-staging-its-own-dead-mans-switch-check` got in a142b33: one operator action plus the documentation correction it obliges, with nothing to specify and no delta to write.

The archived `write-and-rehearse-the-rebuild-runbook` record is deliberately untouched. Its `## Not performed` disclosure of this read is accurate about what that change did and knew, and correcting an archived record is for making it say what happened, not for back-filling what a later read found.

body:
## Why

PR #271 redesigned Budget Automation to match upstream Actual's real type taxonomy but explicitly documented three follow-ups as not done: the "Adjustments" sub-feature (fixed/% increase-decrease on Schedule and Historical automations) and a full income-category picker for % of income. This closes both gaps, verified against Actual's `goal-template.pegjs` and `category-template-context.ts` (commit `2fc69915`) for the exact `adjustment`/`adjustmentType` shape and `runAverage`/`runPercentage` semantics.

While implementing the % of income picker I also found and fixed a round-trip bug: a percentage automation's selected `category` (income source) was parsed but discarded, so it always came back as the default "available funds" on decode.

Also re-verified end-of-month cleanup, Save by date's "start spending in", and issue #253 (long-term target progress / linked schedule) against the current model — all already correct post-#271, no changes needed there.

## What

- `BudgetTarget`: new `AdjustmentType` (PERCENT/FIXED) with signed `adjustmentPercent`/`adjustmentAmountCents`, matching upstream's `increase`/`decrease` modifier grammar. Applied in `suggestedBudget` (From-history average mode) and `BudgetTemplatePlanner` (Cover schedule), clamped at zero. From-history's copy mode carries no adjustment upstream, so it's dropped on encode if present.
- `BudgetAutomationDocument.validate`: adjustments require a value when a type is set.
- `BudgetAutomationScreen`: new "Adjustment" section (Increase/Decrease + % or fixed amount) for Cover schedule and From-history (average); "Income source" picker for % of income listing available funds, all income, and the budget's real income categories (threaded through from `AppNavigation`).
- Fixed `BudgetTarget.fromGoalDef` losing the percentage automation's selected `category` on decode.
- `docs/BUDGET_AUTOMATION_PARITY.md` updated to describe the new parity boundary.

## Risk

Model/codec change is additive (new optional fields, default `null`) and the percentage-source fix only affects round-tripping of an already-stored value — no migration or sync-format break. Adjustment values are clamped at zero before use, so no negative budget amounts can be produced.

## How it was tested

- Standalone `kotlinc` syntax/type-check of the touched model files (`BudgetTarget.kt`, `BudgetAutomationDocument.kt`, `BudgetCategory.kt`) against `org.json` — compiles cleanly. The sandboxed environment couldn't run the full Gradle/AGP build (Android Gradle Plugin's Google Maven repo is blocked by egress policy here), so full unit/instrumented test execution is left to CI.
- Added unit tests: `BudgetTargetTest` (average adjustment scaling/clamping), `BudgetTargetGoalDefRoundTripTest` (schedule/average adjustment round-trip, copy-mode adjustment dropped, percentage income-category round-trip), `BudgetTemplatePlannerTest` (schedule adjustment applied in whole-budget preview).

## Screenshots

Not applicable — no UI screenshots captured in this sandboxed session; the new "Adjustment" section and "Income source" picker follow the existing editor's Material 3 styling.

- [ ] Destructive operations, migrations, restore/archive flows, and rollback/recovery were considered where applicable. *(not applicable — no destructive/migration changes)*

author: thecodinganalyst
body:
## Summary
Implements #55 by making platform tenant creation provision the tenant's first `TENANT_ADMIN` in the same transaction.

### Included
- platform-only tenant provisioning request now includes tenant code/name, admin username, and temporary initial password
- tenant and initial tenant admin are created atomically in one `@Transactional` service operation
- initial password is immediately BCrypt-hashed and never returned by the API
- response contains only tenant and non-sensitive tenant-admin metadata
- duplicate tenant codes and case-insensitive usernames return HTTP 409
- minimum 12-character initial password validation
- authorization tests for anonymous and tenant-admin callers
- integration tests verifying tenant-admin association and no partial tenant creation on provisioning conflict
- updated multi-tenancy/security documentation describing the interim credential strategy and future invitation/reset path

### Security model
The initial password is a temporary bootstrap credential only. It is never logged or returned, and the API stores only its hash. This can later be replaced with an invitation/password-reset flow without changing tenant ownership or RBAC.

Closes #55

author: tsinordin-cell
body:
Sparren `verify-claims` rapporterade **noll fynd** i `guide-content.ts` — en fil med 178 obelagda priser. Den har PR:en visar varfor, lagar det, och gor den andra halvan av spärrens egen regel.

## Blindflacken

`harKallaNara` godtog ett kallmarke var som helst inom fem rader. Markorer som `'waxholmsbolaget'` och `'strömma'` lades in for att fanga rader som `// KALLA: Waxholmsbolagets tabell 11`. Men funktionen laste hela raden oavsett om den var kod, kommentar eller brodtext — och guiderna skriver *"Waxholmsbolagets bat fran Stromkajen"* i lopande text i nastan varje transportstycke.

Foljden: varje pris och klockslag inom fem rader fran den meningen raknades som belagt.

**Mätt 2026-09-17** — av de 190 priser och klockslag som sparren faktiskt sag i guide-content.ts:

| godkandes av | antal |
|---|---|
| ordet "waxholmsbolaget" i brodtext | 37 |
| ordet "strömma" i brodtext | 5 |
| en riktig `KÄLLA:`-rad | 13 |
| `UPPSKATTNING`-markor | 137 |
| ingenting | 1 |

Fyrtiotva pastaenden var alltsa "kallbelagda" av att en operator rakade namnas i narheten.

Det ar exakt den blindflack filens egen inledande kommentar varnar for efter guide-content-incidenten i augusti: **"En spärr med blindfläck ger falsk trygghet."**

**Fixen:** markorer som bara identifierar en avsandare galler nu enbart i en kommentar. `'källa:'`, `'http://'` och de ovriga explicita markorerna galler overallt — dem gar det inte att raka skriva i brodtext.

Effekt: 2 -> 11 fynd. Inga regressioner i odatan. Alla nio nya ar rattade i den har PR:en, sa baslinjen behover inte vaxa — och `--uppdatera-baslinje` ar inte kord.

## Vad som kom fram nar sparren blev tat

Tva av de nio var riktiga sakfel mot publicerade prislistor:

**Fjaderholmarna.** FAQ:n sa *"Biljetten med Strömma kostar ca 120–150 kr tur/retur."* Strommas egen sida anger **170 kr enkel, 205 kr tur och retur**. Odatan hade ratt siffra sedan tidigare — guiden mostsade den alltsa, och lag lagre an verkligheten.

**Cinderellabåten till Sandhamn.** FAQ:n sa *"Ca 350–450 kr tur/retur beroende på säsong."* Stromma publicerar **"from SEK 255"** for enkel resa och inget returpris alls. Spannet fanns inte publicerat nagonstans. Nu star den publicerade siffran och att returpriset varierar.

De ovriga sju var marknadsspann eller obelagda klockslag: charterpriser over flera operatorer (markta som uppskattning, och sagt ut for lasaren), Strommas eget AW-pris (namngiven operators pris ska belaggas eller strykas — struket, med hanvisning till deras sida), och *"kom senast 9:30"* om en parkering pa Tofta strand (gar inte att belagga — nu "kom tidigt pa morgonen").

## Den andra halvan av regeln

`verify-claims` slapper igenom ett pris utan kalla om det ar markt

```
UPPSKATTNING: <vad den bygger på> (åååå-mm)
```

och sager i samma andetag att det da ska **"sägas rakt ut för besökaren i gränssnittet"**. Den halvan har aldrig byggts. Det fanns 173 sadana markorer i guiderna och **noll** av dem syntes pa sidan. Lasaren sag *"ca 300–600 kr/pers"* som om det kom ur en prislista.

`scripts/generera-uppskattningar.mjs` laser markorerna och skriver `uppskattningar.generated.ts`. Guidesidan visar en ruta **fore** innehallet:

> **9 prisnivåer i den här guiden är uppskattade** — de bygger på ungefärliga prisnivåer/tider över flera aktörer, ej hämtat per aktör, senast gjord augusti 2026. De är alltså inte hämtade ur någons prislista. Kontrollera hos operatören innan du bokar eller budgeterar.

Fore innehallet, inte efter. En reservation som lasaren hittar efter att ha budgeterat sin resa ar ingen reservation.

**54 guider, 124 markorer.** Skriptet skriver ocksa ut hur gammal den aldsta ar och sager till nar den passerat ett ar: *"En uppskattning som aldrig omprövas är en gissning med datum på."*

`--kontroll` ligger i `prebuild`, samma monster som kallistan i #296.

## Varfor det har hanger ihop med #294–#296

Samma mekanism tre ganger nu: en markering som bara finns i koden blir aldrig last, och blir darfor aldrig omprovad. 29 procent av KALLA-raderna var fel. 42 priser var "belagda" av ett ord i brodtexten. 124 uppskattningar var osynliga. Det som bryter monstret ar att ge markeringen en konsument som nagon faktiskt ser.

## Guards

```
tsc --noEmit                rent
vitest run src/lib          387/387
verify-claims               inga NYA pastaenden utan kalla (med skarpt regel)
guard-cache-regler          18 sidor, inga dynamiska API:er
kallor:kontroll             30 oar, 301 kallor
uppskattningar:kontroll     54 guider, 124 markorer
eslint                      277 -> 277 (befintliga emoji-fel, inga nya)
```

Baslinjen ar orord: 89 poster, vaktvarde 89.

body:
## ¿Qué cambia?
`nz_call_procedure` (y `nz_job_poll`, que comparte el helper) devolvían `return_value` como string: el valor de retorno se coercionaba con `str()`, así que un SP que retorna `INT` daba `"42"` y el cliente tenía que comparar contra `"0"`/`"1"`. Ahora se devuelve el **tipo nativo** del driver, de modo que `return_value == 0` funciona sin parseo.

## Issue relacionado
Closes #310

## Acción según AGENTS.md
- **Ruta (keywords)**: procedimiento, catálogo, driver
- **Docs leídos**:
  - docs/architecture/tools-contract.md
  - docs/roles/data-engineer.md
- **Rol asumido**: Data Engineer + Backend Developer

## Archivos esperados (según el issue)
- `src/nz_mcp/catalog/call.py` — `_fetch_return_value` ya no hace `str()`; nuevo `_json_scalar` que normaliza a escalar JSON-nativo.
- `src/nz_mcp/catalog/row_shape.py` — sin cambios: se reutiliza `is_sequence_row`.
- `docs/architecture/tools-contract.md` — § 33 (`nz_call_procedure`) y § 39 (`nz_job_poll`).
- Extras justificados: `src/nz_mcp/tools/call_procedure.py` y `src/nz_mcp/tools/call_async.py` (tipo del campo `return_value`), `CHANGELOG.md`, tests.

## Auditoría pre-merge — 7 dimensiones

### 1. Contrato y compatibilidad
- [x] Si toca tools: `docs/architecture/tools-contract.md` actualizado en este PR.
- [x] Si hay cambio observable: `CHANGELOG.md` con entrada bilingüe en `Unreleased`.
- [x] Sin breaking change inesperado (el campo sigue siendo escalar; solo cambia el tipo JSON de string a número cuando el SP devuelve un número).

### 2. Seguridad
- [x] Todo SQL pasa por `sql_guard.validate()` (el `CALL` sigue igual, parametrizado con `?`).
- [x] Sin SQL concatenado.
- [x] Sin credenciales en código, logs, tests, fixtures, comentarios.
- [x] No toca `sql_guard.py` ni `auth.py`.

### 3. Mantenibilidad y diseño
- [x] Toqué solo los archivos esperados (los extras van documentados arriba).
- [x] Sin abstracciones nuevas sin 3 usos reales (`_json_scalar` tiene 1 uso hoy, pero aísla la normalización y se testea directo).
- [x] Sin dependencias nuevas.
- [x] Funciones < 50 LoC, args < 4.
- [x] Una intención por PR.
- [x] PR < 400 LoC sin tests/docs.

### 4. Tests
- [x] Tests para todo comportamiento nuevo (+7: `_json_scalar` numérico/Decimal/otros, `_fetch_return_value` con int y escalar suelto, execute con int nativo, modelo del tool con int).
- [x] `pytest -m "not integration"` verde local: 1608 passed, 1 skipped, 21 deselected.
- [x] Cobertura no cae respecto a `main` (la valida el gate de CI).
- [x] Sin `pytest.skip()` ni `xfail` sin issue.

### 5. Tipado y estilo
- [x] `ruff check .` y `ruff format --check .` limpios.
- [x] `mypy --strict` limpio (187 archivos).
- [x] Sin `Any` en superficies públicas (nuevo alias `ReturnScalar = int | float | bool | str | None`).
- [x] Sin `except Exception:` sin re-raise tipado.

### 6. Documentación
- [x] Si cambia API pública: `tools-contract.md` actualizado (§ 33 y § 39).
- [x] Si cambia comportamiento: `CHANGELOG.md` actualizado (ES + EN, sección `Fixed`).
- [x] Sin ADR: no hay decisión arquitectónica nueva (se sigue el tipo que ya devuelve el driver).
- [x] Sin claves i18n nuevas.

### 7. Idioma y forma

- [x] Branch `fix/310-call-return-value-type`.
- [x] Commit en español.
- [x] Código y comentarios en inglés.

## Validación humana requerida

## Notas para el auditor
- **Diseño**: se preserva el escalar nativo del driver. `int`/`float`/`bool`/`str`/`None` pasan tal cual; un `Decimal` (Netezza `NUMERIC`) se normaliza a `int` si es entero o `float` si no; `datetime`/`bytes`/otros → string (mismo JSON que ya produce `nz_query_select`). No se consulta `_V_PROCEDURE.RETURNS`: el driver ya tipa el valor, así que no hace falta un round-trip extra al catálogo.
- **Verificado EN VIVO** (perfil `nzsaas` / DESA_MODELOS, dejado en `nzsaas`): SP temporal `DWIGHT_310_RET() RETURNS INT4` → `return_value: 42`, `python_type: int` (antes habría sido `"42"`). El SP se borró y la limpieza se verificó (0 filas en `_V_PROCEDURE`).

author: ericgriffin
body:
Closes #2044

## Problem
In the fullscreen profile view, the scrub bar and the main chart disagreed about the start and end of the dive:
- The scrub marker did not line up with the minimap behind it: right of the minimap's start at 0:00, short of its end at the end of the dive.
- Hovering the chart moved playback to a different time than the tooltip showed (00:02 against 0:00, 52:52 against 52:54).
- The last sample could not be reached by hovering.

## Causes and fixes

### Scrub bar minimap inset
The minimap was painted with `Positioned.fill` across the whole slider box, but the slider insets its track by `max(overlayWidth / 2, thumbWidth / 2)` (24px). The overlay radius is now a named constant, `_scrubTrackInset`, and the minimap is inset by the same amount.

### Two selections per hover
Every mouse move reported `onPointSelected` twice: fl_chart's touched spot (what the tooltip shows), then the chart's pointer-hover fallback. The fallback ran second, so playback kept its value. In a probe over Dive #15's shape (1,590 samples every 2s) the two disagreed at 739 of 1,750 pixel positions. The fallback now stays silent while fl_chart has resolved a sample, and only covers the cursor outside the plot or with no sample within the touch threshold.

### Plot insets left out the border
fl_chart lays the plot out inside its 1px border (its border `Container` pads the child by the border width), so data x=0 is drawn at 49px, not 48px. `_plotInsets` now counts the border on every side. This fixes the fallback's time mapping, so past the plot's right edge it snaps to the last sample. It also moves the zoom focal point, range handles and other overlays that use `_plotInsets` onto the drawn plot. The range-handle test pinned the old 48px and is updated.

### Surface lead-in reads as 0:00
The t=0 surface vertex before the first sample has no profile index, so `onPointSelected` resolved it to the first sample. A new `onTimeSelected(int? seconds)` callback reports the time under the cursor, 0 on the lead-in, from both fl_chart and the fallback. The fullscreen page seeks playback with it. The other `onPointSelected` callers track a sample index and are unchanged.

## Tests
- `profile_transport_controls_test.dart`: taps at 25% and 75% of the minimap seek to that fraction of the dive.
- New `dive_profile_chart_hover_selection_test.dart`: one report per hover move over the plot; hovering the depth-axis gutter and the lead-in selects time 0; hovering at the right edge selects the last sample. All three fail against the previous chart, and mutation checks (no border inset, no lead-in flag, no fl_chart ownership) each fail the matching test.
- `fullscreen_profile_page_test.dart`: a chart selection at time 0 seeks playback to 00:00.
- `test/features/dive_log/presentation` and the dashboard profile preview tests pass; `flutter analyze` is clean.

author: alexjba
body:
Part of logos-fleet/logos-workspace#235.

`ShellCallDriver` waited 60 000 ms for every call, which was never a fact about calls. A RAILGUN private send is 154 s on an iPad Air 13-inch simulator and 239 s on a physical iPad Air 4, so the run that SUCCEEDED printed `CALL FAILED ... timed out after 60000ms` while the module went on to finish 94 s later — the verdict line saying the opposite of the console line.

- `--call-timeout <ms>` is parsed by `ModuleCallScript` and carried on each `ModuleCall`. It covers the calls **after** it rather than the whole line, so one long operation does not make a module that is simply not answering take four minutes to say so, and a later `--call-timeout` narrows it again.
- A value that is not a positive number is refused and changes nothing (0 is refused with the rest: a budget of nothing is not a shorter wait).
- A call that runs out of budget now prints that it is **STILL RUNNING** and names the flag — a timeout here is this waiter leaving, not a failure.
- Follow-up commit: the default call budget (60 000) is written down once at namespace scope instead of twice, no behaviour change.

Files: `mobile/appmanager/ModuleCallScript.{h,cpp}`, `mobile/basecamp-shell/src/ShellCallDriver.{h,cpp}`, `mobile/basecamp-shell/README.md`, `tests/module_call_script_test.cpp`.

Verified in the implementer and reviewer sandboxes; no builds were run in the landing phase.

author: cybershape
body:
## Summary
When executing shell commands on Windows, check for `C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe` first before falling back to `cmd.exe /C`.

## Why a static Git Bash path
1. **Agent expectations**: The `bash` tool description does not differentiate platforms, so agents assume a bash environment and generate bash commands/scripts.
2. **Avoiding WSL hijack from PATH**: Searching `PATH` for `bash.exe` on Windows 10/11 frequently resolves `C:\Windows\System32\bash.exe` (WSL launcher). Running commands through WSL executes in an isolated Linux container with different paths (`/mnt/c/...`) and environments, or fails if no WSL distro is installed.
3. **Safe fallback**: If Git Bash is not present at the standard installation path, execution gracefully falls back to the existing `cmd.exe /C` logic.

author: adhanaaan
body:
Follow-up to #157. One change, to `/clinic-signup-id` only.

## What changed

The summary paragraph under the hero is gone. The notice it pointed at is now named and linked inside the required tickbox itself, in both languages:

- **English** — "…and to that data being transferred outside the Republic of Indonesia, **as set out in the** _Personal Data Protection Notice_."
- **Indonesian** — "…serta menyetujui pengiriman data tersebut ke luar wilayah Republik Indonesia, **sebagaimana dijelaskan dalam** _Pemberitahuan Pelindungan Data Pribadi_."

The reference now sits in the sentence being consented to rather than in a block beside it, which is where a reader looking for it would expect it and is one less thing to scroll past. Art. 21 is satisfied by the disclosure being reachable at the moment of consent, not by it being printed underneath: each tickbox still states its own purpose, and the notice is one tap from the sentence that invokes it.

This also fixes a reference that #157 left dangling — the tickbox still ended "as described below" / "sebagaimana dijelaskan di bawah", pointing at the block that PR had already reduced to a summary.

## The one risk worth reviewing

The link now sits inside the tickbox's own `<label>`, and a click on a label normally activates its checkbox. That would silently record **a consent nobody gave**.

The HTML spec says a label must not forward activation from an interactive descendant such as an anchor, and browsers honour it, so this is correct by default — but there is a `stopPropagation` on the anchor as well, because the failure mode here is a false consent record rather than a cosmetic glitch.

Verified in Chromium, in both languages: clicking the link opens the notice in a new tab, the checkbox stays unticked, the typed name and email survive, and the checkbox still ticks normally afterwards.

## Note

The "Consent version" line went with the paragraph. It is still displayed on the notice page and still written to `consent_version` on every row, so the audit trail is unchanged — happy to put it back at the point of consent if that is preferred.

## Testing

- `tsc --noEmit` and `next build` clean on the rebased base; all `/clinic-signup-id` routes emit.
- Browser run of both languages asserting: link click does not tick the box, box still checkable, form contents preserved, and the old section absent from the DOM.

## Still outstanding

Unchanged from #156 and #157, all three surfacing on the notice page:

- `GMS_PDP_CONTACT_EMAIL` (`src/utils/liteOne.ts`) — empty. Art. 21 rights need an address to be exercised at.
- `GMS_PRIVACY_POLICY_URL` — empty, so the policy's name renders as plain text rather than a link.
- `CLINIC_SIGNUP_ID_RETENTION_MONTHS` — 24 months, an assumption rather than a decision from whoever owns the data policy.

body:
## What this does

The `non-null` and `pointer-live` obligations share one discharge function, which reports `present("Nullability guard code was detected")` for the pointer-live slot. A null check proves non-nullness, not that the allocation is live, large enough, aligned, or valid — so a correct guard observation produces a discharged-looking liveness slot and routes the reviewer as though only witness paperwork remains.

**Fix:** split the dispatch. `non-null` keeps nullability semantics unchanged; `pointer-live` keeps genuine same-origin Vec/Box evidence and otherwise reports missing, with a null-only guard retained as a named supporting fact (`supports non-nullness only; pointer liveness remains unresolved`) instead of a discharge. No new evidence model: the binary slot plus summary carries the weaker fact. No class changes in the fixtures.
