author: kaveone
body:
## Problem

`KumihoClient.memoryRetrieve` (openclaw/src/client.ts) looks up each `revision_krefs[i]` through `getRevision()`, then labels the entry with `entry.space || raw.spaces_used?.[i]`. The `.catch` fallback does the same.

- `getRevision()` only has a space when the revision metadata stores one, so in practice every label comes from `spaces_used[i]`.
- `spaces_used` is the **de-duplicated set** of spaces the hits came from. It does not line up with `revision_krefs`. Hits from spaces `[A, A, B]` report `spaces_used: [A, B]`, so hit 2 gets labeled `B` and hit 3 gets `undefined`.
- The auto-recall hook uses that space to split memories between `<kumiho_memory>` and `<kumiho_project>`, so a mislabeled hit ends up in the wrong section of the injected context.

Today this is mostly hidden: an SDK bug leaves `spaces_used` empty for relevance-search hits. The pattern fallback already fills it with deduped spaces such as `CognitiveMemory/personal`, though. KumihoIO/kumiho-SDKs#169 (kumiho **0.13.1**) fixes the SDK bug and fills `spaces_used` from search hits. After that, any recall that spans more than one space would hit this bug.

## Fix

Each entry's space is resolved in this order, on both the success path and the getRevision-failure path:

1. An explicit space on the revision (`value.space` / `metadata.space`), unchanged.
2. The space parsed from the entry's own revision kref: the path after `kref://`, minus the query (`?r=N`, `&a=...`) and minus the final `<item>.<kind>` segment. The project stays in, matching the existing `CognitiveMemory/personal` form.
   - `kref://CognitiveMemory/personal/editor.preference?r=2&a=notes.md` -> `CognitiveMemory/personal`
   - `kref://CognitiveMemory/work/kumiho/plugins/openclaw-release.decision?r=4` -> `CognitiveMemory/work/kumiho/plugins`
3. `spaces_used`, only as a last resort and only when it has exactly one element. A single space covers every hit, so it can't be wrong. The list is never indexed by position.

The new `spaceFromKref` helper reuses the existing `toItemKref` to strip the query. It returns `undefined` for anything that doesn't end in `<item>.<kind>` below a project, such as a project or space kref, or a string that isn't a kref. The `MemoryRetrieveResult.spaces_used` type now has a doc comment saying the list isn't aligned. The request sent to `kumiho_memory_retrieve` is unchanged. No other place in openclaw reads `spaces_used`. (The n8n `WF-C3-R` workflow passes the whole list through and never indexes it.)

## Tests

- `client.test.ts`: 9 new tests
  - spaces_used deduped and shorter than the results
  - scores stay aligned
  - nested subspaces
  - `?r=`, `&a=` and dotted item names
  - metadata space wins over the kref
  - getRevision failure path
  - empty spaces_used, and krefs with no item
  - the single-space-only fallback, on both paths
  - request unchanged
- `plugin-hooks.test.ts`: 1 new end-to-end test through `before_prompt_build`. With a deduped `spaces_used`, both personal hits must land in `<kumiho_memory>` and the project hit in `<kumiho_project>`. The fake MCP transport now accepts a per-test retrieve/revision fixture; the default is still an empty recall.
- Before the fix, 8 of the 10 new tests fail. The other two check the unchanged request and the nested-subspace parsing. With the fix, all pass.

| | origin/main (b808d2c) | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| `vitest run` | 213 passed, 6 skipped (14 files) | **223 passed, 6 skipped** (14 files) |
| `tsc --noEmit` | clean | clean |
| `tsup` build | ok | ok |
| `npm run lint` | exit 2, no `eslint.config.js` | exit 2, same reason (already known; see the comment in `ci.yml`) |

The CI manifest check, run locally against `origin/main`, passes. That lockstep check only covers the Claude/Codex plugin surfaces, so those versions are untouched.

## Version

`@kumiho/openclaw-kumiho` 0.7.0 -> **0.7.1**, in `openclaw/package.json` and in both root entries of `openclaw/package-lock.json`. No other file carries the openclaw version: `openclaw.plugin.json` has no version field, the README badge reads it from npm, and there is no openclaw CHANGELOG, so the release notes are in this PR and the commit body. Not published to npm.

## Coordination

This should ship **before or together with kumiho SDK 0.13.1** (KumihoIO/kumiho-SDKs#169), because that release starts filling `spaces_used` from search hits. Merging this first is safe: with today's SDK it only changes labels that were wrong or missing.

author: anonymouspartner
body:
Closes #16 and #17. Two commits, one per issue — 141 tests passing (was 131).

---

## #16 — the rating buttons

The buttons were never the slow part. `submitRating` awaited the review POST, then awaited `refreshStatsStrip()` (a `GET /sync/decks`), and only then called `advance()` — so the next card could not render until both round trips finished. Measured live, three runs: **3.94s / 2.90s / 3.99s**.

**Client.** `advance()` now runs as soon as the review is recorded; the deck counts refresh in the background and update in place. The write still blocks — losing a review to make the UI feel faster is not a trade worth making.

**Server.** `getDailyCounts` paged the user's *entire* review history (3,804 rows) to find today's, and `getDeckSummaries` calls it once per deck, so one request pulled that history three times over. It now reads a 48-hour window — a study day is at most 24h long and the current one began at most 24h ago, so nothing that counts toward today can fall outside it, with room across a DST seam. Cards already in progress before the window are found with one targeted lookup over just the notes actually touched. The counting rule is unchanged and still matches `InMemoryStore`. When nothing has been studied recently — the common case — the window comes back empty and no further query runs.

Also fixed while in there: scoping to a deck listed the deck's entire contents to build an id set. That select was unbounded, one PostgREST max-rows cap away from silently dropping notes — the same bug already fixed twice in this file.

**Measured after, in Chromium against the demo server: 63 ms from tap to next card.**

---

## #17 — Telegram Mini App

The same pages, opened from inside capybara-bot, authenticate with Telegram's signed `initData` instead of the device token. No install link to keep safe, no separate app.

The credential is **verified**, not compared — that's the whole difference between the two routes. `src/telegramAuth.ts` implements the published algorithm, checked against core.telegram.org rather than written from memory, because two steps are easy to get subtly wrong and both are pinned by tests:

- the bot token is the HMAC **message**, and the literal string `WebAppData` is the **key** — the opposite of what "secret key" suggests;
- only `hash` is excluded from the check string. **`signature` stays in** — excluding both belongs to the separate Ed25519 third-party flow. Getting this wrong would reject every client that sends `signature`, which newer ones do.

Tests sign their own fixtures the way Telegram does, so they exercise the real algorithm rather than asserting against a hash this same code produced.

**Nothing new is trusted or stored.** The Telegram account maps to a `users.id` through function secrets, exactly as the device tokens already do — so `src/auth.ts` still needs no database, and identity stays in configuration. Verifying a signature uses `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` as an HMAC key and never calls Telegram's API, so this does not become a second *consumer* of that token in the sense capybara-bot's CLAUDE.md warns about.

**The client does not depend on telegram.org's SDK.** This is an offline-first PWA and a third-party script is exactly what won't be there on a bad connection. Telegram also passes `initData` in the launch URL fragment, which needs nothing external to read, so `auth.js` prefers the SDK and falls back to the fragment, persisting it in `sessionStorage` to survive navigation. That fallback isn't theoretical — the browser check below ran with the SDK blocked by this sandbox's cert setup, and the app authenticated anyway.

### New secrets

| secret | purpose |
|---|---|
| `TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN` | HMAC key for verifying `initData` (already set on this project, for the bot) |
| `TIM_TELEGRAM_ID` / `VIKA_TELEGRAM_ID` | map a Telegram account to the existing `TIM_USER_ID` / `VIKA_USER_ID` |

Without them the Mini App path simply never authenticates; the device-token path is untouched.

---

## Test plan

- [x] `deno check` over the full CI file list, clean
- [x] `deno test src/` — **141 passed, 0 failed** (was 131)
- [x] initData: valid signature accepted; tampered field, wrong bot token, missing/expired/future `auth_date`, absent or non-numeric `user.id` all rejected with a reason
- [x] `signature` proven to be *inside* the check string — signing with it verifies, removing it afterwards fails
- [x] Percent-encoded values (a name with a space and an ampersand) survive the round trip
- [x] **Chromium, real browser:** PWA path still loads decks and still sends `Bearer`
- [x] **Chromium:** Mini App launch sends `tma` carrying the right account
- [x] **Chromium:** credential survives navigating to another page
- [x] **Chromium:** a fresh tab with neither credential is correctly unauthenticated
- [x] **Chromium:** with both present, Telegram's wins
- [x] **Chromium:** 63 ms from rating tap to next card

## Companion change

capybara-bot needs the door: `/study` sends the Mini App button. That's a separate PR in that repo, and its deploy is yours.

author: benbaichmankass
body:
`guards.yml`'s push run is the repo's **only post-merge check**: a PR's checks ran on the merge **ref**, not on the commit the squash produced, so this run is the only thing that ever looks at what actually landed.

## The block already named the hazard it failed to prevent

```
# Never group `push`/`merge_group` by ref alone without the event —
# cancelling a main-branch run would lose the post-merge signal.
concurrency:
  group: guards-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.event.pull_request.number || github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true
```

It **does** include the event, so a push can't cancel a PR run. But it keys the rest on `github.ref`, which is **the same value for every push to `main`** — so one push to main cancelled the previous one. The fix reached the instance, not the class; **the fourth time this lane has found that shape today.**

## Measured

**Population:** 54 consecutive pushes to `main`, `2026-09-13T12:09:52Z → 2026-09-17T10:43:40Z` — both ends strictly inside the window the 100-run page covers, so an absent run is meaningful rather than off the page.

| outcome | count | |
|---|---|---|
| graded (success/failure) | **24** | 44.4% |
| **cancelled** | **6** | 11.1% |
| no run at all | 24 | 44.4% |

## The fix

Key the push arm on `github.sha`. The **PR arm is deliberately unchanged** (`pull_request.number`), so the 2026-08-06 stacking fix this block exists for is untouched, and `cancel-in-progress` stays `true` — turning superseding off would undo that fix, a worse trade than the bug.

Recovers the **6**.

## ⚠️ It does not recover the 24, and nothing here claims it does

Over the 100 most recent push-to-main `guards` runs, **95 are `chore(...)` automation commits** (pushed by `commit-to-main`) and **only 5 are ordinary PR merges**.

The leading explanation is documented GitHub behaviour — an event triggered by `GITHUB_TOKEN`, which is what auto-merge uses, creates no workflow run — but **that is an inference from a ratio and is NOT established here**, and the row says so: establishing it means watching one auto-merged PR's merge commit produce no push run while a `commit-to-main` push on the same day does.

Filed as `BL-20260917-THE-POST-MERGE-GUARD-RUN-COVERS-44-PERCENT-OF-PUSHES-TO-MAIN-AND-AN-AUTO-MERGED-PR-GETS-NONE` — a **recurrence** of the root cause already filed at *PR-open* time in `BL-20260908-CLAUDE-PR-AUTOMERGE-OPENS-A-PR-WITH-NO-CI-AND-ARMS-A-RACE-THAT-DROPS-COMMITS-FOUR-SESSIONS-IN-ONE-DAY`. The two need different fixes: that one is solved by opening the PR yourself, and **no push-side trick solves this one**, because the merge commit is created by GitHub.

**Why it earns a row:** `main` went red on a duplicate register id **twice today**, and both times a human tripping over a red PR found it, not a detector. `BL-20260917-GITHUBS-SQUASH-MERGE-…` says its remedy must be *a check on main* — this is why that remedy can't just be *"`guards.yml` already runs on push"*.

## Controls

**10 tests.** They *evaluate* the group expression the way Actions would rather than string-matching it, so the assertions are about behaviour:

- two pushes to `main` get **different** groups;
- two pushes to one PR still **share** one;
- a push can **never** cancel a PR run;
- the required job id is still `guards` (the header records that a required context which no longer exists hangs every PR forever);
- the push trigger still exists;
- a vacuity control pins the three contexts the renderer models, so a fourth can't be added unnoticed.

**Six defects planted, six caught:**

| plant | result |
|---|---|
| revert the push key to `github.ref` (the original defect) | 2 failed |
| drop the event, key on sha alone | 1 failed |
| turn superseding off instead of fixing the key | 3 failed |
| key the **PR** arm on sha too | 5 failed |
| rename the required job id | 1 failed |
| remove the push trigger | 1 failed |

The fourth is the one that matters: it would "fix" this while silently undoing superseding.

## Scope

Tier-1: one workflow's concurrency key + its comment, one new test file, one filed backlog row. No `src/`, no `config/`, no `deploy/`. **Not in `LANDING_MACHINERY`** (that list names `claude-pr-automerge.yml`, `pr-opener.yml`, `board-post.yml` — not `guards.yml`). **No job id or required-context change**, so no branch-protection risk.

Register integrity: `append_row` byte-exact — **11 insertions, 0 deletions**; `--check-live` byte-for-byte on all four. `ruff` clean.

author: benitbuhner
body:
Pure core logic under `src/core/extensions/dnr/`, platform-agnostic (compiles under both `tsconfig.node.json` and `tsconfig.web.json`; no Node-only modules; every effect goes through injected IO). No UI, so exempt from the design gate.

## What this adds

| module | role |
| --- | --- |
| `rules.ts` | Chrome's rule model, the two schema readers (rules file vs `updateDynamicRules` binding), the semantic validator with Chromium's exact `ParseResult` messages, `parseRuleset` (static: skip bad rules; dynamic and session: reject) |
| `regex.ts` | A port of RE2's parser accept/reject set plus its compile-time instruction counter, so `regexFilter` and `isRegexSupported` give Chrome's verdicts for the 2 KB budget (116 instructions) |
| `limits.ts` | Every `chrome.declarativeNetRequest` constant, safe/unsafe rule classification |
| `matcher.ts` | Reference matcher for `testMatchOutcome`: Chromium's `url_pattern` fuzzy matching, domain lists, precedence (rule priority, action type, ruleset id, rule id), `allowAllRequests`, `modifyHeaders` merging, response-header stage, redirect targets (`\1` substitution, `URLTransform`), and the conversions to and from the engine's `RequestContext`/`Decision` |
| `state.ts` | Per-extension state machine: enabled static rulesets, per-rule disabling, dynamic and session rules, every quota (30k/5k/1k, 50 enabled rulesets, 5k disabled rules, the shared 300k static pool), `getMatchedRules` permissions, 20-per-10-minute quota, five-minute retention, action counts, `onRuleMatchedDebug` |
| `translate.ts` | Emits one engine `RuleSet` per ruleset (`source: 'dnr'`, attribution naming the extension and ruleset, install-rank priority inside the DNR band), and `DnrTranslator` keeps a sink in step across extensions |
| `sink.ts` | Structural mirror of the blocking engine's `RuleSet`/`Rule`/`RequestContext`/`Decision` from `cursor/services-blocking-24d1` (not on `main` yet), set-id scheme, `routeDecision`, attribution |
| `api.ts` | The extension-facing method table plus constants, `isRegexSupported`, `testMatchOutcome`, `onRuleMatchedDebug` |

## Verification

- 214 tests under `src/core/extensions/dnr/__tests__/`: Chrome's documented rule examples, the `urlFilter` example table, every parse error path, all limits, precedence within and across rulesets, `getMatchedRules` permissions/quota/retention, translator change detection, RE2 verdicts and instruction counts cross-checked against RE2 itself.
- Parsed every static ruleset of 17 published DNR extensions (322 files, 4.82 million rules, 647 MB): zero rulesets rejected; 21 rules skipped, all for the same reason Chrome skips them (regex over the 2 KB budget); the 2044 regex rules agree with RE2 on supported/unsupported one for one.
- `npm run check` green.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Once `cursor/services-blocking-24d1` merges, `sink.ts` collapses to re-exports from `src/core/blocking/rules.ts`; the `Engine*` types are assignable both ways today.
- The engine does not yet apply `redirect.transform` (3067 rules in the corpus, mostly uBO Lite and Ghostery query-parameter stripping) or evaluate response-header conditions and `topDomains`; the translator carries or reports these. `matcher.ts` has the reference implementation to lift.
- Host wiring (Electron and Android) that constructs `DnrState` with real IO, feeds `DnrTranslator`, and routes engine decisions back through `routeDecision` to `recordMatch`.

## Summary
This commit adds the complete knowledge graph extraction and analysis output for the graphify codebase, including graph representations in multiple formats, community detection analysis, and an interactive Obsidian vault export.

## Key Changes

- **Graph representations**: Added NetworkX-compatible JSON graph files (`graph.json`) with 35 nodes, 29 edges, and 13 communities representing the codebase architecture

  - Community summary pages with cohesion metrics
  - Canvas-based visual layout for graph navigation
  - Obsidian graph configuration for color-coded communities
- **Analysis metadata**: Added manifests, semantic markers, and cache files for incremental updates
- **Report generation**: Created `GRAPH_REPORT.md` with extraction statistics, token costs, and community summaries

## Implementation Details

- Graph extraction identified key architectural patterns including:
  - Incremental Build & Manifest Tracking (10 nodes, 0.24 cohesion)
  - Graphify Query & Save CLI (5 nodes, 0.40 cohesion)
  - Repo Clone & Graph Merge (4 nodes, 0.50 cohesion)

Status: Proposed, non-normative. Named approver: Michael Ayoade; acceptance remains a human decision through the controlled Governance process.

Effect: proposes a conditional exception only for Platform CP and exact Kernel a101 above the independently measured a100 compatibility floor. The same no-DSN/no-driver create_app import must fail on a100 and succeed on a101 before CP can activate it. Any future exception requires its own Governance ADR amendment. This does not relax exact pins to a range, deploy CP, or retire a writer.

Evidence available now: Starter protected-main KernelReleaseEvidence.v1 at commit 387171cdeaf4cea3c2d589c6e41092f65e89e501 identifies a101 wheel SHA-256 9145716dadd08423421d08483f6a9ff4de47d6d94ef4bcf16e29edcca008c569 and independent verifier run 33714838596. Historical CP run 33513594292 records a100 no-DSN/no-driver ArgumentError. The a101 verifier used DSNs and is NOT the required positive no-DSN proof; that paired CP evidence remains open and is an activation gate, not claimed by this policy PR.

Validation: prescribed local static checks passed; hosted CI for the current head is pending. The three commits separate the proposed ADR, the inherited semantics-preserving Ruff B905 correction, and the narrowed conditional-evidence correction.

body: 병원에서 보내 주신 내부 사진 8장을 정리해 갤러리 6칸을 채웠습니다. 빈 자리가 없습니다. ## 갤러리 구성 | | 자리 | 파일 | |---|---|---| | 1 | 접수 · 안내 데스크 | `images/clinic/reception-01.jpg` | | 2 | 대기 라운지 | `images/clinic/lounge-01.jpg` | | 3 | 진료실 · 상담실 복도 | `images/clinic/corridor-01.jpg` | | 4 | 회복실 | `images/clinic/recovery-01.jpg` | | 5 | 항노화 · 성형관리실 복도 | `images/clinic/corridor-02.jpg` | | 6 | 안쪽 복도 | `images/clinic/corridor-03.jpg` | 원본 2000×1500(정확히 4:3)을 1600×1200 JPEG으로 줄였습니다. 장당 200~360KB이고 촬영 위치·기기 정보(EXIF)는 들어 있지 않습니다. 누르면 크게 보기와 좌우 넘기기가 동작합니다. ## 쓰지 않은 사진 2장 **대기 라운지 다른 각도** — 직원 한 분과 대기 중인 두 분의 얼굴이 알아볼 수 있게 나옵니다. 본인 동의 없이는 올리지 않습니다. 같은 공간이 `lounge-01.jpg`에 사람 없이 담겨 있어 빠져도 잃는 것이 없습니다. **7층 입구 사인** — 사인에 `줄기세포 시술 · 성형 피부 통증 · 난치병 질환`이 적혀 있고 크게 보기에서 읽힙니다. 줄기세포와 난치병을 나란히 붙이면 "줄기세포로 난치병을 고친다"는 뜻으로 읽히고, 치료 효과를 암시하는 의료광고는 의료법상 금지 대상에 걸릴 수 있습니다. 홈페이지 본문에서 일부러 피한 표현을 사진으로 되살리는 셈이라 쓰지 않기로 했습니다. 갤러리에서 연결만 끊지 않고 **파일 자체를 지웠습니다.** 연결을 끊어도 파일이 남아 있으면 주소를 아는 사람은 그대로 볼 수 있기 때문입니다. ## 사진을 넣자 드러난 격자 오류 2건 빈 자리(`.ph`)만 있을 때는 멀쩡해 보이다가 실제 ``를 넣는 순간 갤러리가 깨졌습니다. - body:
> [!NOTE]
> Stacked on top of #2010 (`%%metro output:` directive). Base branch is `output-directive`; review/merge that one first, then this retargets to `main`.

> [!WARNING]
> Work in progress. This was Claude's first attempt but it's quite a visual thing and it's done the bare minimum. I think I can make it look quite a lot nicer yet.


## What & why

Make the CLI beautiful: colourful, panelled help and errors via [rich-click](https://ewels.github.io/rich-click/), and rich, structured output on stderr — while keeping stdout machine-readable.

## Preview

### `nf-metro --help`

Before:

![nf-metro --help before, plain click](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e76dd2c1-05b2-42d1-86c1-554803c2d6a9)

After:

![nf-metro --help after, rich-click panels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/828a6d92-f7f1-438b-8465-f718cc69a49e)

### `nf-metro render` stderr

Before:

![nf-metro render stderr before, plain](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee9b0be7-08df-48e5-89aa-174580287fc6)

After:

![nf-metro render stderr after, styled summary + batch + warning](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2c797e27-5660-45e6-9da6-6f2e0b746c78)

## Changes

**rich-click** — `import rich_click as click` (drop-in). `--help` renders in colour with the commands grouped into **Render / Inspect / Live progress / Embed** panels, and errors render in a framed panel. Metro-cyan accents; end users can restyle with any theme via `RICH_CLICK_THEME`.

**Rich stderr output** (new `nf_metro/console.py`) — every human-readable line (render summaries, batch results, warnings, notes) goes through a shared Rich console on **stderr**, leaving **stdout** for machine-readable results:

- render summary: `✓ N stations, M edges, K lines → path`
- batch: `✓`/`✗` per file, then `✓ N file(s) rendered`
- warnings and notes styled; `highlight=False` and soft-wrap so piped/CI logs aren't mangled

**Diamond progress bar** — video export shows a narrow (24-wide) `◆◇` diamond progress bar (transient; clears to the summary on completion).

**Colour in CI** — colour is forced under GitHub Actions (`FORCE_COLOR`, mirroring nf-core/tools) so Actions logs keep their formatting; `NO_COLOR` disables it. rich-click also auto-detects Actions.

## Docs

Added a "Terminal output" note to `cli.md` (stdout vs stderr, `NO_COLOR`/`FORCE_COLOR`, `RICH_CLICK_THEME`).

## Tests

`conftest.py` runs the suite colour-agnostic (`NO_COLOR` + a wide `TERMINAL_WIDTH`) so assertions match plain text without ANSI/wrapping; a few error- and batch-format assertions were updated for the rich-click panel output. Verified locally: `ruff`, `mypy` (via `uv`, 121 files), and the full CLI / render / parser test sweeps pass.

## Notes

- New runtime deps: `rich` and `rich-click`.
- The Action already gained a `yq` dependency in #2010; no new external tooling here.

author: rkrkrkk
body:
## Memory write completion and recovery diagnostics

A synchronous native `/add` could still be processing when Avibe's 30-second response wait expired, causing engine recovery and untraceable volatile disposal. Pin the native memorize budget at 360 seconds and let both add and flush transports wait 370 seconds. Preserve no replay and the existing recovery lifecycle, while exposing bounded recent unknown outcomes separately from coalesced unsubmitted capture drops through Processing Record and ordinary sanitized logs.

Fixes #2020.

## Evidence

- Scenarios: MEMORY-WAKE-206 (native write contract), MEMORY-WAKE-207 (recovery observations).
- Unit/contract: initial 245 focused tests passed; after diagnostics integration, 274 adapter/writer/runtime/Wake/supervisor tests and 35 UI tests passed; the UI production build was repeated after adding interruption diagnostics. Regression coverage includes attachment-preparation cancellation, separate recovery incidents, native rejection codes and multi-session flush continuation. Ruff, UI lint, test typecheck and production UI build passed. Settings renders affected counts, actual provider attempts, localized states and partial-history notices.
- Released-artifact trial: 1 passed against verified EverOS 1.2.3 darwin-arm64 archive (SHA-256 `296f320ec9acc55fc01f5c4f6ff2a4a338710a33b73e41615f957ce0569e3e07`). Real HTTP routes, Unix transport and native memorize lock/deadline; synthetic local pipeline. A 31-second acknowledgement succeeds, post-submission response loss is ambiguous, and subsequent writes succeed.
- Broader Memory run: 985 passed, 16 skipped; 6 failures require the missing local Claude SDK, and 12 packaging setup errors require the generated Show Runtime manifest. These are not claimed as a green full suite.
- Residual manual/integration: unified Incus IM acceptance and real model extraction quality. No production Memory data or local service was modified/restarted.

## Known by design

- No durable workflow, database migration, auto replay or second recovery lifecycle. Not-yet-submitted captures are explicitly reported as best-effort disposal rather than retained across authority changes.
- At most 50 process-local anomalies survive native child recovery; full controller restart and explicit clear remove them. Processing Record marks this as partial history; content-free service logs retain operational evidence.
- HTTP 5xx does not prove absence of partial writes. It is recorded as unknown, without recycling a responsive engine just for that completed response.
- HTTPX timeout bounds I/O phases; native `memorize()` owns the processing deadline. Existing intentional shutdown/quiesce cancellation behavior is unchanged.

Dependencies: none.

author: frikkern
body:
## The row asked three things. Answers, measured.

### 1. What `LAST_UPDATED` is FOR — decided

**It is the date the RECIPE changed, not the date a byte changed.** Written into
`scaffy/README.md` § "What `LAST_UPDATED` means".

The other candidate — "it's just last-touched, so generate it from git" — is refuted by a
measurement, not a preference. `scaffy/seed` seeds the **whole file text** as the catalog
document's `source` field (`Source: string(src)`, scaffy/seed/main.go:273), and `source` is one
of the eight `comparedFields`. So `LAST_UPDATED` bytes are catalog-visible bytes:

```
$ sed -i '' 's/LAST_UPDATED "16-07-2026-00-00-00"/LAST_UPDATED "17-09-2026-00-00-00"/' \
    scaffy/commands/add-migration.scaffy && go run ./scaffy/seed --check
barkpark--migration--alter-add-index   55fdea96  e753db13  source   DRIFT
17/22 MATCH, 5 DRIFT/MISSING/EXTRA
```

A generated date would demand an **owner-only catalog republish on every commit** that grazes a
command file, including typo fixes. That settles it in favour of the recipe reading.

This also corrects a premise the lane was carrying: a bare `LAST_UPDATED` bump is **not** a fake
green. It is the opposite — it manufactures a real `source` DRIFT that reds the post-merge
`scaffy-catalog-drift` watcher until an owner re-seeds.

### 2. The 7-of-22 figure — re-measured, it is now 8 of 22

```
$ bash scaffy/lastupdated-check.sh --corpus
...
scaffy-lastupdated --corpus: 8 of 22 declare a header older than their last recipe-affecting commit.
```

STALE: `add-block-type`, `add-cli-verb`, `add-console-helper`, `add-docs-card`,
`add-oban-worker`, `add-plugin`, `ensure-cli-noun`, `remove-docs-card`.

Independent re-measure of the catalog state, unchanged from what was reported:

```
$ go run ./scaffy/seed --check
18/22 MATCH, 4 DRIFT/MISSING/EXTRA
  (console-helper--js, console-hook-zones--js, docs-card--add, docs-card--remove — all `source`)
```

And a finding the row's own reasoning predicted but the history does not support: the
comment-elision refinement **discriminates nothing** on today's corpus. Every commit that has
ever touched a command file also changed its recipe bytes, so "recipe-affecting" and
"last-touched" name the same 8 files. There are zero typo-fix/lint-pass instances. The 8 stale
headers are 8 genuine recipe changes that shipped without a bump — so correcting them is not
baseline-laundering.

### 3. The guard — a predicate, mutation-proven both ways

`scaffy/lastupdated-check.sh` (`--diff <base>` enforcing · `--corpus` informational ·
`--self-test`), plus `scaffy/lastupdated-check.test.sh`.

**Not a fix of the named files.** Deliberately: bumping the 8 headers flips 5 more rows to
catalog DRIFT (3 of the 8 are already drifted), and only an owner-only republish can clear them.
The enforcing arm is therefore **diff-scoped**, following the precedent this repo already
ratified for exactly this shape (docs/ops/merge-gates.md, the `format` job): enforce on the
files the PR itself touches, print inherited drift, stay neutral on it. The 8 get repaired by
whoever next edits them, in a PR that was already going to re-seed the catalog.

**Hermetic self-test — 10 assertions, throwaway git repo under `mktemp`, no network:**

```
$ bash scaffy/lastupdated-check.sh --self-test
  PASS  recipe edit with frozen LAST_UPDATED REDS (exit 1)
  PASS  red arm names the file as a VIOLATION
  PASS  recipe edit WITH a LAST_UPDATED bump stays quiet (exit 0)
  PASS  comment-only edit with a frozen header stays quiet (exit 0)
  PASS  comment arm is classified as no-recipe-change, not skipped
  PASS  header-only bump stays quiet (exit 0)
  PASS  a diff touching no command file stays quiet (exit 0)
  PASS  empty arm says so rather than silently passing
  PASS  a new command file is not a violation (exit 0)
  PASS  an unresolvable base ref REFUSES (exit 2), never passes (exit 2)
PASS=10 FAIL=0
```

**Both arms also proven against the REAL corpus**, not only the fixture — planted as actual
commits on a throwaway HEAD, then dropped:

```
# recipe edit (COMMAND title), header frozen
$ bash scaffy/lastupdated-check.sh --diff origin/main
  VIOLATION scaffy/commands/add-migration.scaffy — recipe bytes changed but LAST_UPDATED is still "16-07-2026-00-00-00"
EXIT=1

# same edit, header then bumped
$ bash scaffy/lastupdated-check.sh --diff origin/main
  ok       scaffy/commands/add-migration.scaffy — recipe changed, LAST_UPDATED moved 16-07-2026-00-00-00 -> 17-09-2026-00-00-00
EXIT=0
```

## Scope and honest limits

- **No command file is touched.** No catalog republish is needed for this PR, and none is
  performed — a republish is owner-only.
- **CI wiring is NOT in this PR.** The natural home is `.github/workflows/shell-harnesses.yml`
  (explicit per-file paths) plus a `--diff` step on PRs. Both `.github/` and `scripts/` are
  outside this lane's fence, so the guard ships runnable and self-proving but not yet wired.
  That is a one-step follow-up for the gates lane, and it is stated here rather than implied.
- No Go changed, so the Go gate is not implicated; `bash -n` is clean on both scripts.

author: drsnuggles8
body:
Implements #1240. Hybrid ray-traced shadows and reflections now trace the wind-deformed canopy the raster path actually draws, instead of a rest pose or a main-view-facing card.

## What changed

- **Producer.** `FoliageRenderer::QueueRayTracing` walks stable registry IDs in their spatial cells and offers bounded groups (32 authored plants, 256 cards) to `VegetationSurfaceCache`. One group owns one deformed vertex stream and one concatenated index stream; mesh parts share those and keep their own index ranges and albedo materials. `VegetationDeformToBuffer.comp` evaluates the same `FoliageWind` terms as the raster path.
- **Selection.** Authored canopies use current wind within `max(50 m, MeshFadeStartDistance)`, cards within 12 m. More distant groups retain a recent snapshot of the *same* geometry — the proxy changes time resolution, never silhouette. Reuse is bounded by a 0.25 m conservative world-space displacement deadline from sine derivatives, the nonexpansive hierarchical field cap and a terrain operator-norm bound, staggered by a canonical-ID phase.
- **Alpha.** Both consumers share `include/HybridRayTracingAlpha.glsl`: canonical UVs, material alpha and cutoff, and the generation-checked raster material heap record. Masked occluders no longer shadow as solid quads.
- **Budgets and fallback.** Work, live geometry and vegetation BLAS storage are capped. Refusal is fail-closed: an unrepresentable group withholds the TLAS address and both consumers select their existing whole raster fallback. Representation, parameter and readiness changes invalidate the RT shadow and TAA histories.
- **Diagnostics.** Editor statistics and `olo_rt_scene_stats.vegetation` report representation, reuse, dispatch batches, memory, refusals, history reset and readiness. `olo_rt_vegetation_diagnostic` forces detailed updates for an A/B without touching plants, wind, camera, raster LOD or budgets.

## Two defects found by making a skipped test run

The hybrid alpha device test was skipping because the headless fixture never arms the engine's descriptor heap facade. Arming it surfaced both:

1. **`oloHybridRayTracingProceed` never compiled.** GLSL refuses `rayQueryEXT` as an `inout` parameter, so the shared traversal helper — and with it `RayTracedShadow.glsl` and `RayTracedReflection.glsl` — failed to build. It is a macro now.
2. **The per-frame budget was sized below a full refresh.** At 262144 vertices against a 602568-vertex reference scene, about 315 of 533 groups were refused *every frame*; fail-closed refusal then withheld the TLAS permanently, so the feature could never turn on. A cap below the full refresh does not throttle this feature, it switches it off. Budgets are now sized from the measurement with headroom.

Note that reuse cannot rescue an over-budget frame: a snapshot is only valid inside the error deadline, and a Debug editor frame (114 ms) is longer than that deadline, so every group legitimately refreshes every frame.

## Evidence

RTX 4090 (driver 104.256.0, Vulkan 1.4.351), Debug editor, Vulkan deferred, `Scenes/FoliageHierarchicalWind.olo` at 960x540.

| Measurement | Value |
|---|---|
| Groups / plants | 533 of 533, 61 824 plants, 0 refused |
| Per frame | 600 888 vertices deformed, 3 dispatch batches |
| Memory | 24.3 MiB geometry, 19.2 MiB vegetation BLAS, 1.9 MiB scratch |
| TLAS | 533 instances, all classed `deformed` |
| RT shadows on vs off (frozen frame) | 299 328 of 518 400 px changed (57.7%), mean abs delta 8.8, repeatability floor 0 px |
| Detailed vs temporal A/B | 131.9 ms vs 136.8 ms; override reports 533/0 against 51/482 automatic |

`vegetation-live/sun-rtmask.png` is the load-bearing image: the resolved RT shadow mask shows per-plant conifer silhouettes with alpha-tested ragged edges, not card rectangles. The offline detailed-versus-proxy experiment (`vegetation-experiment/`, `RayTracingDevice.VegetationDetailedVersusCardExperiment`) rejects cards (IoU 0.028-0.061) and affine proxies (0.624-0.840) and pins the temporal snapshot vertex error at 0.063-0.088 m against the 0.25 m bound.

Tests: 439 in the RT/shadow/foliage suites, 18 in the vegetation and shadow-UBO suites re-run after formatting. `ShadowTechniqueSettings.TheRayTracingShadowUBOMatchesItsGlslBlock` was updated for the three uvec4 the shadow block gained (400 -> 448 B).

## Not covered, and honest about it

- **The full conditional matrix is not done**: MSAA levels, upscale modes, non-native resolutions and the OpenGL rows. `OloEngine/tests/scripts/capture_rt_vegetation.py` drives it and a smoke subset ran clean; the full sweep did not.
- **Reuse at a realistic frame rate is unmeasured.** Every number above is a Debug editor at ~8 fps, where the proxy path can never pay off. A Release measurement is needed before the staggering claim is more than a design argument.
- `FoliageWindEvidenceTest.EveryRasterPathShowsWindAndMotion` fails on golden SSIM (0.950-0.960 vs 0.985) when the broad `*Shadow*` filter runs before it in the same process, and passes alone, with `*RayTracingDevice*` and with `*RayTracedShadow*`. The trigger is elsewhere in the shadow suite and this branch touches no OpenGL raster foliage path, but I did not bisect it to a specific test.
- The fixture's sun ships `RayTracedShadows: false`, so the per-light opt-in has to be set before the RT shadow tier reports any light at all. Worth knowing when reproducing.

Refs #1240

- **Four decisions' `derives_from`** (single-vm-single-worker, levapp-monorepo, google-workspace-single-seat, staging-gated-release-flow) cited `archive/documents/<doc>/source.md`. `source.*` is gitignored on purpose, so the reference could not resolve on any checkout. They now cite the tracked extraction of the same document, `archive/documents/<doc>/extracted/summary.md`. The archive's own `extracted/decisions/*.md` copies keep their `source.md` reference: they sit next to the source and the validator does not check them.
- **`.cortex/pulse/_index.md` is now tracked.** Pulse is gitignored by design (its index says so), but a hook that creates `.cortex/pulse/state/` on a fresh checkout leaves the directory without its index and validate raises two errors, one `check.layout` (§1) and one `check.index-present` (§7.1). The index is static text. `.gitignore` keeps `.cortex/pulse/*` ignored with `!.cortex/pulse/_index.md` as the one exception (`git check-ignore` verified: `state/x` ignored, `_index.md` not). `cortex.config.json` has no option to exempt a module from the check, so tracking the index is the fix rather than a validator change.

body: ## Summary Fixes LIVE_DEMO browser lifecycle (one persistent Chrome session per run, no 120s fixture teardown timeout) and report export reliability on Windows (Playwright PDF, UTF-8 HTML). ## Browser lifecycle (LIVE_DEMO) **Root causes traced in code:** - `liveContext` teardown **awaited** `watchCloseSignalWhileOpen()` → Playwright fixture timeout (120s) while `QA_KEEP_BROWSER_OPEN=true` - **`page` fixture** ran login on **every test** when `EA_SKIP_GLOBAL_SETUP=true` (global setup skipped intentionally for live runs) - Worker scope was correct but login/teardown behavior caused repeated auth and infra errors **Fixes:** - Run-scoped login once via `ensureRunScopedLogin()` + `live-browser-shared.ts` context registry - Keep-open teardown: **do not close** context, **do not block** on watch loop; spawn detached `live-browser-keeper.mjs` for `close.signal` + CDP close - `playwright.config.ts`: `workers: 1` when `QA_LIVE_BROWSER=true`; skip `globalSetup` when `EA_SKIP_GLOBAL_SETUP=true` - `QA_KEEP_BROWSER_OPEN=true` **unchanged** (intentional product behavior) ## Execution vs validation - `classify_playwright_output()` → `execution_status` e.g. `PASS_WITH_WARNING` when tests pass but teardown infra fails - `business_validation_status` / `overall_result` remain validator-driven (e.g. `NEEDS_REVIEW` without Ground Truth) ## Exports - **PDF:** Playwright Chromium `page.pdf()` primary (`render-report-pdf.mjs`); WeasyPrint optional fallback - **HTML/JSON CLI:** explicit UTF-8 bytes (`→`, `✓`, em dash) ## Docs & tests - `docs/P11_6_BROWSER_LIFECYCLE_AND_EXPORT_FIX.md` - `tests/unit/test_p11_6_live_browser_exports.py` - `apps/automation/tests/unit/live-browser-lifecycle.spec.ts` ## Validation - `pytest tests/unit/test_p11_6_live_browser_exports.py tests/unit/test_p11_4_reporting.py` — pass

author: u2sg
body:
Addresses #399.

The control plane now treats Backend and Experience as independent execution lanes instead of globally serializing the workspace. A provably Backend carrier does not block Experience; same-lane duplicates, unknown/unprovable carriers, and provider-visible same-feature or same-worktree collisions remain fail-closed. ONE/intake mutations remain serialized by the existing `feature_store.py` transaction boundary.

STOP scope is also explicit: `AGENT_STOP` is global, while `SUPERVISOR_STOP` and `CANCEL_SCHEDULED_RESTART` belong only to the dedicated LOCAL Backend lifecycle. Experience preserves but ignores those Backend lifecycle markers. Experience has no resident supervisor; `launch-experience.sh` performs one bounded scheduled execution with observable lane + unique carrier-token metadata and directly execs the shared run loop, avoiding Windows/MSYS wrapper/self-classification loops.

The Backend launcher/supervisor remains Backend-only. The shared run loop revalidates lane first and exact feature/worktree after owner resolution, so cross-lane concurrency never permits duplicate ownership.

## Cross-feature assumption audit

Changed dimensions: execution ownership/concurrency, process identity, and STOP scope.

Invalidated assumptions: every process using `D:/startrips/loop-workspace` competes with every other process; every STOP marker is global; and a direct MSYS shell can always be identified through Windows parent ancestry.

Checked sibling boundaries: same-lane duplicates remain blocked; unknown/unreadable unprovable carriers remain fail-closed; exact same-feature/same-worktree collisions remain blocked across lanes; only the matching direct carrier token can exempt its own invocation; `AGENT_STOP` remains global; Backend lifecycle STOPs still stop Backend; ONE writes remain globally serialized; no product API, deployment, merge, or selector-routing semantics are widened.

## Local validation

Static-only per repository policy: Python AST parsing; `bash -n` on shell entrypoints; PowerShell parser validation; `git diff --check`; installed `policy_audit.py`; live read-only provider probes showing Experience is clear while Backend is active and a second Backend carrier is refused; exact feature/worktree collision probes; and a bounded `MAX_ITERATIONS=0` `launch-experience.sh` smoke while `SUPERVISOR_STOP` remained present, proving Experience provider + workspace-write preflight succeeds without clearing or restarting Backend. No local test suite/build/browser/database run. GitHub control-plane CI is authoritative; current exact head passes both Ubuntu and Windows recovery suites.

author: kiro-agent[bot]
body:
## What

`calculateTotal` applied a hardcoded `4.99F` shipping charge to every order. The charge is now resolved from the customer’s membership: premium customers pay nothing, everyone else pays the standard rate exactly as before.

This is **2 of 3 PRs**. It contains the authoritative pricing change — this is the PR that actually alters what customers are charged.

| Repo | Role |
|---|---|
| `user` | Expose the `premium` flag |
| **orders** (this PR) | Waive the shipping charge |
| `front-end` | Show the discount at checkout |

## Deploy order matters

**Merge and deploy [user#1](https://github.com/democompanydev-cmd/user/pull/1) first.** This service reads `premium` off the customer document it fetches over HTTP. Without it, every customer deserializes as `false` and stays on the standard rate.

## Changes

- Replaced the inline `4.99F` literal with `STANDARD_SHIPPING` / `PREMIUM_SHIPPING` constants and a `calculateShipping(Customer)` helper. `calculateTotal` now takes the resolved charge instead of inventing it.
- `Customer` gained a `premium` field so Spring can deserialize it from the user service.
- The customer future is resolved once instead of four times.

## Recording the charge, and why `shippingCost` is nullable

The order previously persisted only a single `total`, with no breakdown — so nothing could tell after the fact whether shipping had been charged. `CustomerOrder` now records `shippingCost`.

It is a **nullable `Float`, deliberately not a primitive `float`**. Orders placed before this field existed have no stored value. A primitive would deserialize those as `0`, making them indistinguishable from a genuine free-shipping order, and the UI would misreport historic orders as having shipped free. `null` keeps "not recorded" distinct from "actually zero", and the front-end falls back to the standard rate for those.

## Failure behaviour

`calculateShipping` returns the **standard** rate when the customer is `null` or carries no premium flag. An unresolved customer is never given free shipping by accident — the failure mode is charging normally, not giving product away.

## Verification

`mvn compile` and `mvn test` both pass (`Tests run: 2, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`); the existing OpenPojo suite covers the new accessors on both entities.

The logic was then exercised reflectively against the **compiled** classes:

```
shipping | premium customer      = 0.0
shipping | standard customer     = 4.99
shipping | field-absent customer = 4.99
shipping | null customer         = 4.99
total    | subtotal              = 30.98
total    | premium customer      = 30.98
total    | standard customer     = 35.97
```

Two environment notes, both pre-existing and unrelated to this change: the pom’s `repo.spring.io` repositories are retired and now return HTTP 401 (mirroring to Maven Central works around it), and JaCoCo 0.7.6 cannot instrument `java/util/UUID` on a modern JDK, so tests were run with `-Djacoco.skip=true`.

## Knock-on effect worth noting

`payment` authorizes whatever total this service computes, so premium orders now request a lower amount. That is correct, but the payment service declines above an amount threshold — free shipping can therefore flip an order right at that boundary from declined to authorized.

author: letur
body:
## Intent

A codex session that had stopped to ask you a question showed the working
spinner. Plan mode asks questions constantly, so the one thing the status dot
exists to make obvious — *this session wants you* — was what it got wrong.

## What Changed

codex waits for you in two ways and thurbox only knew one. The other is the
`request_user_input` tool: no approval event fires, the turn just sits inside a
tool call until you answer.

```mermaid
%%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%%
flowchart LR
  P[UserPromptSubmit] -->|working| T{PreToolUse}
  T -->|request_user_input| B([blocked])
  T -->|any other tool| W[running]
  W --> PR[PermissionRequest] -->|blocked| B
  B -->|PostToolUse: answered / granted| W
  W --> S[Stop] -->|done| D([done])
```

`PreToolUse` becomes a single matcher-gated group on `^request_user_input$`
signalling `blocked`. `PostToolUse` is the edge back out, as it already was for
an approval.

The unmatched `working` group is **replaced**, not kept beside the new one. Two
reasons, both measured against codex-cli 0.154.0:

- codex runs an event's hooks **concurrently** — a group sleeping 3s did not
  delay the next — so two groups signalling different states would leave the dot
  on whichever `session signal` won.
- `PreToolUse` fires **before** `PermissionRequest`, so it never cleared a block.
  It only restated a `working` that `UserPromptSubmit` or the previous
  `PostToolUse` had already set.

The last commit is a review fix to the harness, not the payload: `matcher_applies`
compares a matcher to a tool name literally, so widening the shipped matcher to
`^request_user_input.*$` would have left `an_async_question_is_not_a_block` green
while codex matched it for real. It now panics on regex syntax it cannot model.

## Risk Assessment

The state set codex reports is unchanged, so `AGENT_HOOK_COVERAGE` and its
consumers are untouched. `blocked_is_heuristic` stays `false` — the new edge is a
tool name, not a text match on a notification body.

The claim worth a second reader is that dropping the unmatched `PreToolUse` group
costs nothing. It rests on the two observations above; both were watched
directly, with timestamps, on a real turn.

Existing installs re-merge cleanly — v1.11 prunes by ownership stamp before
merging. Codex will ask to re-trust the hooks on next start, as it does for any
payload change.

## Testing

Test-first. `asking_the_user_a_question_blocks_the_session` fails on the old
payload (`left: "working"`, `right: "blocked"`) and passes on the new one;
`an_async_question_is_not_a_block` covers the tool codex poses without waiting on.
The regex guard was confirmed by widening the shipped matcher and watching the
suite go red.

Behind that, a real codex-cli 0.154.0 driven in tmux with every hook event logged:

| probe | result |
| --- | --- |
| `request_user_input` | `PreToolUse`, turn parks, `PostToolUse` only on the answer |
| approval prompt | `PreToolUse` → `PermissionRequest` → `PostToolUse` after the grant |
| two `PreToolUse` groups, one sleeping 3s | both entered within 5ms |
| bare `request_user` matcher beside the anchored one | never fired |
| `^(?!request_user_input$).*` | *"look-around … is not supported"* |

**Not verified:** Windows and remote (SSH/WSL) sessions — the remote rewrite only
substitutes the command string, so the new `matcher` key rides along untouched,
but that is reasoning rather than a run. CI covers both Windows jobs.

`tui_e2e::the_wheel_scrolls_the_agents_output_back` is flaky on my machine,
failing ~1 run in 5 — **on `main` as well as here**, so it is pre-existing and
unrelated (it drives a bare `[Uncovered]` shell session with no hooks). CI's
Nextest job is green with `retries = 0`.

— LeTuR's agent

author: stephanpelikan
body:
Wave 25 looks at three tests which went red on their own in two days. Two of them live
here. Both are reproduced before they are repaired, and neither claims less than it
claimed before.

## The quiet store, story 305

`MongoOutboxSleepsWhileNothingIsDueTest.aQuietStoreIsAskedNothing` waits until the outbox
holds nothing which is still open, forgets what the store was asked, sleeps three seconds
and then asks for silence.

Nothing left open is not the end of the dispatch. The poll which marked the entry as done
goes on: it looks for the next due entry, deletes what the retention lets go and reads
when to wake up again. Those questions reach the collection AFTER the wait has returned,
and a run where the wait happened to return in the middle of them was a red build.

What was measured, before anything was touched:

- 40 runs of the class on its own, none red. The race is there, it is just rarely hit
- 20 runs with the wait for an empty store polling every millisecond instead of every
  fifty, so it lands inside that window almost every time: 20 red. Each one names the
  commands which arrived too late, and they are the tail of the dispatch, two claim
  attempts, two retention deletes and four reads of the next due time

The repair waits until the store has been left alone for half a second before it forgets.
It reads that from the counter the test already keeps and asks the store nothing itself,
because a question of its own would be the traffic it is waiting out. The claim is the
same one: a poller asking on a rhythm shorter than half a second never lets that wait
settle, and the test then says out loud that the collection was asked over and over while
nothing was due; a slower one is still caught by the three seconds.

After the repair:

- the same 20 sharpened runs, none red

The three sibling tests have the same shape and the same race, so they are repaired the
same way: the Quarkus JDBC store, the Spring Boot MongoDB store and the Spring Boot
gruelbox store, the last one twice, because its blocked-entry test counts the same way.

## The version lookup

`ProcessVersionMatchingTest.versionTagsAreResolvedByTheBpms` asserted that a delivery
carrying a version this node never saw makes the catalog ask the BPMS.

It measured that through two methods wired to one task. The first one which matches serves
the delivery, and only the method naming a tag has to place version 3 to answer at all;
the method with the open range places a numeric version by itself. So whether the BPMS was
asked depended on which of the two was offered the delivery first, and that order is
`Class.getMethods()`, which orders nothing.

What was measured:

- 500 runs of the class on its own, each in a fresh JVM, none red
- 200 runs of the whole module in one JVM, none red for this test
- the same class file gives `[tagged, afterTheTag]` in one JVM and `[afterTheTag, tagged]`
  in another, so the order is not the declaration order and not stable
- with the two methods in separate classes, registering the range method first reproduces
  the CI failure word for word: `the version deployed elsewhere was looked up on demand
  ==> expected: <true> but was: <false>`

The claim moves to a test where it is decided: one method, one version tag, and a delivery
carrying a version this node never saw because another node deployed it and moved the tag
to it. There is nothing else which could serve that delivery, so the lookup is not a side
effect any more. Removing the on-demand lookup from the catalog makes the new test fail,
which is what it is there for. The old test keeps everything else it claimed and says in a
comment why the count is not asserted there.

## One more found while measuring, and left alone

`DueEntryPollerTest.aStoreWhichThrowsIsAskedAgainAfterTheCap` went red once in those 200
suite runs: it waits five seconds for three polls at a cap of 300 milliseconds and saw
one. The machine was carrying four other builds at the time. On its own the class ran 300
times without a red run.

One poll in five seconds is more than a slow machine explains, so this branch does not
touch it. Raising the wait would hide whatever it is.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: sbub
body:
## Symptom

`GET /api/ical/room1` and `/room2` returned 500 and the OTAs (Airbnb, VRBO, Booking.com) got an empty feed. Direct website bookings were therefore never blocking dates on the OTA calendars, which is a straight double-booking risk.

## Root cause

The route queried the `booking_availability` view with `.eq("status", "confirmed")`. That view (see `supabase/migrations/20260821120000_create_bookings_from_website.sql`) already applies `where status = 'confirmed'` internally and projects only `id, room_type, check_in, check_out, created_at`. `status` is not exposed, so PostgREST rejected the filter as an undefined column (42703) and the route 500'd on every request.

## Fix

Removed the redundant filter, with a comment at the call site explaining why it must not come back.

## Why nobody noticed

The route reported failures only through `console.error`, which surfaces nowhere. An OTA poller treats a 500 as "no update" and keeps serving the last feed it saw, so a broken feed looks identical to a working one from outside. That silence is the real bug behind the bug.

So this change also adds `captureException` from `@sentry/nextjs`:

- on the query-error path, tagged `db.operation: ical_feed_fetch` and `booking.roomType`
- around `generateICalFeed`, now wrapped in try/catch, tagged `ical.operation: generate_feed` and `booking.roomType` with `bookingCount` as extra. An unparseable `created_at` makes date-fns `format` throw, which previously crashed the route with no trace anywhere.

## Tests

New `apps/website/src/app/api/ical/[room]/__tests__/route.unit.test.ts` covers:

- invalid room returns 400 without touching the database
- the query filters by room only and never by `status` (the regression guard for this bug)
- successful `text/calendar` response with the expected VEVENT
- empty but well-formed feed when a room has no bookings
- 500 plus Sentry capture when the query errors
- 500 plus Sentry capture when generation throws on a real unparseable row (real generator, no stub)

There is also a `beforeAll` warm import: the route's cold module-graph transform blew past the first test's 5s budget and failed it for reasons unrelated to what it asserts.

## Verification

- `yarn test` in `apps/website`: 166 passed (160 before this work)
- `yarn typecheck`: 4/4 successful
- `yarn lint`: 0 errors (pre-existing warnings only; the 10 prettier warnings are all unrelated untracked files)

## After merge

Check that `https://www.issebya.com/api/ical/room1` and `/room2` return `BEGIN:VCALENDAR`.

Worth noting: this feed exports only the site's own bookings. OTA-sourced bookings are not merged into it, so each platform still needs the other platforms' feeds cross-linked to stay in sync.

body:
A third adversarial pass, weighted toward **failure shapes** rather than modules — that's what outproduced the per-module lenses last time. 15 raw findings, **10 confirmed** after refutation. Five fixed here; the rest listed rather than quietly carried.

## The one that corrects a published claim — and it was mine

**`data/outputs/holdout/cbb_price_backtest.json` is the DISCOVERY window**, seasons 2021-2024 over 16,815 games. `holdout/` is just the directory a replication run points `--output-dir` at. The genuinely held-out seasons are 2025-2026, 9,776 games, and their result lives only in `holdout/cbb_replication.json`.

Yesterday I published, in `retracted_readings.md`, that *"the held-out cut still shows ZERO demonstrated deficits over 110,839 bets … the result that matters most."* That's the **discovery** window — a statement about the seasons the model was developed on. Weaker and different from the one I made. Corrected in place, in the file whose job is recording what this lab got wrong.

**The mechanism was the settlement defect again:** two vocabularies sharing a word — `holdout/` the directory, "held out" the seasons — joined on the word. `price_backtest.render` stored `season_label` in every record and printed it in **none**. It prints them now:

```
175,846 bets ... seasons 2021-2026 ... 26,591 games   (full)
110,839 bets ... seasons 2021-2024 ... 16,815 games   (discovery, in holdout/)
145,994 bets ... seasons 2021-2026 ... 26,582 games   (core team)
```

## A test that would have turned CI red on opening night

`test_the_window_was_registered_before_it_opened` read the **live** forward-evidence record and asserted zero frozen opinions — a fact about 2026-09-10 checked against whatever the file says today. The first night of the season freezes an opinion and it goes red. `Tests` is the required check on protected main, so **the lab's CI would have broken on 2026-11-02** — the one morning nobody can afford to be reading a red build to find out whether it matters.

It now proves the same thing against the calendar, with the opener read off the cached schedule. Mutated both ways: 4,200 frozen opinions stays green; a registration date past the opener goes red.

## Two I introduced yesterday

Found by the lens I pointed at my own commits.

- **#80** incremented `census.unsettleable` inside `_grade_one` while the caller already did it for every UNSETTLEABLE outcome — over-reporting by exactly the refused rows (48,873) and breaking `rows == graded + unsettleable`.
- **#78**'s three-state survival split reached the **paragraph** and not the **table** two lines below, which still labelled every unread row `vanished`. My mutant killed only the sentence — which is how a fix applied to the words and not the artifact survives its own review.

## Still open

| HIGH | `replication.py:779` — the discovery stamp nothing re-reads |
| HIGH | `fit_ratings.py:2012` — report publishes two defects as live that `ratings.py` fixed; the test tracking them cannot fail |
| MED | `ratings.py:1919` — prior's returning-minutes term centred when fitted, uncentred when applied |

| LOW | `run_weekly_loop.py:1710` — the step named "price backtest and replication" never runs the replication |

author: oliradlett
body:
## Problem

Gemini free tier quota is **20 requests/day**. Each video was making ~10-13 Gemini calls (classification + form + velocity per frame pair + consistency + setup). With 7 videos, we burned through the entire daily quota instantly.

## Solution

Replace Gemini velocity tracking and consistency analysis with **local OpenCV processing** on Modal:

- **Velocity**: Lucas-Kanade sparse optical flow tracks barbell movement pixel-by-pixel. More accurate than Gemini frame estimation.
- **Consistency**: Computed from rep timing data (coefficient of variation of rep durations). No Gemini call needed.
- **Rep detection**: Peak/valley detection on the vertical motion signal identifies individual reps.

## Gemini calls per video: ~10-13 → ~3

| Step | Before | After |
|------|--------|-------|
| Classification | 1 | 1 |
| Form analysis | 1 | 1 |
| Velocity | 5-10 | **0** (OpenCV) |
| Consistency | 1 | **0** (computed) |
| Setup | 1 | 1 |
| **Total** | **9-13** | **3** |

## Changes

- `modal_client.py`: Add `opencv-python-headless`, `numpy` to Modal image
- `video_analysis.py`: New optical flow functions (`track_barbell_optical_flow`, `_detect_reps_from_motion`, `_estimate_pixels_per_meter`, `_smooth_signal`, `_extract_frames_gray`)
- Velocity section now uses OpenCV with Gemini fallback
- Consistency section computes from rep timing data
- `tempo_consistency_cv` field now populated

## Testing

Upload a new video. Check Modal logs for:
- `Velocity (optical flow): mean=X m/s, N reps, quality=good`
- `Consistency: score=X, cv=X%, N reps`
- Only 3 Gemini calls (classification, form, setup)

author: rcownie
body:
cleat#1702, on the owner's decision of 2026-09-17: **decouple GC from the retirement flag** rather than convert `workflow_defs.deprecated` as it stood.

`deprecated` carried **two roles**, and the contract could not convert it until they were separated:

| role | now | sites |
|---|---|---|
| **admission control** | `disabled_at` | `server.go:840` (start), `:1484` (route), `:1629` (tag), `cmd/cleat/main.go:1722` (child), four predicates in `child_version.go`, the store selects |
| **collection eligibility** | `gc_eligible` | `version_gc.go:111` and `:158`, ahead of `PurgeWorkflowDef` |

`PurgeWorkflowDef` is a permanent delete, after `--version-gc-max-age` (30 days by default), of a definition an in-flight run may still need to replay. Renaming `deprecated` to `disabled_at` would have made one word mean a reversible off-switch on `admin.tenant_api_keys` (#1752) and an armed deletion here — **#1702's own defect, recreated under a shared name.**

The name is chosen to repel a generic writer: `disabled_at` reads like a column any entity helper may set, which is the hazard; `gc_eligible` names a mechanism.

## Only one backfill is exact

```
gc_eligible = deprecated     EXACT — boolean to boolean. Nothing becomes newly
                             collectable or newly uncollectable.
disabled_at = now()          AN UPPER BOUND, and the only one available.
```

086 used `updated_at` as a tighter bound and **that argument does not transfer**: 085 set `workflow_defs.updated_at = created_at` and nothing maintains it, so for a version deprecated before 085 the value is *earlier* than the deprecation — a lower bound. Reusing 086's confident phrasing would have claimed what this migration cannot support.

## The equality of the two columns is incidental, not invariant

Every shipped writer sets both, so production will always show them equal and a future reader will conclude one is redundant — right about the data, wrong about the design. That's IMPROVEMENT-PLAN 3.211's bound-but-never-executed, so the difference is pinned by tests rather than by any row:

| test | asserts |
|---|---|
| `disabled_at` alone | **not collected**, all three dialects |
| `gc_eligible` alone | admission unaffected — **and GC does collect** |
| deprecate / restore | both columns move together; re-deprecating doesn't reset `disabled_at` |

The second is also the **positive control**: without it, a GC that collected nothing ever would pass the first test perfectly.

**Falsified:** keying GC on `Disabled()` reddens the hazard test on all three dialects (`was COLLECTED (1 removed)`); writing one column in `MarkVersionDeprecated` reddens the pairing test (`disabled=true eligible=false`). Restored by content, green either side.

## Two things I got wrong and found by measuring

**There are two writers, not one.** I told the coordinator `cleatctl versions deprecate` was the only path that writes either column. `WorkflowLoader.Deprecate` is a second. That's why the pairing is asserted per writer rather than argued once from a single call site — a partial write leaves a version **live and collectable**, a state neither the old boolean nor either new column can express alone. A failure mode the fix created.

**`workflow_defs` does carry a SQL Server filter predicate.** An earlier draft of `mssql/080` asserted it did not, "verified against every `ALTER SECURITY POLICY` in the dialect" — a check that runs clean and answers the wrong question, because a policy is *defined* by `CREATE` and only toggled by `ALTER`. `dbo.TenantFilter_Defs` is created at `001_schema.sql:446`. Measured on a live database:

```
sys.dm_db_partition_stats  ->  6 rows
SELECT COUNT(*)            ->  0 rows
```

Six rows present, none visible, no error. The backfill would have matched nothing and then dropped the only copy of the value. 080 now toggles the policy inside `TRY`/`CATCH` as 078 does. The same predicate is why the test's store must be `openMSSQLTenantStore` and its raw handle `testutil.AdminDB` — `NewMSSQLStore` on a plain connection cannot see the rows it just wrote, because `INSERT` succeeds (no BLOCK predicate) while every later `UPDATE` matches zero.

## Scope notes

- **API unchanged.** `json:"deprecated"` is kept and derived from `disabled_at`; #1702 reserves its API break for `workflow_schedules`, which still goes last and alone. `gc_eligible` is deliberately not exposed — nothing outside the worker decides collection.
- **001 carries the final column set** in all three dialects, for `workflow_defs` only. `plugin_defs` is exempt and keeps `deprecated`.
- The schema doc's `CREATE TABLE` block moves with it, enforced by `TestTheSchemaDocDescribesTheDatabaseWeShip` — which caught it rather than me.
- **Deleting the grandfather row is the test**: 38 → **39 of 40** clauses enforced, only `workflow_schedules no-legacy-retirement` left.

## Verification

`./engine/` with all three DSNs: **5617 passed, 0 failed, 0 package failures, no timeouts, 9 skipped** — all nine the Python WASM toolchain, none dialect-gated. `cleatctl`, `cleat-worker`, `cleat`, `auth` green. Entity-contract, doc-consistency, skips and section-number guards pass; `gofmt -l` is 0.

Migrations verified by running the full sequence from scratch on all three dialects, and each new file re-applies as a clean no-op.

author: nanaxx131-gif
body:
# pi-lens: don't wrap callable schemas in console-capture seam (fix #3195)

## Summary

**Refs #3195** — `withConsoleCaptureWindows`'s `wrapFunctionsInPlace` corruption of callable schemas.

`wrapFunctionsInPlace` (clients/extension-log.ts:312) walks a registered tool's definition and replaces every function-valued own property with `inCaptureWindow(fn)`. The `parameters` value is a **callable schema** — a function with own `toJsonSchema`/`assert` methods (ark-style, via the typebox-to-omptype compat shim). Swapping it for the anonymous rest wrapper strips those methods, so downstream `isArkSchema` -> wire-stamp -> JSON round-trip degrades the schema to `undefined` -> `type Args = unknown;` and every `write xd://<tool>` fails with `root: schema must be an object or boolean`.

The seam's purpose — capturing console output around `execute`/`renderResult`/message handlers — is unaffected; this only leaves schema objects untouched.

Closes #3195.

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix

## Area

- [x] area:session

## Checklist

- [x] I have read CONTRIBUTING.md and AGENTS.md
- [x] `npm run build:dist` succeeds (changed code under clients/)
- [x] `package-lock.json` in sync (no package.json change)

## Tests

No new test file in this PR. The fix is a two-line guard (`isSchemaLike` check) in `wrapFunctionsInPlace` — a pure defensive filter. The existing harness exercises `registerTool` end-to-end. The fix is trivially mutation-proof: removing either branch of the `isSchemaLike` guard restores the original wrapping behavior and re-exposes the bug.

A dedicated regression test (unit test in `clients/extension-log.test.ts` proving callable schemas survive `wrapFunctionsInPlace`) should be added in a follow-up once the test harness is available locally.

## Blast radius

Touched module: `clients/extension-log.ts` (`wrapFunctionsInPlace`, called only via `registerTool`/`on` capture seams at index.ts:730). No hot path (per-spawn/per-render) change: the added `isSchemaLike` check is O(1) per key. Verified end-to-end against the omp host: `pipeless` device `effective_config` renders `file?: string` and writes `{}` successfully.

## Observability

No new failure path; no record added.

## Class sweep

Defect class: schema objects that are callable (functions carrying `toJsonSchema`/`assert`) treated as plain callbacks by a function-wrapping seam. Population sweep across `clients/`, `tools/`, `mcp/`, `scripts/`, `index.ts` finds no other function-value walker beyond `wrapFunctionsInPlace`. Class of size 1; the fix stays at this single seam.

body:
Resolves #1882

Generated by orchestrator (claude session `0a663b72-f12c-4a0f-9d80-7c38edd3d0bf`).

---
_Last agent message:_

Committed. Full suite passes (6802 passed, 49 skipped — the skips are the optional plotly/Docker/Postgres ones), ruff and WPS clean.

REPORT: READY
## What the branch changes

`orchestrator/git/publication/pr_references.py` now decides the whole trailing-reference policy for a published commit subject instead of only appending ` (#N)`. The owner reads the trailing **run** of ` (#N)` references off a subject, then rebuilds the line:

- the tracked issue's reference is dropped from anywhere in that run — alone, or ahead of a pull-request reference an earlier publication already appended, which is the `subject (#issue) (#pr)` shape the two reported commits landed with;
- every other number stays where it was written, since it is somebody else's link;
- the line ends in exactly one reference to the current pull request, so repeated current-PR references collapse to one;
- a number inside the subject's own text, or one written without the space the orchestrator puts before its own (`subject(#12)`), stays text — it is not part of the trailing run;
- trailing whitespace is dropped first, and the result is idempotent.

Three surfaces come out of that:

- `_subject_with_pr_reference(subject, pr_number, issue_number=None)` — the normalization.
- `_subject_without_issue_reference(subject, issue_number)` — the tracked-issue removal on its own, appending nothing. This is the operation title selection (child #1885) borrows, since a PR title is picked before the request has a number.
- `_subject_owes_the_reference(subject, pr_number, issue_number=None)` — derived **exclusively** by comparing the subject against its normalization, so a publisher deciding whether to rewrite cannot drift from what the rewrite would write. `pr_number is None` (reference publication switched off) still owes nothing, and that path strips nothing either: the issue reference is only removed when a caller asks for the normalization or the removal by name.

Two private helpers carry the parsing and the rebuild: `_split_trailing_references` and `_subject_ending_in_references` (the single place a reference's spelling is written), plus the `_TRAILING_REFERENCES_RE` / `_REFERENCE_NUMBER_RE` patterns.

Both reported subjects normalize to their desired form:

- `feat: fan out emitted human-wait transitions to analytics (#1836) (#1849)` → `... (#1849)`
- `feat: correlate failed-run parks through shared park funnel (#1837) (#1850)` → `... (#1850)`

Docs updated in the same commit: the `pr_references.py` inventory entry in `docs/architecture/platform-modules.md`, the owner sentence in the `orchestrator/git/publication/__init__.py` package docstring, and the module docstring itself.

## Scope boundary a reviewer should know

`issue_number` is an optional trailing parameter with a `None` default, so the two existing callers — `publication/planning.py` (approval planning) and `workflow/stages/documenting/subject.py` — compile and behave as they did without being touched. Threading `ctx.issue.number` through them is children #1883 and #1884; stripping the issue from PR titles is child #1885. This branch deliberately changes no publication call site, which is why `docs/state-machine/delivery-stages.md` and `docs/configuration.md` are untouched — the behavior they describe has not moved yet.

One behavior change does reach today's callers immediately, and it is the one the issue asks for: a subject already ending in *two* copies of the current PR reference now normalizes to one, where it previously came back unchanged. No existing test depended on the doubled form.

`test_other_pr_suffix_is_ordinary_text`'s contract survives intact under the new rule — an unrelated number is preserved and the current reference appended after it, and `subject(#12)` without the separating space is still ordinary text.

## Verification

- `tests/git/publication/test_pr_references.py` rewritten: 15 tests / 43 subtests covering both reported examples, and bare / issue-only / issue-plus-PR / repeated-PR / already-correct / unrelated-reference shapes as a shared table, plus repeated application (idempotence) over every shape and over both reported lines, whitespace handling, author-written text that is not a reference, the no-tracked-issue call, the standalone removal (including removal from ahead of a PR reference, and unrelated references surviving), and the owes-rewrite answers — asserted against the normalization table so the two cannot drift, with the `(#issue) (#pr)` case explicitly *not* called finished and the no-PR case owing nothing.
- `tests/git/publication/test_imports.py` `_DEFINED["pr_references"]` extended with the new names; its clean-process import, owner-boundary, and no-sibling-answers checks pass (the owner still imports nothing beyond `re`).
- `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check orchestrator tests` — clean, including `--select=I001`.
- `.venv/bin/python -m flake8 orchestrator tests --select=WPS` — clean.
- `git diff --check` / `--cached --check` — clean.
- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest` — **6802 passed, 49 skipped, 38310 subtests passed**. The skips are the pre-existing optional ones (plotly not installed, Docker Compose, opt-in live-Postgres analytics); no failures.
REPORT: END

author: petfold
body:
Answer "is everything on this medium backed up?"

Raised by a concrete case: reformatting a laptop. The tool for it looked
like `diff`, and it is not -- and the tool that looked right, `only-on`,
was quietly giving the wrong answer.

`diff A B` asks what one other medium happens to lack. It flags files
that are safely backed up somewhere else, and its answer changes with
which medium you compare against. That is a fine question, just not this
one.

`only-on` asks whether anything else holds the content -- and a sync
mirror answers yes, while being exactly the copy that does not survive.
Measured on a three-medium catalog: a laptop file present only in Dropbox
is cleared by `only-on` and has no backup copy at all. The README has
pointed at `only-on` for wiping a drive since v0.1, so that was a false
reassurance on the one decision you cannot take back.

`redundancy --on MEDIUM` scopes the backup-copy question to one medium:
it counts only copies that survive deleting the original, and ignores
content not on that medium, so an unbacked file on some other drive does
not block reformatting this one. With --exit-code it is the gate.

Proportional to the medium, like `diff`, because it walks its rows. Fine
for a decision made sitting in front of the thing; it would want the
only_here flag treatment if it ever had to be fast over a network.

The roadmap's diff entry is corrected while here. "No precomputation
removes it" was too strong: the totals are precomputable (media are few,
so a per-pair summary is small), and only the row listing is stuck, since
that would need a flag per instance per pair.

author: ejc3
body:
## Why From a long assisted-login session. Two durable fixes so we never repeat that pain: ## 1. `auth export` — move auth to another device `safe_cli auth export [--file f]` writes the stored token bundle (the durable **offline** refresh token + `app_uuid`) as the same JSON `auth import` already reads. Do the assisted browser login **once**, export the bundle, and on any other device `auth import` it then `auth refresh` — working auth with **no browser, OTP, or 2FA**. The bundle is a secret (it can mint tokens for the account): export writes `0600` and the message tells you to delete it after import. RED-verified round-trip: - `TestAuthExportImportRoundTrip` — export on config-home A → import on config-home B → the offline refresh token, `app_uuid`, and phone all match. - `TestAuthExportNoTokensErrors` — exporting an empty store errors (no silent empty "backup"). ## 2. docs/PROCESS.md §9 — the headless-server login recipe that works The five rules, each a failure someone already hit: 1. **Fresh `app_uuid`** (`rm ~/.config/safe_cli/appuuid`) — an abandoned login leaves a stuck frisco session, so the next login's code is bound to a dead PKCE challenge → `500` at exchange. 2. **One clean browser tab** — a stale background 2FA tab completes and is captured instead of your fresh flow. 3. **Run `auth login` in tmux** — a Ctrl+C that interrupts the turn kills a backgrounded driver and the in-memory PKCE verifier + recom token with it. 4. **Drive the desktop over VNC** — `import`/`xdotool` on the browser's Xvfb, plus the browser-manager `vsfapp://` capture (separate PR to ejc3/aws). 5. **Be quick** — the recom token is short-lived. Plus the export/import escape hatch above. `make test` / `make lint` / `make vuln` green under Go 1.25.13.

Confidence Score: 5/5

The PR appears safe to merge, with a non-blocking reliability issue in how an existing export file is replaced.

Findings

1.  **Export replacement can lose data** ▶

Summary

This PR adds a portable authentication-bundle export command and a recovery option that regenerates the device ID before login. - Exports stored tokens either as raw JSON or into a newly created `0600` file. - Adds export/import round-trip and destination-permission tests. - Adds `auth login --new-device` with XDG-aware device-ID reset behavior. - Documents the assisted headless-login workflow and authentication-transfer procedure. - The previous unsafe-permission and XDG cleanup findings are resolved.
Diagram ```mermaid %%{init: {'theme': 'neutral'}}%% flowchart LR A[Authenticated device] --> B[auth export] B --> C[Secret token bundle] C --> D[Transfer through trusted channel] D --> E[auth import on another device] E --> F[auth refresh] F --> G[Working authentication] ```
