author: huang195
body:
## Summary

A plugin can reject in a response phase that runs AFTER the response has already gone downstream.
The action is dropped, correctly — there is nothing left to refuse — but the refusal is still recorded,
and `OutcomeFromContext` maps any deny to `OutcomeDeny`. Every Finisher, audit row and dashboard then
reads **"this request was denied" for a request answered with a 200**.

Measured: `FinalAction=deny, StatusCode=200, DenyingPlugin=…` — one outcome contradicting itself.

## The fix

`Context.MarkResponseDelivered()` is a fact only a listener can state; the pipeline cannot know whether
bytes reached a client. From then on:

- Invocations are stamped `Late`, exactly as they are stamped `Shadow` under `on_error: observe`, and
  for the same reason: a decision recorded without being applied. The framework sets it, because plugin
  code is identical either side of delivery.
- `OutcomeFromContext` skips a late deny on **both** of its paths — the rejecting-plugin state and the
  deny Invocation. Fixing one would leave the other lying about the same request.

**Marked, not erased.** `RejectingPlugin` still names the plugin and the deny row still says deny,
because a gate that would have blocked a response after it shipped is exactly what a rollout wants to
see. What stops being true is the claim that the request was refused.

## The snapshot is the design

`rejectedAfterDelivery` is captured WHEN the refusal is recorded, not read at outcome time. The obvious
simplification — asking "is the response delivered?" when deriving the outcome — inverts this fix for a
real case: a gate that refuses BEFORE anything is sent, whose error page is then delivered, is a
delivered response with a genuine block. Mutation-verified, that simplification reports it as
**allowed**, and the whole module passes:

```
bare Deny pre-delivery, then delivered   FinalAction=allow DenyingPlugin=""    (mutant)
bare Deny pre-delivery, then delivered   FinalAction=deny  DenyingPlugin=gate  (this code)
```

The bare-`Deny` shape is the one that discriminates: with an Invocation on record the mutant still
reports deny, because `lastDenyingPlugin` finds a row that is not `Late`. Both are pinned anyway.

## Scope

13 lines of logic across three files, and **five subtests**: the two late-refusal paths, the
pre-delivery control, a pre-delivery refusal that is then delivered on each path, and
`MarkResponseDelivered`'s documented idempotence and one-way properties.

Nothing calls `MarkResponseDelivered` yet; the listeners that need it are the next PR in this series
(#1034 is the first). Stacked on #1034 only because these were extracted from #1012 in order — they are
independent changes.

---

author: oliviera999
body:
Suite de [#496](https://github.com/oliviera999/ForetMap/pull/496), qui avait unifié les champs et les onglets. Celui-ci traite les deux **conteneurs** qui les portent, le **libellé** qui les nomme, et la **conformité entre produits** — les trois chantiers laissés ouverts en §5 de l'audit.

## Panneau — la surface qui manquait

ForetMap n'avait **aucune primitive de surface** : chaque écran réinventait la sienne (`.about-card`, `.stat-card`, `.pin-card`, `.notif-panel`, `.forum-panel`), avec à chaque fois son fond, son rayon, son ombre et sa marge intérieure.

Pire : **huit écrans posaient `className="card"`, une classe qui n'existait dans aucune feuille**. Le catalogue de QCM, le réseau trophique, le rattachement des questions, les réglages de validation des lectures, les stats et le carnet croyaient poser une carte blanche et rendaient un bloc **transparent**.

`src/shared/styles/surfaces.css` pose `.fm-panel` (+ `--flush`, `--quiet`, `__head`, `__title`, `__body`) et ses tokens `--fm-panel-*`. `.card` en devient l'alias : ces huit écrans retrouvent une surface **sans que leur balisage change**.

## Tableau — cinq habillages, dont deux inexistants

| Classe | État avant |
| --- | --- |
| `.moodle-table` | habillage propre (filet `#e5e7eb`, gris hors palette) |
| `.pedago-links__table` | habillage propre (filet `#e2ebe5`) |
| `.data-table` (stats) | **aucune règle** → rendu brut du navigateur |
| `.visit-mascot-pack-detail-table` | **aucune règle**, compensée par des styles **inline** |
| `LearningGatingLocksPanel`, `DataList` | aucune classe |

`.fm-table` / `.fm-table-wrap` (+ `--dense`, `__actions`) portent désormais filets, en-têtes, états de ligne et densité. Un tableau large **défile dans sa propre boîte** au lieu d'élargir la page — ce qui comptait surtout sur téléphone.

La fiche de pack mascotte réécrivait son apparence en styles inline (largeur, `border-collapse`, filets, marge de chaque cellule, taille de texte) : à cette spécificité-là, aucune feuille ne pouvait la reprendre. Ces styles sont sortis, et un test le fige.

## Libellé — sept dialectes, un seul retenu

`.field label` en capitales interlettrées vert feuille, `.pedago-filter-field` en minuscules gris-vert, `.profiles-admin-filter > label` en capitales `--text-xs`, `.media-library-menu__filter-label` en capitales gris ardoise, et trois autres — plusieurs cohabitant dans le même écran.

**Les capitales interlettrées disparaissent**, au profit des minuscules en demi-gras (`.fm-label`). C'est le point le plus visible de cette PR, et le raisonnement est explicite : les capitales se lisent moins bien, en particulier pour un élève dyslexique, et ForetMap est une application de lycée. Aucun libellé n'est réécrit — le texte était déjà en minuscules dans le balisage, seule la règle `text-transform` est retirée. **Revenir en arrière tiendrait en une ligne.**

## Conformité inter-produits — ce que la relecture des dernières PR a trouvé

Relecture de #493, #495, #497 et #498. Un constat neuf, que le lot précédent n'avait pas vu :

**#497 a introduit un quatrième produit** — le plan des personnels (`src/staff/`) — dont l'entrée ne chargeait **aucune feuille du contrat**. Le Plan public était dans le même cas.

Ce n'est pas une négligence : rien ne le signalait. `src/plan/styles/plan.css` va jusqu'à réaliaser `--forest` et `--leaf` sur sa charte marine, en toutes lettres « pour les contrôles partagés » — **l'intention de réutiliser le contrat était écrite, la feuille n'était simplement pas chargée**. Dans les faits ces produits n'ont que deux champs, tous deux habillés à la main : le manque ne se voyait pas encore.

Le reste de ces PR est conforme, et c'est le point important : `SurfaceVisibilityField` (nouveau champ partagé) emploie `.fm-surface-field`, `StaffPlanSettingsPanel` (nouvel écran d'administration) emploie `.field` et `.muted`. **Le contrat est suivi quand il est disponible** ; ce qui manquait, c'est qu'une entrée nouvelle le charge d'office.

Traité : les quatre entrées chargent `form-controls.css` et `surfaces.css`, **et un test échoue si l'une cesse de le faire**. Le Plan teinte les tokens à sa charte marine au lieu de réécrire ses bordures. `.plan-topbar__input` reste nu — il vit dans une pilule de recherche qui porte déjà la bordure — et c'est documenté sur place.

> Le chevron est le seul token qui ne se dérive pas : sa couleur est cuite dans le SVG, un produit à une autre palette doit le remplacer en entier. Aucun ne le fait aujourd'hui — ni le Plan ni le plan des personnels n'ont de liste déroulante.

## Tests

- `tests/form-controls-guard.test.js` passe de **7 à 10 assertions**. Les trois nouvelles : chaque produit charge les feuilles du contrat ; aucune apparence de tableau réécrite hors `.fm-table` ; aucun libellé de champ en capitales.
- `PackBehaviorDetailTable.test.jsx` fige la sortie des styles inline.
- Suites au vert : **3 617 backend**, **4 444 UI**, **64 contenu**. `lint` et `format:check` propres. Rendu vérifié au navigateur sur le bundle de production.

## Reste ouvert (§6 de l'audit)

Les surfaces historiques (`.about-card`, `.stat-card`, `.pin-card`, `.notif-panel`, `.forum-panel`) ne sont **pas** migrées sur `.fm-panel` : elles sont correctes et cohérentes entre elles, les toucher aurait élargi la PR sans gain visible. Restent aussi les tableaux de G&L et le lot C de `AUDIT_UI_2026-09-16.md` (couleur, styles inline).

Audit complet : [`docs/AUDIT_UI_FORMULAIRES_ONGLETS_2026-09.md`](https://github.com/oliviera999/ForetMap/blob/claude/gracious-keller-zaulfx/docs/AUDIT_UI_FORMULAIRES_ONGLETS_2026-09.md) — §5 pour ce lot, §6 pour la suite.

> Note anti-conflit : aucune migration ajoutée, note de `CHANGELOG.md` en fin de `[Non publié]`. `main` avance vite — cette PR est courte et prête, autant la fusionner tant qu'elle l'est.

author: raymondmars
body:
本次改动分两条线：**Year 9 词库与全仓释义清理**，以及**按认知心理学重做记忆机制**。中间还修了一个会删空线上站点的构建隐患。

代码改动集中在 33 个文件；另有 6480 个数据文件（词库和单词详情）是脚本生成的，建议 review 时按路径过滤掉 `public/`。

---

## 一、构建隐患（建议优先看）

`vite.config.ts` 取 commit hash 的出错分支从不调用 `resolve`：

```ts
getLastCommit((err, commit) => (err ? 'unknown' : resolve(commit.shortHash)))
```

git 一旦不可用，config 的 promise 永远挂起，vite **静默退出、退出码 0、零产物**。而 `make deploy` 是 `yarn build` 之后 `rsync --delete build/`——构建无声失败，`--delete` 足以把线上站点删空。

这不是理论风险，开发过程中就触发了（macOS 升级后没接受 Xcode 许可，git 返回 exit 69）。已修复，并给 Makefile 加了产物守卫。

## 二、Year 9 词库

原来是从 COCA 词频表第 2001-3500 名切出的 1500 词。词频分段和课堂用词对不上：`analyse` / `justify` / `hypothesis` 这类学科术语和指令词在通用词频表里排得很靠后，反倒是一堆美国新闻高频词挤进来。

改用按学科整理的 **489 词**，分 10 类（学术通用、阅读与文学分析、语法写作、连接词、描写性词汇，以及科学/数学/社会研究/健康体育/技术）。源文件顺序即章节顺序，同一章的词属于同一主题。

489 个词全部生成了例句和词组（每词 3 条例句，词组共 1110 条），其中 366 个复用了其他词库已有的详情。

顺带修了 `gen-word-details.mjs` 对多词条目的变形判定：整串加后缀得到的 `rely ons` 不是真实写法，而模型写出的 `relies on` 反被判为没用到该词、例句被丢弃。现在首尾两个词都展开，动词短语和名词短语都能认。

## 三、全仓释义统一

313 个词库的释义来自不同抓取源，风格完全不统一：142 个库几乎都标词性，120 个几乎都不标，37 个混着来。另有 4.4% 的释义嵌了英文例句，2% 带 `【搭配】` 标注块，6146 条把 `(Suffer)人名；(意)苏费尔` 接在正常释义后面，`Oxford5000` 有 19 条把整页词典抓了进来（最长 **304618 字符**）。

不用 AI——内容本来就在源数据里，坏的只是格式。两步：归一化（解 HTML 实体、剥标注块、截掉嵌入例句和专名义项、分隔符归一、拆开糊住的词性、修不配对括号、按词性切分并封顶），然后跨库统一（每个词选得分最高的一份写回所有含它的词库）。前端读的还是 `trans`，**运行时零成本**。

| 指标 | 前 | 后 |
|---|---|---|
| 带词性标注 | 38.2% | **68.6%** |
| 释义长度 p99 | 123 字 | **50 字** |
| 最长释义 | 304618 字 | **203 字** |
| HTML 实体 / 【】/ 〔〕/ 专名义项 / 语法表 | 有 | **全部归零** |
| word-details 的 senses 残渣 | 11.1% | **0%** |

三类不参与：14 个英文释义词库（换成中文会毁掉词库设计）、人工整理的 `NZ_K12_Year9`（`characterisation` 在文学分析里是「人物塑造」，通用词典给的「描述；人物之创造」是退步）、以及降为兜底来源的 `Oxford5000`（源头就丢了义项分隔符，粘成一坨后任何规则都还原不回来）。

脚本跑一次即终态（内部迭代到收敛，实测 3 轮）。

**注意一个隐式依赖**：归一化会剥掉 `【记忆】【搭配】` 标注块，而 `build-word-notes.mjs` 正是靠它们产出助记和固定搭配。所以剥之前先把标注块原样存进 `scripts/data/dict-annotations.json`，两边同时取数。改动任一边都要同步另一边，否则助记会静默归零（开发中踩过一次，助记从 1227 掉到 0）。

## 四、长单词不再撑满屏幕

字号一直是 `clamp(基准×1.2, 11.5vw, 基准×3.5)`，只看视口不看词长。`independent variable` 在 1440px 屏上要占 2200px，直接横向溢出，发音图标也被顶出可视区。

按字母数再算一个上限压住：`可用宽度 ÷ (字母数 × 0.68em)`。`0.68em` 不是估的——JetBrains Mono 严格等宽，从字体表里读出 `unitsPerEm 1000 / advance 600` = 0.6em，加 Letter 的左右内边距 0.045em×2、字距 -0.01em。

可用宽度是实测的，不是 `90vw` 硬算：外层是 Tailwind 的 `.container`，最大宽度按断点跳变（1400px 视口下容器只有 1280px）。

短词字号完全不变；另加 22px 下限 + `flex-wrap`，承接雅思口语库那种整句入库的极端条目（最长 194 字符）。

## 五、按认知心理学重做记忆机制

以记忆理论完整评估了打字流程，分三批落地。评估结论和已否决的方向记在新建的 `CLAUDE.md` 里。

### A 批：发音时机、音标、反馈卡片

原来每个词都在**拼写开始前**播读音。但核心训练是「看中文 → 盲拼英文」（默写默认 hideAll、中文常驻可见），提前把答案的语音送到耳边，就把线索回忆降级成了听写——检索难度塌了，记忆收益跟着塌。

改成查 `wordRecords` 判定练过没有：**首次遇到**在开头播（没听过无从下手，这是编码材料）；**练过的词**拼完之后播（此刻屏幕上是自己生成出来的拼写，声音进来正好和它绑在一起）。拼错时同样播——那才是纠正性反馈最该发生的时刻，改之前拼错反而什么都听不到。

音标默认打开（形音双通道编码）。详情卡片按对错分流：拼错时逐字母标出错在哪 + 「你拼成了 xxx」，例句收到一条不跟纠正抢注意力；拼对时维持原样。

### B 批：章末自动重测

一章 20 个词，每个词只被检索一次就翻篇——这是集中练习。原有的「复习错词」按钮绑在 `r` 键，而 Enter（反射会按的键）直接去下一章，实际几乎不会被用到。

现在一章练完自动进入重测，词表从「拼错的」扩到「拼错的 + 拼对但拼得犹豫的」。犹豫用敲对的相邻字母平均间隔判定，阈值 `max(本章中位数 × 1.6, 300ms)`——用本章中位数自动适配打字速度，再压一条绝对下限避免整章飞快时误伤。

重测词表**刻意不洗牌**：保持练习顺序让每个词离上次检索的间隔尽可能长。洗牌会把刚练完的词甩到最前面，那时它还在工作记忆里，再测几乎没有成本也就没有收益。

### C 批：间隔重复调度

此前一个词练过就永远不再出现。算法用 SM-2 变体，相对原版两处改动：

1. **评级由表现推导，不让用户自评**。这是打字练习，中断流程去点「困难/良好/简单」既打断节奏又不可靠。改成从「拼错没有」和「敲得多犹豫」推导，判定基于**个人基线**（敲对间隔的指数滑动平均）而非绝对毫秒——400ms 对基线 200ms 的人是犹豫，对基线 500ms 的人是正常。
2. **答错不安排当天重来**。原版要求失败卡片当天再过一遍，而 B 批的章末重测已经承担了这件事。

验算：一路 good 间隔 `1 → 3 → 8 → 20 → 50 → 125 → 313 → 365` 天封顶；一路 hard `1 → 3 → 6 → 12 → 22 → 37 → 56 → 77`，EF 衰减到 1.38；顺利四次后答错 20 天打回 1 天，EF 2.50 → 2.18。

新增 `wordReviewStates` 表（DB v4）。状态**按单词存、不分词库**——记住了就是记住了；但会话只取当前词库的交集，练 Year 9 时被塞一堆 GRE 词只会让人困惑。到期时间压到当天零点，否则早上 8 点练的词第二天 8 点才到期，7 点来的人会看到「待复习 0」然后过一会儿又冒出来一批。老用户有 `wordRecords` 但没有调度状态，首次加载补一次历史。

入口是顶栏的「今日待复习 N」，N 取「到期数」和「今日剩余额度」的较小者——真实积压可能是四位数，摆出来只会让人不想开始。每日上限可选 20/50/100/不限，默认 50，只统计复习会话里练的词（正常章节练习是学新词，不占还债名额）。

同时删掉了旧的「错题回顾」：它自己标着「实验阶段」，生成的是没有到期概念的一次性清单，现在被真调度器取代，留着只会让人分不清两个「复习」的区别。「查看错题」标签页保留，那是错题展示，和调度是两回事。

---

## 验证

`tsc --noEmit`、`eslint`、`yarn build` 均通过。脚本类改动都验过幂等性（归一化脚本三轮收敛后零改动）。调度算法和慢词判定都在 node 里跑过数值自测。

**UI 未做浏览器验证**，需要人工看一眼：长单词的缩放、拼错时的卡片标注、顶栏的「今日待复习」。

## 已知事项

- 本 PR 是 4 段工作叠在同一分支上的，想分开 review 的话可以按 commit 边界拆。
- `reviewRecords` 表保留未删——那是历史数据，删表是破坏性的且没有收益，只是现在没有写入方了。

body:
Adds the `TeleportStub` API discussed in #2632 (with the three-way semantics confirmed there by @cexbrayat), and unblocks the Teleport stubbing problem from #2628. Credit to @victor141516 for the original analysis in #2632 — this PR follows the agreed direction from that thread instead of the earlier `disabled`-teleport approach of the stalled PR.

### What

1. **`TeleportStub` is now exported.** It renders its default slot content in place (no wrapper element, no target needed), so it behaves closer to a real `<Teleport>` while keeping `findComponent(TeleportStub)` working.

2. **Built-in stubs (`teleport`, `keep-alive`, `transition`, `transition-group`) now honor custom component stub values.** Previously a component value for a built-in tag was silently ignored: the `DEFAULT_STUBS` resolution only handled `true`/`false`, and built-ins have no component name to reach the custom-stub path. The full semantics are now:

| `stubs.Teleport` | behavior |
|---|---|
| `false` | no stubbing (real Teleport) — unchanged |
| `true` | default `<teleport-stub>` — unchanged |
| `TeleportStub` / any component | renders that component in place — **new** |

### Why the stub component is returned as-is

Built-ins bypass the transformation cache (`util.ts` skips cached transformations for Teleport/KeepAlive), so a fresh component type per render is what makes the default stub unmount/remount its subtree on every parent re-render — the reactivity break reported in #2628. Returning the user's stable component reference keeps Vue patching in place, which the new regression test in `tests/features/teleport.spec.ts` locks down via mount/unmount lifecycle counters.

### Verification

- `vitest run`: 506 passed, 0 failed (54 files)
- `vue-tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.volar.json`: clean
- `oxlint`: 0 errors
- New tests: in-place rendering + `findComponent` + custom-component stubs in `global.stubs.spec.ts`; child-persistence-across-re-renders regression in `teleport.spec.ts`

Docs: added a `TeleportStub` section to `docs/api/index.md` next to `RouterLinkStub`.

The settings sidebar in #1325 uses separate window chrome and a custom search field. On macOS 27 it also opens and closes without animation: the workaround in #1106 deliberately switched to a fixed-width `HStack` to avoid an AppKit scroll-pocket overlay covering page headers.

Use SwiftUI's `NavigationSplitView` on macOS 26 and later, with native sidebar search and the system sidebar toggle. This lets macOS provide the sidebar material, toolbar placement, resizing and collapse animation. Reuse the existing rows, grouping, filtering, badges and selection binding. Keep the existing macOS 14 and macOS 15–25 shells.

Closes #1325

Captured from the actual app on macOS 27 using the existing screenshot fixture mode. Images contain example data, no production history, account details or personal device names. No generative edits or blur were applied.

author: root-lump
body:
## Background

Worktree directories were always named `<repo>-<branch>`, a single flat
directory next to the main worktree or under `base_dir`. When `base_dir` holds
the worktrees of several repositories, nothing separates one repository's
worktrees from another's — they all sit side by side in one listing.

## What this PR delivers

- A `[worktree] layout` setting accepting `flat` (the default, unchanged
  behaviour) and `nested`, which places each worktree at `<repo>/<branch>`.
  It resolves through the same global-then-repository precedence as `base_dir`.
- `copsy config global` and `copsy config repo` now offer the layout, and both
  render it into the generated TOML.
- The repository directory is removed once its last worktree is gone, since
  `git worktree remove` deletes only the worktree itself. The parent is matched
  by path against the layout's own computation rather than by name, so changing
  the layout or `base_dir` later cannot delete a shared `base_dir`.
- `README.md` and `README.ja.md` document the setting, both layouts and the
  fallback described below.

Branch-name slashes stay flattened to `-` in both layouts. Keeping the depth
fixed at two levels preserves the uniqueness of the directory basename, which
`find_worktree` matches against when resolving a worktree by name.

### The `-worktrees` fallback

With `layout = "nested"` and no `base_dir`, the repository directory would be
`<parent of main worktree>/<repo>` — which is the main worktree itself,
because `git clone` checks out into a directory named after the repository.
Worktrees would then be created inside the main worktree, where they also show
up as untracked directories in its `git status`. In that case the layout falls
back to `<repo>-worktrees`.

## Validation

- [x] `cargo fmt --check` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo test` — 77 passed, 0 failed
- [x] Manual run against throwaway repositories, with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` pointed
      at an empty directory so the developer's own global config could not
      interfere:
  - `base_dir` set, `nested`: worktree created at `<base_dir>/<repo>/<branch>`;
    `list` shows it and `switch <branch>` resolves it
  - two worktrees, one removed: the repository directory stays; removing the
    last one prunes it
  - `layout` unset: `<repo>-<branch>` as before
  - `base_dir` unset, `nested`, main worktree named after the repository:
    created at `<parent>/<repo>-worktrees/<branch>`, and the main worktree's
    `git status` stays empty
  - removing the last worktree in that case prunes `<repo>-worktrees` too

## Notes

- Existing worktrees are not migrated. Changing the setting affects only
  worktrees created afterwards.
- No CLI flag was added: the layout is a per-repository/global setting, so
  `src/cli.rs` and the completion definitions in `src/commands/init.rs` are
  untouched.
- The collision check compares paths without `canonicalize`, matching how the
  surrounding code already treats paths. A `base_dir` reached through a symlink
  would not be recognised as the main worktree.

author: pedramamini
body:
Closes #1602

## What was wrong

`maestro-cli dispatch <agent> "..." --new-tab` failed with `NEW_TAB_NO_ID` whenever the target agent was mid-turn. No tab was created and the prompt was dropped. Two separate defects stacked up.

**1. The renderer refused the request outright when the agent was busy.**

`onRemoteNewAITabWithPrompt` bailed on `session.state === 'busy'`. But busy is an AGENT-level state, so a brand-new tab inherits it even though it owns no process - and `--new-tab` rejects both `--force` and `--queue` as meaningless ("a fresh tab is never busy"), which left no flag able to express what the caller actually wanted. Every dispatch aimed at a working agent was a dropped prompt.

**2. The refusal was misreported.**

`MaestroClient.sendCommand` resolves on any reply, success or not. A refusal carries no tab id, so it fell through to the `NEW_TAB_NO_ID` branch and was reported as "Maestro desktop acknowledged --new-tab without returning a tab id" - a protocol fault, which is the one thing it is not. The renderer's own reason never left the renderer.

## What changed

- **The tab is created either way.** A prompt that cannot start now is queued against that fresh tab through the canonical `enqueuePromptForTab()`, so `useQueueProcessing` drains it the moment the current turn ends. The item is built by the shared builder, so it is identical to one the composer would have queued - frozen model/effort, and `@mention` flags fired at drain time rather than at queue time. This is exactly the two-call workaround from the issue (`tab new` + `dispatch --tab --queue`), done in one round trip.
- **Failure reasons travel with the ack.** `sendRemoteNewAITabWithPromptResponse` now takes a result object (`{ success, tabId?, queued?, error? }`), threaded through preload, the main-side callback, and the websocket result. The CLI reports the desktop's own reason under a new `DISPATCH_REFUSED` code, checked before the substring sniffing in `mapDispatchError` so a verbatim reason cannot be re-classified by whatever words it happens to contain. `NEW_TAB_NO_ID` is kept for what it was meant for: a success that really did omit the id.
- **The response says which happened.** `queued: true` when the prompt is waiting behind a running turn, so an automated caller can tell "running now" from "next in line".
- Help text, `docs/cli.md` and `docs/cli-reference.md` updated - the old "a fresh tab is never busy" rationale is no longer true of what happens, only of why `--force` still has nothing to bypass.

`--force` and `--queue` remain rejected alongside `--new-tab`: the former has no turn to bypass, the latter is now redundant. Their error messages say so accurately.

## Branch note

Based on `rc`, not `main`. The enqueue machinery this reuses (`enqueue_command`, `services/queuedPrompt.ts`, `dispatch --queue`) does not exist on `main`, and the web-server handlers this touches live in the `messageHandlers/` decomposition that is rc-only. The reporter's own workaround uses `--queue`, so the failure was observed on an rc build.

## Testing

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.lint.json` clean.
- `eslint --max-warnings=0` clean on every changed source file.
- `src/__tests__/cli` + `useRemoteIntegration.test.ts`: 1547 passed, 1 skipped.
- New coverage: the renderer creates the tab and queues the prompt for a busy agent (asserting the queue item targets the NEW tab and that no immediate spawn is dispatched); the ack carries a reason when the agent is missing; the CLI reports `DISPATCH_REFUSED` with the desktop's message rather than `NEW_TAB_NO_ID`; the CLI surfaces `queued: true`.
- Note: `src/__tests__/main/web-server/routes/mediaRoutes.test.ts` and one `WebServer.test.ts` case fail in this environment, on a pristine `origin/rc` checkout as well. Pre-existing, untouched by this change.

<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

## Summary by CodeRabbit

- **New Features**
  - `dispatch --new-tab` now queues prompts when the agent is busy and reports `queued: true`.
  - Dispatch responses provide clearer refusal reasons when a new tab cannot be created.
  - Queue status is consistently reported for both new-tab and existing-tab dispatches.

- **Documentation**
  - Updated CLI help and reference documentation to explain new-tab queuing behavior and clarify interactions with `--force` and `--queue`.

- **Bug Fixes**

author: mgravell
body:
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Blocked on #3191, and not only a planning branch.**
>
> This currently adds notes and no product code. It is opened as a draft now so the investigation is
> reviewable while the dependency clears — **this branch becomes the feature branch** once
> [#3191](https://github.com/StackExchange/StackExchange.Redis/pull/3191) merges, with the
> implementation landing on top of these same commits rather than starting again elsewhere.
>
> The plan is a proposal. Where it leans, it says so; where the evidence does not decide, it leaves
> the question open rather than inventing an answer.

## What this is

Investigating whether Redis Enterprise's
[lag-aware database-availability API](https://redis.io/docs/latest/operate/rs/monitoring/db-availability/)
belongs in the geo-redundant failover health checks in `src/StackExchange.Redis/Availability/`
(currently behind `SER007`), using
[Lettuce's `LagAwareStrategy`](https://github.com/redis/lettuce/blob/main/src/main/java/io/lettuce/core/failover/health/LagAwareStrategy.java)
as the reference implementation.

| file | what it is |
| --- | --- |
| `notes/lag-aware/findings.md` | the research — evidence, with sources |
| `notes/lag-aware/plan.md` | the sequence that follows from it — **proposed, blocked on step 0** |
| `notes/readme.md` | the `notes/` convention (see "overlap" below) |

## Findings worth surfacing

- **This is a cross-client feature, not a Java curiosity.** Lettuce and Jedis have
  `LagAwareStrategy`; redis-py has `LagAwareHealthCheck`. It is the client-side geographic failover
  family. The check is not liveness — `extend_check=lag` asks whether a replica is *synchronised
  enough to be a safe failover target*, which is what stops a failback onto a region that is
  reachable but stale.
- **Our abstractions already fit, nearly one-to-one.** `HealthCheckProbe` ↔ `AbstractHealthCheck`,
  `AllSuccess`/`AnySuccess`/`MajoritySuccess` ↔ `HEALTHY_ALL`/`ANY`/`MAJORITY`, Ping default,
  circuit breaker, per-member configuration. Two details make it land cleanly: `HealthCheckProbe`
  has **no internal abstract members**, so it is already subclassable from outside the assembly; and
  `ConnectionGroupMember` already carries a per-member `HealthCheck` override, which is exactly what
  a per-cluster REST endpoint needs.
- **The defaults disagree across clients.** 100 ms from the cluster default, the REST documentation's
  explicit recommendation, and redis-py — but **5000 ms in Lettuce**. Fifty times more permissive
  than its own documentation advises. The plan measures rather than copies.
- **We are better placed than Lettuce on one point.** `HealthCheckResult` has `Inconclusive`;
  `HealthStatus` has two states, and Lettuce maps a failed REST call to `UNHEALTHY` — so a
  *management-plane* outage is indistinguishable from the data plane being down, and can fail over a
  database that is serving traffic perfectly. Proposed as a deliberate, documented deviation.
- **`src/` may need no changes at all.** The probe is subclassable, `RawConfig` and
  `ConfigurationOptions.Tunnel` are public. The only candidate core change is an optional `Tunnel`
  addition so the management plane honours tunnels — and if we do that, it should return a **stream**,
  composed into `SocketsHttpHandler.ConnectCallback` by the consumer, so no `System.Net.Http` type
  enters the public API.

## Corrections made while investigating

Recorded rather than quietly fixed, because the reasoning is the useful part:

1. I assumed a real cluster could not be made to show "reachable but stale" on demand, making fakes
   the only route to the scenario that matters. Wrong twice: Redis ships a fault injection service
   for exactly this, **and we already have a test tier built on it** — in #3191.
2. I framed the HTTP dependency as a significant cost. It is not: `System.Net.Http` needs no package
   reference on any target we ship. `System.Text.Json` is the only genuinely new dependency, and it
   is avoidable. So "where does this live" is a judgement call about scope, not a technical
   constraint.

## Why step 0 is "wait"

#3191 carries `tests/StackExchange.Redis.FaultInjector.Tests`, and with it `ClusterRestClient` —
already a Redis Enterprise REST client on 9443 doing Basic auth, CA pinning and
`GET /v1/bdbs?fields=…` — plus a `FaultInjectorClient` that can be *asked* which lag-inducing effects
a deployment supports. Starting now would mean writing a second REST client against the same cluster
and reconciling them at merge, for a feature whose implementation is smaller than the client that
tests it.

That tier also settled three things empirically that I had only from documentation: the management
certificate is **self-signed per environment** (so the probe needs CA configuration, not ambient
trust), auth really is Basic, and the `bdbs` listing returns the requested fields.

The one thing that can start earlier is validating the availability API against a real deployment,
because it produces notes rather than code — and #3191's own summary is the argument for doing it
first: *"the specifications are prose, the payloads were never published, and nearly every assumption
I started with was wrong in some way that mattered."*

## Deliberately undecided

- **Where the code ships** — core, a separate Enterprise package, or documented extension point. The
  plan leans toward a separate package and says why, but this is a scope judgement.
- **The tolerance default** — measured in step 1, not copied.
- **Whether the `Tunnel` addition happens at all** — separable; the probe works without it.

## Overlap to be aware of

`notes/readme.md` also appears in
[#3241](https://github.com/StackExchange/StackExchange.Redis/pull/3241), which introduced the
`notes/` convention. Whichever merges second gets a one-line conflict in its Topics list; the rest of
the file is identical.

Draft until #3191 lands.

author: kailashsharma282
body:
## Summary
Harden Hash Time Locked Contract (HTLC) atomic swap relayer and service with cross-chain SHA-256 / Keccak-256 preimage verification, timing-attack safe comparison, strict timelock duration boundaries, cross-chain lock delta hierarchy, and lifecycle state transition enforcement.

## Motivation
Atomic swaps provide trustless cross-chain and intra-chain asset transfers using hashlocks and timelocks. However, without strict cryptographic validation:
1. Low-entropy preimages (<16 bytes) or malformed formats (e.g. hashing hex strings as raw ASCII) risk hash collisions or protocol desynchronization.
2. Missing timelock boundaries allow race conditions, griefing attacks (e.g. extremely short timelocks where the refund can be frontrun before claim propagation), or locked funds (unreasonably long horizons).
3. Cross-chain atomic swaps require a strict hierarchy where the initiator chain lock duration exceeds the counterparty chain duration by at least a safety margin ($\Delta t \ge 3600$s) to prevent the initiator from claiming the target funds and simultaneously refunding on the source chain.
4. Swap lifecycle states (Pending $\to$ Claimed / Refunded) must strictly enforce timing gates so expired swaps cannot be claimed and unexpired swaps cannot be refunded.

This PR upgrades `AtomicSwapRelayer` and integrates it into `AtomicSwapService` with comprehensive validation and 16 unit tests.

## Changes
- **`backend/atomic-swap/swap_relayer.js`**:
  - Implemented `generateHashLockSecret()` supporting Keccak-256 and SHA-256.
  - Implemented `hashPreimage()` supporting 0x-hex, unprefixed hex, Buffer/Uint8Array, and UTF-8 strings with minimum 16-byte entropy guards.
  - Implemented constant-time `verifyPreimage()` using `crypto.timingSafeEqual()`.
  - Added `validateTimelock()` enforcing 1-hour minimum and 30-day maximum safety horizons.
  - Added `validateCrossChainTimelocks()` enforcing $\Delta t \ge 3600$s hierarchy.
  - Added `validateParticipantAddress()` enforcing EVM format and rejecting ZeroAddress.
  - Added `validateAmount()` enforcing positive bounds and 1,000,000 unit caps.
  - Added `validateStateTransition()` enforcing non-reentrancy and time-based claim/refund permissions.
  - Added `computeCanonicalSwapId()` for deterministic swap identification.
- **`backend/atomic-swap/swap.service.js`**:
  - Integrated `atomicSwapRelayer` validation into `createSwap`, `createCrossChainSwap`, and `generateHashLock`.
  - Added resilient fallback initialization for RPC providers and signer wallets in testing environments.
- **`backend/atomic-swap/test_atomic_swap_service.js`**:
  - Created 259 lines of unit tests covering 16 distinct test suites for hashlock verification, timelocks, address validation, state transitions, and canonical IDs.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Preimage hashing and verification support both Keccak-256 and SHA-256
- [x] Constant-time equality checks prevent timing side-channels
- [x] Timelock boundaries and cross-chain hierarchy enforced
- [x] Address format and zero-address checks implemented
- [x] State transition machine prevents premature refunds and expired claims
- [x] Minimum 200 lines of code changes achieved (547 additions)
- [x] All unit tests pass with zero errors

## Impact & Side Effects
- Zero breaking changes to existing routes or API contracts.
- Dramatically increases protocol security against HTLC race conditions and front-running griefing.

## How to Test
Run the atomic swap test suites:
```bash
node backend/atomic-swap/test_atomic_swap.js
node backend/atomic-swap/test_atomic_swap_service.js
```

## Quality Checklist
- [x] My code adheres to the project's coding conventions.
- [x] All unit tests pass cleanly.
- [x] Only production and test files staged.
- [x] No scratch or temporary files committed.

body:
## What

OpenRouter reports a dropped upstream *inside* an HTTP 200: `finish_reason: "error"`, with the detail in `choices[0].error` (here, 504 `Upstream idle timeout exceeded`). The SDK validates that envelope against the OpenAI schema, where `error` is not a legal `finish_reason`, and raises `UnexpectedModelBehavior` — which hit the catch-all in `execute_job` and marked the job `failed`, so arq never retried.

A dropped upstream now raises `TransientJobError` like any 429/5xx. A model that genuinely returned nonsense still fails, because retrying that just spends the budget again.

## Why

Two `basic-porter` jobs died this way today, each about three minutes into generation. The same request succeeded when OpenRouter routed it to a different upstream. Nothing was wrong with the agent, the prompt or the model.

## How it's detected

By message, for the same reason `_rejects_forced_tool_choice` matches on message: the distinction has no status code of its own. The test asserts against the verbatim error text from one of today's failed jobs.

## Tests

- `test_in_band_upstream_failure_is_transient` — raises `TransientJobError` and records a `transient_error` event.
- `test_model_misbehaviour_still_fails_the_job` — the other half of the split stays `failed`.

body:
## Summary

Native Codex create no longer starts, resumes, or completes a Projmux-private app-server generation. The official `codex app-server daemon` owns the app-server lifecycle, so a default endpoint that cannot be attached now ends in a typed refusal that names the daemon step.

**Behavior change**
- `rollingCodexNativeThreadController.Current` no longer has a managed activator.
  - With no generation journal, it returns the attach-only default controller's answer unchanged.
  - With a journal, it reads the journal as it stands and does not run an incomplete managed activation forward.
  - Journal-present route interpretation is otherwise unchanged; a follow-up change converts it.
- An unattachable default endpoint ends in the existing typed refusal `generation-unavailable`. This covers managed version skew, unmanaged version skew, and a daemon that is not running.
  - The refusal's operator action is the exact daemon step: `codex app-server daemon restart`, `bootstrap`, or `start`.
  - The refusal headline points at `codex app-server daemon`.
  - An ownership-inspection recovery keeps its inspect-first sentence and adds the owner-agreed `codex app-server daemon restart` step. The unmanaged-only `bootstrap` prescription is unchanged.
  - The old action named `projmux doctor … generation action` and version-pair qualification.
- Doctor's Codex app-server block prints the same daemon step as `Guidance:` for any endpoint that is not ready or carries a recovery. A dead endpoint used to print no guidance.

**Refactor / plumbing**
- Removed the production activator wiring in `app.go`, along with its constructor and the now-unreferenced activator interface.
- The activator implementation and `codex_managed_generation.go` stay until the generation-pool removal deletes them.
  - Their now-unreachable symbols are recorded in `.deadcode-must-keep.txt` with that reason.
- Added a `probe` seam to `defaultCodexNativeThreadController` so tests can drive the real attach-authority decision.

## Tests

**New**
- `TestCodexNativeCreateEndpointSkewRefusesWithoutPrivateGeneration`
  - Covers both prompted spellings across all three readiness decisions.
  - Checks: typed reason and daemon step, one read-only probe per create, zero Registry/tmux mutation, native pane launcher zero, and no state directory created (no journal, bundle, qualification, or private runtime root).
- `TestCodexDaemonGuidanceRefusalAndDoctorGolden` (new golden `internal/app/testdata/codex_daemon_guidance.golden`; covers managed skew, unmanaged skew, daemon not running, and ownership-unknown skew)
- `TestDoctorAttachableCodexEndpointHasNoDaemonGuidance`
- `TestIncompleteManagedActivationIsNeverResumedByCreate`: the journal bytes and mtime are unchanged after `Current`.

**Removed**
- `TestOrdinaryCodexCreateSpellingsActivateRollingManagedCurrent` and `TestOrdinaryCodexCreateActivationGateReturnsExactActionWithZeroMutation`. They pinned the removed behavior.

`docs/agent-workflow.md` test list updated.

## Validation

- `make fmt`, `make fix` (deadcode baseline exact), `make test`: pass
- `make security-static` (staticcheck baseline clean), `make security-go` (gosec baseline clean): pass
- `make test-integration`, `make test-e2e`: running locally on this head
- Isolated installed smoke with separate HOME, CODEX_HOME, and tmux socket:
  - Setup: an official pid-backend daemon on CODEX_HOME running 0.153.4, then the managed install switched to 0.154.0.
  - Input: a prompted `create agent --provider codex`.
  - Result: typed `generation-unavailable` refusal with a daemon step. No `codex-generations` state, no HOME tree change, no new app-server process, no Agent.
  - The pre-change binary entered the managed activator (`managed-generation-activation-blocked`) on the same fixture.

## Known pre-existing issue (not addressed here)

On every Codex server/CLI pair tried (0.147–0.154), the attached endpoint's version comes back empty. As a result, manager evidence agreement stays `insufficient`, ownership resolves to `unknown`, and native actions are refused even without a skew.

This is why real installs currently receive the ownership-inspection guidance. This PR does not change that decision.

author: rcbjbluemars
body:
An RFC 9101 request object's `jti` is now accepted **once**. Until now it was not remembered, so a captured signed request object could be replayed until it expired. `oauth-oidc/request_object.ts` said so itself.

## What changed

**When the `jti` is checked and when it is spent.** The authorization endpoint reads every request twice, before and after the sign-in screen, so a once-only check at the read would refuse the request's own second pass. The check therefore splits the same way `par.ts` does for a pushed `request_uri`:

- **Checked on every pass.** `RequestObject.lookUp()` uses a new, read-only `used_assertions.peek()`. A spent or reserved `jti` is refused with `invalid_request_object` (`STS-OAUTH-0374`), before the sign-in screen.
- **Spent at the authorization endpoint.** It is spent only where something is issued on the object: in `issueAuthorizationResponse()`, below every refusal and beside the pushed `request_uri`'s claim. The claim is bound to the response. A new `keepBelow` option on `claim()` keeps it for any status under 400, which covers a redirect or a `form_post` page. A failure releases it.
- **Spent at a push.** The PAR endpoint spends it just before it keeps a pushed object, and the 201 keeps the claim. The push is the object's one use: its URN resolves to the stored parameters and spends nothing again.
- **A refused request spends nothing.**

**Where it is kept.** It goes in the used-assertion history as a third use of a `jwt`, `request-object`, keyed by the client and the `jti`.
- It shares one namespace per issuer with the RFC 7523 JWTs (RFC 7519 §4.1.7).
- It persists wherever that history does, and the claim is atomic on postgres.
- The postgres driver gains one read, `findUsedAssertion()`. There is no schema change, because `used_as` is free text.

**How long it is kept.** Until `exp` plus `oauth2.clientAssertionSkewS`. An object without `exp` is kept for the new `oauth2.requestObjectJtiRetentionS` (default 3600); after that, a replay of it is accepted.

**Settings and failures.**
- The new `oauth2.requestObjectJtiOnce` (default **on**, both modes) turns the check off.
- An object without `jti` is accepted as before. There is no setting to require one, since no specification asks for it.
- A full history refuses with `STS-OAUTH-0375` (503). A store that cannot record the `jti` refuses with `STS-OAUTH-0376` (500).

**Documentation.** Every place that said "not remembered" is rewritten: the module header, `oauth-oidc/CLAUDE.md` rule 3ak, README (the chapter and two settings rows), the `sts_metadata.ts` coverage text and `docs/what-is-not-checked.md`. The used-assertion page, the `GET /admin-api/used-assertions` enum and description, `docs/caches.md` and `docs/persistence.md` now name the new use. `docs/error-codes.md` is regenerated.

## Tests

`tests/rfc9101_request_object_jti.js` is new: 16 checks in process and 22 in a child process. The child-process checks cover:
- the passes before sign-in, after sign-in and after consent counting as one use;
- a replay refused before the sign-in screen;
- a flow started before the spend refused when it returns;
- a `login_required` error spending nothing;
- an object with no `jti`, and another client's `jti`;
- the switch turned off and on;
- an object sent by reference;
- a pushed object spent at the push, with its URN still issuing;
- the used-assertion listing.

**Mutation checks:** four mutants (the authorization-endpoint spend, the check on each pass, the PAR spend, `keepBelow`), all caught. The mutant that removes the check on each pass still refuses a late flow at the spend, which confirms the spend is what enforces the rule.

**Results:**
- `tsc -p tsconfig.json`: clean.
- `./docker-npm-test.sh`: 194 files, 8853 assertions, 0 failed.
- `./docker-run-tests.sh --modes=memory` (isolated project): 252 jobs, 9717 checks, 0 failures.
- postgres and dispatch modes were **not** run. The new `findUsedAssertion()` statement has not run against a real database.

No vendored job sends a request object with a `jti`. The parent project's own JAR tests would need fresh `jti`s per request if they reuse one; that was not checked here.

Closes #35

author: toddmedema
body:
## Why
The first step of the first tutorial had nothing to do. It showed a goal statement, ringed the entire top bar, and put about a dozen competing controls in front of a brand-new player: Next, Build, Exit, the ⋮ menu, four speed buttons, bottom nav, and drag handles. The first real action came at step 4.

Three reviewers (player flow, engineering, visual/copy) each proposed changes, critiqued each other's proposals, and agreed on the changes below.

## What changed
**Every step names one action.**
- `TutorialStepType` has a required `action` (plus optional `desktop.action`). The objective HUD renders it as a distinct row with a tap icon, above a short reason.
- All 45 steps across Missions 1–7 now have one. Where a prompt just repeated its action, it was rewritten as the reason.
- A new authoring test (`Scenarios.test.tsx`) enforces this. Every action is non-empty and ≤60 characters. Gated steps never say "Next", and steps where Next is the only way on always say it. No step targets chrome it hides.

**Mission 1 starts with an action and reveals controls as it goes (5 → 4 steps).**
1. **Tap your gas plant.** Gated on selecting the plant; the ring sits on that one row.
2. **Find the supply and demand lines, then tap Next.**
3. **Tap 1× to start time.** Speed controls appear here, and only 1× is ringed.
4. **Capstone:** keep supply above demand until midnight. Speed, menu and row actions are back.

A step can list chrome to hide in `hideUi` (`nav`, `build`, `menu`, `speed`, `facilityActions`, `yearProgress`, `sidePanes`). `Compositor` puts the list on `.app_container` as `data-tutorial-hide`, and CSS hides the matching controls. Speed uses `visibility` so cash and date don't jump when the buttons appear. Keyboard shortcuts for hidden controls are ignored, so pressing Space on step 1 can't start the clock. Mission 1 hides nav, Build and the year bar throughout.

**Tablet and desktop get the Facilities pane alone in Mission 1.** `sidePanes` is applied in `Compositor.renderCard` rather than with CSS: the resizable pane grid sizes its tracks from the pane count, so hiding a pane with CSS would leave an empty column and a stray splitter. This also removes the red "forecasted shortfall" line that showed beside the first objective at 1300px and wider.

**Clearer cue, one main button.**
- The target ring pulses once as soon as a step starts. The 10 s reminder is unchanged, and reduced motion is respected.
- Next is a filled button only when it's the step's only way forward. When the step can also advance on an in-game tap, Next becomes a quiet text button.
- On phones the concept-icon row is hidden, to leave room for the action.

## Screenshots
Mission 1, step 1 (phone): no nav, Build, menu or speed buttons, one ringed target.
![Mission 1 step 1 on a 390px phone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/dc94020b-32f7-4bf7-ba22-2c5a5418d82a)

Mission 1, step 3 (phone): speed controls appear, 1× is ringed.
![Mission 1 step 3 on a 390px phone](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/2b1cda9d-e243-4b22-89d9-1acc7ed0448b)

Mission 1, step 1 (desktop 1440px): Facilities pane only.
![Mission 1 step 1 on desktop](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/05206a74-6b76-4dd1-a4c8-9ca24ba478e2)

## Deliberately left out (follow-ups)
- **Hard-coded step indices** in `Facilities.tsx` / `TransmissionPanel.tsx` / `Insights.tsx` for Missions 6–7. Those missions keep their step counts in this PR, so nothing breaks.
- **A short "done ✓" flash** when an objective completes.

## Testing
- `npm run check`: typecheck, lint, format, all 128 Jest suites, and `sim --all` pass.
- Playwright: all `tutorial-*` specs and `contextual-learning` pass on all 5 projects. The capstone spec now also asserts which chrome step 1 hides and step 3 shows, and that desktop step 1 renders a single pane with no splitter. `contextual-learning`'s help test uses Mission 2, since Mission 1 no longer offers the Insights nav.

<!-- Plantilla CAMEIA v2.0 — instalada 11-sep-2026. Título: CM-NNN | tipo(scope): resultado [IA-ASISTIDO] si hubo IA. -->

<!-- Rama: CM-14-registro-usuario → develop. SHA revisado: <SHA del último commit al abrir el PR> -->
## Cambio
- Jira: https://f0rktech.atlassian.net/jira/software/projects/CM/boards/1?filter=&groupBy=none&selectedIssue=CM-14 (incluye trabajo de CM-104, spec `CM-104-correcciones-OIDC`) <verificar enlace>
- Responsable: Juan David Vela Coronado | Backend
- Cambio: El Gateway deja pasar el registro (`POST /api/v1/users`) sin sesión, compara las rutas públicas por método y ruta exactos, abre los health v1 de cada microservicio solo con el perfil `local` y ya no activa `local` por defecto. Además firma toda llamada saliente con un token OIDC de Google (`specs/CM-104-correcciones-OIDC/`), apagado por defecto y forzado con el perfil `prod`; **no** activa esa firma en Cloud Run (los workflows no se tocan) ni valida `email_verified` (`GW-TBD-17`).
- Tipo de tarea (DoD): Backend — no aplican los avisos a otros equipos (T-00m a T-00q de CM-14, siguen pendientes) ni el bloque de despliegue de OIDC (Bloque 0: requiere GCP y una decisión de DevOps, T-INF-05).

### Por qué este PR incluye la firma OIDC
La spec de registro no se podía cerrar sin ella:
1. **`REQ-REG-10`** exige que `POST /api/v1/users` salga firmado como cualquier otra ruta (T-20 de CM-14). Sin el componente OIDC esa prueba no existía.
2. **Plan CM-14 §3.3** pide que la guardia de desarrollo falle si `local` y `prod` están activos a la vez, y el perfil `prod` lo crea la spec OIDC.
3. **El registro es la primera ruta pública que recibe datos sensibles** (contraseña en el cuerpo). Abrirla sin que el Gateway pueda firmar hacia Cuentas dejaba incompleto el modelo de `AGENTS.md` §6.2, donde el Caso B existe precisamente porque el paso OIDC ocurre igual.
4. CM-14 quitó el `Authorization` del cliente en las rutas públicas (`REQ-REG-07`); OIDC es quien vuelve a poner ahí la única credencial válida. Revisarlos por separado obligaba a razonar el contrato de cabeceras dos veces.

La firma sigue gobernada por su propio spec y sus requisitos; aquí solo se integra.

## Evidencia
- Evidencia: compilación limpia — `mvn clean compile test-compile -Xlint:all` → 9 + 9 archivos, sin advertencias, `BUILD SUCCESS` — **PASA** (17/09/2026).
- Evidencia: suite completa — `docker compose run --rm verify` → `Tests run: 62, Failures: 0, Errors: 0`, `BUILD SUCCESS` — **PASA** (17/09/2026). <pegar salida>
- Evidencia: CM-14 integrada con `develop` sin OIDC — worktree temporal con `origin/develop` fusionado: `Tests run: 47, Failures: 0`, sin conflictos — **PASA**.
- Evidencia: health solo en desarrollo (REQ-REG-01 a 04) — `DevHealthRoutesTest` (5 rutas llegan sin token ni `X-User-*`; `/health/`, `/health/extra` y `POST` → `401`), `devHealth_withoutLocalProfile_returns401`, `devRoutes_onCloudRun_failsStartup`, `devRoutes_withProdProfile_failsStartup`, `applicationYaml_hasNoDefaultLocalProfile` — **PASA**.
- Evidencia: registro (REQ-REG-05 a 09) — `registration_withoutToken_reachesAccountsWithoutClientCredentials`, `usersRoot_nonPostWithoutToken_returns401` (GET/PUT/PATCH/DELETE), `registration_downstreamError_isReturnedUnchanged` (409 y 422 intactos), `versionedYaml_doesNotEnableWiretap` — **PASA**. `wompiWebhook_withoutToken_reachesDownstreamWithoutIdentityHeaders` sin cambios.
- Evidencia: firma OIDC (REQ-OIDC-01 a 09) — `OidcSigningFilterTest` (Caso A y B firmados con un solo valor, audience sin path ni barra final, token de Firebase nunca sale, registro firmado, fallo de la fuente → `503` sin reenvío, timeout del destino sigue en `504`), `OidcSigningGlobalFilterUnitTest` (`set` y no `add`; `https://*.run.app` sin `:443`), `prodYaml_declaresSigningEnabledAsLiteral`, `prodProfile_withSigningDisabled_failsStartup`, `prodProfile_oidcVariableCannotDisableSigning`, `oidcSigningFlagOff_noSigningFilterBean` — **PASA**. Límite: con una fuente de tokens falsa; que Google emita el token y Cloud Run lo acepte es **PENDIENTE** (T-INF-04).
- Evidencia: sin secretos — revisión de `git diff origin/develop...HEAD` — **PASA**.

## Riesgo
- Impacto: contrato, permisos, despliegue
- Riesgo: medio — (1) `POST /api/v1/users` queda público: sin rate limit en el Gateway, depende de Cloud Armor delante (C-4, pendiente de DevOps). (2) Las rutas públicas ya no reenvían el `Authorization` del cliente; si Cuentas lo leyera en el webhook de Wompi, dejaría de verlo (`GW-TBD-14`). (3) Quien arranque desde el IDE sin `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=local` pierde `application-local.yml` y los health de desarrollo. (4) La firma OIDC está en el código pero **apagada** en Cloud Run hasta T-INF-05. Recuperación: revertir el merge; sin datos ni migraciones. Documentación actualizada: `AGENTS.md` §3, §4, §5, §6.2, §6.5, §8, §9; `docs/COMO-FUNCIONA.md`; `.env.example`; `docker-compose.yml`; los dos `specs/`.
- Observabilidad: `WARN Solicitud rechazada por autenticación [requestId=…]` (proporción de `401`, sobre todo en `/api/v1/users`); `ERROR No se pudo firmar la llamada saliente [requestId=…, audience=…]` (solo cuando se active `prod`); log de arranque sin `The following 1 profile is active: "local"` en staging.

- Contrato: `POST /api/v1/users` pasa a Caso B; `GET`/`PUT`/`PATCH`/`DELETE /api/v1/users` siguen en Caso A. Rutas públicas: sin `X-User-*` ni `Authorization` del cliente. Con la firma encendida, `Authorization: Bearer <token OIDC>` en toda llamada saliente. Consumidores: cameia-cuentas (**aviso: el registro llega sin `X-User-*` y debe quedar exento de su contrato de entrada**, T-00o), cameia-web (**tras el `201`, iniciar sesión y `sendEmailVerification`**, T-00p), cameia-entrevista (**su health debe ser `GET /api/v1/interviews/health`**, T-00n). Prueba: ver Evidencia.
- Permisos: la firma usa la identidad de ejecución `cameia-gateway-run` (#39). Según el comentario de `desplegar-servicio.yml` ya tiene invocación sobre Perfil, Cuentas y Entrevista de staging; **no verificado**. Sin secretos ni archivos de clave.
- Despliegue: al fusionar en `develop`, CI y luego el CD de staging despliegan la imagen. Staging arranca **sin perfil** (los workflows no definen `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE`), así que la firma queda apagada y los health de desarrollo cerrados. Smoke: `GET /actuator/health` → `200`; `GET /api/v1/users/health` sin token → `401`; `GET /api/v1/users` sin token → `401`. Rollback: redesplegar la imagen anterior. Autorización: <quién aprueba>. Pendientes para DevOps: **T-INF-05** (decidir cuándo añadir `SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=prod`, con confirmación escrita de `run.invoker` y prueba de extremo a extremo en staging antes de producción); **producción** sigue con `CAMEIA_*_URL` de contenedor y su `--set-env-vars` no incluye `FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID` (`despliegue-continuo.yml:113`, previo a este PR, no comprobado en Cloud Run); **Cloud Armor** para el registro (C-4).

## IA y responsabilidad
- IA: si — Claude Code (Claude Opus 5). Alcance: bloques 1 y 2 de `specs/CM-14-Registro-usuario/tasks.md`, bloques 1 a 7 (salvo Bloque 0 y el PR) de `specs/CM-104-correcciones-OIDC/tasks.md`. Correcciones propias registradas en `Entregables/16092026_BitacoraIA_Codigo_E2.md`: `:443` en el audience, orden del `onErrorResume`, prueba que no detectaba `add`.
- Control humano: revisado por el autor— Juan David Vela Coronado;

author: jamesdh
body:
## Fixes

None

## Related

- #10 — the window-server regression this works around (destroyed windows stay in CGWindowList until the process exits). Still present on macOS 27.0; the switcher can still list a ghost until it is selected once, so the issue stays open.

## TLDR

A window closed while its Space was not current lingers in the switcher forever, because the AX liveness check only covers the current Space and that Space is only ever current for a few hundred milliseconds inside activation itself. Selecting the ghost then fronts the app's real key window and drags the display to that window's Space. Activation now takes the AX verdict at the moment the window's Space is current, tombstones a confirmed ghost, and fails with windowNotFound before SkyLight fronts anything.

## Summarized Work

- Added SpaceManager.confirmWindowClosedOnCurrentSpace, which reaches the refresh-time verdict for one window on demand (off-screen, on a current Space, absent from the app's AX window list on two reads) and tombstones it; activateWindow calls it after the instant-switch attempt and throws windowNotFound on a confirmed ghost (c9b688c, c35993d).
- Added SystemDataSource.axWindowPresence, a present/absent/unknown answer that stays unknown whenever any AX element fails to map to a window ID, so an incomplete read can never condemn a live window; the activation check requires absent on both reads (c35993d).
- Ran the check on every activation, not only after a successful DockSwipe, so a ghost whose Space is already current (stale panel row, raw CLI ID) is caught too (c35993d).
- Covered the verdict with tests: ghost on a now-current Space, minimized window, AX unavailable, on-screen window, non-current Space, incomplete mapping, second read unavailable, window arriving on-screen mid-check, Space leaving mid-check, and the presence fold (c9b688c, c35993d).

## Operational Impact

None. A confirmed ghost's activation now fails with windowNotFound and leaves the display on the ghost's Space rather than jumping to another window's Space; the ghost disappears from the switcher on the next refresh.

- Each tray has **four 5 × 1 mm outside grooves**, feeding **eight 2 mm-wide × 1 mm-high underside passages**. Their 45° roofs leave at least 2 mm of floor, with a 1 mm bearing rib between each pair. Storage floors remain closed.

body:
## Summary

- Closes #2280
- Refs #2173, #2276
- E0 on C52 proved lexical dominates `descriptor_query_batch` (~98% of hot Rails batch; max lex 16616ms / batch 16862ms; `remaining_before_handoff` 0). Dense/seal are not the problem; frozen caps stay.
- Bound packet-descriptor lexical recall to `DESCRIPTOR_LEXICAL_FUSION_WINDOW` (64, same as dense calibration) and cap per-lane FTS rows at 256 instead of expanding the full 4096 fusion pool. Ordinary full retrieval is unchanged.

## What changed

- `codestory-retrieval` planner: `DESCRIPTOR_LEXICAL_FUSION_WINDOW`
- executor: clamp Stage1Lexical `top_k` on `CandidatePayloadMode::DescriptorOnly`
- lexical index: descriptor-only `lexical_candidate_limit` + component-set bound
- focused hostile tests for the bound; changelog note

## How to review

- Confirm full-path lexical still uses `LEXICAL_FUSION_WINDOW` / `MAX_CANDIDATES`
- Confirm descriptor path never raises caps or restructures SLA sharing
- Challenge owns exact-head / hostile overlay after this draft

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p codestory-retrieval --lib descriptor_`
- `cargo test --locked -p codestory-retrieval --lib packet_descriptor_lexical_stage_uses_bounded_fusion_window`

## Risk / non-claims

- Does **not** raise 18s/180s/20s/3GiB caps

author: gigio1023
body:
## Context

The catalog has skills for commits, pull requests, and PR review comments, but none for tracker issues, and `draft-pr` explicitly excludes issue workflows. Issues written by agents tend to fail in the same ways: a long templated body, a path on the author's machine or a pile of loosely related links standing in for the actual finding, and an assignee picked by guesswork. `write-issue` covers writing, editing, splitting, and closing out issues in any tracker, with Linear and GitHub Issues specifics kept in reference files.

| Area | Default the skill sets | File |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Body | One task, one purpose sentence, three to five facts | `SKILL.md` |
| Links | Findings stated in the text, only links readers can open | `SKILL.md` |
| Assignee | The author, or empty when ownership is ambiguous | `SKILL.md` |
| Table, figure, collapse | Concise first; table or figure only when faster to read; collapse as a last resort | `SKILL.md` |
| Splitting | Sub-issues only for lumps already found in the work | `SKILL.md` |
| Tracker forms | Linear and GitHub Issues | `references/` |

## Changes

- **Body:** the skill reads the team's template and neighboring issues first and matches them. By default it leaves out acceptance-criteria sections, as-is and to-be framing, and repeated background. Research work is named as a question or a deliverable with no estimate, and results stay in the experiment log with a two or three line outcome on close.
- **Shared-document rules:** the issue text stands on its own for a teammate who was not in the session, and it carries no defensive writing: no hedges, author-protecting caveats, or lists of everything left unchecked. An unknown is named once, next to the claim it limits.
- **Links:** a link verifies a statement and never replaces it. Paths on the author's machine or a server, unpushed branches, private documents, and dead links are not usable, and local-only material is summarized in the body and reported as not yet shared. A three-step check runs on every link, including ones the user supplied and ones already in an issue being edited.
- **Assignee:** empty when the work belongs to another team, the issue is a report for someone else's triage, several owners are plausible, or nothing shows it is the author's own work. Another named person only on request.
- **Table, figure, collapse:** an overview table may follow the purpose sentence when the same few fields repeat over several items, with named columns and rows and short cells. A figure is made with `technical-diagram` when structure is the point and uploaded into the issue. A collapsed section is a last resort: the skill first cuts the detail or moves it to a comment, pull request, or shared document, because a shorter issue beats a folded one.
- **Splitting:** sub-issues are created as not started, and a rising in-progress count is raised with the user before any status change.
- **References:** `linear.md` and `github-issues.md` hold the tracker forms (containers, inheritance, relations, collapsible sections, diagrams, upload, field names). `examples.md` has seven invented drafts. `sources.md` lists the public sources with the strength of each and the rules that are local choices. The README catalog count goes from 27 to 28.

author: nghaiz
body:
Chặng 19.D: tầng **trình bày** của game CI/CD. Engine, level, bộ chấm và ô soạn YAML không đổi một dòng.

Kế hoạch: `plans/devops-learning-platform/phase-19-d-exec.md`.

## Làm gì

- **Nền hợp đồng (19.D.1)** — `buildGraphView` (producer còn thiếu của `CicdView`), `placeWorkflow` (toán thuần, không một dòng `three`), bảng mã hoá ba kênh, và hợp đồng props chung mà cả hai renderer đọc.
- **Cảnh 2D (19.D.2)** — SVG + framer-motion. Chế độ mặc định, không phải bản dự phòng: node, cạnh góc vuông, chấm chạy, đường găng tô sáng, dải môi trường chương CD, bàn phím đi được giữa các job.
- **Cảnh 3D (19.D.3)** — kiểu arena K8s. `InstancedMesh`, camera orthographic bốn góc, `frameloop="demand"`, ba bậc chất lượng tự hạ, bàn phím trong cảnh + `aria-live`.
- **HUD toàn màn hình (19.D.4 + 19.D.5)** — sân chiếm trọn màn hình, mọi bảng là lớp phủ thu được, bảng ba trục thường trực, màn chuyển tiếp giải thích trục Y đổi nghĩa giữa hai chương.

## Ba chỗ lệch khỏi kế hoạch, cả ba đo được trên mã

**Hợp đồng đặt chỗ đi qua `CicdView`, không đọc thẳng `WorkflowSpec + RunRecord`.** `contract.ts` §7 đã viết sẵn rằng `core/layout` tính vị trí *từ view đó*, nhưng `grep` ra **0 producer** — hợp đồng thiết kế rồi bỏ đó, và kế hoạch không có mục nào dựng nó.

**Node khoá theo `InstanceKey`, không theo `stageId`.** C12/C13 có `fanOut`, nên cách khoá cũ gộp `test#node20/22/24` thành một. Ô AC-D1 nguyên bản đếm theo *số stage* nên nó **xanh ngay trên chính con bug đó** — đã siết lại và bắt buộc chạy trên C13 (C12 không quạt ra trong `initialWorkflow`).

**Màn chơi dọn sang `/games/cicd/<levelId>`.** AC-D7 đòi sân rộng > 95% viewport, nhưng vỏ ứng dụng chừa 224px sidebar cho route không-immersive. `isImmersiveRoute()` chỉ nhận `pathname`, và `levelId` trước đây là React state nên bấm một màn không đổi URL — cùng một `/games/cicd` phục vụ cả hai trạng thái. `?level=` cũ chuyển hướng sang đường mới.

## Hai lỗi sản phẩm mà e2e tìm ra

Không cổng tĩnh nào thấy chúng:

1. **Bảng núm CD đóng mặc định ở chương CD** — nó là thứ quyết định kết quả (cùng YAML lời giải, đổi đường phục hồi thì mới đạt). Người chơi sẽ gõ lại YAML nhiều lượt mà không hiểu vì sao vẫn trượt.
2. **Thân lớp phủ `overflow-y-auto` không focus được** — người dùng bàn phím không cuộn được. axe đỏ thật, luật `scrollable-region-focusable` mức `serious`, trên cả hai theme.

## Nghiệm thu

9/10 ô đo được, mỗi ô mang đối chứng riêng. AC-D3 đạt **một phần**: chọn tay 2D/3D đi đúng nhánh có đối chứng dương, nhưng ca "máy không cấp được WebGL2" (`--disable-3d-apis`) cần một project Playwright riêng, chưa dựng.

```
turbo build lint typecheck test   32/32 successful
games-cicd.spec.ts                15/15
games-cicd-scene.spec.ts          10/10
tokens:check                      837 file, 0 miễn trừ mới
bundle:check                      42 route không chạm chunk three
```

## Ba thứ chưa chứng minh được

Ghi đúng như vậy, không làm mềm đi:

- **Chưa ai nhìn hai theme bằng mắt.** `mcp__playwright__browser_navigate` treo tới hết idle timeout. Thứ làm thay: kiểm cả 18 token có mặt ở `:root` và `.dark` rồi đối chiếu tỉ lệ tương phản (cặp thấp nhất 4.95). Cách đó tìm ra một lỗi đảo theme thật, nhưng không thay được mắt người.
- **`color-contrast` của axe không chạy trong jsdom.** Ô e2e có chạy luật đó, nhưng chỉ trên những gì đang hiện; lớp phủ đang thu thì không được quét.
- **Lỗ hổng hợp đồng đã ghi nợ:** `StageNodeView` thiếu `steps` (nên cấp 3 của drill-in nằm ở inspector chứ không trong SVG), `CicdGraphView` thiếu `tickSeconds`, `DagEdgeView` không có đại lượng lưu lượng.

author: mvaligursky
body:
Preparing a bake bound a black lightmap to both the color and the directional slot of every receiver, but a color only bake never rebinds the directional one. Every baked mesh instance was left holding a black directional lightmap that no shader declares, and the renderer pushed it to the scope on every draw of that mesh instance.

**Changes:**
- The bake binds the starting black lightmap only to the slots the bake writes, matching the loop that assigns the finished lightmaps. A color only bake, which is the default, now leaves one lightmap parameter per baked mesh instance instead of two.

**Performance:**
- Removes one shader parameter, and so one scope write per draw, from every mesh instance baked with `BAKE_COLOR`.

body:
Fixes #14842. Replaces #14921.

The "Second subtitle file (on video player)" dialog reset font size, bold, colour, border style and alignment to defaults every time it opened, so adjusting an already-loaded second subtitle meant setting everything again.

## Changes
- **Dialog:** new "Remember these settings" checkbox. With it on, OK saves the style to `Se.Settings.Video`, and the dialog starts from it next time. With it off, the dialog behaves as before. Cancel saves nothing.
- **Dialog:** new "Do not show this dialog again" checkbox, enabled only with remembered settings. Picking a second subtitle file then applies the saved style directly.
- **Settings > Video player:** "Show style dialog when opening a second subtitle file" brings the dialog back (same pattern as the format limit warning).
- **Font size** is stored in `AdvancedSubStationAlpha.DefaultHeight` units (like `MpvPreviewFontSize`), as a decimal, so it scales to the loaded video and round-trips to the same pixel size.
- **`SecondarySubtitleStyler`:** the style and header building moved out of the dialog so the dialog and the no-dialog path build the same subtitle. The dialog's live-preview merge branches are unchanged.

Four new English strings in the language classes; English.json is not regenerated. Changelog left to the maintainer.

author: june3474
body:
## Summary
- Forcibly skipping a video clip during a slideshow (arrow key) left BGM resuming correctly, but Kodi's own slideshow frozen on the next picture forever. Letting a clip end naturally never hit this.
- Root cause, verified against `xbmc/xbmc` master source (`GUIWindowSlideShow.cpp`): `GUI_MSG_PLAYBACK_STOPPED` (a forced skip) sets `m_bPause = true` and nothing else in Kodi clears it, unlike `GUI_MSG_PLAYBACK_ENDED` (a natural end), which clears it itself.
- `_on_clip_end` now calls `xbmc.executebuiltin("Action(Play)")` whenever `Slideshow.IsPaused` still reads true before resuming BGM. `Action(Play)` maps to `ACTION_PLAYER_PLAY`, confirmed via source (`ActionTranslator.cpp`, `OnAction`) to be a non-toggling "ensure playing" action, so this is safe to call defensively even if the read races a natural end.
- Documented as D-014 in `research.md`, including the one residual timing risk (same category as R-6/R-7) that still wants real-device (Tier 2) confirmation.

## Test plan
- [x] `ruff check .`
- [x] `ruff format --check .`
- [x] `mypy --strict .`
- [x] `pytest` (405 passed, including two new cases: the skip scenario and a regression guard proving the fix is a no-op on a natural end)

author: tomasusi
body:
## The instructions cannot currently be followed

The page tells the reader to enable the backend with:

```python
import abtem
abtem.config.set(enable_mps=True)
```

That does not work, and the verification snippet immediately below it then fails:

```
config says enable_mps = True
backend actually loaded  = False
RuntimeError: The Metal (MPS) backend is experimental and disabled by default. Set
'enable_mps' to true before importing abTEM -- it selects the library load order ...
```

`enable_mps` decides whether PyTorch is imported *before* FFTW. The two bundle separate copies of `libomp`, and a process that loaded FFTW's first crashes inside ordinary PyTorch calls — so the flag has to be read before abTEM is imported, and a `config.set` afterwards is far too late. The two routes that work are an `ABTEM_ENABLE_MPS=true` environment variable and `~/.config/abtem/abtem.yaml` (both available since abTEM/abTEM#416 taught abTEM to read its own configuration).

## Also corrected

- **Install command.** abTEM now ships an `mps` extra, so `pip install "abtem[mps]"` replaces the conda nightly line. `torchvision` and `torchaudio` were never used by abTEM — verified that neither is installed in a working Metal environment — and the `pip install scipy --force-reinstall --no-deps` line was a workaround for the conda/pip mix the extra removes.
- **"Features not currently supported will fall back to the NumPy implementation."** They do not: an operation without a Metal implementation raises and names itself. That is deliberate — a silent host fallback in a simulation package surfaces only as unexplained slowness — but the page currently promises the opposite.

## Added

Two things a reader hits immediately otherwise:

- Metal is single precision. `precision` must be `float32`, and pairing `device="mps"` with `float64` is refused rather than silently narrowed.
- Grid size matters far more than on other backends: Metal's FFT degrades sharply on sizes with prime factors above 7, which is the difference between no speedup at all and several times the CPU.

## Verification

Every command and snippet in the new section was run against abTEM with the Metal backend from abTEM/abTEM#414 — the install extra resolving, both enabling routes, the verification snippet, the `device="mps"` usage, and the float64 refusal.

Depends on abTEM/abTEM#414 for the `mps` extra and the `device="mps"` API; abTEM/abTEM#416 (already merged) for the configuration routes.

body:
## What

Two layers that keep `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` and `🤖 Generated with ...` out of the commit log:

- **`CLAUDE.md` §4.4** — states the rule, so an agent session reading the repo instructions follows it without being re-told. Says explicitly that **human** co-author trailers stay: `Co-Authored-By: <teammate>` on a pairing branch is real attribution.
- **`.githooks/commit-msg`** — enforces it mechanically. Narrow by design: matches the Claude trailer and the "Generated with" line, nothing else.
- **`.gitattributes`** — pins `.githooks/*` to LF. Checked out with CRLF on Windows, `sh` fails with "bad interpreter" and the hook silently never runs.

## Why

On GitHub the trailer renders as a second contributor on the commit. This is coursework — the log is the record of who did the work.

## Setup, once per clone

```
git config core.hooksPath .githooks
```

The hook is opt-in and `--no-verify` bypasses it, so it's a backstop, not the rule itself.

## Already-pushed history

Rewritten separately, before this PR:

| Branch | Rewritten | Verified |
|---|---|---|
| `a/resolution-replay-and-kind-tests` | 5 commits | tree byte-identical, 77 commits, authors + dates unchanged |
| `ac/app-shell-transport-merge` | `216e045` (merge commit, rebuilt with both parents intact) | tree byte-identical, 75 commits, authors + dates unchanged |

All 15 `Co-Authored-By: Amritha-M` trailers were preserved on both. Backups at `backup/coauthor-rewrite-2026-09-17/*`.

**@monish1929 — your local `ac/app-shell-transport-merge` diverged.** Commit anything unpushed first, then:
```
git fetch origin && git reset --hard origin/ac/app-shell-transport-merge
```

## Reviewer

`CLAUDE.md` has no owner in the §3.3 table. Requesting **C**. Note that **B (@Amrithaa-M) has not committed since 21 Aug**, so the §3.3 reviewer rules cannot be satisfied as written on any current PR — flagging rather than quietly skipping.

author: skavhaug
body:
## Summary

Increment 4, and the goal line of the plan set out in increment 1: **a constrained Delaunay triangulation over a polygon with holes.** 261 non-comment production lines across six files, **465/465 tests**.

Design: [`docs/increments/04-cdt.md`](docs/increments/04-cdt.md). Six commits with the red→green trace intact, and the first increment to run all four steps of the `CLAUDE.md` §3 loop — architect, tester, developer, **reviewer**.

## The design was overturned by reading the source

The brief handed this increment a hazard it was told it owned: Detria stores spans without copying, so the wrapper had to build **one** scratch index buffer per triangulation, each chain followed by its repeated first index. Increment 1 invented that scheme; increment 3 built `closed_index_buffer_size` to serve it.

`@architect` read `createConstrainedEdges` instead of trusting the brief. At `detria.hpp:3549-3562`, when `front() != back()`, `prevVertexIdx` is seeded with `polyline.back()` — **so the first emitted edge is `(back, front)` and open polylines are auto-closed.** Verified by probe: `{0,1,2,3}` and `{0,1,2,3,0}` give identical output.

So `Pslg::indices_of(c)` goes straight into `addOutline`. No closing index is materialised anywhere, the whole scheme is **deleted rather than protected**, and `closed_index_buffer_size` — which had nine test references across two suites — is removed as a function that will never have a caller.

Because this is now a dependency on library *behaviour* rather than documented API, it is paid for with a characterisation test and a written fallback.

## What the tests found that the design got wrong

- **The entry point's postcondition was `out.ok() != out.message.empty()`** — false in *both* cases, so the assert fired on every call. `@tester` transcribed it literally and three suites aborted before running. Should be `==`.
- **"Every constraint edge appears in the output" is false for legal input.** A breakline outside the outer ring, or inside a hole, is legal in a `Pslg` — which promises no disjointness and no nesting — triangulates `Ok`, and appears in no interior triangle. Measured. Now scoped to in-domain constraints, with the exception pinned by its own fixture.
- **Two degeneracy rows were missing**, both reachable from a valid `Pslg`: `HoleNotInsideOutline` has two arms, and a closed-loop breakline spelled with a coincident closing vertex is `DuplicatePointsFound`, not `Ok`.

18 mutants, 18 killed. Two initially reported false kills — they died to `-Wunused-parameter` under `-Werror` before any test ran — and were re-run in a form the warnings don't catch rather than banked.

## What `@reviewer` found that every gate passed over

`src/cdt/detria_backend.cpp` opens with *"See `lib/detria/README.md` for why that is a rule"* — and that README still said detria is included by exactly one TU. **The pointer landed on a document contradicting the line that sent the reader.** The rule is one TU per backend, none in any header; the gate script was updated and the README wasn't.

Also: the governance job's comment carried the same stale facts; `project_structure.md`'s `cdt/` listing omitted a header *this PR created*, one line short of its own stated scope; and two of three `testing.md` fixes hadn't landed — including the carve-out protecting the characterisation test above, whose absence the design had predicted in one sentence.

## Checks no gate makes

- [x] **Red-step scaffolding is gone.** Verified by scan; the CMake entries needed no green-commit edit.
- [x] **Every prose claim re-checked.** Four blockers found and fixed in `8cc672f`.
- [x] **LOC reconciled:** 261 measured against a ~342 estimate — *under*, and the 4a/4b contingency correctly did not fire. The status mapping the design named as the likely overrun site came in at 32 lines.

## Verification

- [x] Release + `ctest` — 465/465
- [x] Debug + `-fsanitize=address,undefined -fno-sanitize-recover=all` — 465/465, including the multi-ring ASan fixture
- [x] `-ffp-contract=off` — 465/465
- [x] Governance gates, including `check_detria_boundary.py` reporting detria in exactly the two permitted TUs
- [x] Zero warnings at `-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Werror`

## Notes

- **The seam is proved by the link line**, not asserted: `test_cdt_backend_seam` links neither `terrain_cdt` nor `terrain_predicates`, so a generic path naming `DetriaBackend` fails to *link*. Verified in the generated link line.
- **`cwTriangles` defaults to `true`** and must be passed `false`, or the constrained-edge mask transposes bits 0↔2 and triangles come out clockwise.
- **Largest open risk:** `DuplicatePointsFound` is a hard Detria failure on input a valid `Pslg` accepts, and real terrain data is full of coincident vertices. Unfixable here — a coordinate key needs increment 5's snap grid.

## Merge

- [x] Merge commit, not squash — the red commits must stay ahead of the green one.
