author: onamfc
body: Stacked on #55 (shares `buildAppSchemeUrl()`); retarget to `main` once that merges. ## What was wrong The mobile scheme interstitial built its JavaScript like this: ```js var schemeUrl = "${safeSchemeUrl}" + hash; setTimeout(function() { window.location.replace("${safeFallbackUrl}"); }, 1500); ``` with `safeSchemeUrl` being the configured value with `"` → `"` and `<` → `<`. That is HTML escaping applied inside a JavaScript string literal: a quote is neutralised (as `"`, which the script then sends to the app verbatim), but a **backslash** before the closing quote or a **line terminator** in the value ends the literal early and takes the whole script with it — no auto-open, no fallback timer, a page that sits there. `deep_link_parameters` are percent-encoded on the way in, so they can't carry either; a custom scheme URL is operator-configured free text and can. Separately, `app_scheme` is validated at write time as a scheme *token* (`^[a-z][a-z0-9+.-]*$`), which does not exclude `javascript`, `data`, `vbscript`, `file`, `blob` or `about`. A link configured with one of those produced an interstitial whose `href` and `window.location` were `javascript://…`. ## What changes **No configured value in the script.** Both URLs reach the document only as escaped attribute values on the two buttons that already existed; the script reads them back with `getAttribute('href')`. The title goes through the shared `escapeHtml` (an `&` was left raw before). The redirect module's local `escapeHtml` — a byte-for-byte duplicate of the one in `link-safety.ts` — is removed in favour of the shared one. **Executable schemes are treated as no scheme.** `safeSchemeHref()` in `link-safety.ts` accepts anything with a scheme except the six above (matched on the raw string, case-insensitively — WHATWG parsing of unknown schemes is too permissive about whitespace and case for this). On the response path a link whose `app_scheme` fails it takes the store / web-fallback route like a link without a scheme: no interstitial, no launchpad "Open in app" button, no such URL in a `Location` header. The assembled URL is checked again at the interstitial so a custom scheme URL naming an executable scheme is refused even when `app_scheme` itself is fine. `safeHref()` was the wrong tool for this — it admits only http(s), the one family a scheme link is not. Behaviour for every well-formed link is unchanged: same page, same buttons, same auto-open, same 1.5 s fallback. The `store`-mode byte-identity test in #55 pins the absent and explicit setting to the same body, and continues to. ## Verification `tsc` clean, **380 tests pass** (7 new in `redirect.interstitial.test.ts`). The one test that changed assertion pinned the old `var schemeUrl = "…"` line; it now pins the `href`. Covered: the script contains neither URL and reads both from the DOM; a custom scheme URL carrying `"`, `\`, `` and an `` produces exactly one `` in the document and an escaped `href`; `Cats & Dogs <3` in the title renders as `Cats & Dogs <3`; `app_scheme: "javascript"` with `deep_link_path: "/%0aalert(1)"` gets a 302 to the store with no interstitial; `custom_scheme_url: "javascript:alert(1)"` is refused at the interstitial; `safeSchemeHref` accepts `demo://`, `com.example.app://` and `https://` and rejects each of the six schemes plus a scheme-less string.

author: amirradjou
body:
## Summary

Brings the thesis experiment tree (`cnsim-updated/cnsim`, branch `processingtime`, 1 unpushed commit + 62 dirty paths, last touched 2025-07-15) into the fork as the reproducible artifact behind *Simulation-based Evaluation of Transaction Finality in Bitcoin using CNSim* (MSc, York University, 2025) and the CCS26 submission. Until now the configs, nodelists, attack refinements and analysis scripts that produced the RQ1-RQ3 figures existed only on one machine.

The annotated tag **`thesis-v1.0-artifact`** is pushed and points at 9093f51, the head before the review fixes below; it should be re-pointed (see "Review fixes").

## What changed (10 commits, source only)

- [x] **Attack model** (`MaliciousNodeBehavior.java`): target transaction is kept out of both pools once the hidden chain is revealed (`isAttackCompleted`), filtered at every attack step, and the attack is abandoned when the public chain outgrows `MAX_CHAIN_LENGTH` without the hidden chain being longer. `MaliciousNodeBehaviorTest` gets a real `setUp` and two executable tests (one of them made meaningful in the review fixes).
- [x] **`workload.targetTransaction`** (`BitcoinNodeFactory.java`): attack target read from the new key, falling back to `workload.sampleTransaction[0]`. The Persian debug `println` from the experiment tree is removed.
- [x] **`sim.initialMiningPoolTransactions`** (`BitcoinMainDriver.java`): mining-pool pre-seeding loop, key optional with default 0 (every thesis config sets 0).
- [x] **Configs**: `bitcoin-config/thesis.bitcoin.*` replaced by the June-2025 10-sim pilot set (12 scenarios, each differing from base in one parameter, the two throughput variants in `net.throughputMean` + `net.throughputSD`), plus `nodelist-malicious{1,2,3}.csv`; new `new-config/` + `new-nodelist/` = the final 30-sim set behind every figure. `application.properties` / `bitcoin.application.properties` synced (inline `# comments` moved to their own lines because `java.util.Properties` would have read them as part of the value).
- [x] **Analysis scripts**: `tools/beliefAnalysis/*` updated + `finality_modified.py`, `finality_3plot.py`; `tools/hashpower_helper.py` (blocks-found based); `run_configs.sh`.
- [x] **Post-processing that produced the figures** (from `Thesis/PostProcessing/test-Jul8` and `Thesis/ScriptLogs/Juul15-malicious`, matched to the thesis PNGs by checksum): `tools/postprocessing/rq3-settlement/`, `tools/postprocessing/rq2-malicious/`, and the RQ1 block-interval validation under `tools/validation-rq1/` with its two small derived CSVs.
- [x] **`examples/thesis/README.md`**: scenario -> config -> run ID -> script -> figure map, the two config sets explained, and the list of out-of-git logs.
- [x] Two new network tests (`PropagationTimeTest`, `NetLogOverflowTest`) from the experiment tree; one wrong expected value (1 GB @ 1 Mbps = 8e6 ms, not 8e9) corrected.

## Decisions to be aware of

- `sim.initialMiningPoolTransactions` and `workload.targetTransaction` were hard-required (`Config.getPropertyInt` -> `System.exit`) in the experiment tree; they are made optional here so the 14 pre-existing configs are not broken further. Behaviour is identical for every thesis config.
- `Main.R` keeps `library(nptest)` (the experiment tree dropped the line but still calls `np.boot`).
- Not committed: `.project` IDE filter change, `TestPropagationCalculation.{java,class}` scratch file at the repo root (duplicated by `PropagationTimeTest`), five generated PNGs and `Rplots.pdf` in `tools/beliefAnalysis/`.
- The experiment tree also had `tools/beliefAnalysis/BeliefLog - 2024.09.13 13.56.59.csv` staged for deletion; that is left for the hygiene PR.
- Finding worth knowing: the attacker fractions quoted in the thesis text (16.61 / 29.28 / 64.73 %) are those of the June malicious configs, while the runs behind the figures used the `new-config` set (16.78 / 29.68 / 66.25 %). In both sets the attacker's power is `node.maliciousHashPower` from the config (`node.maliciousPowerByRatio = false`), and the fraction is that value over the honest nodelist rows plus itself; the two sets differ in `node.maliciousHashPower`, `workload.targetTransaction` (malicious.first) and `node.maliciousRatio`, not only in the nodelists.

## Not in git: archive these as a release asset for the tag

All under the `Thesis/` working directory on the author's machine (next to `cnsim-updated/`); none is source and every file is far over 5 MB:

| Path | Size |
|---|---|
| `cnsim-updated/cnsim/new-thesis-log/` (30-sim runs, all 12 scenarios, RQ3 + RQ1 base) | 25 GB |
| `cnsim-updated/cnsim/new-thesis-log-newer/` (30-sim malicious re-runs, RQ2; includes `malicious-logs.zip`, 690 MB) | 12 GB |
| `cnsim-updated/cnsim/new-thesis-log2/` | 2 GB |
| `cnsim-updated/cnsim/thesis-log/` (10-sim June pilots + `analysis_results*`) | 9.8 GB |
| `PostProcessing/` (per-scenario log copies + every analysis attempt) | 186 GB |
| `ScriptLogs/` (incl. `Juul15-malicious/` final RQ2 outputs) | 76 GB |
| `validation-RQ1/EventLog - 2025.06.18 11.36.16.csv` (+ Blockchair TSVs) | 1.45 GB |

The specific run IDs used for each figure are listed in `examples/thesis/README.md`, so a minimal archive is `new-thesis-log/<scenario>/<run id>/` for the nine RQ3 runs + `new-thesis-log-newer/malicious*/<July 14 run id>/`.

## Verification

- `JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk mvn -B -ntp verify` -> `Tests run: 101, Failures: 0, Errors: 0, Skipped: 0`, `BUILD SUCCESS` (was 86 on master).
- Smoke run of all 12 `new-config/*.properties`, all 12 `bitcoin-config/thesis.bitcoin.*.properties` and `bitcoin.application.properties` with `sim.numSimulations = 1`, `sim.terminate.atTime = 600000`: every one exits 0 and writes a BeliefLog (0.5-3 s each; `bitcoin.application` 13 s because of its 1000 pre-seeded transactions).
- `grep` for absolute personal paths in every copied script: none.

## Review fixes (2 commits on top of 9093f51)

- [x] **f80930e docs(thesis)**: `examples/thesis/README.md` no longer claims the two config sets are identical apart from three keys or that the attacker fractions "come from the nodelists". It now lists the malicious-config differences (`node.maliciousHashPower` all three, `workload.targetTransaction` 40000 vs 20000 in `malicious.first`, `node.maliciousRatio`), explains that `BitcoinNodeFactory` takes the attacker's power from `node.maliciousHashPower` and shows the formula that reproduces 16.61/29.28/64.73 % (June) and 16.78/29.68/66.25 % (final). - **Nova flag `--no-profile`** (pula agents de perfil + `default_agent`).
- **Uninstall seguro**: agents por marcador, vendas por tree-compare (`sameTree`), `default_agent` só se era nosso.
- **Update snapshot-based das vendas**: atualiza skill nossa mesmo desatualizada (comparando com `.bento/skills` anterior), preserva modificada pelo usuário.

Review por task (7 tasks, TDD) + review final whole-branch; 3 fixes aplicados e re-revisados:

author: darshani8
body:
No issue — this is the presentation pack the owner asked for: recorded videos of the Student, Faculty (mentor), Main Admin and Alumni portals with live typing and spoken narration, the workflows that link them, and a PowerPoint deck built from the same screenshots.

## Why

**Symptom** — nobody could show REEP working end to end without driving it by hand: there was no recording of the four portals, no walkthrough of how a student's claim reaches the mentor, or how the office's approval turns an application into a signed-in mentee, and no deck to present it with.

**Mechanism** — `tools/demo/record-walkthrough.mjs` drives the RUNNING portal in a real Chromium, at 1920×1080, through every role's screens while Playwright records the session: slowed-down keystrokes you can watch, a drawn cursor, a chapter card per segment, a caption bar saying what each screen is for, and a camera move that scales the page in around each box as it is typed into and back out before the next click. Every caption is spoken: the recorder logs the moment it appears, synthesizes the words (Piper's `en_US-lessac-medium`, offline; `DEMO_TTS_CMD` takes any engine) and holds the next caption until the line would have finished; `mix-narration.mjs` lays the clips onto the video at those times. Six segments: `student`, `faculty`, `admin`, `alumni`, `interlinked` (student claims a skill and asks for a 1:1 → mentor verifies, records the meeting, applies for leave → the office writes SWOC, posts a job, sanctions the leave → it all lands back on the student's screens) and `onboarding` (public form → approve → the emailed link's address/code/password steps → first sign-in → faculty assigned → the mentor sees the mentee; the two mails are read off the API log, which is where the console transport writes them). `render.sh` makes H.264 MP4s and a combined file; `build-deck.cjs` builds the deck from the screenshots the recorder saved; `reset-dev-db.sh` re-seeds the dev database so every recording starts from the same state; `fetch-voice.sh` pulls the voice model.

**Why this fix and not the obvious alternative** — a screen recorder driven by hand cannot be re-run after the next redesign, and mock-ups drift from the product the day they are drawn. A scripted recording against the real app is reproducible: the next person re-runs three commands and gets fresh videos, screenshots and slides for whatever the screens look like then.

**Deliberately not done** — the mock interviewer is shown up to the round picker and never started, because the speech engine needs the cloud and a failed connection is not a demo; nothing in the product itself changed. The 23-minute combined MP4 that `render.sh` also produces is not committed, for size only.

**What is in `docs/presentation/`** — `video/student.mp4` (3:59), `faculty.mp4` (3:05), `admin.mp4` (5:17), `interlinked.mp4` (5:39), `onboarding.mp4` (4:35), `alumni.mp4` (0:58), all 1920×1080 with narration and none above 24 MB; `REEP-portal-walkthrough.pptx` (32 slides with speaker notes); `screens/` (86 screenshots, one per screen visited); `README.md` (what each video covers, the logins used, how to re-record). All recorded from one pass on a freshly seeded dev database with zero skipped steps.

**Found on the way, not fixed here** — copying `apps/api-py/.env.example` to `.env` verbatim turns the blank `SES_*` lines into their trailing comments (pydantic-settings keeps them as the value), so mail silently goes to boto3 and fails instead of the console outbox; the recorder's onboarding walk only worked once those three lines were quoted blank. That belongs in its own change to the example file plus a guard.

---

- [ ] It adds one, and **every** new call site passes `carries_student_data=` as an explicit keyword.

The recorder's own check is its console output: a control it cannot find is reported as a `SKIP` line rather than silently dropped from the video, and the committed videos come from a pass with none.

## Schema

author: harper-joseph
body:
Stacked on #168 — **base that branch, not `main`**, so the diff here is just the settle-correctness work.

Three gaps that make a per-page-type settle config unsafe to author. All found while reading a
measured handoff on Kohl's PDPs.

## 1. `navigation.finalDomStable` — a plateau AFTER the gates

`domStable()` runs *before* the `waitFor` gates, so a gate can release the snapshot onto a DOM that
is still filling. Measured on a real product page: gated on the reviews widget, serialized with
**107 product links instead of 547**. Reviews were complete and correct — the recommendation rails
simply had not arrived when the earlier plateau ran, and the review gate then let the snapshot go.

The alternative is a `waitFor` rule per widget, forever, and the page is only ever as complete as
the widget someone remembered to name. A plateau after the gates is the general form of the same
check, so this should be preferred over growing the rule list.

It is also the **only** plateau that runs under `scroll.settleUntilStable`. That branch calls
`scrollSettle()` and never calls `domStable()` at all — so a config using it has had no
DOM-stability check of any kind.

Default `false`, so existing deployments render byte-identically. The regression test builds the
exact shape (a gated widget plus a later one) and pins 0 rail items without it, 40 with.

## 2. Per-gate telemetry

`waitForResults` on the job and on the `renderOnce` result — `name`, `satisfied`, `count`,
`minCount`, `waitedMs`, for every rule whose scope **matched**.

A gate that never satisfies is invisible today: it times out best-effort, the render succeeds, and
nothing anywhere says a rule spent its whole `timeoutMs` finding nothing. That is both a silent tax
on every matching render and a silently missing guard — and when you are authoring one settle
profile per page type, "this rule never fires on catalog pages" is exactly what you need to see.

**Deliberately a local surface only** — not added to the posted variant metadata. This is for
confirming a config locally before it goes anywhere near the fleet, so it costs the wire nothing.

`WaitForRule.name` is the (optional) label; it falls back to the selector.

## 3. `waitFor[].pageTypes` now throws at config load

Rule scopes AND together and no job carries a declared page type, so a rule naming `pageTypes`
matches nothing, never runs, and the content it guards is quietly absent from every render. Named
page types were abandoned deliberately. Failing loudly at load is the only point at which anyone
finds out.

## Also

Validates the two `navigation` booleans that were never checked (`finalDomStable`,
`skipSettleWhenNonIndexable`).

249/249 tests pass; lint and format clean.

author: vheun
body:
- Commands for one key (e.g. `cameraOn`) can arrive out of order under network delay. A late, older command had a different id, so it ran and overrode the newer one ("press Stop, the camera turns back on").
- Command ids already carry their mint time (`${Date.now()}-<random>`). `consumeRemoteSignal` now ignores a command minted before the last executed one for that key — without recording it, so the newer command stays the processed one.
- **Fallback:** the comparison only applies when BOTH ids have the timestamp shape. Legacy ids, ids from other tooling and a missing last id keep the previous rule unchanged; the 60-minute expiry is untouched. Message format unchanged — compatible with older clients in both directions.
- Applies to every signal consumed this way (cameraOn, setAssignedId, restartDevice, clearCache, runSpeedTest, setFreezeKioskCoordinates).
- **Measured** (real control path, paired A/B, random 0–4 s delivery delay): wrong final camera state 13/20 before → 0/20 after; 0/20 for both without delay.
- Note: mint times come from the sending client's clock, so between different operators clock skew decides conflicts that fall within the skew.

author: xavientois
body:
## Description

The Turn panel's legacy fallback rendered the block's flat totals as a single expandable model row labelled **"Models"**, which reads like a model name, and in Credits mode showed "N tokens / 0 credits" because it summed credit fields that are never populated on that path.

Legacy charges are now modelled explicitly (`LegacyCharges`) and rendered as a header-only INFERENCE USAGE row:

- `Breakdown { totals, credits }` → "N tokens / $X" in Dollars mode, "N tokens / Y credits" in Credits mode (hidden if `credits` is unknown).
- `CreditsOnly(credits)` → "Y credits" in Credits mode; section hidden in Dollars mode.
- `Unknown` → section hidden.

The records path (real per-model rows) is unchanged. The legacy path no longer fabricates a `RequestModelCharge`; the header and tooltip render from `LegacyCharges` directly.

### Where the data comes from

**New path — turn has `Message.RequestMetadata` records** (`turn_panel_records`): one record per request, with per-model charges carrying both cents and credits.
- Live: streamed by the server as an `AddMessagesToTask` client action at request end.
- Rehydrated: the records are ordinary task messages, so they come back with the task list — local SQLite `agent_tasks` or cloud `ConversationData`. Same rendering either way.

**Legacy path — no complete records for the turn** (`turn_panel_data`, latest turn only):
- Live: `StreamFinished.request_charges` → `charged_usage_for_last_block` (tokens + dollars; the server's `RequestChargesToProto` sets no credit fields), and `StreamFinished.request_cost` → `credits_spent_for_last_block` (credits). Both reset on each user-initiated request.
- Rehydrated from local SQLite: both fields are persisted in `AgentConversationData.conversation_usage_metadata`, so the last block renders as it did live.
- Rehydrated from cloud (GraphQL): the conversion (`crates/graphql/src/api/ai.rs`) sets both fields to `None` — the schema exposes only cumulative figures — so the turn is `Unknown` and the section is hidden. Unchanged by this PR.

### Reading order

1. `app/src/ai/agent/request_metadata.rs` — `LegacyCharges` shapes.
2. `app/src/ai/agent/conversation.rs` — `turn_panel_data` builds `LegacyCharges`.
3. `app/src/ai/blocklist/usage/request_metadata_turn_view.rs` — `legacy_inference_header_text`, tooltip.
4. `crates/persistence/src/model.rs` — `ChargedUsageTotals::inference_cost_in_cents`.

author: morshedvarzandeh
body:
**Merge this first.** The Lemonergy Data API deployment fetches this repository by pinned commit and runs the exporter this pull request adds. Nothing else can be deployed until it is on `main`.

## What it adds

`tools/export_catalog_snapshot.py` writes one deterministic `catalog.json` from `contrib/`:

- every record validated against the contribution schema and the quantity registry, reusing `tools/validate_contrib.py` rather than a second copy of those rules;
- sorted by product UID, with the source commit and a SHA-256 content hash;
- refuses an invalid record, a duplicate UID, an empty library, a dirty `contrib/` tree, and any path outside `contrib/`, so `review/`, `seed/` and patent candidates can never enter it.

One invalid contribution refuses the whole export. A snapshot that silently dropped a record would look complete and be wrong.

## Why it belongs here

The file is what the hosted API is built from, and what anyone can rebuild locally to check what that API serves. It is a data tool like the other exporters in `tools/`; this repository still distributes no API server.

## Validation

- `python -m unittest discover -s tests -p 'test_*.py'` — 46 tests pass, including the new `tests/test_export_catalog_snapshot.py` (sorting, hashing, byte-for-byte repeatability, and each refusal above).
- Run against the real library at `3bd20c0`: 2,170 records, 12,335 observations, exported and hashed in one pass.

## Not covered

The export has not been run inside the deploy workflow yet. That happens on the first run of "Deploy Lemonergy paid edge" in test mode, after the matching battery-design pull request merges.

author: moerai
body: Fixes #1443 ## Root cause The root `check` script led with `biome check --write --error-on-warnings .`, and the CI **Static checks** job runs exactly `npm run check`. With `--write`, biome reformats the offending files inside the runner and exits 0. The rewrite is discarded when the runner exits, so the drift stays in the repository while the job reports success — a gate that cannot fail. `releasability.yml` had already worked around this by hand-inlining a read-only biome step plus a verbatim copy of the remaining check sub-scripts, with a comment naming the hazard. That copy had since drifted from the real chain: it was missing `check:entry-graphs` and `check:claude-sdk-platform-lock`. Root `AGENTS.md` also states the local check and CI run the same commands and must stay in sync. With autofix in the shared script they disagreed by construction: a contributor running `biome check` without `--write` saw a failure CI could never show. ## Change - `package.json`: `check` now runs `biome check --error-on-warnings .` (read-only). New `check:fix` keeps the autofix form (`biome check --write --error-on-warnings . && npm run check`) for local use. - `.husky/pre-commit`: calls `npm run check:fix`, so the hook's autofix-then-verify behavior is unchanged. - `.github/workflows/releasability.yml`: drops the inlined duplicate and calls `npm run check` directly, removing the drift source. - `changes.md` / `.husky/changes.md`: tracker entries for the two upstream-tracked paths. No dependency, lockfile, or release-version changes. ## Test `scripts/ci-format-gate.test.mjs` (runs under `npm run test:scripts`) parses `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, resolves the script the Static checks job actually invokes, and asserts: 1. that script's biome invocation carries no `--write`/`--fix`; 2. running it against a drifted file inside a biome-included path exits 1 and leaves the file byte-identical; 3. an explicit local autofix script still exists. It derives the flags from the live script string rather than hardcoding them, and resolves the biome binary from `node_modules` instead of a package-manager runner, so it behaves the same under npm, bun and pnpm. ### RED (before the fix) ``` $ node --test scripts/ci-format-gate.test.mjs AssertionError: CI biome invocation rewrites files and exits 0 on drift: biome check --write --error-on-warnings . AssertionError: expected drift to fail. stdout: Checked 1 file in 33ms. Fixed 1 file. AssertionError: expected a check:fix script for local autofix ℹ tests 3 ℹ pass 0 ℹ fail 3 ``` ### GREEN (after the fix) ``` $ node --test scripts/ci-format-gate.test.mjs ✔ runs a biome form that reports drift instead of rewriting it ✔ fails on unformatted input with the CI biome invocation ✔ keeps an explicit autofix script for local use ℹ tests 3 ℹ pass 3 ℹ fail 0 ``` ## Verification on the real command A deliberately unformatted file was placed under a biome-included path and the actual CI command was run: ``` $ npm run check EXIT=1 × Some errors were emitted while running checks. # fixture afterwards: export const qaDrift = 1; (unchanged) ``` The same fixture under the previous form, for contrast: ``` $ biome check --write --error-on-warnings Checked 1 file in 38ms. Fixed 1 file. EXIT=0 # fixture afterwards: export const qaDrift = 1; (silently rewritten) ``` Clean-tree `npm run check` exits 0 on current `main` content (4262 files, "No fixes applied", 6 pre-existing infos that `--error-on-warnings` does not escalate), so making CI read-only does not turn `main` red. ## QA CLI smoke via `.agents/skills/senpi-qa/scripts/cli-smoke.mjs --self-test` — 8/8 passed, including the credential-isolation assertion that the real `auth.json` is unchanged: ``` [PASS] --help prints usage with flags — code=0 [PASS] --version prints a version — 2026.9.17-2 [PASS] --list-models lists built-in models offline (no API) — lines=1681 [PASS] unknown option is reported, not silently ignored — code=1 [PASS] real auth unchanged cli-smoke.mjs --self-test: 8/8 passed ``` This change touches build/CI tooling only — no source under the release-managed runtime packages — so the CLI channel is the applicable surface. The pre-commit hook exercised the new `check:fix` path when this commit was created. ## Note on the local full-suite run `npm test` fails on this machine at `test:scripts` with 6 failures in `scripts/probe-native-grep.test.mjs`, all `Internal Error: cargo metadata failed to run`. These are pre-existing and environmental: `cargo`/`rustc` are not installed here, the file is byte-identical to `main`, and a pristine `main` checkout (d35d45d1c) with none of these changes reproduces the identical 6 failures. All other 288 script tests pass, including the new gate test. CI has the Rust toolchain and will run the full suite. --- ## Summary by cubic Fixes #1443 by making the root `check` script run Biome read-only, so the CI format gate can actually fail. `check` used `biome check --write`, which silently rewrote format drift in the CI runner and exited 0; now it reports drift and exits non-zero. **Changes** - `check` now runs `biome check --error-on-warnings .`; the new `check:fix` script keeps the autofix form for local use. - The pre-commit hook runs `check:fix`, preserving its existing autofix-then-verify behavior. - `releasability.yml` now calls `npm run check` directly, removing an inlined duplicate that lacked `check:entry-graphs` and `check:claude-sdk-platform-lock`. - Adds `scripts/ci-format-gate.test.mjs` to enforce that the CI biome invocation cannot autofix, that drift makes it fail, and that an explicit local autofix script exists. Written for commit 5b996e7fab48cdce2e88b1c2c04b8fbb57d63230. Summary will update on new commits.

author: evanion
body:
The typed builder exists so keys are valid keys and autocomplete resolves. The React binding dropped that at the provider, so every `useCan` in a tree lost it.

## The premise in the brief was wrong

I said `Access<Shopper, Record<'listing', Listing>>` failed to satisfy the bare `Access` prop. It does not. `Access` declares `can`, `canMany`, `canFields` and `capabilities` with method syntax, so parameter comparison is bivariant and `strictFunctionTypes` never reaches them. On TypeScript 6.0.3 the assignment compiles both directions and `<PolicyProvider access={typed} />` compiles.

The defect is that nothing was checked. `useCan('lsiting', 'update')` compiled on `feat/acl`.

## The shape

`createPolicyContext(access)` returns `{ PolicyProvider, useCan, useCanMany, useCanFields, useCapabilities }` with `Sub` and `R` closed over. Inference works from the argument, so a consumer writes no type parameter and restates nothing.

Each call makes its own React context, so two policies nest. The provider it returns also publishes to the shared context, so a component holding the imported `useCan` keeps reading underneath it.

## Two alternatives, both compiled before rejecting

**Generic `PolicyProvider<Sub, R>`.** The provider infers at the JSX site and the hooks get nothing: `createContext` fixes its type at creation and `useContext` returns that type regardless. Every call site then restates the policy, either `useCan<typeof shop, 'listing'>('listing', …)` because there is no partial type-argument inference, or curried, which is a second call in every component.

**Module augmentation.** The best call sites of the three, and it works for one policy. With two in one program: `TS2717 Subsequent property declarations must have the same type`, and `TS2345 Argument of type '"listing"' is not assignable to parameter of type '"ticket"'` in files that declared nothing. A library shipping a policy takes the single slot from every app that installs it, and a monorepo type-checking two apps gets whichever loaded.

## The untyped path is unchanged

`hydratePolicy(matrix)` with the imported provider and hooks needs no type argument and no factory, signature for signature. The only other source edit is re-exporting `AnyObjects`, which the new signature's default names.

## What did not survive the code

The object check disappears when the row type is declared `extends Record<string, unknown>`. That is the consumer's type rather than the design, and it is a passing case in the type tests and a sentence on `api.mdx`.

`useCapabilities` stays `Record<string, Decision>`. It is keyed by permission key while `R` holds object kinds, and actions are plain strings no builder collects.

A docs review caught a wrong runtime claim I wrote: an unknown key in open mode throws `UnknownObjectKeyError`, it does not answer `unknown-action`. That is the `closed: true` answer.

## Verified

21 type tests, 12 runtime, 10 example. `libs/react-acl/examples/typed.tsx` authors the same policy the other five run against and `examples.test.tsx` asserts `shop.matrix` deep-equals the documented one, so the two forms cannot drift.

`getting-started.mdx` went 109 words over the prose budget, so the new section came back down rather than the allowance going up.

author: mk-aify
body:
## What and why

`ClientTelemetryAllowlist.RouteNamePattern` accepted any string built purely from letters, digits,
slash, hyphen, underscore and colon, so a resolved route parameter (for example a phone number
standing in for `:orderId`) passed the filter exactly like a real route template — the character
class could not tell `orders/:orderId/draft` from `orders/9876543210/draft`; it reliably rejected
only a full URL. Tightened it to a segment-aware pattern: each `/`-separated segment must now be a
static word (letters/hyphens) or an explicit `:placeholder`.

Separately, the batch envelope's own `RouteName` (`ClientTelemetryBatchRequest.RouteName`) never
passed through `ClientTelemetryAllowlist.Filter` — that only ever sees an event's per-attribute
bag — so it reached `ClientTelemetryHandler.Emit`'s structured log line straight from
client-controlled JSON, unvalidated, despite its own doc comment saying "never a URL" and
`docs/nfr/data-classification.md` §5.18 forbidding personal route-parameter values in telemetry.
Added `ClientTelemetryAllowlist.SanitizeRouteName(string?)` and call it in `Emit`, substituting
`null` on failure — the same way a rejected attribute is dropped rather than the whole batch being
refused.

## Linked issue

Refs #387

Security notes: no new secret, no new personal-data field. This is a redaction-tightening change to
existing telemetry logging — see item 6 below.

## Risk and rollback

Low risk: the change only narrows what `RouteName` string survives into a log line. A route name
that previously logged verbatim may now log as `null` if it does not match the segment pattern
(static word or `:placeholder` per segment) — this is the intended behaviour, not a regression, and
matches how an unallowlisted event attribute is already dropped rather than logged raw. No HTTP
response shape, status code or schema changed, so there is nothing for a client to notice. Revert is
a plain `git revert` of this commit; no migration, no data to restore.

## Follow-ups

`docs/nfr/data-classification.md` §5.18 promises a redaction test that posts a batch carrying a
customer name, phone number, measurement value, stack trace and a URL, and asserts none of six
sentinels appears in any emitted log record. That test doesn't exist yet — there is no
infrastructure anywhere in the test suite today for asserting on emitted structured log content
(`ClientTelemetryEndpointTests` only asserts HTTP status/body). Building a log-capturing test sink
is a separate, sizable piece of work in its own right and is already tracked under the open #387
checklist, so it is not duplicated here.

---

## Definition of Done

- [x] 1. Linked to issue #387 (sub-issue of #52); change is scoped to the `RouteName` validation gap
      only, no unrelated edits. Branch is this session's exempted automation branch
      `claude/compassionate-montalcini-37360f` (the `claude/` reserved prefix the pull-request
      policy check itself exempts from the `feat/eXX-fYY-<slug>` naming rule).
- [x] 3. Unit tests added for the tightened regex and the new `SanitizeRouteName` helper
      (`ClientTelemetryAllowlistTests`); architecture tests still green; existing
      `ClientTelemetryEndpointTests` integration coverage still passes end to end. No E2E journey is
      new or critical-path here (backend-only log-sanitisation change, no UI). Synthetic data only —
      no fixture carries a real customer name, phone number or measurement.
- [x] 6. No secret or personal data is added anywhere. This change *is* the redaction review: it
      closes a gap where `RouteName` — both the event-level attribute and, after this PR, the
      envelope field — could carry a resolved value (e.g. a phone number in place of `:orderId`)
      indistinguishable from a legitimate route template under the old character-class-only check.
      Reviewed against `docs/nfr/data-classification.md` §5.18. Threat-model reference: the closest
      existing entry is **TM-022** ("Logs and telemetry" / Information disclosure, controls CTL-40,
      CTL-41) in `docs/security/threat-models/authentication.md` — there is no telemetry-flow-specific
      threat-model document yet, since the threat-model programme opened in #555 has not reached
      Observability. This change closes the concrete instance of TM-022's risk for this flow; a
      dedicated telemetry threat-model entry remains open work, tracked under #387.
- [x] 9. This evidence checklist is complete, and this pull request depends on the linked issue,
      branch name and checklist being verified by the "Pull-request policy" required check.

author: jakebromberg
body:
## Summary

Epic #2534 shipped the account-audit trail (#2535/#2536/#2537) auditing the token-based password-reset flow (`/request-password-reset`, `/reset-password`) but allowlisting the live OTP-based equivalents, flagged as review finding M5 on PR #2545 and shipped as-ratified with an explicit "needs a re-decision" comment. The re-decision (2026-09-17): OTP password resets are audited.

- Moves the three password-reset-flow OTP endpoints from `ALLOWLIST` to `FLAT_MOUNTS`' public partition in `apps/auth/audit-coverage.ts`, with path-derived dotted action slugs (`email-otp.request-password-reset`, `email-otp.reset-password`, `forget-password.email-otp`) distinct from the token flow's `forget-password` slug, and the existing `email-lookup` subject strategy (unchanged machinery — no new extraction logic, submitted email never persisted).
- Rewrites the OTP allowlist comment block: the password arms are resolved (moved out); the two email-change OTP arms (`/email-otp/change-email`, `/email-otp/request-email-change`) stay allowlisted pending their own re-decision.
- Updates `docs/authentication.md`'s audited-surface description. `docs/pii.md` needed no change — it doesn't enumerate individual audited flows.

Verified against the installed better-auth (`node_modules/better-auth/dist/plugins/email-otp/routes.mjs`) that all three endpoints take `email` in the request body, so no deviation from the issue's plan was needed.

## Review fixes

A first review pass on this PR found zero High, four Medium, four Low findings. All addressed. M3 went through a second pass after the first fix (below) turned out to still be wrong.

- **M1 (real bug, fixed)** — `resolveUserIdByEmail` (`apps/auth/account-audit-middleware.ts`) looked up `eq(user.email, email)` on the raw submitted value. better-auth lowercases the email in every OTP/token handler and again in `findUserByEmail`, storing it lowercase at create time, but the OTP arms' request schemas are plain `z.string()` (not `z.email()`), so a mixed-case submission (`DJ@wxyc.org`) reached this lookup unchanged. The reset itself still succeeded (better-auth normalizes internally), but the audit row recorded `subject_user_id` NULL — a fully anonymous row for a successful credential change on a public mount where actor is also never resolved. Fixed by trimming + lowercasing before the lookup, matching better-auth's own normalization. This also fixes the already-shipped `/request-password-reset` mount, which shares the same helper. New regression test drives a mixed-case, whitespace-padded email and asserts `eq` was called with the normalized value and that a subject still resolves.
- **M3 (operational regression, fixed — twice)** — the three OTP paths had been added to `rateLimitedPaths`, which shares ONE `rateLimit()` instance (10 requests / 15 min, keyed on `X-Real-IP` only) with `/auth/sign-in` and the rest of the brute-force tier. An OTP reset is a hand-copied-code flow, so two DJs resetting before a shift from the control room's shared egress IP could drain that bucket and lock out everyone's sign-in for 15 minutes with no operator recourse — the exact failure mode this repo already rejected for station-signup (BS#2361). First fix: gave all three OTP paths one dedicated `otpPasswordResetRateLimit` (60s/120), copied from `checkRequestBanRateLimit`'s shape. That was itself wrong — the donor's justification ("cheap per call") never held for two of the three paths. `/email-otp/request-password-reset` and `/forget-password/email-otp` both call `sendVerificationOTP`, which fires a real SES email; `emailOTP()` sets no `resendStrategy`, so there is no internal resend cooldown and every call sends a fresh email. 120/min was a mail-bomb vector against any address a caller names, plus an SES cost/reputation hit — ~180x looser than the token-based `/request-password-reset`, the identical operation at the identical cost, which sits at 10/15min. **Corrected**: split into two limiters. The two email-sending paths now share a dedicated 10/15min instance matching the token flow's tier (still its own instance, not folded back into `rateLimitedPaths` — that coupling is what the original M3 fix was about). `/email-otp/reset-password` sends nothing and is already attempt-bounded server-side (`allowedAttempts: 5`), so it keeps a separate, looser 60s/30 sized for hand-entry across a shared control-room IP. New regression test asserts the two tiers are mounted on different limiter instances so a future edit can't silently re-merge them.
- **M4 (drift-check gap, fixed)** — the coverage check was one-directional: every reachable `auth.api` endpoint must be audited-or-allowlisted, but nothing asserted the reverse. better-auth marks `/forget-password/email-otp` `@deprecated`; when it's actually removed in a future major, the forward check stays green while the `FLAT_MOUNTS` row, the `app.ts` limiter string, and the documented slug all silently become dead strings that can never fire — the same defect class the BS#2537 M1 fix closed for the dead `/auth/forget-password` string. Added `findDeclaredMountsMissingFromAuthApi` (arm 3, `apps/auth/audit-coverage.ts`), wired into `scripts/check-audit-route-coverage.ts`, asserting every `FLAT_MOUNTS.path` and every non-hand-written `ADMIN_ACTIONS` key is still reachable. Two hand-written Express routes (`provision-user`, the six station-signup ops) reuse `ADMIN_ACTIONS` for the runtime dispatcher's convenience but were never real `auth.api` endpoints — marked with a new `AdminAction.handWritten` flag so arm 3 doesn't false-positive on them (verified: it did, on `/admin/provision-user`, before the flag was added). Manually verified the check fails on a temporarily-added bogus `FLAT_MOUNTS` path, then reverted. Unit tests added for arm 3, including the `handWritten` exclusion.
- **M2 (comment only, fixed)** — `/email-otp/send-verification-otp` accepts `type: 'forget-password'` and will mail a working reset code, an unaudited twin of the request step this PR audits, writing the same verification row `/email-otp/reset-password` later consumes. The previous allowlist comment read as though the whole flow were out of scope, concealing the gap. Rewritten to state plainly that this endpoint is unaudited for the reset-request case, that reset *completion* is audited on every path, and why it isn't fixed here (the table is path-keyed and this endpoint also serves the deliberately-allowlisted sign-in OTP flow — auditing it correctly needs body-discriminated classification, a mechanism extension out of scope for this re-decision). Tracked as a follow-up sub-issue of epic #2534: #2551.
- **L2 (fixed)** — the rate-limiter test pins used a bare `.toMatch(/\/auth\/email-otp\/reset-password/)` against the whole `app.ts` source, which would pass on the literal appearing anywhere at all (a comment, the wrong limiter, a dead string) and asserted nothing about registration. Rewritten to the idiom the file's own station-signup tests already use: extract the exact source block for each of the two OTP limiters and match within it (updated again for the M3 split, above).
- **L3 (fixed)** — the new per-mount tests in `tests/unit/auth/account-audit-middleware.test.ts` built the test request's path from `mount.path` — the exact same field the dispatcher's Map is keyed on, so the test would pass for any value there, including an un-stripped `/auth/...` (the H1 mount-path-stripping failure shape). Hardcoded the mount-stripped literal paths instead, the way this file's admin-side tests already hardcode `'/set-role'` rather than deriving it.
- **L4 (no change, documented)** — kept the slug `forget-password.email-otp` as-is: it's the faithful path-derived form and decision 14 is ratified. Added a sentence to `docs/authentication.md`'s OTP paragraph instead, noting that (a) `forget-password` and `forget-password.email-otp` are distinct flows despite the shared prefix, so a `LIKE 'forget-password%'` query would wrongly merge them, and (b)

author: copilot
body:
The failing Actions job came from a mismatch between the repository’s Python CI runner and the new Trust Wallet adapter test: CI executes `unittest`, while the test file depended on `pytest`. This change rewrites that test to use the standard-library test stack already used elsewhere in the repo.

- **Root cause**
  - `tests/test_trust_wallet_adapter.py` imported `pytest` and used `pytest`-specific helpers, causing CI to fail during test discovery with `ModuleNotFoundError`.

- **Change**
  - Convert the Trust Wallet adapter test module to `unittest.TestCase`.
  - Replace `pytest.raises` with `self.assertRaises`.
  - Replace `monkeypatch` usage with `unittest.mock.patch.dict` for environment isolation.

- **Result**
  - The test now matches the repository’s existing Python test harness and can be discovered and executed by the current GitHub Actions workflow without adding a new test dependency.

```python
with patch.dict(
    os.environ,
    {"TW_ACCESS_ID": "access-test", "TW_HMAC_SECRET": "secret-test"},
    clear=False,
):
    credentials = TrustWalletAdapter().credentials()
```

author: lagunavinicius
body:
Revisão: @enzilla

## Resumo

Faz os testes e o clippy do workspace `server/` voltarem a passar na `main`, sem mudar comportamento. Consertar o delta revelou que **quatro bumps do Renovate já tinham quebrado a compilação de crates inteiros**, não só os testes.

### O que não compilava
- **delta (testes):** o rand 0.10 removeu `thread_rng` e `distributions`. Migrado para `rand::rng()`, `rand::distr::Alphanumeric` e `RngExt`. Os dois `PartialMember` de `message_send.rs` ganharam `show_tag: None`.
- **revolt-files:** o #144 subiu o `usvg` para 0.48 e deixou o `resvg` em 0.44, e o `resvg::render` passou a receber tipos de outra versão. Fixado em `usvg = 0.44`.
- **january / autumn / gifbox:** o #145 subiu o `utoipa-scalar` para 0.3, que exige `utoipa` 5, e o workspace está no 4. Fixado em 0.1.
- **autumn:** o digest do `sha2` 0.11 não implementa `LowerHex`, então `{hash:02x}` não compila. Agora a string hex é montada à mão. A saída é a mesma de antes, e um teste confere contra o sha256 de `""`.
- **pushd:** no `web-push` 0.11, `WebPushError::Unauthorized` virou variante de tupla.

### Checkout no Windows
Com `autocrlf`, os `.txt` embutidos por `include_str!` chegavam com CRLF, e o `split('\n')` guardava `"password\r"`. Com isso, uma build local no Windows aceitava senha vazada, e o `fail_invalid_password` falhava. `.gitattributes` fixa LF nesses arquivos. No Linux do CI o defeito não aparecia.

### Clippy
Cerca de 110 avisos zerados. A maior parte foi pelo `clippy --fix`, revisado à mão. Nas três trocas de `if` dentro de braço por guarda de `match`, o braço seguinte já era no-op. `sort_by` decrescente virou `sort_by_key` com `Reverse`, e os dois são estáveis. A única remoção de código é `calculate_server_permissions`, que era privada e não tinha chamador. Onde silenciar exigiria mudar tipo público ou serialização (enums grandes, o `Result` do `main` do voice-ingress, os `insert_attachment` do autumn), ficou `#[allow]` explícito.

## Verificação
Em Docker (`rust:1.98`), na rede do `vortex-teste` (mongo, keydb, rabbit, maildev):
- `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings`: ok. Com `--all-targets`, também ok.
- `TEST_DB=REFERENCE cargo nextest run --workspace`: **177/177**, em três corridas seguidas.

⚠ Os testes fixam `localhost:14025/14080` (maildev) e `127.0.0.1:14009` (S3). Dentro do contêiner, essas portas foram redirecionadas com `socat` para os serviços. O `minio/mc` não baixa, então o minio subiu à parte com as credenciais do `Revolt.toml`, e os testes de S3 criam o próprio bucket. Numa corrida anterior, `login::tests::success` falhou uma vez e depois passou isolado e nas três corridas completas. Parece corrida no canal de eventos `global`, compartilhado entre testes paralelos. Não mexi nisso.

## Pendência
O Renovate vai propor de novo `usvg` 0.48 e `utoipa-scalar` 0.3. Os dois só sobem junto com `resvg`/`tiny-skia` e `utoipa` 5, respectivamente, e vale agrupá-los no `renovate.json`.

author: aznikline
body:
## Change

Adds a Lean 4 + Mathlib formalization for **JSP-000554** (Erdos's question on rough numbers between consecutive primes; resolved asymptotically by Gafni–Tao, arXiv:2508.06463): between consecutive primes, is there an integer whose least prime factor is at least their gap?

`submissions/jsp-000554/` contains the pinned Lean project:

- `jsp_000554` — two-sided answer: an exceptional gap exists (`(7, 11)`) and a gap containing a rough number exists (`(3, 5)`, `m = 4`); `jsp_000554_not_forall` refutes the universal reading.
- `twin_gap_rough` — every twin-prime gap `(p, p+2)`, `p ≥ 3`, contains the rough number `p + 1`.
- `cousin_gap_exceptional` — every cousin-prime gap `(p, p+4)`, `p > 3`, is exceptional.
- `sexy_gap_iff` — complete mod-15 characterization: a gap-6 prime gap with `p > 5` is exceptional iff `p % 15 ∈ {1, 8}`.
- `jsp_000554_least_exceptional` / `jsp_000554_first_rough_gap` — kernel-checked (`decide`) minimality: `(7, 11)` is the least exceptional gap with `p ≥ 3`; `47` is the least start of a gap `≥ 4` containing a rough number (`49 = 7²` in `(47, 53)`).

Scope: the Gafni–Tao asymptotic theorem is explicitly not claimed; the submission formalizes the existential/finite content of the catalogue statement.

Pinned proof source: https://github.com/aznikline/jsp-000554-lean @ `7267199304c4430235de4947634900e8355ba1d4`

## Record or policy impact

No records, candidates or published decisions are modified. Adds one submission directory only. No conflicts or recusals known.

## Checks

- [x] All text is in English; candidate text does not announce an award.
- [x] No recipient identities, private contacts, payment details or deliberations appear in files or commit history.
- [x] Verification artifacts: `verification/sha256.txt` records SHA-256 checksums of all source files; axiom report and toolchain pins in `verification/`. No external archival ID is claimed.
- [x] `python scripts/manage.py validate` and `python scripts/manage.py links` pass.

- [x] `verify.sh` runs end-to-end: `lake build --wfail`, warnings-as-errors Lean compile, prohibited-token scan, bundled `leanchecker` kernel replay. `#print axioms` reports `[propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]` for all theorems; no `sorry`/`native_decide`/custom axioms.

author: dklassen
body:
Fixes a rendering artifact in exported resume PDFs: a section divider
left stranded at the bottom of a page with a band of white space under
it, and the heading it introduces pushed onto the next page.

## Cause

`renderBlock`'s `ThematicBreak` case does its own page-break check,
because `Line()` draws directly and doesn't participate in fpdf's
`SetAutoPageBreak`. That part was already understood. What it got wrong
is that it reserved only the rule's own height
(`lineHeight(baseFontSize) * 1.5`).

So a rule near the bottom of a page passes its own check and draws, and
then the heading right after it, rendered at a larger font and therefore
a taller line, trips fpdf's auto page break and moves to the next page.
The divider is left behind as the last mark on the page.

## Evidence

Confirmed on real content before changing anything. In
`assets/12/resume.md` the rule drew at y=94.82 as the last mark on page
2, with the last line of text at y=114.90 and the bottom margin at 56.7,
and "Education" pushed to page 3. `assets/15/resume.md` had the same
shape. After the fix the rule and its heading sit together at the top of
page 3 (rule at y=727.51).

Minimal synthetic reproduction: 26 filler paragraphs, then `---`, then an
H2.

## Fix

Reserve the rule's height plus the first line of whatever follows it, via
a small `firstLineHeight` helper that uses the heading's own font size
when the next sibling is a heading, the base size otherwise, and zero
when the rule is the last block in the document.

## Test

The property asserted is "a thematic break is never the last mark on a
page", swept across document lengths from 1 to 45 filler paragraphs
rather than pinned to the single count that reproduced it. Pinning 26
would encode today's spacing constants into the test and let it go green
for the wrong reason as soon as any of them changed. This follows the
caution already recorded in `decisions.log` about not pinning fpdf's
internal point math in tests.

## Scope note

This does not remove the white space at the bottom of that page, and the
band is marginally larger than before (58pt rather than the 38pt below
the old stranded rule): moving a divider to the next page necessarily
ends the previous page earlier. What it removes is the orphaned rule
floating in that space, which is the part that reads as a rendering error
rather than an ordinary section break.

A ranked sweep of vertical gaps across all 29 currently drafted documents
confirms nothing larger is outstanding: those two 58pt bands are the
largest gaps anywhere, and every other gap is the 51.8pt spacing a `---`
divider is designed to produce.

## Verification

`go build ./...`, `go test ./...`, `go tool golangci-lint run ./...`
(0 issues), `go tool task fmt:check` all clean. All 29 drafted documents
re-rendered before and after and compared.

Packet: `research/publication_packets/moment_common_row_edges/`. Durable scope/provenance: `accepted-evidence.md`. Reproduce: `python3 scripts/test_moment_common_row_edges.py`.

Do not resubmit this accepted theorem. #293 integration, #292 compactness, #289 catalogue, #291 support and every other owned branch/pending proof are unchanged. A future route proof can invoke this result for each genuine one-row exchange; it still must establish such exchanges exist and bound their number.

author: zhaokai-mgzn
body:
Closes #4052

关联 #4043（母单，本条对应其 C 组第 1 条「会话记录分不出工具『调了』与『成了』」）。

## 判据（改前 / 改后，基线 origin/main @e58d5f0d）

```
$ cd backend/ai-agent-service && grep -c tool_results app/api/chat.py
0          # 改前
7          # 改后
```

改前落库的只有 `metadata.tool_calls`（工具名 + args = 「调了什么」）；工具**结果**只经 SSE
`SSEEvent.tool_result(...)` 发给前端、**从不落库** ⇒ DB `session_messages.metadata` 无法区分
「调了 order_create」与「order_create 真落库」。

## 改法

- `app/api/chat.py`：`tool_result` 分支按**同名调用 FIFO 配对**收集
  `[{"tool","success","error"}]`，随收尾 `save_message(...)` 落进 `metadata.tool_results`，
  与 `metadata.tool_calls` **逐项对齐**（`tool_results[i]` = 第 i 次调用的成败）。
- `app/memory/session_memory.py`：`save_message` 新增**可选**参数 `tool_results`
  （默认 `None` ⇒ 不写该键，向后兼容）。
- 3 个 `SessionMemory` 替身签名同步补齐（原因见「未做项」）。

## 红证（行为级：真 SSE 桥 → 真 save_message → 断言落库 metadata 内容）

新增 `backend/ai-agent-service/tests/test_tool_results_metadata.py`（5 条，`# case_ids: CH-010, CH-011`）。
断言对象是**DB 拿到的 metadata JSON 字符串**（只把 DB 会话换成记录 SQL 入参的替身），
不是替身记下的调用入参。CH-010 = chat.yml 里正是记录本缺陷假绿形态的那条用例
（「order_create 两次都返回 tool_execution_failed，订单一条没落，用例却因『工具名出现在
tool_calls』判 100%」，#3361/#3778）。

改前（把两个源文件换回 origin/main 版本、跑同一个测试文件）：

```
$ .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_tool_results_metadata.py -q --no-cov
5 failed in 0.15s
E AssertionError: 落库 metadata 缺 tool_results ⇒ 区分不出「调了」与「成了」:
  {'tool_calls': [{'tool': 'order_create', 'args': {'customer_name': '甲'}}]}
```

更直接的形态证据（同一轮里「失败调用」 vs 「成功调用」的落库 metadata）：

```
改前  FAILED_META    = {'tool_calls': [{'tool': 'order_create', 'args': {'customer_name': '甲'}}]}
改前  SUCCEEDED_META = {'tool_calls': [{'tool': 'order_create', 'args': {'customer_name': '甲'}}]}
改前  IDENTICAL = True      ← 逐字节相同：取证无从区分订单是否真落库

改后  FAILED_META    = {..., 'tool_results': [{'tool': 'order_create', 'success': False, 'error': 'tool_execution_failed'}]}
改后  SUCCEEDED_META = {..., 'tool_results': [{'tool': 'order_create', 'success': True, 'error': None}]}
改后  IDENTICAL = False
```

## 非执行调用（#3976 同口径）与脱敏

- `tool_not_found`（工具未注册、**从未执行**）**既不进** `tool_calls`（#3976 既有语义），
  **也不进** `tool_results` —— 不得把未执行的调用记成「执行结果」。
  顺带修掉同名多次时的错配：剔除的是**与本次结果配对的那一次**调用（按到达顺序），
  不是「最后一条」（旧实现是 LIFO ⇒ 红证测试第 3 条在改前正是红在这条错配上）。
- 只落元信息三键：**不放** `result.data` 载荷与用户 PII；`error` 文本先过既有脱敏层
  `_mask_for_customer`（C 端脱敏、B 端照实，沿用既有口径，不新增第二套脱敏策略）；
  `success` 判定保守 —— 只有明确真值才算 `True`，缺字段一律 `False`（宁可少报成功）。
- 代码收口执行（`base_skill` 8.4：模型没发起调用、由代码执行写工具）只有结果、没有
  `tool_call` 事件 ⇒ 结果照样落库、且不挤掉同名调用的配对位（测试第 4 条钉住）。
  语义分工：`tool_calls` = **模型发起**的调用；`tool_results` = **实际执行**的结果。

## 净行数（相对 origin/main @e58d5f0d，两点 diff `origin/main..HEAD`）

```
backend/ai-agent-service/app/**            +51  −4   net +47
全部改动（含新增测试 233 行）                +300 −6   net +294
```

## 门禁结果

```
./verify-all.sh gate         → ✅ 1 通过 / 0 失败 / 0 未就绪
   （gate 内部日志：Growth Gate ✅ 全部通过；新增测试 0 处弱断言；
     B/C 两端评测覆盖体检 ✅）
./check-ui-regression.sh     → ✅ UI 无回退（关键文件与 main token 一致）
ai-agent 全量单测（pytest -q）→ 4526 passed, 20 skipped, 0 failed（172.99s, exit 0）
./contract-check.sh          → ❌ intent 归属契约违规 3 项 —— **改前即红**且与本改动无关
   （本 PR 未触及 intent / skill 配置，纯 ai-agent 会话落库路径）
```

## 未做项 / 不确定的地方

- **不改**：SSE 事件协议、admin-api、历史回放渲染、前端；不碰 S5（`_read_cached` fail-loud）等其它包。
- `metadata` 会随 `GET /history` 的 `messages[].metadata` 整包透传（该字段本来就整包透传
  `tool_calls`/`interactive`），前端类型未声明、也未消费该键 ⇒ **不构成契约变更**；
  把 `tool_results` 呈现在回放 UI 属后续独立改动。
- **替身签名漂移**（本 PR 实测踩到并已修）：`tests/` 下 3 个 `SessionMemory` 替身是**显式签名**，
  生产签名新增参数后，真实调用会抛 `TypeError` 被 SSE 桥的 `try/except` 吞掉 ⇒
  **assistant 消息静默不落库**（本轮 `test_business_verification` 红 1 条、
  `test_e2e_chat_flow` 红 2 条验证了这条链；`test_integration_multimodal` 未红但签名同样落后）。
  本 PR 已同步这 3 个替身；但「替身签名 vs 生产签名」目前**没有语义门禁**
  （`app/api/chat.py` 在 `.github/qa-exemptions.yml` 里是**既有**豁免，本 PR 未新增任何豁免），
  建议单独开单加签名一致性守卫 —— 不在本 PR 做。
- `tool_not_found_relocked`（`base_skill` 里另一个「未执行」变体）仍按 #3976 既有口径**不**从
  `tool_calls` 剔除，会以 `success=False` 进 `tool_results` —— 不产生新的假绿
  （它如实说明这次调用没成），是否一并按「未执行」处理留给 #3976 族裁定，本 PR 不扩大范围。

author: ayushnangia
body:
## Summary

`session.branch` (the interactive `/branch` path) can leave a durable, partial or empty child session row behind when the transcript copy fails mid-way. This passes `compensate=True` at that call site so the committed child row is deleted when its copy did not complete — the same rollback merged follow-up #107562 applied to seeded sessions, and which that PR's description already assumed applied to branch children.

## Root cause

`_persist_branch` (tui_gateway/methods_session.py) commits the child session row first, then copies the parent transcript in bounded 500-row chunk transactions, then writes the title. On any copy failure it raises — but only deletes the child row when the caller passed `compensate=True`.

Of the two callers, only the desktop seeded path (`_seed_branch_row`) passes it. The interactive `session.branch` handler (methods_session.py:2003) uses the default `compensate=False`, so a failed copy leaves the committed row behind:

- with zero messages (failure before the first chunk commits), or
- with a truncated partial transcript (failure after one or more committed chunks — injected after the first committed chunk, a 500-of-1200 row child survived).

#107562 (merged 2026-09-10) describes the same cleanup for branch children — "The row is now deleted when the copy did not complete, the same compensation `_persist_branch` applies to branch children" — but that flag was never actually set on the `session.branch` call site. A surviving row is not just clutter: it defeats the lazy first-prompt seed (`_ensure_session_db_row` is INSERT OR IGNORE, so the seed never lands) and shows a truncated/empty branch in lineage listings.

## Changes

One keyword at one call site:

```diff
             _persist_branch(db, new_key, old_key, title, history, source=source, cwd=_session_cwd(session),
                             profile_name=profile_name_for_home(home) or _current_profile_name(),
                             copy_fields=_BRANCH_COPY_FIELDS,
-                            title_source="user" if params.get("name") else "derived")
+                            title_source="user" if params.get("name") else "derived",
+                            compensate=True)
```

The compensation machinery itself is unchanged and already maintained by #107562 review (including its disk-full exception, where the delete cannot land and the row is left for the recovery paths). The desktop seeded path keeps its existing explicit `compensate=True`.

## Validation

- New invariant test `tests/tui_gateway/test_branch_copy_failure_cleanup.py`: drives the real `session.branch` handler against a real SessionDB (subclassed so the `chunk_rows` recursion flows through the injected failure), with 1200 synthetic messages and the copy failing after the first committed 500-row chunk. **Fails on unfixed main** ("partial branch child survived copy failure"); passes with this change.
- `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_branch_copy_failure_cleanup.py tests/tui_gateway/test_seeded_branch_title_routing.py tests/tui_gateway/test_seeded_session_create.py` → 7 passed / 0 failed.
- Broader slice: `scripts/run_tests.sh -j 2 tests/tui_gateway/test_tui_gateway_server.py -k 'branch or seeded'` → 10 passed / 0 failed.
- Direct seam probes (fault injected at the real `append_messages_batch` seam, temp `HERMES_HOME`, synthetic data, verified import origins): before the fix a mid-copy failure leaves a durable child row with 500/1200 messages; with `compensate=True` (this change) the same failure leaves no child row. Logs: probe output with both boundaries and the red/green runs are archived locally.
- `git diff --check` clean.

## Scope and limits

- Covers the `session.branch` call site only; the seeded path was already compensated. Together the two callers are the complete caller inventory of `_persist_branch`.
- Verified on macOS with synthetic data and subprocess-isolated temp homes; the injected failure is an exception at the production seam, not a real disk-fault test. The disk-full compensation exception (`is_disk_full_error`) is inherited unchanged from #107562's design.
- Self-review labeled: this is my own verification, not external review. An OPEN PR (#107037) touches the same helper for a different defect (timestamps/origin_json on the seed path); no overlap with this change's hunk or semantics.
- Credit: the compensation design is #107562's / the #93959 review's; this PR only completes it on the call site it missed.

body:
기능 #136. Foundry `apf.public.license-obligation-gate`를 privacy 단계의 digest-pinned 합성 통제로 결속합니다. 모든 운영 권한은 false이며 병합·배포·실결제를 허용하지 않습니다.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Very large payment-adjacent governance and CI surface area, but policies and evidence consistently fail-closed with no enabled money movement or production paths; main risk is review burden and misinterpreting CI green as operational approval.
> 
> **Overview**
> This PR turns the repo from a minimal stub into an **ARKAON-controlled, `UNREGISTERED_SYNTHETIC_ONLY`** payment-platform bootstrap: expanded README/docs, Korean governance PR template, `CONTRIBUTING`/`SECURITY`, workspace manifest, and a long tail of **fail-closed JSON policies** (regulatory registry, external blockers, synthetic ledger/payment lifecycle, webhooks, reconciliation, operator packets, patch-draft promotion through activation dry-run metadata).
> 
> It adds a **GitHub Actions CI** job that compiles Python, runs unit tests, validates governance manifests, executes many `scripts/run_*_evidence.py` harnesses, checks whitespace, and uploads deterministic `build/*.json` evidence plus SHA-256 sidecars as artifacts.
>

Better Auth rejected the schema at initialization, which surfaced as an admin build error, and any new account row — sign-up or account linking — was refused. The schema now matches what better-auth writes, so account rows are accepted again; applying the included migration makes the database agree. ## What caused this **Affected:** [Deployment `ticketeur-admin`](https://console.polylane.com/ticketeurs-workspace/resources/vercel%23team_CXFJYsfbWRiNplRC8EE3jQGM%23earth%23vercel.deployment%23dpl_G9isENqzT548zKrf3aBmNdrK8NEM?ref=github.autofix-pr) · Vercel account `team_CXFJYsfbWRiNplRC8EE3jQGM` **Log lines that fired the check** | Level | Count | Log line | Last occurrence | | --- | ---: | --- | --- | | ERROR | 2× | `admin:build: 2026-09-17T16:46:25.717Z ERROR [Better Auth]: Drizzle schema mismatch` | Sep 17, 2026, 16:46 UTC | | ERROR | 1× | `admin:build: note: If this column came from Better Auth 1.7.0 through 1.7.2,` | Sep 17, 2026, 16:46 UTC | | ERROR | 1× | `admin:build: follow the upgrade guide before removing it:` | Sep 17, 2026, 16:46 UTC | | ERROR | 1× | `admin:build: https://www.better-auth.com/docs/guides/1-7-upgrade-guide` | Sep 17, 2026, 16:46 UTC | ## Why this fix The admin production deployment `dpl_G9isENqzT548zKrf3aBmNdrK8NEM` (sha `4fcd6753`) logged `admin:build: ERROR [Better Auth]: Drizzle schema mismatch` twice at 2026-09-17T16:46:25Z, followed by the note `If this column came from Better Auth 1.7.0 through 1.7.2,` and the upgrade-guide link. The 1-day window holds 177 events (8 ERROR, 7 WARN). The error traces to `account.issuer`. Migration `0016_account_issuer.sql` added and backfilled that column for better-auth 1.7.0–1.7.2, where account lookups keyed on it, and the Drizzle schema declared it `NOT NULL`. The installed `better-auth` / `@better-auth/core` resolve to 1.7.5, where the 1.7 upgrade guide states the account schema is unchanged from 1.6 and new rows no longer write `issuer`. The `@better-auth/drizzle-adapter` inspects the Drizzle schema at init and reports a required column it never writes as `unexpected-required-column`; the same check blocks account inserts. Removing the column (and its compound unique index) from the schema is the guide's own remedy for Drizzle users. I reproduced the mechanism against the repo's real schema with better-auth 1.7.5: the pre-change schema produced `[{"kind":"unexpected-required-column","table":"account","column":"issuer"}]` and the post-change schema produced `[]`. The `Drizzle schema mismatch` line stops firing once the schema no longer declares the column. The change is safe: `issuer` is not read or written anywhere in the application after the upgrade (only the admin seed script wrote it, updated here), so no caller depends on the field; dropping a nullable-or-constraining column is reversible, and the accompanying migration drops the index before the column, which is the order the guide requires. The migration must be applied for the account-write path to recover — see below.
Causal chain - **Signal** (log template): admin:build: ERROR [Better Auth]: Drizzle schema mismatch - **Surfacing site**: dpl_G9isENqzT548zKrf3aBmNdrK8NEM (vercel.deployment, ticketeur-admin) at Giftobafaiye/Ticketeur:packages/auth/src/server.ts#createAuth -> @better-auth/drizzle-adapter registerSchemaCheck / findDrizzleSchemaProblems - **Mechanism**: The Drizzle schema declares account.issuer as NOT NULL with no default; Better Auth 1.7.3+ never writes that column, so the drizzle adapter's init-time schema check reports it as an unexpected-required-column and logs `[Better Auth]: Drizzle schema mismatch` (the same check would reject account inserts). - **Producer**: @ticketur/db account schema (packages/db/src/schema/auth.ts#account), at Giftobafaiye/Ticketeur:packages/db/src/schema/auth.ts#account - **Trigger**: better-auth upgraded past 1.7.3 (repo now pins ^1.7.5) while the schema retained the 1.7.0-1.7.2 issuer column added by migration 0016 - **What happens to the failed unit today**: drizzle-adapter registers a schema check at init (checksSchema -> registerSchemaCheck); a required-but-unwritten column is reported and blocks account writes. Migrations are applied separately via `pnpm --filter @ticketur/db db:migrate` (drizzle-kit migrate), not during build. - **Cadence check**: 2 ERROR rows in one build (~16:46:25Z); 1d window 177 events (8 ERROR, 7 WARN); both deployments on sha 4fcd6753 - **Blast radius**: unknown other resource(s), unknown other tenant(s); data at risk: No account rows are lost, but every new account row (sign-up, OAuth account linking) is rejected while account.issuer stays NOT NULL. - **Producer evidence**: - packages/db/src/schema/auth.ts (HEAD): issuer: text('issuer').notNull() plus uniqueIndex('account_issuer_account_id_unique').on(t.issuer, t.accountId) - packages/db/drizzle/0016_account_issuer.sql backfills issuer and sets NOT NULL (the 1.7.0-1.7.2 column) - pnpm-lock.yaml resolves better-auth/@better-auth/core 1.7.5; manifest declares ^1.7.5 - Reproducer: BEFORE schema -> {"kind":"unexpected-required-column","table":"account","column":"issuer"}; AFTER schema -> [] - Better Auth 1.7 upgrade guide: 'New rows no longer write issuer, so a NOT NULL column rejects every sign-up and account link.'

author: thorewi
body:
Session data go into a text column, but a session may legitimately hold binary values (a WebAuthn challenge, a raw token). Those bytes are not valid UTF-8, so MySQL either rejects the write (1366) or - without strict mode - truncates it at the first invalid byte. A truncated blob cannot be decoded, so every request carrying that cookie then dies with 'Failed to decode session object' until the session expires: the whole application, not just the feature that wrote it.

Binary payloads are now stored base64 encoded behind a 'b64:' prefix that no session serializer can produce; text payloads are stored as before, so existing rows keep working.

## summary
convert promotion workflows from direct merge-and-push to pr-based approach, and add the stable→rhoai promotion workflow.

## description
- convert the existing `promote-main-to-stable.yml` from direct merge-and-push to a pr-based approach that creates or updates a promotion pr with a commit log, conflict check status, and merge instructions.
- add weekly cron schedule (sunday midnight utc) alongside manual `workflow_dispatch` trigger for main→stable.
- narrow permissions from `contents: write` to `contents: read` + `pull-requests: write` since the workflow no longer pushes directly.

- add new `promote-stable-to-rhoai.yml` workflow following the same pr-based pattern, triggered on-demand only via `workflow_dispatch` (cron schedule commented out for future enablement).
- both workflows follow the [models-as-a-service reference implementation](https://github.com/opendatahub-io/models-as-a-service/blob/main/.github/workflows/promote-main-to-stable.yml).
- both workflows are idempotent — if an open promotion pr already exists, it is updated in place rather than duplicated.

author: johnnyt
body:
**This is a MIXED pull request: a `lib/` half and a `docs/adr/` half, in two
commits.** They are one change because the second is caused by the first, and
separating them would put a false statement on `main` for as long as the
follow-up took. Each half is summarised on its own here, for a reader who sees
only one of them.

- **`a2cdbf8`, the code half** - renames
  `priv/schemas/element-document.schema.json` to
  `priv/schemas/screen-document.schema.json` and carries every reference with
  it. Unchanged since it was reviewed; the rebase below moved it but did not
  edit it.
- **`79cb6e7`, the record half** - a dated Note by addition at the foot of
  `docs/adr/0002-element-document.md`, re-labelling the three citations in
  that record that read the schema by its earlier path. Added after the
  rebase revealed them.

---

# The code half

Renames `priv/schemas/element-document.schema.json` to
`priv/schemas/screen-document.schema.json` and carries every reference with
it. The file kept its pre-reframe name while its own title and description
already said screen document; a screen's children are nodes, and this closes
that vocabulary in the file's name.

`git mv` records it as a rename (100% similarity), so the schema's content is
untouched.

## What moved

- `lib/riddler/corpus.ex` - the `@schema_files` entry.
- `test/riddler/corpus_test.exs` - the `@document_schema` module attribute.
- `test/mix/tasks/riddler_corpus_test.exs` - two hits: the expected
  emitted-path list and the separate `File.exists?` assertion on the emitted
  path.
- `changelog.d/rd-mnp.md` - a `### Changed` fragment. The emitted schema path
  is an observable change for anyone reading the corpus, which is what
  `changelog.d/README.md` asks a fragment for.

The per-file case-count map in `test/riddler/corpus_test.exs` is NOT touched;
only the `@document_schema` line in that file changed.

## Rebased onto `main` at `4208433`

This branch was written against `e7d76bf` and sat open while twenty commits
landed on `main`. It has been rebased onto `4208433` ("Narrows two pieces of
prose to what the code does"); the old head `53828e8` was replaced by
`a2cdbf8` with `--force-with-lease` against that old head, on this branch
only.

**Nothing conflicted.** Three of the twenty commits touch the two files the
code half also touches:

- `9d4b652` and `fc69b8d` both edit `lib/riddler/corpus.ex`, but at the
  runner and root-building lines, not at the `@schema_files` list entry this
  change rewrites.
- `77f76d0` rewrites the retired-spelling guard in
  `test/riddler/corpus_test.exs`, but the block it rewrites is the walk and
  its tests, not the `@document_schema` attribute line.

So git replayed the commit with no conflict markers and no resolution was
needed; nothing was resolved keep-both and nothing was dropped.

**The code half's change is unchanged; its diff text is not byte-identical,
and `cmp` will say so.** Both diffs are 2299 bytes and they differ at char
392, line 12. The whole divergence is two `index` lines - the blob hashes for
`lib/riddler/corpus.ex` and `test/riddler/corpus_test.exs`, which differ on
both sides of each line because `main` moved those two files under this
branch. Every other byte, including every hunk header and every `+`/`-` line,
is identical. So: the same patch text, over two files `main` moved beneath it.

---

# The record half

The rebase is what surfaced this. Commits that landed on `main` while this
branch was open added three citations to `docs/adr/0002-element-document.md`
that read the schema by **path**, not by the record's name. The code half
renames that file, so the moment it merges those three would name a path that
does not exist - an accepted record on `main` citing a file that is not there.

`79cb6e7` answers that with a **dated Note by addition at the foot of the
record**, following the shape the record's own preceding notes use: a
horizontal rule, then a dated paragraph naming the campaign and the bead.

- **The record is accepted, so it changes by addition only.** The three
  citations are left exactly where they sit; the Note is what corrects them.
  `git diff origin/main -- docs/adr/` on this branch is **47 added lines and
  zero removed**.
- **The Note claims no SHA it cannot know.** It does not name a merge commit.
  It says the file those three cite was named
  `element-document.schema.json`, that this change renames it, that the
  rename is recorded at full similarity so the schema's content is untouched
  and each SHA the citations name still reads exactly what they say it reads
  under the file's earlier name, and that from this change onward the path is
  `screen-document.schema.json`. That form is true before the merge and stays
  true after it.
- **Each of the three is located by the passage it sits in, not by a line
  number** - the rebase moved this file, and a line number in a record ages
  worse than an anchor.
- **Every quotation in the Note was checked verbatim against `origin/main`**,
  including the limiting clause each one depends on. No emphasis was added
  inside a quotation; the record's own emphasis is preserved where quoted.
- The Note is at the foot, so it cites nothing as "below": everything it
  refers to is above it.
- **Cured once after the direction review**, for two advisories about the
  Note's own accuracy, neither changing what it records. It had said it "does
  not bear on either amendment above" while its own third bullet re-labels a
  citation inside the second amendment; it now says it changes nothing either
  amendment above decides. And it had presented the clause "so that
  schema-valid means admitted" as part of what that amendment quotes from the
  schema's description; that clause is the amendment's own prose drawing a
  conclusion from the description it quotes, and it is now attributed to the
  record rather than to the schema. The clause itself is unchanged.

## What the record half does NOT touch

Two references to the earlier name are correct as they stand and are
deliberately untouched by both halves:

- `docs/adr/0002-element-document.md` - the record's **own filename**. A
  record is cited by number and filename, including by ADR-0001's
  cross-references and by the `docs/adr` wildcard `mix.exs` uses for the doc
  extras.
- `docs/adr/README.md` - the **index row** that links to that filename.

Neither names the schema; both name the record. They were exactly three
in-body path citations, verified by re-locating every occurrence in the file
rather than by the line numbers first reported, and all three are in the Note.
`docs/adr/README.md` is not in this pull request's diff at all.

---

## Provenance

- The bead's file map named "the README". `README.md` in this repo carries
  zero occurrences of the old schema name or of the schema path, so it is not
  a file of this change. No edit was made to it.
- The rebase forced no edit: no sibling's lines were kept, rewritten or
  dropped.
- `docs/adr/` was not in the bead's file map. The Note is there because the
  bead's own rename forces it, and it is reported here rather than made
  silently.

## What does NOT happen here

The emitted path in `riddler_spec` follows this rename in the campaign's one
re-emit at the tail, run by a different worker. No intermediate re-emit is
opened and nothing in `riddler_spec` is touched by this pull request.

## Verification, on the head that carries both halves

Full `mix quality` green on `79cb6e7`, staged tree
`fe65c7aee28585063925098f0a95afc385cd3d1b`, run under the repo gate lock and
one machine slot with no edit after it: format, compile (warnings as errors),
deps, credo, **178 of 178 tests at 94.9% coverage**, dialyzer no warnings.
That run includes the widened retired-spelling guard from `77f76d0`, which
now walks every key and every string value of every corpus and schema file -
including the renamed one - and is green over it.
