author: janlauber
body:
Refs #2353. **No version changes** — every action was resolved to the commit its current major tag already points at, so every job runs byte-identical code. This is hardening only.

## Why

A tag is a movable pointer in someone else's repository. Whoever can push to it can replace the code that runs inside every job here, on every branch, with the secrets those jobs hold — and nothing in this repo changes, so nothing here notices. `tj-actions/changed-files` was turned against thousands of repositories in 2025 exactly that way, by repointing tags that had never moved before.

The jobs are not toys. `publish.yml` holds `packages: write` and `contents: write` and pushes the image production pulls. `desktop-release.yml` holds the Apple signing and notarization credentials.

## What changed

31 `uses:` lines, 7 workflows, 11 distinct actions, all now `owner/repo@<40-hex> # vX.Y.Z`:

| Action | Was | Pinned at |
| --- | --- | --- |
| actions/checkout | `@v5` | `fbc6f39` # v5.1.0 |
| actions/setup-go | `@v6` | `924ae3a` # v6.5.0 |
| actions/setup-node | `@v6` | `2499707` # v6.5.0 |
| actions/upload-artifact | `@v4` | `ea165f8` # v4.6.2 |
| actions/download-artifact | `@v4` | `d3f86a1` # v4.3.0 |
| golangci/golangci-lint-action | `@v9` | `ba0d7d2` # v9.3.0 |
| golang/govulncheck-action | `@v1` | `032d455` # v1.1.0 |
| pnpm/action-setup | `@v4` | `b906aff` # v4.3.0 |
| docker/setup-buildx-action | `@v4` | `f87e599` # v4.4.1 |
| docker/login-action | `@v4` | `dbcb813` # v4.6.0 |
| docker/build-push-action | `@v7` | `c3c9e26` # v7.4.0 |

Every SHA was checked against its repository through the API, and each carries **both** the exact release tag and the major tag it replaced — which is the proof that nothing moved. That check matters most for `publish.yml` and `desktop-release.yml`: neither runs on a pull request, so CI here cannot exercise them at all.

The trailing `# vX.Y.Z` is not decoration. A bare SHA tells a reader nothing about its age, and it is the comment Dependabot rewrites when it bumps the pin.

## The guard, which is really the point

Pinning once is easy; staying pinned is not. One agent typing `@v4` out of habit silently undoes all of it, and no existing check would care. So ci.yml's `docs` job — required on main's ruleset, and free of a paths filter so it runs on every PR — now rejects any `uses:` that is not a commit SHA with a version comment, and prints the `gh api` incantation for resolving one.

Both failure modes were **seen to fail** before this landed, per `.claude/rules/code-quality.md`:

- a tag ref (`actions/cache@v4`) → red
- a bare SHA with no version comment → red
- the pinned tree → green

`uses: ./…` (a local action) is exempt; there are none today.

## Follow-ups

- `.github/dependabot.yml`'s `actions` group comment said "every workflow in this repo pins by major tag", which this makes false. Rewritten with the new reason grouping matters: a tag pin moved only on a major, a commit pin moves on **every patch**, so ungrouped this would become the noisiest ecosystem in the file rather than the quietest.
- **#2348 will conflict** and needs a rebase — Dependabot does that itself. It is also a six-major jump (checkout 5→7, upload-artifact 4→7, download-artifact 4→8, and more) that wants a real review rather than a rubber stamp; `actions/checkout` v7 changes fork-PR checkout behaviour for `pull_request_target` and `workflow_run`.
- No ADR: the reasoning lives in ci.yml beside the check that enforces it, which is where someone hitting it will actually be. Happy to write one if you'd rather it were in `docs/decisions/`.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: its-janghoon
body:
v0.1.0 failed twice in a row at the same step, both times transiently and on a different asset:

```
HTTP 504: 504 Gateway Timeout                  ... /assets?name=redrob-linux-arm64-musl.zip
HTTP 500: Error creating asset temp dir        ... /assets?name=redrob-darwin-x64.zip
```

`gh release create "$TAG" ... assets/*` uploads all twenty assets in one command and rolls the whole release back if any one of them fails, so a single 5xx discards a run that has already spent about forty minutes building every platform, signing and notarizing macOS, and signing Windows. With twenty assets that is not an unlucky edge case, it is the expected outcome often enough to block a release.

Now: the release is created empty, each asset is uploaded on its own with up to three attempts and a backoff, and anything still failing is named in the error. Because the tag and the release both already exist at that point, re-running the job resumes instead of restarting.

It also collapses the create and the re-run paths, which needed the same clobbering upload anyway, and adds a check that the published asset count matches what was built. A release missing one archive installs nothing on that platform while looking published.

Verified: the workflow parses, and the added block passes `bash -n`.

author: masonlee277
body:
`AtmosphereModel` collects boundary conditions for every prognostic name, validates them, and passes the regularized inventory to `materialize_microphysical_fields`. P3's method accepts that argument and never reads it:

```julia
function AM.materialize_microphysical_fields(p3::P3, grid, bcs)
    ρqᶜˡ = CenterField(grid)  # Cloud liquid
    ρqʳ  = CenterField(grid)  # Rain mass
    ...
```

Because the P3 names are legitimate — they come from `prognostic_field_names`, so `validate_boundary_condition_names` accepts them — a prescribed surface rain flux or a Dirichlet value on any P3 prognostic was **silently dropped**. No error, no warning, no effect. `DCMIP2016Kessler` gets this right one file over (`dcmip2016_kessler.jl`):

```julia
ρqᶜˡ = CenterField(grid, boundary_conditions=boundary_conditions.ρqᶜˡ)
```

The optional field groups (`aerosol_activation_fields`, `supersaturation_fields`) need the inventory for the same reason. A name that is absent falls back to the default, because diagnostics may materialize these fields with an empty tuple — `predicted_particle_properties_integration.jl` and `..._processes.jl` both do.

### A second problem this exposes

Giving P3 prognostics real boundary conditions surfaces a latent bug. `compute_auxiliary_thermodynamic_variables!` refills the halos of the *whole* microphysical inventory — which holds the prognostic densities as well as the diagnostics it just computed — but did so without `boundary_condition_args(model)`:

```julia
fill_halo_regions!(model.microphysical_fields)
```

A constant condition does not notice. A function-valued one is evaluated with the wrong signature. That fill now passes the same arguments as the prognostic fill in `update_state!`, which is what the three other `fill_halo_regions!` calls in that file already do.

I kept this here rather than in its own PR because it is only reachable once P3 prognostics carry conditions, so the two belong to the same change.

### Scope

This is the first of three pieces split out of the closed #983, which bundled them behind a P3-shaped title. This piece is the P3 plumbing only. The remaining two concern translating a `Value` on a prognostic *density* onto the *specific* field that transport actually reconstructs — which is not P3-specific and is a live bug for moisture and `ρθ` under every scheme today. That deserves its own review and its own model-level test, so it will come separately.

### Test

A P3 model built with a constant flux on `ρqʳ` and a function-valued `Value` on `ρqⁱ`: the conditions are on the fields, an unspecified prognostic keeps its default, and `update_state!` runs and leaves the field finite. The function-valued condition is the part that exercises the halo-fill fix. 6/6 passing on GPU.

author: jedwardsche
body:
Reported from a running daemon: `the recording overlay failed and will retry: depythonifying struct of 2 members, got tuple of 4`.

Two defects, both shipped in #56, both green in the suite.

## 1. A flat NSRect handed to a CALayer

PyObjC depythonifies an `NSRect` as `((x, y), (w, h))` — two members, nested. `pill_frame` returns this module's flat four-tuple convention and it went straight to `CALayer.setFrame_`.

The window path converts through `NSMakeRect(*rect)` and never had the problem. The layer path has no such call. `as_rect` is now that call, and the bars route through it too — the bars used a correct nested *literal*, which is exactly how the pill came to be written differently from them without anything noticing.

**This is the second time this error has reached a running daemon.** The first is in the module preamble, dated 2026-09-02, and its note already reads "every test passed against a flat fake". `_FakeLayer.setFrame_` stored whatever it was given — a fake that accepts a shape the framework rejects, in the forgiving direction, which is the direction reading cannot catch. It now validates, and patching it made the suite reproduce the shipped bug before anything was fixed.

## 2. `CATransactionBegin` does not exist

`CATransaction` is a class with class methods. The invented free functions raised `AttributeError` on the first transition, which `_render`'s guard converted into the "failed and will retry" message rather than anything naming the cause. The fake had invented the same four names, so the suite agreed with itself about an API that was never there.

## What changed about how this is tested

Three contract tests ask the **framework** rather than the stand-in:

- a real `CALayer` accepts every pill rect, and rejects the flat form (negative control — without it, `as_rect` returning its input would pass)
- `Quartz.CATransaction` has `begin`, `commit`, `setAnimationDuration_`, `setDisableActions_`
- `NSWorkspace` has `accessibilityDisplayShouldReduceMotion`

The third was checked only because the other two were wrong. Two of the three framework calls added that day were broken, which is the only useful evidence about how carefully the set was reviewed.

## Verification

754 passed, 6 skipped. (An earlier revision of this description said 818 — a number that was never run. Corrected rather than silently edited: the figure was wrong.) `mypy --strict` and `ruff` clean.

Sabotage: `as_rect` returning its input — the shipped bug — fails six tests including both real-CALayer controls.

Verified against live AppKit outside the suite: the panel builds, the pill moves 34x10 → 72x22 → 34x10, the window stays 72x22 throughout, border 1.0, no error reported.

**No test builds a real NSPanel.** That would put a window on screen during CI, so the end-to-end reading is still lane 2's — which is owed anyway.

author: skayy47
body:
The footer link to `/services` has been sitting uncommitted while the page it points at was never tracked, so **`/services` returned 404 in production**. Landing the link on its own would have put a dead link in the footer of every page on the live site, so the page and its proxy ship with it.

`src/proxy.ts` is Next 16's renamed middleware: it rewrites the `services.*` subdomain onto `/services`, so the page is reachable both ways.

## One change to the page itself

Its `<style>` block declared `a:focus-visible, button:focus-visible` and `::selection` unscoped. Both are now scoped to `.svc-root`.

**Correcting my own earlier claim:** I said three times that those rules leaked site-wide. They did not — the `<style>` unmounts with the page, verified by navigating away and finding zero of its rules left behind. What they actually did was override the site's own `--accent` focus ring on shared chrome *while that page was mounted*. Worth fixing, but a much smaller thing than I described.

The footer link becomes a `next/link` so it navigates client-side rather than reloading, which also clears the lint rule it was tripping.

## Left as-is

The page is a parallel design system — its own dark palette, its own EN/FR store, its own `Reveal`/`Magnetic`/`useReducedMotion` shadowing the site's, and Inter hardcoded over the site's font tokens. That is a real fork worth reconciling, but not while landing a link.

Of the nine mapper kinds this build runs, the organization rule was the one nothing weighed end to end. The plane's benches proved it could be **stored**: the answer came back `CREATED` and nothing asked what it then wrote.

A rule that stores and never answers is exactly what the configuration door added in an earlier slice was built to refuse, so the gap was worth closing rather than noting again.

Modelled on the group rule's, beside it in the same file. Two organizations, so the answer is a list and its order is the one the store promises rather than the one the rows happened to arrive in. Ada belongs to both.

It also weighs the half that is easy to forget: a grant carrying no organization rule reads nothing at all. That is the bargain the lazy loading strikes, and without it the registry could be filled on every grant and no bench would notice.

- Both benches in the file, live Postgres: 2/2.

author: ahernsean
body:
## Summary

`_COST_MODEL_MIN_WEIGHT` was `1.0`, so a **single observation** flipped a `(size_bucket, budget)` cell from "no prediction, use the size heuristic" to an authoritative geometric mean. Every sub-branch whose size and budget land in that cell was promoted on that one sample. Raised to `25.0`.

### Choosing the value

Counted against the live `cost_model` table (66 cells) and weighted by epoch 21's node volume:

| threshold | warm cells | node volume covered |
|---|---|---|
| 1 (current) | 66 | 100.0% |
| 5 | 60 | 91.4% |
| 20 | 55 | 89.0% |
| **25** | **55** | **89.0%** |
| 30 | 53 | 83.8% |
| 50 | 49 | 54.2% |

20 and 25 give identical coverage, so 25 takes the stronger claim for the same price. 30 would drop the 918–1192 word cell at budget 5 (weight 29.3, 4.3% of node volume) for no gain.

### Why the cold regions are safe

Every cell this turns cold falls into one of three groups:

- **Well above `PROMOTE_MIN_SIZE = 60`** — 1551-2015, 1193-1550, 543-705 words at budget 5; 191-247, 248-321, 322-417 at budget 4. The size fallback promotes these exactly as the warm path did, so cold and warm agree.
- **Budget 2** — promotion is blocked outright by `_maybe_cooperative`, so the cell is never consulted.
- **Budget 3, 31-66 words** — the only group whose behaviour actually changes, and it carries **0.04%** of epoch 21's nodes. These now inline rather than promote, which is the intended direction: per the stage 1 measurements, 97.8% of the over-promoted `<= 2s` population is below 60 words.

It also clears the four cells that read warm today on 10-16 day old writes, the largest of which asserts a cost on weight 18.

The value matters most for work that has not arrived yet: a new size/budget region starts thin, and the 50 lowest-entropy openers now queued will open several.

### Tests

Seeding tests carry `_COST_MODEL_MIN_WEIGHT` per sample so they track the constant rather than a hardcoded weight. A uniform weight leaves every fixture's geometric mean and log-normal sigma unchanged, so the estimator assertions are untouched.

- `test_single_sample_leaves_the_cell_cold` replaces `test_single_sample_round_trips`, whose name asserted the defect. Verified to fail with the constant reverted to 1.0.
- `test_weight_just_below_the_threshold_reads_cold` / `test_weight_at_the_threshold_reads_warm` pin the gate relative to the constant.
- `test_cold_specific_cell_stays_cold` now asserts its warm cell is actually warm; previously both cells read cold, so it would have passed even with budget keying broken.
- `seed_cost_model` passes the weight through, so the trap fixtures warm exactly the cells they did before with the same predicted curve.

## A related gap, not fixed here

`_warm_bucket_row` gates on the stored `weight_sum`, and decay is applied only on write. A cell that stops receiving samples keeps its weight indefinitely rather than fading — contrary to #342's note that "a cell that is warm during a busy sweep can go cold overnight". Raising the threshold clears every stale-warm cell present today, but the mechanism remains. Worth its own issue.

Closes #342

author: theclifmeister
body:
Closes #156.

## What

`killactive` (SUPER+W) on an application's **last window** quits the application — ⌘Q in place of ⌘W — so a program with no window left is a program that has exited, as on Omarchy. On any other window it presses the close button as before. Two Safari windows: SUPER+W closes one and leaves the other alone.

Behind `[misc] quit_on_last_window`, on by default, with a fifth Setup row, **Quit app on last window**, after the #151 pattern.

## How

- `CloseVerdict` (ToeCore) decides `.closeWindow` / `.quitApplication` from the application's own window list, its bundle id and activation policy, and the switch. Every doubt is `.closeWindow`: an empty list, an unreadable id, a list without the window being closed. The Finder is never quit; a non-`.regular` application only loses the window. The application is passed as an autoclosure so the switch is read before any AX call.
- `WindowMover.application(of:)` gathers it from `kAXWindows` — app-wide, every Space, minimized and never-adopted windows included — and `WindowMover.quit` is `terminate()`, never `forceTerminate()`. Quit is sent *instead of* the close so an unsaved-document sheet is the app's own, and the user can decline.
- `Coordinator.closeWindow` sits behind both arms of `dispatch(.killActive)`, so `--window` follows the same rule.
- `[misc] quit_on_last_window` in `Config`, `DefaultConfig` and `toe.example.toml`; `ConfigSwitch.quitOnLast`; a bullet in the skill document's "Things that will surprise you".

## Tests

`make test`: 1779 assertions. New: the verdict in every shape (exactly one → quit; two, either order, unreadable, empty, foreign list → close; Finder → close; no bundle id → quit; accessory → close; switch off → close and the app never asked); the config default / `false` / bad value warns; the Setup row list.

Verified in `build/ToeDev.app` over the socket: two TextEdit windows — first `killactive` closed one and TextEdit stayed, second quit it. A Finder window closed and Finder stayed. A TextEdit window with a *minimized* sibling (which toe no longer tracks) closed and TextEdit stayed.

## Summary
- Tom: "Claire seems stuck or limited, trying to get her to change employees' start and stop times for each day." Investigated `edit_employee_hours`/`get_employee_hours` (PR #176) — they already fully support setting an explicit start/end **time** for a specific date, writing to `manual_hour_overrides`. Claire's hours tools are strictly one-employee/one-date per call, with a 10-tool-call round cap per message, and there's no recurring/template start-time concept. author: aditya-nambiar
body:
## What does this PR do?

Fixes the Codex early-reopen quota probe so it stops benching a **working** `openai-codex` credential when paid credits are covering the overage.

The probe added for #43747 (`_probe_codex_quota_restored`) reads `rate_limit.{primary,secondary}_window.used_percent` from the Codex usage endpoint and reports "restored" only when the worst window is `< 100`. On plans with paid credits that is the wrong question: once the plan window is exhausted, the overage is served from the credit balance, and `used_percent` stays pinned at `100` until the window resets. So the probe answers "not restored" for an account that is actively serving requests, and the pool keeps the credential `exhausted` until `last_error_reset_at` — hours or days away. Every turn then fails over to the fallback chain (or fails outright) against a healthy account.

The usage response already carries what is needed to tell the two cases apart — a `credits` block (`has_credits`, `unlimited`, `overage_limit_reached`, `balance`) and a `spend_control` block (`reached`). This PR consults them: spendable credits mean the account serves, so the stale cooldown is lifted. With no `credits` block, or credits that cannot cover the overage, the existing window verdict is unchanged.

**Observed in production (Plus plan):** a 429 `usage_limit_reached` benched the only Codex credential with a `last_error_reset_at` ~2.5 h out. Credits were then added to the account. From that point a direct `POST /responses` with the stored token returned `200`, while the usage endpoint kept reporting `primary_window.used_percent = 100` with `credits.has_credits = true` and a positive balance — and the probe kept returning `False`. All gateway sessions stayed down for over an hour until `hermes auth reset openai-codex`, after which the same credential served normally.

## Related Issue

No separate issue filed — the bug report is above. Follow-up to the early-reopen fix for #43747 (closed): same stale-cooldown symptom, different cause (credits covering overage rather than the window reopening).

## Type of Change

- [x] 🐛 Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)

## Changes Made

- `hermes_cli/auth_codex.py`: add `_codex_credits_usable(usage)` and consult it in `_probe_codex_quota_restored` before the window verdict. Conservative by construction: requires `has_credits`, no `overage_limit_reached`, no `spend_control.reached`, and a positive (or `unlimited`) balance; a missing, malformed or non-dict block falls through to the existing behaviour.
- `tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_codex_quota_probe.py`: cover credits covering the overage, unlimited credits, credits that cannot cover it (zero / malformed balance, `has_credits: false`, `overage_limit_reached`), `spend_control.reached`, and the unchanged window verdict when no credits block is present.

## How to Test

1. `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_codex_quota_probe.py -q` → 11 passed.
2. Revert only `hermes_cli/auth_codex.py` and re-run: `test_probe_restored_when_window_exhausted_but_credits_cover_overage` and `test_probe_restored_with_unlimited_credits` fail (2 failed, 9 passed), confirming the tests detect the bug.
3. Regression: `pytest tests/hermes_cli/test_auth_codex*.py tests/agent/test_credential_pool*.py -q` → 179 passed.
4. Live check on a Plus account with an exhausted 5-hour window and a positive credit balance: the patched probe returns `True` where the unpatched one returned `False`.

- [x] I've read the [Contributing Guide](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] My commit messages follow [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/) (`fix(scope):`, `feat(scope):`, etc.)
- [x] I searched for [existing PRs](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/pulls) to make sure this isn't a duplicate

## Overview & Objective
Implements compliant direct message (DM) automation and keyword engagement workflows for CreatorOS creators (issue #1231). Creators can configure auto-response trigger rules (exact, contains, regex), enforce anti-spam per-user cooldown windows, set daily send quotas, and safely simulate rule matching before activating in production.

## Problem Statement & Architecture Gap
Content creators regularly receive hundreds of inbound DMs requesting collaboration links, pricing details, or freebies. Without compliant automated reply workflows, inbound engagement is lost or creators risk violating platform spam rate limits due to uncontrolled concurrent webhook responses.

## Technical Implementation
1. **DM Automation Rule Model (model/dmAutomationRule.js)**: Schema for keywords, match strategies, response templates, delay intervals, cooldown windows, daily send tracking, and execution metrics.
2. **Automation Engine (services/dmAutomationEngine.js)**: Implements regex-safe keyword evaluation, in-memory/fallback user cooldown cache, template variable substitution ({{senderName}}, {{creatorName}}), and quota gating.
3. **Controller (controller/dmAutomationController.js)**: Rule CRUD, simulator preview endpoint (testRuleMatch), and live incoming webhook processor (processIncomingWebhookMessage).
4. **Routes (routes/dmAutomationRoutes.js)**: Exposes creator rule management and webhook evaluation endpoints.
5. **Unit Tests (tests/dmAutomation.test.js)**: Validates case-insensitive trigger matching, exact keyword matches, regex safety, template rendering, and cooldown tracking.

author: dprater-st
body:
Writes a small manifest into `out/` and uploads it with the bundle:

```json
{
  "st_build": "49",
  "freeswitch_version": "1.10.3-st-build-49",
  "configure_ac_version": "1.10.3",
  "ref": "master",
  "sha": "821fe34e...",
  "ubuntu_codename": "jammy",
  "built_by_run": "35268698901"
}
```

## Why

telephony-iac's new `ship-freeswitch-build` workflow names the AMI it bakes after the FreeSWITCH version. The `.deb` version encodes nothing — `debian/changelog` has read `1.2~rc2-1` since 2012 — so the only real source is `configure.ac` at the built commit. Without this, the consumer has to reach back into this repo and resolve the `st-build-<N>` tag at ship time, which couples an ST infra repo to a personal fork's tags.

Recording `ref` and `sha` is the more valuable half: **an artifact in S3 currently does not say which source line produced it.** Every shipped build — `st-build-46`, `47`, `48` — is tagged on `master`, while this workflow's `ref` input *defaults* to `v1.10_opensll3`, a divergent branch (183 commits one way, 322 the other). Nothing in the bundle distinguished those two possibilities.

## Notes

`ship-freeswitch-build` treats this as optional and falls back to reading `configure.ac` at the tag, so existing bundles without it still ship.

Verified by extracting the step's script and running it against this tree: produces valid JSON, label `1.10.3-st-build-49`, matching the existing `1.10.3-st-build-47` convention. This repo runs no PR checks.

author: drkevorkian
body:
Optimization/correctness cleanup for the same-provider viewpoint badge layer.

Problem:
- the main dynamic dashboard already obtains one authoritative AI_BRIDGE_ADAPTIVE_SELECT response and atomically commits its health + recommendation.
- dashboard-viewpoint-badges.js then reacted to the recommendation DOM mutation by issuing a second AI_BRIDGE_ADAPTIVE_SELECT request purely for cosmetic badge rendering.
- that redundant IPC usually reused cache, but it was unnecessary and could observe a different health snapshot than the visible recommendation if state changed between reads.

Fix:
- expose the dashboard's already-committed lastHealth through a read-only getCommittedHealth() accessor on the existing immutable dynamic-dashboard API.
- advertise committedHealthSnapshot: true.
- viewpoint badges synchronously read that committed snapshot after the existing recommendation mutation cadence.
- remove all chrome.runtime.sendMessage / AI_BRIDGE_ADAPTIVE_SELECT usage from the cosmetic badge adapter.
- no new events, timers, permissions, routing changes, provider policy changes, identity exposure, or >5-agent work.

Regression:
- dynamic-agent-dashboard pins the committed health accessor contract.
- dashboard-viewpoint-badges proves startup and later recommendation mutations read the committed snapshot only and never contact the worker.

body:
**Pixee Scan:** [6fc57f4e-1d22-4ebb-98d3-778439f795f6](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/6fc57f4e-1d22-4ebb-98d3-778439f795f6?fix-finding-id=AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK)
Confidence: HIGH Fix confidence is a rating derived from an internal benchmark and includes High, Medium, and Low confidence fixes. It comprises three weighted scores reflecting the safety, effectiveness and cleanliness of Pixee's code changes within a fix. [View Details in Pixee.](https://app.pixee.ai/scans/6fc57f4e-1d22-4ebb-98d3-778439f795f6?fix-finding-id=AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK)
--- ## Remediation This change fixes finding AZVdjxO-h0BHfERFoIIK. ## Details Prevent Command Injection in introduction/views.py ## Summary Prevent Command Injection in introduction/views.py ## Vulnerability Description Command Injection occurs when an application constructs an operating-system command from untrusted input and passes it to a command interpreter. This is dangerous because an attacker can append extra arguments or shell metacharacters to execute arbitrary commands with the application's privileges. In a web application, that can lead to data theft, service disruption, or full server compromise. ## Changes Made The `/cmd_lab` handler in `introduction/views.py` previously combined the user-controlled `domain` and `os` POST fields into a command string for `nslookup` or `dig`, which made the lookup operation vulnerable to command injection. The fix added a strict `DOMAIN_RE` allowlist for valid hostnames, localhost, and IPv4 addresses, and it now rejects requests with missing input or an unsupported `os` value. The code also normalizes the optional `https://www.` prefix before validation so only the intended domain text is accepted. Finally, the lookup command is now assembled as an argument list, which removes the unsafe string-concatenation pattern that allowed untrusted data to influence command execution. ## Guidance Adherence **Source**: Pixee Knowledge Base Applied the following guidance from the remediation prompt: - **Prevent command injection vulnerabilities by sanitizing inputs and/or validating user input**: the fix now rejects missing/invalid `domain` and `os` values, strips the known `https://www.` prefix, and validates the remaining domain against `DOMAIN_RE` before any command execution, which directly follows the guidance to ensure user input does not contain malicious commands. - **Avoid constructing OS commands from user-controlled data**: the code no longer builds a shell command string with `"nslookup {}".format(domain)` / `"dig {}".format(domain)`. Instead it passes a command list (`["nslookup", domain]` or `["dig", domain]`) to `subprocess.run`, which avoids shell interpretation and mitigates command injection, aligning with the guidance and the Sonar S2076 warning. - **Library/framework usage**: no special preferred library was specified in the guidance, so the existing Python standard library approach is acceptable; the change uses `re` for validation and `subprocess.run` for execution without introducing unnecessary frameworks. - **Style consistency**: the modification stays within the existing Django view style and error-handling pattern by returning the same fallback template response (`"Something went wrong"`) on invalid input or execution failure, consistent with surrounding code. - **Dependency manifest**: no new third-party dependencies were introduced, so no manifest update was required.

author: 3lvis
body:
Closes #56.

A method declared in `extension UIViewController` was counted only where it was called unqualified. `hosting.detachFromParent()`, where `hosting` is a `UIHostingController`, resolved to a type the run never declares and was dropped — `locate` answered `.outside` for any external receiver. Three callers read as one.

That made it the worst-shaped of the bugs fixed this round: it does not merely miss something, it instructs you to inline a function with three callers. Taking the advice re-duplicates UIKit's unparenting sequence across three sites, and that sequence has an ordering contract — `willMove(toParent: nil)` has to reach the child while it still has a parent.

A receiver whose type is not declared here can still be served by an extension written here, so those are now searched. Only extensions on **undeclared** types are candidates, since a method on a type the run declares cannot be reached through an external receiver; several matching names is `.ambiguous` rather than attributed, which withholds the verdict the way the graph already does elsewhere.

### Measured

`tienda-ios`: **648 before, 648 after** — no true positive lost, and none gained. The shape is specific enough that tienda does not contain it.

Pinwheel, where it was found, on its real source with the `oida:disable` removed:

| | violations on `UIViewControllerExtensions.swift` |
|---|---|
| 0.17.1 | 1 |
| this build | 0 |

That disable carries a four-line comment explaining a false positive, which the issue rightly called the least useful kind of comment to leave behind. All five lines can go.

### Testing

A non-triggering example for the shape — an extension on `UIViewController`, one unqualified call and one through a `UIHostingController` instance — red before the change. The rule's existing examples are unchanged.

Full suite green, self-lint clean.

author: usernanni
body:
> **Empilhado sobre o #367** (`t3code/sisub-inventory-review-fixes`). Mergear o #367 primeiro; o diff aqui mostra só o que é desta branch.

A saída do estoque passa a ser do **dia**, não da tarefa.

O desenho anterior amarrava a baixa a uma tarefa de produção já concluída, uma vez só. Na cozinha o material sai **antes** de cozinhar, em várias idas ao estoque, e o que sobra fechado volta para a prateleira. Por isso a requisição é do dia e aceita emissões, devoluções e complementos.

**A produção SUGERE, o almoxarife DECIDE.** Sair a menos ou a mais é normal — o efetivo muda, a produção rende diferente — e a tela não trava quantidade nenhuma. O motivo do desvio é pedido **uma vez**, no fechamento, e só onde o desvio passa da tolerância **e** do piso da cozinha: pedir justificativa a cada ida ao estoque é o que ensina todo mundo a marcar "outro".

---

## Correções da revisão

Cada item abaixo foi localizado no `git diff` antes deste texto ser escrito — a tabela de conferência está no fim.

### Corrida ao abrir a requisição do dia

Era check-then-act sobre `unique (kitchen_id, issue_date, origin)`. Dois almoxarifes entrando na tela ao mesmo tempo — o normal, na troca de turno — não veem linha nenhuma, os dois inserem, e o segundo toma 23505 com "Erro ao abrir a requisição" na cara.

Quem resolve a corrida é o índice, não o `select`: o insert ignora o conflito e a leitura seguinte devolve a linha que o outro acabou de criar.

### A refeição da sugestão era a que o planner devolvesse primeiro

Sem `order by`, a mesma sugestão saía "Almoço" num carregamento e "Jantar" no seguinte.

A consulta das tarefas agora é ordenada, e o insumo que aparece em **mais de uma** refeição do dia fica **sem** refeição, em vez de receber uma arbitrária: o arroz que vai no almoço e no jantar sai do estoque uma vez só e não é de nenhuma das duas — rotulá-lo com a primeira manda o almoxarife separar metade da quantidade. A consulta também parou de descartar o próprio erro.

### O bloco de leitura não fazia nada

Lia o GTIN e respondia *"informe a quantidade na linha do insumo abaixo"*. O operador lia o código e seguia procurando a linha na mão — o trabalho que a leitura existe para poupar.

`resolveScanToIngredientFn` resolve a leitura ao insumo da cozinha por três caminhos: GTIN do SKU no catálogo, alias aprendido na operação (`gs1_integration.gtin_alias`), ou a **etiqueta interna do lote** — que é o único caminho para o item **sem GTIN**, e o caso que o requisito pedia explicitamente. A linha é destacada e o campo de quantidade recebe o foco; insumo com saldo mas fora da sugestão do dia cai no campo "fora da sugestão", em vez de mandar o operador de volta a um select de 300 itens.

O destaque é borda inteira + tint de fundo, **sem faixa lateral colorida** (proibição global do repo).

### Chave de NF-e caía em "Código não reconhecido"

O domínio reconhece a chave perfeitamente — ela só não é desta tela. Dizer o contrário manda o operador procurar defeito num leitor que está funcionando. Agora a mensagem diz o que é e para onde ir.

### `return_issue` não tinha guarda de replay

`issue_stock` tem desde o começo. **Devolução é o mesmo dinheiro indo para o outro lado**: repor duas vezes infla o saldo tanto quanto sacar duas vezes o esvazia.

Sem a guarda, o retry de rede batia no índice único e voltava como violação de constraint — o almoxarife lê "erro", conclui que não passou e lança outra, agora com um `emission_id` diferente que nada impede. O identificador também passou a ser obrigatório: o índice de emissão é **parcial** (`where emission_id is not null`), então devolução sem ele não era coberta por nada.

### Fuso no fixture do teste

O fixture media validade com `current_date` (UTC) enquanto a função mede em Brasília. Era **só isso** que derrubava a asserção de alocação — `issue_stock` já ordenava pelo `coalesce` correto.

---

## Verificação

As migrations **não estão aplicadas** no banco compartilhado; entram no merge. Para provar sem aplicá-las, as três foram carregadas dentro de uma transação com `rollback`, e o cenário do teste rodado contra as funções novas:

```
 movements | without_lot
         2 |      0.0000

   lote    | quantity
 L-SEM-VAL |  10.0000     ← sem validade, entrada mais antiga: sai primeiro
 L-VALIDO  |   2.0000
                          ← L-VENC intocado (excluído)

--- devolução: primeira chamada ---
 7ec8b184-c48c-49de-b711-bad781554fc1 | 4.0000
--- devolução: MESMA emissão (retry) ---
 7ec8b184-c48c-49de-b711-bad781554fc1 | 4.0000   ← mesmo movimento, não um novo
--- total de movimentos de devolução ---
 1
ROLLBACK
```

Suíte:

```
bun run check                    22/22
SISUB_RUN_INTEGRATION=true       103 arquivos, 1295 testes, banco real, verde
```

| achado | marcador no diff |
|---|---|
| corrida ao abrir | `ignoreDuplicates`, `readRequest` |
| refeição não determinística | `order("production_date"`, `mealTypeId ? current` |
| erro descartado | `taskError` |
| leitura chega na linha | `resolveScanToIngredientFn`, `data-issue-qty` |
| chave de NF-e | `nfe_access_key` |
| replay da devolução | `Retry da MESMA`, `Devolução sem identificador` |
| fuso do fixture | `America/Sao_Paulo` |

author: gerrod3
body:
Repository-version retention can erase the delta an asynchronous index builder needs, while HTML generation can still make a small upload expensive. This connects the experimental index to Maven with durable captures taken before retention, publication after completion, and direct-child directory state that regenerates only changed pages.

**Depends on #497.** This draft is based on its current head, `52a2e97`. Since that branch lives in a fork, this PR targets `main` and temporarily includes the engine commits. Review only the [four integration commits / incremental diff](https://github.com/gerrod3/pulp_maven/compare/52a2e97c7da9b819cc1b27245fa4d31c628f075c...fbfc8a0). The inherited changes should drop out after #497 merges and this branch is rebased.

### Behavior

- Disabled by default. A repository must set `pulp_labels["path_index"] = "true"`, with global `off`, `shadow`, and `serve` modes.
- Checksummed journals and completed-version receipts preserve exact changes through retention. A separately reserved publisher sends deltas to S3; bootstrap reserves the repository so normal asynchronous modifications queue.
- Readers combine a published index with a complete confirmed journal suffix ending at the selected version. Tombstones win over older entries. Incomplete views fall back; only a complete miss returns an indexed 404.
- Per-pod file locks, shared mmap files, reader leases, and disk budgets coordinate content workers. HTML has its own shared cache. Directory links omit descendant sizes/dates so unchanged ancestor pages can be reused.
- Repository build, reconciliation, and status actions expose operation and recovery. A periodic Pulp task repairs lost dispatch/confirmation.
- Content uses the existing guard flow, indexed HTTP validators, public artifact streaming, and configurable S3 redirects. No pulpcore changes, new auth endpoint, or Redis guard cache.

Start with the [rollout and recovery guide](https://github.com/gerrod3/pulp_maven/blob/cx/pulp-2423-index-integration/docs/dev/path-index-integration.md). A review-order comment accompanies this draft.

### Validation

- Full unit suite: **205 passed, 4 subtests passed**, including real PostgreSQL lifecycle tests and S3 wire tests against disposable MinIO.
- A 200-version journal test retains only one repository version. Four independent processes reuse the same base download and serve the exact journal overlay.
- HTTP tests cover HEAD, validators, range streaming, S3 redirects, and HTML cache failures/pins.
- Ruff lint/format, public pulpcore import check, migration consistency, and Maven OpenAPI validation pass. Verified the public response API exists in the minimum supported pulpcore release.
- Added `benchmark_maven_versions`. The recorded 1,000-artifact smoke run measured median updates of 0.58 s in shadow mode, 0.74 s with the existing path, and 0.21 s with Maven finalization bypassed. These are development-machine smoke measurements, not production capacity estimates.

### Limits to review before rollout

Real large-repository version creation, 200 concurrent API uploads, and the deployed hosted middleware remain unmeasured. Shadow mode prepares views but does not automatically compare production responses. Serving descriptors use a process-local two-second TTL; existing core distribution/guard work remains. Cold/full caches can increase fallback DB load, and there is no index-aware readiness gate yet.

For the known pulp-service large-file redirect policy, configure `MAVEN_PATH_INDEX_REDIRECT_THRESHOLD = 1_700_000_000`. Builder scratch needs disk space beyond the content-cache budget. S3 objects and journals are retained without automatic collection in this experiment.

### Checklist

- [x] Changes grouped into four review commits
- [x] Changelog, documentation, and test coverage added
- [ ] Human review of AI-generated code and hosted rollout behavior

AI disclosure: implementation, tests, documentation, and this PR description were generated with Codex. Commits include `Generated-by: Codex`; human review is pending.

author: pher217
body:
## Goal

Two independent macOS defects in the inline-completion UI, found reviewing the
`claude/2026-09-16-inline-ux-wip` branch.

This fixes the *alignment* half of Creative-Pandas-Sarl/officelabs-project#194; the "disappears too fast" half is [#67](https://github.com/Pher217/libreoffice-fork/pull/67), which is what closes that issue.

Closes Creative-Pandas-Sarl/officelabs-project#193

## Changes

**Sidebar could not receive Cmd keys (#193).** `-[VCLApplication sendEvent:]` intercepts every Cmd keyDown for a `SalFrameWindow` and either sends it to the main menu or force-dispatches it to `[pKeyWin contentView]`, which is always the `SalFrameView`. The CEF sidebar shares the frame's `NSWindow` rather than owning one, so an embedded view never saw Cmd-V/C/X/A and its text field could not be pasted into at all.

**Ghost text was off the document baseline (#194).** The window was grown around the caret's vertical *centre*, which coincides with the line top only when caret height and text height are equal. Caret height is a Writer layout quantity with no relation to the ghost font's metrics, so the text drifted by half their difference — and `Paint`'s centring misplaced it again, since a real typeface's ascent is nearer 80% of its height than 50%.

## Approach

For #193, step aside only for a view that is *genuinely embedded*: an `NSView`, below this frame's content view, that is not the `SalFrameView` itself. Testing "not a SalFrameView" alone would also match the `NSWindow` being its own first responder — the ordinary no-focus case — and would break every menu shortcut.

Verified the guard is tight: `contentView` **is** the `SalFrameView`, and the only foreign descendants are CEF's child view (`officelabs/source/WebViewPanelHostMac.mm:79`) and `AquaSalObject`'s (`vcl/osx/salobj.cxx:53`) — the latter are stock `NSView`/`NSOpenGLView`, which do not accept first responder. **With focus in the document this path is unreachable.**

For #194, anchor to the caret rect's top and size the window to exactly this font's text height, so `Paint`'s centring term is always zero and the ghost baseline lands at (window top + ascent).

## Known behaviour change

While the sidebar has focus, Cmd-M / Cmd-Option-M / Cmd-W lose their explicit handling (`vclnsapp.mm:131-185`) and fall through to AppKit. Skipping `endExtTextInput` is not a regression — it only acts when the first responder is a `SalFrameView`, which the guard excludes.

Suggested manual pass before release: with focus **in the sidebar**, check Cmd-W and Cmd-M. With focus in the document the code path is provably unchanged, so a full shortcut sweep is not required.

This is the first fork-local patch to `vcl/osx/vclnsapp.mm`, so it adds one rebase point against upstream LibreOffice.

## Test Summary

author: shu1513
body:
## What

Updates the AI ballot-measure prompt (`ballotMeasuresPrompt.ts`) so automated measure research follows the same writing and tagging rules the manually written measures already follow.

## Rules added

- **Reader test**: `summary`, `what_yes_means`, and `what_no_means` must let an average voter tell what the measure does and whether it costs them anything.
- **Plain words**: replace each legal or finance word, or explain it in a few words (binding arbitration → a neutral third party decides; bond → borrow; levy or millage → property tax; ordinance → city law).
- **Who pays**: public money is taxpayer money, so say who pays, and say so when the reader's taxes do not change.
- **Real effect, not the title**: titles and sponsor wording can mislead; take the effect from the fiscal note, legislative analyst, or official text.
- **Tags**: do not tag from the title or the sponsor's framing, and never force a tag. The old line ("Return an empty research_area_tags array only if no allowed area clearly applies") pushed toward always tagging something; an empty list is now stated as a valid answer.

These sit next to the shared `PLAIN_LANGUAGE_STYLE_RULES` and do not change the length caps or the payload shape.

## Why

A review of the 332 November 2026 measures found descriptions an average reader could not follow (Maryland Question 1's "binding arbitration") and stance tags forced onto mixed measures (a Labor Rights tag on a measure that also bans strikes). Those rows were fixed by hand; this keeps new AI-written rows from repeating it.

## Tests

One new prompt test asserts the rules are present and the old tag line is gone. Ballot-measure prompt and enrichment tests pass; backend typechecks. No AI calls are made by this change.

author: docgerd
body:
Closes #1303
Closes #1305
Closes #1280

## What changed

**A1 — one confined-water prune rule for #1303 and #1305.** `solve()`
classifies each prune cell as CONFINED (any mask cell within one cell of it is
land or sub-gate water at this solve's gate) and keys confined cells on a grid
`CONFINED_PRUNE_DIV = 2` times finer per axis; open water keeps the coarse
grid. Classification is per coarse cell and cached per solve, so a node gets
the same key at the dominance lookup and at the stamp, and the `f` prefix keeps
the two key spaces disjoint. `CONFINED_PRUNE_DIV = 1` restores the previous
keys exactly — the BASE control every measurement below used. `solve()`'s ok
arm now also carries `costMs` (the ranking clock); `PlanResult` is unchanged.

**A2 — #1280 part B.** The budget is read every `DEADLINE_CHECK_NODES` (128)
frontier nodes at a node boundary (read-only between nodes; children are never
reordered or skipped), and `findRelaxedGate` takes an optional deadline read
between probes and between a probe's BFS passes. `planRoute` re-reads the
deadline right after that call, so the typed budget failure wins over a
mask-level verdict the probes never reached. Unbudgeted solves are
byte-identical.

## Target rows (real mask, `solve()`, uniform 12 kn/225, sweep T0, tier 1)

cost h / nm, `CONFINED_PRUNE_DIV` 1 (BASE) → 2 (HEAD):

| row | BASE | HEAD |
|---|---|---|
| Svendborg S45 fock capped | 8.8246 / 51.24 | 8.7749 / 51.20 |
| Svendborg S45 fock uncapped | **15.4877 / 97.25** | 8.7658 / 51.37 |
| Rudkøbing S44 genoa capped | **15.2027 / 97.28** | 9.8641 / 60.50 |
| Rudkøbing S44 genoa uncapped | 9.9763 / 60.29 | 9.8748 / 59.79 |
| Rudkøbing S44 fock capped | 10.3562 / 63.41 | 9.9653 / 60.54 |
| Rudkøbing S44 fock uncapped | **15.2000 / 96.24** | 9.9383 / 60.19 |

The three bold rows are the defect and red at BASE; the other three were
already on the short family and are non-regression controls.

## Why ×2 and not ×4

`CONFINED_PRUNE_DIV = 4` also fixes all six rows, but costs more and buys
nothing: it RAISED cost on Svendborg capped (8.8282 vs BASE 8.8246, the capped
regime truncating a bigger frontier), while ×2 is at or below BASE cost on
every row. Plan-level wall time (`planRoute`, both rigs, tier 1, solo, load ≈1,
against `PLAN_BUDGET_MS` 240 s): S44 Flensburg→Rudkøbing BASE 121.0 s, ×2
137.9 s, ×4 206.9 s; S45 Flensburg→Svendborg BASE 111.0 s, ×2 94.3 s, ×4
133.2 s. Per-solve peak frontier uncapped: 46–49k BASE, 58–64k at ×2, 92–102k
at ×4; slowest ring 2.4 s / 3.2–3.7 s / 4.8–5.5 s.

- `src/routing` at HEAD: 518/518 (39 files). At `CONFINED_PRUNE_DIV = 1` the

- Each new literal reds at BASE; per-pin evidence in each test's own comment.
- A2 mutations: deleting the mid-ring check, planRoute's re-read, or
  `findRelaxedGate`'s loop checks each reds exactly the new row that names it.

A #282 sweep. Pre-registered predictions are posted as a comment before any
run; the sweep is not run yet.

author: atrios-lab
body:
## O que muda

A serventia passa a responder o roteiro do Provimento **sozinha, pelo celular, em linguagem simples e sem login**. A equipe gera um link único por diagnóstico e envia por WhatsApp; as respostas caem no mesmo diagnóstico, e a equipe revisa e conclui como hoje.

### Como se sabe qual cartório respondeu
A equipe gera o link a partir de um diagnóstico (ou lead) já existente: token de 256 bits, validade de 30 dias, regeneração (mantém respostas) e revogação. Não existe formulário aberto sem token; a entrada aberta continua sendo o pré-cadastro da landing.

### Lado da equipe (`/diagnosticos`)
- Bloco **"Link para a serventia responder"** no roteiro e na tela de lead: copiar, abrir WhatsApp do contato com mensagem pronta, estado (não iniciado / aberto / enviado / expirado / revogado), respondente, progresso, regenerar, revogar.
- Faixa **"Autoavaliação recebida por X em Y"** no roteiro, chip **"Classe declarada pela serventia"** no cabeçalho e chip **"Autoavaliação recebida"** na lista.
- E-mail para `LEAD_NOTIFY_EMAIL` e evento realtime quando a serventia envia. O status fica `em_andamento` até a equipe concluir (portão de revisão).

### Lado da serventia (`/autoavaliacao/[token]`, público)
- Identificação de quem responde (nome, cargo, e-mail ou WhatsApp) + aceite da Política de Privacidade, com versão da política e IP truncado, no padrão do pré-cadastro.
- **Enquadramento declarado pela serventia** (faixa de receita e modelo de solução) quando o diagnóstico não tem classe. Lead do pré-cadastro sai de "Novo" para "Em andamento" ao declarar. Base: art. 16, §1º.
- Perguntas **só na versão `perguntaSimples`**, agrupadas pelos títulos leigos de etapa, com legenda das quatro opções; itens dispensados para a classe não são exibidos. Autosave por resposta; o mesmo link retoma de onde parou.
- Envio final exige tudo respondido ("Não sei" vale); depois disso o link vira somente leitura. Telas de link inválido, expirado e "em análise". `noindex`.
- **Tema claro fixo** nesta rota: `[data-theme="light"]` redefine os tokens em `globals.css`; nenhuma cor literal no formulário; `theme-color` claro. App interno, landing e site continuam escuros e idênticos.

## Por que
O roteiro só existia como entrevista interna, atrás de login, o que trava a operação na agenda da equipe. O blueprint do módulo já previa "comercial gera link → cartório preenche"; agora existe. O tema claro é para o público-alvo: titular ou escrevente no balcão, sob luz do dia.

## Detalhes técnicos
- Nova tabela `autoavaliacao` (1:1 com `diagnostico`) e coluna `diagnostico.enquadramento_declarado_em`. Migração `0011_autoavaliacao_publica` (aditiva).
- Lógica pura em `src/lib/diagnostico/autoavaliacao.ts`; actions públicas resolvem o diagnóstico **só pelo token** e recusam `requisitoId` fora do conjunto aplicável.
- Upsert de respostas extraído para `src/lib/diagnostico/respostas.ts`, compartilhado entre roteiro interno e público.
- Testes novos: estados do link, validações, faltantes, **vazamento do payload público** (pergunta técnica, referência, peso, roteiro e contatos nunca chegam ao cliente) e **cores fixas na rota** (hex/rgba literal quebra o teste).
- `src/proxy.ts` libera `autoavaliacao` sem sessão.
- Specs e design: `openspec/changes/formulario-publico-serventia` e `openspec/changes/modo-claro-autoavaliacao`.

## Para o revisor
- **Lado público verificado no browser** em celular e desktop: identificação, validação de consentimento, autosave, bloqueio de envio com pendências, envio completo, reabertura somente leitura, fluxo de lead (Novo → Em andamento com classe 1 e DPO oculto), link inválido/expirado. Contrastes medidos: corpo ≥ 5:1, texto auxiliar ≥ 3.4:1.
- **Lado interno só passou por typecheck/lint**: a sessão de verificação não tinha login. Vale abrir um diagnóstico em andamento e conferir o bloco do link, gerar/regenerar/revogar e a faixa de recebimento.
- Leads do pré-cadastro têm escopo `inicial` (Etapas 1 e 2); o link herda esse escopo. Se a intenção for a serventia responder as 5 etapas sozinha, dá para trocar o escopo ao gerar o link (uma linha em `gerarLinkAutoavaliacao`). Deixei como está para decisão do time.
- O `vercel-build` já roda `drizzle-kit migrate` e o seed do provimento; nada extra no deploy.
- Testes: 116 passando (`npm test`), `biome check` e `tsc --noEmit` limpos nos arquivos alterados.

author: jerry73204
body:
Closes issue 1312: `zephyr/cmake/nros_system_generate.cmake` passed `--target zephyr-<rmw>`, which names no `[image.*]` / `[deploy.*]` block, so the tier resolver resolved no board id and answered with host defaults. A Zephyr image baked through that path got host-flavoured tier values instead of `[tiers.*.zephyr]` ones.

## The fix: a shim names its ENTRY, and the image that claims it answers

A framework configure is the one caller that *cannot* know which block it is — west and IDF know the application directory and nothing above it. So `codegen-system` gained **`--for-entry <PKG|dir>`** (`conflicts_with = --target`), resolved through the existing resolver `nros_orchestration_ir::leaf_system::for_entry` — the same question `nros image-facts --for-entry` and `nros ws board-facts` already ask. No substring of any target string is read, so the 1285 follow-up's substring guess is not reintroduced. An entry that no image claims degrades to today's defaults and prints a note naming the `entry =` to add.

**What `zephyr-${_rmw}` was used for besides the tier resolver: nothing.** It reached `nros-plan.json`'s `"target"` (no reader), the resolved domain/rmw/locator and per-image launch selection (each naming no block, so each fell to the `[system]` default), and `check_executor_capacity`, which reads `--target` as a *platform* name — `None` before and `None` now, so that check is bit-identical.

Two additions the fix forced rather than chose:
- **`--rmw "${_rmw}"`** — naming the image newly exposes `[image.*] rmw` to the bake, so the baked `NROS_SYSTEM_RMW` is pinned to what Kconfig actually compiled. No in-tree fixture image declares `rmw`, so no current value changes, and the west cyclone row's baked string was already wrong (`"zenoh"` while Kconfig built cyclonedds) and is now right.
- **`--nano-ros-path`** (issue 1263's rung) — resolving a board id loads the board catalog, and the CLI's walk-up rung finds nothing for a downstream project whose nano-ros sits below it. Without this the fix would trade a silent wrong answer for a `FATAL_ERROR` on some downstream configures.

## Acceptance

`a_zephyr_image_named_by_its_entry_bakes_the_zephyr_tier_table` — one workspace, two bakes, tiers carrying posix 80/10 and zephyr 7/9. It fails without the fix two ways: its own body re-runs the old `--target zephyr-zenoh` and asserts the host values, and a mutation making `resolve_target_block` ignore `for_entry` fails on "the zephyr sub-tables (7/9) must be the baked priorities".

On the real in-tree fixture, the module's invocation verbatim:
```
codegen-system: target `zephyr_native_sim` — the image claiming entry `zephyr_app` (--for-entry; issue 1312)
nros codegen system: wrote bake tree at …/nros-system      # rc=0
nros-plan.json:  "target": "zephyr_native_sim",
```
The same command with the old `--target zephyr-zenoh` prints no image line at all. Both edge paths were checked live: an unclaimed entry prints the note and exits 0, and `--target` with `--for-entry` is rejected by clap.

Three fixture images gained the `entry` key that makes the live path resolve (zephyr, zephyr_self_pkg/sibling, esp_idf). The `self` shape needs none — the application is the package, so its own `system.toml` answers first.

## Sweep: four shims synthesise a `--target`, and no bringup declares those names

- **Zephyr** `zephyr-<rmw>` — fixed.
- **ESP-IDF** `"esp-idf"` — fixed the same way (`--for-entry ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}`, the IDF project dir, which *is* the entry package). Not buildable on this host, but it cannot subtract an answer: an unclaimed entry gives today's defaults plus a note.
- **NuttX** `nuttx` — **left deliberately.** Its application lives in the NuttX apps tree, not the nano-ros workspace, so no `[image.*]` can claim it and `--for-entry` would resolve nothing. The fix belongs in `nros_bringup.mk`, which already pins bringup and workspace; and `nuttx` is the one synthesised target that means something to `check_executor_capacity`'s platform read.
- **PlatformIO** `platformio` — **left.** That invocation cannot run today: a bare `--ahead-of-vendor` plus a `--framework` flag the verb does not define, so it dies in argument parsing and the script swallows it.

No gate was added for the class, because CLAUDE.md requires a tolerated gap to carry a tracked issue id and the two remaining literals have none yet. Two issues are worth filing: the NuttX/PlatformIO shim targets, and the adjacent finding below.

## Adjacent finding, recorded not fixed

`--target` has a third, undeclared reading: `check_executor_capacity` passes it as a *platform* name into `resolve_max_cbs_through_ladder`. That is true of `native`/`posix` only because images are conventionally named after them. No platform declares `max_cbs` today, so both paths end at the same number and nothing is measurably wrong — which is how long a second reader stays invisible.

## Verification

- `cargo test --locked -p nros-cli-core --lib`: **1258 passed, 0 failed.**
- The four integration targets that construct `codegen_system::Args`: 7 / 12 / 3 / 2 passed, 0 failed.
- `just check cli-fresh`: OK. `cargo +nightly fmt`: clean. `markdown-links`, `doc-refs`, `issue-ids`: all OK.
- `just check fast`: 2 of 324 failed, both this worktree's missing vendored trees (`capability-conditionals` needs zenoh-pico, `xrce-vendored-versions` needs the xrce pair). The third failure was mine — a phase-453 link to the un-archived issue path — and is fixed.
- `just check cli-tests`: one target was red on `nros-launch-resolve not found`; after initialising `play_launch` at its pin and running `just setup-launch-resolve`, **32 passed, 0 failed**.
- **`just ci gate`: not run** — this worktree cannot give it a verdict (two fast gates need vendored trees, and `check build` needs generated bindings and `.compile-ok` stamps nothing here builds). Everything in it the diff can reach was run individually. **No Zephyr west build was run**, so the end-to-end image build is unverified; the evidence is the module's exact invocation on the real fixture plus the tiered synthetic test.

Side note for whoever owns `cli-tests`: that test's documented "resolver absent → fall back" branch probes `entry.is_dir()`, but the settings writer creates that directory, so on an unprovisioned host it takes the wrong branch and panics instead of asserting the fallback.

author: themaestr-o
body:
## What does this PR do?

Lexend ships no Cyrillic, so every Russian string on all four public sites and in the admin was drawn by the device's own font while the German beside it stayed in Lexend.

Closes #177

---

### The mechanism, and why it is not a fallback stack

The faces are declared **under the name `Lexend`** with a Cyrillic `unicode-range`, not appended to the stacks as `'Noto Sans'`. There are ~100 `font-family: 'Lexend'` declarations across four apps and `@sdarm/ui` — editing each is ~100 chances to miss one, plus a rule the next new selector silently skips. One `@font-face` per weight lets the browser pick **per glyph** and leaves every existing rule untouched.

⚠️ **`@fontsource`'s own `cyrillic-*.css` cannot be used for this.** Those files carry no `unicode-range` — the subsetting is in the file, not in a codepoint guard — so imported under the name `Lexend` they would take the Latin glyphs too and replace the UI face everywhere. The ranges are written out by hand, matching Google Fonts' `cyrillic` / `cyrillic-ext`.

Weights are 300–700 so both consumers are covered (`tokens.css` loads 300/400, admin 300/400/500/600). A weight present in Latin but missing here would be synthesised — a fake bold beside a real one.

### This is more urgent than when the issue was filed

The Synodal Bible went live in **1.6.0**. Its abbreviation, **"СП"**, renders on the Bible shelf today, and the book names are Cyrillic throughout the reader.

### The admin gets its own copy

`apps/admin` does not import `@sdarm/ui`'s design system — it has its own palette and loads Lexend itself. Coupling it to the public sites' stylesheet for one `@font-face` block buys nothing. `@fontsource/noto-sans` added as a dependency.

### `.book-title` also takes a `line-height`

It had none, so the line box was decided by whichever font actually rendered, and the fallback's taller metrics pushed "Псалмы Сиона" into the song count 6px beneath it. The webfont fixes today's case; the `line-height` stops the next face reopening it.

### ⚠️ One trap worth knowing about

The `url()`s are relative paths into `node_modules`, **not** `~@fontsource/…`. The tilde resolves under webpack, so `next build --webpack` and CI both pass — but Turbopack does not honour it and `next dev` dies on every one. It was caught only by running the dev server *after* a green build. Documented in `docs/gotchas.md`.

**Verified in both bundlers:** 10 Cyrillic faces emitted with `unicode-range` intact, 12 Latin Lexend faces untouched (so Latin is provably not hijacked), and the woff2 served `200` from the dev server.

---

## Creator checklist

### Code & correctness

- [x] The feature/fix works end-to-end locally — verified in **both** the webpack production build and the Turbopack dev server
- [x] I tested edge cases — confirmed Latin still resolves to Lexend, not Noto Sans
- [x] No `console.log`, `TODO`, or `FIXME` left in the diff
- [x] No secrets, API keys, or `.env` values committed

### Git hygiene

- [x] Branch is rebased onto `develop` — no merge commits
- [x] **Exactly one commit** on this branch
- [x] Commit message follows the format in `docs/gitflow.md`

### Documentation

- [ ] `docs/api.md` — n/a, no route changed
- [ ] `docs/schema.md` — n/a, no schema change
- [ ] `docs/frontend.md` — n/a, no component changed
- [x] `docs/conventions.md` updated (typography rule) and `docs/gotchas.md` (both traps)
- [ ] i18n keys — n/a, no new strings

### Responsive & visual

- [x] `pnpm turbo build` (11/11) and `pnpm turbo lint` pass
- [ ] Verified at 1280/1024/768/375px — **reviewer please confirm**
- [ ] Verified in both dark and light theme — **reviewer please confirm**
- [ ] Screenshot baselines updated — **likely required: baselines shift wherever Cyrillic is on screen (songbook list, admin songbooks grid, Bible shelf). Please review each diff rather than blanket-updating.**

### Reviewer notes

The two success criteria from the issue worth re-testing by hand, ideally on iPadOS where it was reported:
1. A Russian and a German title side by side in the songbook list are in the **same** typeface.
2. "Псалмы Сиона" no longer touches the line beneath it in the admin songbooks grid.

**Out of scope, flagged for a follow-up issue:** DM Serif Display also ships no Cyrillic (issue's point 3). I checked its 12 call sites — the exposed ones are `.tome-name` / `.book-detail__title` (Russian book titles) and `.projector__amen-slide`. There are currently **0** Russian treasures in production, so nothing regresses today, but it will the moment one is added.

body:
## Summary

- Service artifacts bake an effective `CODEX_SQLITE_HOME` (launchd plist, systemd unit, Windows task XML), but `ServiceInstallState` never recorded it. A later `ocx service stop`/`uninstall`/`repair` from a shell with a different or absent `CODEX_SQLITE_HOME`/`sqlite_home` could then pass the environment-match guard while targeting a different SQLite database than the one the service actually uses.

- Extend `assertServiceEnvironmentMatchesInstall()` to compare the recorded sqlite home against the currently resolved one and fail closed on divergence. Legacy state files without the field keep the previous behavior.
- New `tests/service/service-sqlite-home.test.ts` covers mismatch rejection, match acceptance, env-override divergence, and parse validation (empty value rejected).

body:
Caught by the last review on #94, after the merge and **before the tag** — so `v0.15.0` can carry the correct sentence.

The 0.15.0 changelog described #88's saving as applying because "source maps are off by default". They are not, on the path that matters. The CLI writing to a file defaults them **on**, as dart does:

```rust
// dart: source maps default ON when writing to a file; an explicit
// `--embed-source-map` implies one.
file_source_map: cli.source_map.unwrap_or(true) || cli.embed_source_map,
```

(`src/main.rs`.) It is the *library* API where a source map is off unless asked for, and the entry did not say so.

The optimisation itself is unchanged and its numbers are unaffected — it skips collecting argument spans when nothing will read them — so the row now states that condition instead of claiming a default the CLI does not have.

One line, docs only.

body:
## LLM decisions

- **Kept as one unit, not two.** Splitting membership from reach would
  have left reach converting places back into organisation ids for a
  release — more code than doing both at once, and none of the shape
  either function ends up.
- **`organisation_places_of` replaces two hand-rolled copies** of the
  "which organisation is accountable here" walk, one in `/me` and one in
  the feature gate. A place with no organisation above it contributes
  nothing rather than itself, which stops a member of a detached place
  having the run of somewhere nobody is accountable for.
- **`RegistrationVerificationOut.organisation_id` became `org_unit_id`**
  — renamed, not reinterpreted, so it takes a decision file.
  `/patients/{id}/shared-organisations` still answers organisation ids;
  nothing reads it, and changing that belongs with the table's removal.

## Risks

Two behaviour changes worth a look. `AssessorRevokeOut.place_id` now
holds a place id whichever kind `place` says — it held the
organisation's own id for `organisation`, which the name never said, and
nothing in the frontend reads it. Setting a bank live at a place that is
not an organisation is a 403 rather than a 404: it used to fail on a
translation, and it is now the same answer as naming somebody else's
trust.

## What has changed

`organisations.py`'s read side, its consumers in messaging, gating,
teaching, the passport and `main`, and their tests. Teaching's
`_places_of` scaffold is gone, as its docstring said it would be.

Backend: 2600 passed. Frontend: 2326 passed. One decision file,
validated.

author: jmanhype
body:
## Summary

- Honor the GNU-style `--format=text` and `--format=json` forms already documented by `pvg verify --help`.
- Preserve the existing default output and separated `--format value` behavior.
- Keep invalid values fail-closed with the existing `--format must be text or json` error.
- Add focused CLI tests for default text, separated text, equals text, equals JSON, and invalid equals values.

## Problem

`pvg verify --help` advertises:

```text
--format text|json
```

but both documented equals forms were rejected:

```text
pvg verify: unknown flag "--format=text" (see pvg verify --help)
pvg verify: unknown flag "--format=json" (see pvg verify --help)
```

The parser only handled the separated form:

```bash
pvg verify <path> --format text
pvg verify <path> --format json
```

## Implementation

Normalize `--format=value` before the existing argument switch:

- valid text/json values update the selected format;
- invalid values return the existing validation error;
- separated values continue through the original branch unchanged.

## Validation

The new tests were added first and reproduced the bug before implementation.

Focused tests:

```bash
go test ./cmd/pvg \
  -run 'TestRunVerifyFormat|TestRunVerifyRejectsInvalidEqualsFormat' \
  -count=1 -v
```

Result: all focused tests pass.

Full validation:

```bash
go test ./...
go vet ./...
go test -race ./cmd/pvg
go build -o /tmp/pvg-verify-format-fix ./cmd/pvg
git diff --check
```

All passed.

Real temporary-binary smoke test:

```text
VERIFY: PASSED (1 files scanned, 0 issues)
```

JSON output:

```json
{
  "passed": true,
  "files_scanned": 1,
  "issues": null
}
```

Invalid value:

```text
pvg verify: --format must be text or json
```

Exit code: `1`.

## Notes

While validating this change, I noticed an unrelated pre-existing verifier false positive: a legitimate `return ""` in `cmd/pvg/main.go` is reported as a stub. This PR does not change that detector behavior.

author: geekycrescent
body:
Follow-ups the spec's own summary listed as debt, none of them behaviour the owner asked for beyond what was already decided.

- The sessions module answered its three 409s with `invalid-request`, the code that means "you called it wrong". Losing a race is not calling it wrong, and `conflict` was added to the kernel's code list for exactly this. A client that branches on the code could not tell a malformed body from an expired ask. The docblock in core now says every 409 carries it.

- `boot` had no test for an unusable keys.json, though task C3 asked for one: every other test of criterion 5 covers createPushService or doctor in isolation, and the decision that push degrades rather than aborts (ADR-0004) is taken in boot's step 7 bis. Mutating that step to throw turns it red.

- The test for criterion 48 launched ONE session, so it could not tell a concurrent shutdown from a serial one. It now launches three and asserts the three notices are in flight together.

- The test for criterion 44 never called `cancel`. A version that did was written and deleted: `cancel` finalizes with `notify: false` (criterion 51), so no send is ever started on that path and the test stayed green under mutation. The test now says what it measures, and why cancel cannot pay.

author: kud360
body:
A ratchet population defined by a FEATURE with multiple element spellings —
`{open content}` is established via either `<openContent>` or
`<defaultOpenContent>` — could only be censused one element name at a time.
#1516's landing had quoted both figures side by side without unioning them,
which under-predicts against cases that actually moved.

Both arms land together, per this issue's grounding:

- **Docs (`CLAUDE.md`)**: the `suiteindex` paragraph now says a
  FEATURE-defined population takes the union of every element that
  establishes it, joined with `|`, using `{open content}`'s two spellings as
  the instance — with a caveat that this bounds from above rather than
  counts exactly, since `<openContent mode="none">` establishes nothing
  (xmlschema11-1.md §3.4.2.3.3 clause 6.1) and a local `<openContent>` can
  override a `<defaultOpenContent>` in the same fixture.
- **Tooling (`tools/suiteindex/main.go`)**: the query DSL accepts `|` (OR)
  in the element-name position (previously attribute-position only, since
  #1391); `,` there is refused with a new semantic-refusal message rather
  than silently matching nothing, which would have minted #1536's defect in
  a new position. `renderMatched`'s `element=` print decision moves from a
  per-pattern `isOpen()` to a query-level `elementOpen()` predicate, since a
  union query's matched element name is no longer derivable from a single
  pattern.
- A third commit absorbs a stale test comment (arbiter's non-blocking
  finding 3) claiming the query language was a plain conjunction — false
  since #1391's attribute `|` and now also this landing's element `|`.

**Measured, corrected figures** (the issue body's own count was
`saxonData/Open/`-scoped and undercounted by one; recorded here since
`docs/PLAN.md`'s Working band row for this issue is replaced wholesale by
the next `/backlog` pass and cannot carry the correction): corpus-wide, 18
fixtures carry `defaultOpenContent` and no `openContent` (not 12), 9 of
which were flipped by #1516's landing (not 6), carrying 18 of its 41
flipped `instance`-lane cases. `openContent|defaultOpenContent` reproduces
the full union — 104 occurrences in 69 fixtures — from one query.

Full grounding, implementation account and arbiter verdict are on the issue
thread.

Closes #1554.

Spec: n/a — repo tooling and repo documentation (xmlschema11-1.md
§3.4.2.3.3 clause 6.1 cited for the `mode="none"` caveat in the doc sentence
only; no `cvc-*`/`cos-*`/`src-*` rule is charged or touched)
Ratchet: unchanged — `tools/suiteindex` is `package main` behind a
`go.mod` tool directive, reachable from no conformance lane; confirmed
structurally and with a `GOXSD_RATCHET=1` run banking nothing.

author: nelson1602
body:
Continues gate **E1** from where Codex's BUG-018 fix (PR #169) left it.

## BUG-018's fix is verified on device

Built a release APK from `6fce7c1` and re-ran the journey against a local disposable stack. **The profile now saves**, the app navigates back to the dashboard, and the profile / birth-date / height gaps all close. The first step of onboarding is unblocked.

## The defect class was isolated, not systemic

I swept every repository for the same shape — and **validated both detectors before trusting them**:

| Detector | Shape | Positive control | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| helper-without-tx | a DB-touching helper called from a transaction that doesn't take the executor | flags the real pre-fix bug (2 sites); clean on the fix | **CLEAN** |
| direct-call | `queryFirst`/`run` inside a transaction omitting the executor | flags a synthetic `badWrite`, ignores `goodWrite` | **CLEAN** |

My first attempt reported "no findings" and I **discarded it** — run against the known pre-fix code it didn't flag the bug either, so its clean result meant nothing. That check is the only reason the current all-clear is worth anything.

## New: BUG-019 (P2) — the dashboard is stale when returned to

Record a weight from the onboarding checklist, press **back**, and the dashboard still reads **"1 of 3 complete"** and still asks you to *"Record your first weight"* — while the Progress preview **on the same screen** already shows 82 kg.

**Cause:** `DashboardScreen` reads its data in a **mount effect only**, and **no screen in the app uses `useFocusEffect`**. `back` pops to a dashboard instance that never unmounted, so nothing re-reads. The profile step masks this by accident — `/profile-edit` finishes with `router.replace('/dashboard')`, which remounts.

**Control:** `am force-stop` and relaunch, changing nothing else, renders the full assessment — calorie target, macros, training plan. The data was always sufficient; only the surface was stale.

It lands on the **first-run path**, the one surface whose entire job is telling a new user what's left to do.

## A correction I'm recording rather than burying

I first diagnosed this as *"ADR-P027 made the goal a baseline prerequisite, so profile + weight no longer reach `ready`"*. **That was wrong** — a fresh launch with exactly profile + weight reaches `ready` under the default maintenance goal. I'd already edited the journey to encode that misdiagnosis (asserting "2 of 3 complete" and a goal step before the assessment); those edits are **reverted**, not shipped.

`onboarding-loop.yml` therefore still asserts the **correct** behaviour and still fails. Making it pass would mean encoding a product defect as expected.

## Gate E1

Still blocked — **now on BUG-019 rather than BUG-018**. Updated in `docs/RELEASE_READINESS.md`.

## Validation

- `mobile`: **203 suites / 2812 tests green**
- `git diff --check` clean; markdown tables validated; backlog anchors intact
- Disposable stack throughout; port 3001 freed before starting so the API could not silently bind to a leftover process, as happened once previously

author: llxprt
body:
## TLDR

Replaces the process-global `schedulerSingleton` module with a per-Config `SessionSchedulerRegistry` keyed by **owner object + purpose** instead of session-id strings. This is PR 2 of issue #2615 slice E (PR 1: #3710 landed the port contracts).

The bug this closes: two consumers with colliding session-id labels (two subagents reusing one id, a subagent matching the foreground id) silently shared one `CoreToolScheduler`, cross-delivering completion callbacks. Object-identity keys make that collision structurally impossible.

Reviewer focus: `sessionSchedulerRegistryImpl.ts` (new, ~180 lines) and the owner choices in the three migration sites.

## Dive Deeper

- **Registry semantics carried over from the deleted singleton**: refcount per entry, in-flight creation dedup (concurrent `getOrCreate` joins one factory call), dispose at zero with swallowed cleanup errors, first-acquisition-wins `interactiveMode` with a debug log on mismatch, `disposeAll` joining in-flight creations before disposing every handle (WeakSet guards double-dispose).
- **Release during creation**: if every acquirer releases while the factory promise is pending, the resolution path disposes the unowned handle and drops the entry; a swept-mid-flight creation cedes dispose ownership to `disposeAll`.
- **Migration sites**:
  - `AgenticLoop` keys on `(this, 'agentic-loop')` — the loop instance is the natural owner; prompt-id scheduling behavior is unchanged.
  - Subagents key on their per-run `createSchedulerConfig(...)` facade object (fresh per `initScheduler`), so sibling subagents with identical session labels get distinct schedulers.
  - Non-interactive executors key on `(this, purpose)`.
- **Deleted**: `packages/core/src/config/schedulerSingleton.ts` and its UUID key-field escape hatch.
- New unit tests (8) cover the same-label distinct-owners acceptance case, refcount dispose-at-zero, concurrent dedup, disposeAll join, unknown-key no-op, first-wins interactiveMode, failed-creation retry, and swallowed dispose errors. Existing suites migrated from string keys to owner objects.

## Reviewer Test Plan

1. `bun test packages/core/src/session/sessionSchedulerRegistryImpl.test.ts` — the acceptance case is the first test.
2. `bun test packages/agents/src/core/agenticLoop/__tests__/agenticLoop.scheduler-isolation.test.ts` — loop-level isolation unchanged.
3. `bun test packages/agents packages/core/src/config/config.scheduler.test.ts` — migrated call sites.
