author: lilseyi
body:
Dragging the file tree's edge to the right worked. Dragging it to the left died a few points in, and only a pull slow enough got anywhere. Two defects wearing one symptom, both found by measuring the shipping bundle in a browser rather than reasoning about the source.

## A drag is a text selection, and a selection ends the gesture

A pointer moving with the button down is a text selection as far as a browser is concerned. react-native-web's responder system listens for `selectionchange` on the document and terminates the current responder the moment the selection becomes a real one — a non-empty string with a text node at either end — asking `onResponderTerminationRequest` first, which **defaults to yes**. Mid-drag that is `onPanResponderTerminate`, and nothing says so except the column stopping under the pointer.

Dragging left crosses the tree's note names, so the gesture died on the first name the pointer got ahead of. Dragging right crosses CodeMirror's editing host, where a selection begun outside does not extend — so that direction never hit it. What was left answered only a pull slow enough to stay inside the handle's own 7pt strip, the one place on that side with no text in it.

The resizer now answers `false` to the request: `selectionchange`, `scroll` and `contextmenu` are the only events routed through it, and none of them should end a drag somebody is in the middle of. A real cancel (`dragstart`, a lost touch) does not ask, and still terminates. For the length of the gesture it also holds `user-select` and the resize cursor on the document, handing both back on release *and* on a cancel — a page left unselectable would be a worse bug than the one this fixes.

## Half the handle was under the editor

The strip straddles the column's border, because people aim *at* an edge rather than a few points inside it, so three of its seven points lie over the editor. Drawn as the column's last child they lay *under* it — later siblings are on top — and every press that landed on the outer half reached the editor instead. That is the grab that felt ignored, and the reason a drag had to start well inside the tree.

It is drawn after the editor now, positioned from the column's width (`explorerSeamOverhang`), and still before the scrim and the peek, which have to cover it.

## Measured, not assumed

Against the shipping bundle **before** the fix, in Chromium on the fixture with the real tree behind it:

- a 45pt pull left moved the seam **3pt** and then froze, leaving `privacy / generated / 19 notes, 14 folders` selected across the tree;
- `elementFromPoint` at the middle of the handle answered the editor's region, not the handle.

After it, both drag the full 45pt, in either direction, and nothing is left selected.

## Guards, each sabotage-checked

- `appFrameRender.test.ts` — drives a real `selectionchange` mid-drag and holds that the column keeps tracking; holds the document's hand-back on release, on a browser cancel and on an unmount mid-gesture; pins the handle's place in the row and its offset from the column's width, at rest and through a drag. Reverting each half fails exactly the case that names it.
- `panels.spec.ts` — drags the seam in a browser, on `?screen=app-frame-visual` (the real `Explorer` in the real frame), including a grab on the half of the handle that lies over the editor. Both new cases fail against the pre-fix bundle.
- Full suites: 6,369 jest tests and the WebKit suite's chromium project (71 passed) — chromium here, because this sandbox has no WebKit binary; CI runs the same specs in WebKit.

The decision is recorded in `docs/decisions/app-and-console.md`, beside the rest of the seam's design.

author: derpimort
body:
Slice 2's fix, for the half of the families my audit found **not** covered ([audit table](https://github.com/Derpimort/mew/issues/139#issuecomment-5721646451)). coderpa's half came back fully covered, so this PR is only the families that needed code.

## The two gaps

**Gap 1 — the label minus its own bracketed day lands in the inbox.** Two Gyms on Wednesday, so the chips read `the 8:30 (Wednesday)`:

```
typed: the 8:30 (Wednesday) → Moved — Gym now lives Wednesday at 15:00.
typed: the 8:30             → Captured "8:30".        ← an inbox thought
```

**Gap 2 — MEW's own question offers words it then refuses.** The ask is:

> two "gym" blocks — **8:30 or 18:30**? Which one?

```
typed: 8:30 → I can place that for you — try "block thursday morning for the deck"…
```

Gap 2 is the one I fixed first, and my peer independently reached the same order for the same reason: this is not a missing feature, it is MEW contradicting itself in two consecutive sentences. The owner did exactly what they were told.

## The fix

A second pass in `typedChipLabel`, after the exact match, accepting a label **without its bracketed qualifier** and **without a leading article**. Deliberately general rather than tied to the which-block family, so an ask whose labels gain a qualifier later is answerable the day it ships — and `labelReadings` excludes the exact label, since that pass has already run.

### Order is the safety, not the rules

@coderpa asked for this specifically before I built it, and it is the part a reviewer cannot see from the rules alone:

- the **exact** pass runs first and always, so a chip reading exactly what was typed can never be beaten by a looser reading of a different chip
- an **ambiguous exact** match refuses rather than falling through — two chips reading the same way are not resolved by trying harder
- a **loose** reading that fits more than one chip refuses too

The precedence case is *constructed*, because no shipping ask produces that collision: chips `the 8:30` and `8:30`, typing `8:30` must pick the exact one. It exists because a future ask might, and because order is invisible in a diff.

### An alternative I did not take

Reword the question to speak the labels (`the 8:30 or the 18:30?`). That fixes one family's sentence and leaves every other family's natural phrasings unanswered — and the current copy reads better. Fixing the reader fixes the class.

## Mutants

Sources restored byte-identical after each:

| mutant | tests failing |
|---|---|
| the second pass never runs (the RC's own behaviour) | 2 |
| the bracketed day is not stripped | 1 |
| the leading article is not stripped, so MEW's own question stays unanswerable | 1 |
| the exact pass is skipped | 8 |
| **the loose pass runs first, so it can beat an exact label** | 1 (the constructed precedence pin) |

## Tests

Three store cases through the **real** asks — the bracketed label, the bare time the question offers, and the day-load offer (whose label has neither a bracket nor an article, so it proves the second pass did not disturb a plain label) — plus three pure cases: the precedence pin, the loose-ambiguity refusal, and the readings a label carries.

### My own guard from #156 caught me

All three new store tests landed **outside their describe** again — a third recurrence of the same slip. `pnpm lint` failed with the file and line before this reached CI:

```
check-test-structure: 3 tests sit outside a describe.
  src/state/__tests__/typed-chip-labels.test.ts:327  it('the which-block ask: the label without…
```

That is the guard doing exactly the job it was written for, on its author, one PR later. Fixed; the file now reads zero top-level tests.

## Gates — RC `f465eba`

```
tsc 0 · build 0 · coverage 0 · lint 0 · format 0 · bundle 0
Test Files  186 passed | 2 skipped (188)
      Tests  2916 passed | 4 skipped (2920)
main 397.2 KB / 440.0 KB · first load 800.8 KB / 1200.0 KB
```

CHANGELOG: one bullet under the section slice 1 added, hand-written; guard 33 sections (33 unique) / 72 bullets (72 unique), no repeats. Tree clean. No `ui/` or `scripts/` change, so shoot and overlap are not required.

## Not closing #139

Per the manager: coderpa's pins land second and carry the `Closes #139` line. That issue stayed open honestly all night and should close the same way.

## Two findings outside this slice, reported not fixed

Both from the audit, both in the ask-when-ambiguous family (#124, #131), and coderpa has offered to file them with repros from my table:

- same title on two **different days** raises no ask at all — `move the gym to 15:00` with Gym on Wednesday and Thursday moves Wednesday's silently
- a day word in a **move** target is not read — `move the wednesday gym to 15:00` → `I couldn't find "wednesday gym" to move`

author: chris-wolfgang
body:
## Summary
Ships `net5.0`, `net6.0` and `net7.0` assemblies alongside the existing targets (`net462;net481;netstandard2.0;net5.0;net6.0;net7.0;net8.0;net10.0`).

**Why.** `Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions` ships per-runtime assets, and an `init` accessor's `IsExternalInit` modreq differs between its `netstandard2.0` build (internal polyfill) and its `net5.0`+ builds (`System.Runtime`). This package's `netstandard2.0` assembly is compiled against the former but, on .NET 5/6/7, is loaded beside the latter — so any write to an inherited options-record property (`SkipItemCount` / `MaximumItemCount` / `ReportingInterval`) from *this* assembly throws `MissingMethodException`. Etl-Csv hit exactly that in its v0.9.0 release gate (Chris-Wolfgang/Etl-Csv#287). Nothing in this repo writes an inherited init property today, so there is no live crash — the extra targets make the class of bug impossible to reintroduce, which is the same shape Abstractions, Etl-DbClient and Etl-Csv already have.

## Verification (local, Release)
- `dotnet build` 0 warnings / 0 errors across all targets.
- Unit suite green on `netcoreapp3.1`, `net5.0`, `net6.0`, `net7.0`, `net8.0` (counts in the commit body of the verification run).

## Release
PATCH (`v0.12.1`) — no API change; new runtime assets only. Per the one-release-per-day rule, tag no earlier than tomorrow. CHANGELOG `### Fixed` and the README framework line are updated here.

body:
## Что меняем и зачем

**Распоряжение владельца 17.09.2026:** никаких массовых выгрузок — они бесполезны и жгут ресурс. Порядок: читаем сделку → читаем запросы поставщикам → видим файлы → качаем по одному. И брать надо **не наши исходящие запросы**, а то, что пришло от сорсеров и контрагентов.

Первая версия повисла на 28-й минуте и не дала ничего. Разбор двенадцатью агентами вскрыл, что она не просто медленная — **она не получила бы ни одного файла**, а часть «разобрала» бы как спецификацию страницу входа в портал.

### Четыре ошибки, все исправлены

| Ошибка | Следствие |
|---|---|
| `crm.deal.list` для файлов не годится: его ссылки ведут на `crm_show_file.php`, где нужна сессия портала | **вебхук получает страницу входа с кодом 200** и разбирает её как спецификацию |
| Маска `select=["*"]` файловых полей не возвращает вовсе | файлов было бы ноль даже при успешном прогоне |
| `urlMachine` уже лежит в объекте, но спрашивался у `disk.*` **перед** этим | два дросселированных вызова на файл впустую, при ошибке шесть повторов с паузой до 3,5 мин — отсюда 28 минут |
| Результат писался только в конце | таймоут унёс всё: ни артефакта, ни описи |

Рабочий путь — `crm.item.list` с `entityTypeId=2` и ссылка `urlMachine`. Это уже было **измерено и записано** в `base/collect_attachments.py` и `base/fetch_files.py`; я написал пятый сборщик вместо того чтобы взять проверенный.

### Снятая ложная гипотеза

Я считал, что Битрикс молча проигнорировал фильтр `parentId2` и отдал весь смарт-процесс. **Проверка по снимку опровергла:** на 219 сделок всего 513 привязанных запросов, максимум 92 на одну. Фильтр работал, дело было не в нём.

### Направление определяется именем поля, а не догадкой

Состав восьми файловых полей СП-166 уже был выверен в `base/fetch_rfq.py`, и он прямо делится:

| Поле | Направление |
|---|---|
| «КП поставщика», «Offer from supplier», «Offer, old», «Processed offer» | **входящее** |
| «Request file» | наш запрос — исключается |
| «Мануал, чертеж, шильд», «Bank Details» | не цены |

Это и есть очевидность из контекста, которую требовал владелец. Где имени поля нет (таймлайн, чат) — читается `DIRECTION` дела или текст рядом с файлом, и **при любом сомнении ставится «неизвестно», а не «наш запрос»**: отброшенное КП мы не увидим никогда, а наш же запрос виден сразу по отсутствию цен. Цена ошибок разная, и правило это учитывает.

### Добавлен обход того, куда я не смотрел вовсе

Комментарии таймлайна · дела с полем `DIRECTION` · **чат сделки**. Владелец прямо сказал, что КП кидают в переписку.

## Как проверено

- [x] `python -m pytest -q` — 630 passed, 45 skipped
- [x] `ruff check .` — без ошибок
- [x] **17 тестов на сборщик**, пять из них новые: файловый объект без `urlMachine` не файл; crm-привязка `CO_9634` не файл; направление по имени поля; сомнение в тексте даёт «неизвестно»; **страница входа не принимается за файл**
- [x] Ранее тесты уже поймали шесть ошибок разбора, включая `964587C1` → цена 964 587 из pdf
- [x] Холостой прогон стоит по умолчанию — правило 3 CLAUDE.md: правило сначала меряют, потом применяют

## Влияние на прод

- [x] деплой какого сайта затрагивается: **никакой**
- [x] секреты не тронуты; воркфлоу только `workflow_dispatch`, без расписания
- [x] бот-файлы в диффе отсутствуют

### Живучесть воркфлоу — три дефекта исправлены

Артефакт теперь **первым и с `if: always()`** · у шага свой таймаут 45 мин меньше таймаута задания 60 · страж цен стоит **после** артефакта и валит только коммит, а не результат.

## Данные

- [x] коммерческих данных в репозиторий не добавлено: цены уезжают артефактом, в коммит идёт опись без цен, греп-страховка отменяет коммит при находке цен

## Summary

Add the SA 2024.1.0508.5 Python client alongside SA 2026.1.0529.7 as independent products under `targets/<exact-sa-release>/`. Both pin the published Briosa v0.6.0 protocol and conformance artifacts. Their initial PyPI distributions are `briosa-2024-1-0508-5` and `briosa-2026-1-0529-7` v0.1.0; applications keep `import briosa`. Install one target per virtual environment because the distributions provide the same import package.

The 2024 facade follows its reviewed protocol: 996 MP operations, including Run Crib Sheet, Project Objects, and Stop Projection. It omits later commands/fields, preserves reserved enum values, requires explicit CAD compatibility and QDAS timestamps, and exposes the exact 2024 statistics outputs. Target identity gates reject a mismatched server.

Correct 33 existing input annotations that used collection-object names where the protocol requires collection-item names, including relationship inputs and the picture-callout anchor. This pre-publication correction applies to both targets and has regression coverage. Portable conformance now disables the desktop monitor explicitly so child process output closes reliably.

- SA 2024: 36 unit/contract tests passed. SA 2026: 19 passed.
- All 12 shared portable conformance scenarios passed for each target.
- Both targets passed Ruff formatting/lint, strict mypy, generated-code drift verification, wheel/sdist builds, package identity checks, and isolated imports from the actual built wheels.

Registry publication and Installer catalog publication are separate work. Licensed SA runtime CI and enterprise Artifactory validation remain outstanding; this change does not promote v1.0.

author: clamberti
body:
## What

Adds the `dark` class to `<html>` in `apps/web/src/app/[locale]/layout.tsx`.

## Why

Each page paints `bg-black text-white` on its own `<main>`, but the shadcn tokens in `globals.css` (`--background`, `--primary`, `--muted`, `--border`) only take their dark values under `.dark`, and no element ever carried that class. `Button` reads those tokens, so on the organizer flow and the public event page:

- `variant="outline"` (Add prize, Close registration, the back buttons) paints `bg-background` = white and inherits the page's white text. You cannot see the label until you hover, and then it flips to light gray with black text.
- `variant="default"` (Save draft, Deposit, Create, Go live, Register) paints `bg-primary` = oklch 0.205 on pure black. You can see it, barely.
- `variant="ghost"` hover paints `bg-muted` = light gray with black text.
- The footer (`border-t text-muted-foreground hover:text-foreground`) shows on the body's white background under a black page.

With `.dark` active the same variants resolve to what the component ships for dark mode: outline gets `border-input bg-input/30` (white/15 border, translucent fill), default becomes a light button with dark text, the same look as the header "Connect wallet", ghost hover is a dark gray fill with white text, and the footer turns dark with light text.

The class is static. The app has no light theme to preserve.

## Not changed

`tx-hash-link.tsx` keeps the explicit zinc classes from #210. They read correctly under `.dark`; moving them back to tokens is a separate cleanup.

## Branch

Based on `fix/web-html-hydration-warning` (#217) because both PRs touch the `<html>` tag. Merge #217 first; this diff then shrinks to the class change plus its comment.

## Checked

- Computed styles on production `/en/organizer/new`: outline buttons `rgb(255,255,255)` background with `rgb(255,255,255)` text; default buttons `lab(7.78)` on `rgb(0,0,0)`.
- `dark:` appears only inside `button.tsx`; no other component changes under the class.
- `globals.css` defines `@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *))`, so the class on `<html>` reaches every element.

author: ezraellette
body:
## Description

Long chat tool sequences can exhaust a 32K context window before automatic compaction runs. The proactive extension waited for a successful settled response, and Pi's default 20K retained-history budget could return “nothing to compact” even when the full request, including the system prompt and tools, exceeded the window.

Backport the fix to the pinned Pi 0.84.1 runtime: check the existing compaction path at 70% between completed tool steps, then supply the rebuilt context to the next model call. Size retained history and summaries against the space remaining after prompt/tool overhead and output allowance. User Stop cancels an in-flight summary; queued instructions are delivered once; failed summaries retain the original history.

The patch is applied atomically and idempotently to Screenpipe's managed runtime during installation and before launch, shared by native Pi, Pi-over-ACP, and managed pipe execution. Unknown runtime source is rejected without overwriting it. Remove the settled-only extension hook while preserving tool-result pruning and provider-overflow normalization. Add the isolated runtime eval to frontend CI.

## Before / after

Reproduction uses the real pinned Pi SDK with a synthetic 32K model, a large system prompt, and sequential lookup results:

```text
Before: lookup 1 -> ... -> lookup 11 -> context overflow
        no successful settled response -> proactive hook never runs

After:  lookups -> 70% context -> summarize -> rebuild context -> continue
        all 14 lookups execute once -> answer completes
        saved compaction summary survives session reload
```

Baseline eval: 1 passed, 4 failed as expected. Patched eval: all 5 passed. Every request in the successful regression remains within the 32K window.

## Historical intent

Inspected [#6867](https://github.com/screenpipe/screenpipe/pull/6867) / `d144428984`, which enabled the shared pruning extension, proactive compaction at 70%, and bounded recovery for the provider's generic overflow error. Preserve those protections and move proactive compaction into Pi's safe boundary between tool steps. The old mocked tests only proved the settled-event callback fired; replace them with tests of actual SDK execution, persisted context, queued instructions, cancellation, and summary failure.

## Validation

From `apps/screenpipe-app-tauri`:

- `bun scripts/eval-pi-compaction.ts --baseline` — 1 passed, 4 failed; reproduces the unpatched failure after 11 lookups.
- `bun scripts/eval-pi-compaction.ts` — 5 passed.
- `/Applications/screenpipe.app/Contents/MacOS/bun scripts/eval-pi-compaction.ts` — 5 passed with bundled Bun 1.3.10.
- `bun x bun@1.2.2 scripts/eval-pi-compaction.ts` — 5 passed with CI's Bun version.
- `bun run test:vitest lib/__tests__/context-pruning.test.ts` — 33 passed.
- `bun run test:tauri shared_pi_extensions_cover_every_pi_harness -- --nocapture` — 1 passed through the native build queue; native app compiled successfully.
- `bun run typecheck` — passed.

From the repository root:

- `cargo test -p screenpipe-core pi_compaction::tests --lib` — 2 passed.
- `bunx --bun @biomejs/biome check apps/screenpipe-app-tauri/scripts/eval-pi-compaction.ts apps/screenpipe-app-tauri/lib/__tests__/context-pruning.test.ts` — passed.
- `git diff --cached --check` — passed before commit.
- `git merge-tree --write-tree HEAD upstream/main` — clean against `a6a915d0a1`.

Evidence covers the real SDK lifecycle with synthetic provider/tool responses and macOS native integration. No packaged-app or live-provider end-to-end test was performed. The backport is tied to Pi 0.84.1; the runtime eval must continue passing when that dependency is upgraded. No Tauri command signatures or frontend bindings changed.

## AI assistance and human ownership

- AI tool: Codex; autonomy level: `agent`.
- Implementation and the automated checks above were performed by Codex at the maintainer's request. No personal manual-testing or human-review attestation is claimed.

## Änderung

Begrenzter Hardening-Scope. Compiler wird Change-Impact-Sensor.

**Invariante:** Untrusted boundary may be `string`. Trusted product domain must be `PlanId` / `EntitlementKey`.

- `assertNever(value, context?)` — Rest auf `never`.
- `ENTITLEMENT_LABELS satisfies Record<EntitlementKey, string>` — neuer SSoT-Key bricht diese Map. `entitlementLabel(string)` bleibt Boundary mit Fallback auf den Key.
- `parsePlanId(string) → PlanId | null` — volle `PlanId`-Union inkl. `governance_launch`. `scale` / `free_audit` / yearly bleiben `null` (`normalizePlanKey` / `PlanKey`).
- `AIGenerationResult` als Literal-Union. `html` nur auf `success: true`.

**Nicht in diesem PR:** Auth-Umbau (`instanceof Response` bleibt), keine neuen internen `PlanId | string`-APIs, Wizard-`invoke`, #1401/#1406 (Overlap auf derselben Function — ältere PRs danach `sync:main`).

CI auf dem Head: Build SPA, hygiene, Playwright, CodeQL, Pages deploy grün.

---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Mostly compile-time and display labels; the edge function change is a typing-safe refactor with the same fallback behavior on AI failure.
> 
> **Overview**
> Hardens pricing/catalog typing so **new SSoT keys fail at compile time** instead of silently missing UI labels. **`ENTITLEMENT_LABELS`** replaces a partial map with an exported object that **`satisfies Record<EntitlementKey, string>`**, adds German labels for previously unlabeled keys, and keeps **`entitlementLabel(string)`** as an untrusted boundary with key fallback.

> Adds **`assertNever`** for exhaustiveness in switches and **`parsePlanId`** to narrow external strings to **`PlanId | null`** (full union including `governance_launch`; rejects aliases like `scale` / `free_audit`).

author: tristan-stoltz-erc
body:
## Purpose

Freeze the first evidence/conservation boundary for compost and co-compost modeling before any predictive or adaptive process intelligence becomes load-bearing.

Program: `Luminous-Dynamics/mycelix#940`
Parent: #3769 / REGEN-032

## Exact subject

ProductHead:
`efa30c85872c2b3c2d251c0580b0c41d031f76c9`

Parent:
`0ab0e556efd451df8c3a6d299bf6a96f6ead035e`

Exactly **one docs-only child commit / one file**:

`docs/regenerative/REGEN-033_COMPOST_ACCOUNTING_V1.md`

## Important existing-model correction

Current `symthaea-circular::DecompositionPredictor` embeds fixed category half-lives plus heuristic Q10, moisture, oxygen and C:N response functions. REGEN-033 does **not** adopt those values as normative compost science. Until separately qualified, that predictor is treated only as an explicitly identified `HeuristicShadowModel`.

```text
predicted decomposition %
!= measured mass loss
!= stability
!= maturity
!= sanitation
!= agronomic suitability
```

## Core theorem

```text
evidence-bound consumed inputs
+ explicit process-observation lineage
+ explicit material/nutrient accounting
+ identified model assumptions
= bounded compost accounting result
```

not mature/safe compost, agronomic suitability, process authority, or physical action.

## Key firewalls

- elapsed time != maturity;
- material closure != nutrient closure;
- total nutrient != plant-available nutrient;
- maturity != sanitation != contamination clearance != suitability;
- scenario accounting != evidence reconciliation;
- co-compost child does not inherit strongest parent state;
- no universal C:N/moisture/O2/temperature/turning/time recipe;
- model output does not mint real batch evidence.

## First executable target

Start smaller than the existing heuristic predictor: exact input/output/loss mass accounting with explicit unresolved residual and an independent conservation oracle. Add multi-input blends, nutrient ledgers, observation bindings, and shadow-model comparisons only in later qualified increments.

## Status

Preregistration only. Keep draft.

author: justinclayton
body:
## What changed

Crowbar — *"Play: if you get any Good Stuff this turn, get an additional one."* — is `onPlay` in `app/src/domain/cards/stuff.ts`, a one-shot resolved the moment it enters the play zone. It no longer works as a standing trigger that listens while the card sits in a hand, so it can never count its own arrival: a room handing Crowbar to a hand is not Crowbar being played.

The designer ruled it a second time (open question #16): a played Crowbar's "this turn" covers the whole turn it sits in the play zone, including a room's own payout at Outcome, which resolves after the whole Play phase has already run — that ordering is specifically the primary use case, not an edge case. So Crowbar checks both halves of the turn:

- `onPlay` looks backward, once, at `thisTurn.goodStuffTaken` — a gain its controller already got earlier in the same turn.
- A new `onEvent`, listening only while the card sits in the play zone (the same shape Covering Fire uses for `CARD_PLAYED`), catches a gain that lands later — a room's Outcome payout being the one there is today.

Only one of the two ever pays out. The once-per-turn `fired` marker from the original design (open question #16) is back, keyed by each Crowbar's own card id: whichever hook pays first marks it, so the other stays quiet, and the bonus piece it grants — itself a `STUFF_TAKEN` for good_stuff — can never retrigger it. Two Crowbars each carry their own key, so two played in one turn pay two.

`design/cards.yaml` keeps the `Play:` prefix; nothing else needed it.

## Media

Crowbar's printed face, showing the `Play:` line (`prototype/card-sheet.html`):

body:
Encontrado en el log de Madre del 2026-09-17, en el primer arranque real con recordatorios (#37):

```
asyncio - ERROR - Task was destroyed but it is pending!
task: <Task pending name='Task-5' coro=<bucle() ...recordatorios.py:88>>
```

Dos fallos en la misma línea:

1. **`asyncio.create_task` no guarda una referencia fuerte.** `arrancar()` la devolvía y `bot.py` la tiraba: el recolector de basura podía llevarse el bucle a media ejecución y dejar el bot sin avisos **sin que nada lo dijera**. Es el caso que la documentación de asyncio avisa con esas palabras («save a reference to the result of this function»). Ahora se guarda en el módulo.
2. **Nadie la cancelaba al apagar.** `parar()` lo hace, enganchado en `post_shutdown`. No rompía nada —el proceso se iba igual— pero un ERROR en el log de cada reinicio es justo lo que enseña a no leer los logs.

## Verificación
202 pruebas (2 nuevas), ruff limpio, `verificar.py` en verde. Las nuevas comprueban que `arrancar()` deja la referencia puesta, que `parar()` cancela y recoge, y que parar sin haber arrancado no revienta.

author: alex-arguello
body:
Ticket: [PLA-3021](https://linear.app/payabli/issue/PLA-3021/clientios-a-conflict-is-classified-as-settled-so-an-outcome-that-may) (a conflict is classified as settled, so an outcome that may have taken the money reads as known)

A `409` on a money-moving route was classified as an answer, so a host was told the payment's outcome was known. It is not. The service writes its idempotency marker before the request is handled and never rolls it back, so a `409` says only that it has seen the key inside its window — the attempt that key named may have taken the payment, and may have failed while taking it. This moves `.conflict` to the arm that leaves the outcome open, so a `409` now arrives as `submissionInterrupted` and a host reading `code` still sees `.conflict`.

## Structure

**The classification stays decidable on the error code alone.** This client publishes no key on any route, so it never has to ask whose key was sent, and the rule can be stated as one member of a switch. That is why the change is a single move between two arms rather than a new branch on the call site.

**The same claim was stated in three places and only one of them was the code.** The doc on `submissionInterrupted` listed a recognised repeat among what "arrives as itself", and `PayabliErrorCode.conflict` in core said a money-moving `409` settles. Both now say what a `409` establishes, because a reader who finds either one first would reintroduce the defect.

## Notable changes

- `PayInPaymentFlowClient.leavesOutcomeUnknown` returns true for `.conflict`. A `409` on a route that carried a key is wrapped; every other code's classification is unchanged.
- `PayabliPayInPaymentFlowError.submissionInterrupted` and `PayabliErrorCode.conflict` doc comments now describe the wrapped case. The core one also dropped a claim that the sibling platform has no `CONFLICT`, which it does.
- The sample's duplicate-submission message no longer ends by telling an operator to start a new attempt. Its unresolved flag derives from the wrapper, so a `409` flips it, and the old text invited a second payment while the first one's fate was open.
- Both `causeType` values are now asserted. A `409` answered with a body names the flow's error type and a bodyless one names core's; neither was pinned.

## Verification

`xcodebuild test -scheme PayabliSDK-Package` on iPhone 17 (iOS Simulator): 160 tests, 0 failures. `xcodebuild test -project Example/PayabliDemo/PayabliDemo.xcodeproj -scheme PayabliDemoFlowTests` on the same destination: 136 tests, 0 failures. `swiftlint --strict --baseline .swiftlint-baseline.json`: 0 violations over 253 files. `swiftformat --lint .`: 0 of 254 files need formatting.

The two cases that pin the new behaviour were run against the unchanged classification first and both failed, reporting the raw error where the wrapper was expected, while the other 23 in that file passed. A second reviewer ran an independent pass over the finished branch.

## Not included

A `409` on a reversal is left reporting an open outcome like any other keyed route, and no handling is built for it. `voidTransaction` mints a fresh key per call, so no repeat of one can be recognised, and the repeat this change is about does not arise there.

The transaction identifier does not survive the wrapper on any route, which is a standing gap on this platform rather than something this change introduces — the carrier a `409` replaces holds no identifier either. It is tracked separately.

body:
Cloudburst production can rewrite `funnel=1`/`from=cloudburst` into JSON-quoted query tokens, which caused Interfractal to miss funnel arrival and show Light/Whole instead of close rail. This change makes funnel parsing tolerant of quoted tokens and removes wildcard `postMessage` targeting in favor of a strict parent-origin allowlist.

- **Funnel ingress compatibility (quoted token normalization)**
  - Normalized query/object token values before evaluation (trim + unquote single/double-quoted wrappers).
  - `parseFunnelSearch` now correctly treats values like `%22cloudburst%22` and `%221%22` as `cloudburst` / `1`.
  - Preserves existing behavior for non-funnel traffic (`/` still lands on Light/Whole).

- **Cross-origin messaging hardening**
  - Replaced `window.parent.postMessage(payload, "*")` with resolved parent origin only when allowlisted.
  - Allowlist:
    - `https://keep-your-judgment.vercel.app`
    - `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` preview origins
  - If parent origin is missing/unknown/not allowlisted, no message is sent.

- **Regression coverage**
  - Added focused tests for quoted `from`/`funnel`/`warmup` tokens.
  - Added guard test to ensure wildcard `postMessage` is not reintroduced.

```ts
function tokenOn(value: unknown): boolean {
  const normalized = normalizeToken(value);
  return normalized === "1" || normalized === 1 || normalized === true || normalized === "true";
}

// ...
const parentOrigin = resolveAllowedParentOrigin();
if (!parentOrigin) return;
window.parent?.postMessage(payload, parentOrigin);
```

Do not merge. Do not deploy.

Continue from that host may arrive here as from=%22cloudburst%22&funnel=%221%22. parseFunnelSearch / tokenOn on main only accepts 1 / "1" / true / "true" and exact from=cloudburst. Quoted tokens will miss skipIntro and drop the visitor on Light/Whole.

body:
## 🤖 Installing Claude Code GitHub App

This PR adds a GitHub Actions workflow that enables Claude Code integration in our repository.

### What is Claude Code?

[Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) is an AI coding agent that can help with:
- Bug fixes and improvements  
- Documentation updates
- Implementing new features
- Code reviews and suggestions
- Writing tests
- And more!

### How it works

Once this PR is merged, we'll be able to interact with Claude by mentioning @claude in a pull request or issue comment.
Once the workflow is triggered, Claude will analyze the comment and surrounding context, and execute on the request in a GitHub action.

### Important Notes

- **This workflow won't take effect until this PR is merged**
- **@claude mentions won't work until after the merge is complete**
- The workflow runs automatically whenever Claude is mentioned in PR or issue comments
- Claude gets access to the entire PR or issue context including files, diffs, and previous comments

### Security

- Our Anthropic API key is securely stored as a GitHub Actions secret
- Only users with write access to the repository can trigger the workflow
- All Claude runs are stored in the GitHub Actions run history
- Claude's default tools are limited to reading/writing files and interacting with our repo by creating comments, branches, and commits.
- We can add more allowed tools by adding them to the workflow file like:

```
allowed_tools: Bash(npm install),Bash(npm run build),Bash(npm run lint),Bash(npm run test)
```

There's more information in the [Claude Code action repo](https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code-action).

After merging this PR, let's try mentioning @claude in a comment on any PR to get started!

body:
## Summary
Ships `net5.0`, `net6.0` and `net7.0` assemblies alongside the existing targets (`net462;net481;netstandard2.0;net5.0;net6.0;net7.0;net8.0;net10.0`).

**Why.** `Wolfgang.Etl.Abstractions` ships per-runtime assets, and an `init` accessor's `IsExternalInit` modreq differs between its `netstandard2.0` build (internal polyfill) and its `net5.0`+ builds (`System.Runtime`). This package's `netstandard2.0` assembly is compiled against the former but, on .NET 5/6/7, is loaded beside the latter — so any write to an inherited options-record property (`SkipItemCount` / `MaximumItemCount` / `ReportingInterval`) from *this* assembly throws `MissingMethodException`. Etl-Csv hit exactly that in its v0.9.0 release gate (Chris-Wolfgang/Etl-Csv#287). Nothing in this repo writes an inherited init property today, so there is no live crash — the extra targets make the class of bug impossible to reintroduce, which is the same shape Abstractions, Etl-DbClient and Etl-Csv already have.

## Verification (local, Release)
- `dotnet build` 0 warnings / 0 errors across all targets.
- Unit suite green on `netcoreapp3.1`, `net5.0`, `net6.0`, `net7.0`, `net8.0` (counts in the commit body of the verification run).

author: westkitty
body:
## Summary

Establish the production-safe Three.js foundation and the first canonical-state-driven machine without replacing the existing mystery engine.

### Runtime foundation
- pin `three@0.186.0`
- prepare `three.module.js` + `three.core.js` locally for browser/Pages delivery
- remove the runtime CDN dependency
- use one managed WebGL renderer and one animation-loop owner
- keep Three.js failure non-fatal with explicit no-WebGL fallback
- handle context loss/restoration and scene cleanup
- add dedicated CI coverage

### Canonical state projection
- add a pure read-only `MachineState -> PhysicalState` projection layer
- establish `docs/THREEJS_STATE_CONTRACT.md` as the authority/invariant contract
- make DEIMOS the reference implementation:
  - canonical orientation drives the 3D apparatus in 45-degree steps
  - canonical `safeOpen` drives a modeled persistent safe door
  - CEILING alignment produces a restrained visual apparatus cue
- keep puzzle/state/navigation authority in the existing store and machine modules

## Protected behavior
- existing puzzles and machine rules remain authoritative
- semantic DOM controls remain available
- room traversal, persistence, archive, notebook, and endings remain unchanged
- Three.js is derived presentation state, never sole gameplay authority

## Verification
Exact branch checkpoint `8d2954db25aa182e13b8edf7e629aa21f9b9f4ee` passed GitHub Actions run `35279256642`:
- Core QA: 74/74
- Browser QA: 29/29
- Three.js resilience QA: pass
- Three.js state projection QA: pass

Real GPU/WebGL visual correctness remains explicitly unverified until the merged Pages build is observed in a real WebGL browser. That limitation is recorded in `OPERATIONAL_STATE.md`.

body:
## Le problème

Testé sur iPhone : le CV partagé depuis Safari arrivait sous le nom **« fr »**.

Safari sur iOS ignore `Content-Disposition` et nomme le fichier d'après le
dernier segment de l'URL. Servi sur `/v1/cv/fr.pdf`, ce segment était `fr`.

## Le correctif

L'API sert désormais `/v1/cv/amissan.ag-cv-{langue}.pdf` (déployé, PR #2 sur
`portfolio-api`, l'ancien chemin répond 301). Le site suit.

## Ce que les tests protégeaient vraiment — et ne protégeaient pas

Quatre tests verrouillaient `/v1/cv/{langue}.pdf`. Ils comparaient une chaîne :
le chemin fautif les passait **tous** tout en produisant « fr » au partage. Un
test qui ne peut pas échouer sur le vrai défaut ne protège rien.

Ils vérifient maintenant l'invariant : le nom que lit un recruteur est porteur,
distinct d'une langue à l'autre, et servi par **les deux voies** —
`Content-Disposition` pour un navigateur de bureau, dernier segment d'URL pour
Safari iOS.

## Vérifications

- `npm run verify` — 77 tests unitaires, lint, types, tokens, secrets
- `E2E_API=1 npm run test:e2e` — 119 tests, 2 navigateurs (bureau et 400 px)
- Contrat inter-dépôts contre `api.amissan.dev` **réelle** : octets `%PDF-`,
  `304` à la revalidation par `ETag`, et
  `content-disposition: inline; filename="amissan.ag-cv-fr.pdf"`

author: lilseyi
body:
The desktop canvas's second half. #633 was the frame; this is what the frame is around — plus one bug the phone screenshots turned up on the way. Measured against `App-Dark.dc.html` and `App-Light.dc.html` at 1440×900 in both schemes, in a real Chromium.

## A note nobody has touched draws no markup

Live Preview hides markup away from the caret — and a caret exists the moment a document does. `openingCaret` puts it past the frontmatter, which is the first line of the writing, and on most notes that is `# Title`. So every note *opened* rather than edited drew its own page title as `# Context.LC — build decisions`, hash and all, at a reader who had not touched anything. The canvas draws it clean, and so does every editor with a live preview: markup comes back **where you are working**.

`editorEngaged` is the gate, and it reads engagement rather than DOM focus. That distinction is the whole feature, and it cost a measurement to find: written first as focus, it broke Bold-from-the-menu *invisibly*. The right-click popover blurs the editor, `runMenuAction` calls `view.focus()` straight back, `document.activeElement` really is `.cm-content` — and a blur transaction still arrives last. So the `**` went in and rendered hidden, and Bold looked like a no-op. Chasing that ordering would be a fresh round for every popover, toolbar and side panel this product grows.

So the gate is: closed by `replaceDocument` on every note put on screen (explicitly, because this view is built once and has notes swapped through it — otherwise the second note inherits the first one's engagement); opened by a click in the text, an edit, or focus; and never closed by a blur, because reaching for a menu is not leaving.

A state with no such field reveals exactly as before, which is what keeps every direct `decorationsFor` call in the unit suite asking about constructs rather than about focus.

## The line above it says the one thing nothing else does

It was `@seyi / 1-projects / Context.LC — build decisions`, and two thirds of that is drawn twice within 90pt: the workspace is the switcher chip directly above, the note's name is the H1 directly below at 30pt. A line that repeats its neighbours in a smaller face is a line a reader learns to skip. It is the folders now.

The access clause loses three of its four colours and its long wording. A hue per case is how a *chip* tells states apart, and this is a clause in a sentence; what keeps a colour is the one state that widens who can read the note — `team`, in the same violet the file tree marks it with. `private` narrowing access is the safe direction and does not need one.

**The phone's line is untouched, and stays that way.** `pathOnly` returns before any of this. `Phone-Note.dc.html` draws the same trim up there — `bible-study / kings`, no context, no leaf — and it should not be copied: `noteChrome.test.ts` records that the phone's leaf was **deleted once before and came back**, because the inline title lives *inside the scroller* and is gone the moment you read past the first screen, and `index.md` has no folder above it, so a folders-only band would name nothing at all. At pointer width the tab strip covers that; on a phone nothing does. The artboard's note happens to open with a `# heading`; a note captured by email does not, and its filename is a content hash.

## The editor's heading ladder is the type scale

30 / 23 / 19 against a 16px body — `pointerType`'s own `title`, `h2` and `h3`. It was 1.625 / 1.3 / 1.15, which was a *third* ladder after the 1.7 / 1.4 / 1.2 it replaced, and neither was the tokens'. Two scales in one application is one of them being wrong wherever they meet, and where they met was the note: a 30pt title in the tokens, a 26pt one on the page.

## The status bar

No character count. "61 words" and "390 characters" are the same fact told twice, and the second needed its own tooltip to explain that it was counting UTF-16 code units rather than anything a reader can see. `countUnits` went with it rather than staying as a helper nobody calls.

Storage gets the canvas's 6pt pip — the bar's one *health* claim rather than a measurement. A flag rather than "every toned segment gets one", because every segment has a tone and a row of lights is the opposite of a bar you can read at a glance.

## And the tab strip stays off the phone

`AppFrame`'s `tabs` prop has said "pointer layouts only" since #633 added it, and nothing enforced it. `console/_layout.tsx` guards with `!phone` — worth keeping, it avoids building a strip nothing draws — but a contract that lives only in its callers is one a caller can break in silence.

One did: `AppFrameVisualFixture` passes `tabs` unconditionally, so a 390pt board came back with a pointer tab strip lying across the top of the phone's note. Nothing in the suite failed. It was visible only in a screenshot taken to compare the phone against the canvas.

The frame refuses the slot at compact now, and `appFrameRender.test.ts` passes `tabs` at **every** width to say so — including a rotation from 1280 to 390, because the condition is render-time and a fresh mount would not catch a slot that checks its width once.

## Self-review

- **Four tests broke and none of them were noise; each is a fact that moved.** `folderViewMenu`'s "the leaf has no menu" is now "the leaf is not on this line at all", asserted beside the folders so it cannot pass on an empty render — absence is the stronger claim and the one a reversal breaks. `browseShare`'s read-only case proved the note was open by finding `privacy` in the pane; it uses `access map` and the editor's own placeholder now, both better witnesses than a filename that could have come from anywhere. `settings.spec.ts`'s `openConsole` waited on `breadcrumb-leaf` — a wait that passed at 390pt and hung for the full 30s at 1280, which is how it surfaced: two pointer-width cases timing out in a helper rather than in an assertion.
- **The comment claiming `typeScale.test.ts` held the ladder to the tokens was false when written.** It is true now — a guard nobody has checked is not a guard. It reads `livePreview.ts` as text rather than importing it, because that suite's jest project does not transform `@codemirror/*`, and an import fails the file to *run*: nothing reported rather than green, but still not a guard.
- **The backtick trap caught me again**, in the same file that carries a warning about it: a comment inside a template literal with `pointerType` in backticks ends the string. The rewritten comment says so, with the incident attached.
- Every new guard here was sabotaged before committing. The reveal gate: one failure, the right one, every other reveal test green — which is the third claim (a state without the field behaves as before) checking itself. The tab slot: two of three fail, the wide case stays green.

## What this does not close, said out loud

- The canvas draws a count on `0-inbox` in the visibility marker's slot. That is a feature with a meaning to decide, not a restyle.
- It has no "19 notes, 14 folders" foot on the tree and no panel toggle in the status bar. Both are controls with no other route, so removing them to match a picture is a call worth making out loud.
- **The phone and the landing page are measured but not closed.** What is genuinely missing on the phone: the `@seyi` pill at the head of the context strip (filled, with an 18pt mark — today the current workspace is the breadcrumb's first crumb and a floating circle in the corner), and `Phone-Browse.dc.html`'s grouped 48pt rows in an 18pt card, its 56pt floating toolbar and its FAB. Neither can be reviewed from `?screen=app-frame-visual` yet: its top and bottom slots are the stubs `"actions"` and `"toolbar"`, so there is no phone chrome there to compare. The type scale already agrees — `touchType` is 28 / 22 / 17, exactly the artboard. The three Landing boards have not been read.

6,402 mobile checks, lint and typecheck clean; CI green including WebKit.

🤖 Generated w

author: nthomsencph
body:
On top of the codec branch (#25). The third of six PRs from the code-first review of the 2.0 line: the type vocabulary belongs to the registry.

**What changed**

- **Declaring a type records nothing.** `DType._by_id` and `registered_dtypes()` are gone. A notebook cell that declares `class Text(DType, str): id = "text"` runs twice; a host declares its own `Text` beside the standard library's. The README's blocks now run in order in one process, and a test keeps it so.
- **A subclass names itself.** `id` must be in the class's own body; a subclass that leaves it to its parent is refused at definition, so a `Whole` never travels as `number` unnoticed. A parameterisation — `Series[Text]`, a host's `Table[columns]` — is built with the class keyword `parameterises=Base`, keeps the base's id, and is the one exemption. The mark needs a concrete `DType` among the class's bases, refuses an id of its own, and is not inherited.
- **A registry owns its vocabulary.** `register(cls)` files the words a node's versions declare (a scalar as itself, `Series[X]` as `X`, nothing for `Any` or a closed input's plain type); `add_types(*types)` files the host's. `registry.types` reads them by id. One id from two classes is refused where the second arrives — inside one call as well as against what is filed — naming both modules, and nothing is filed on a refusal. `extended_with` carries the vocabulary over.
- **`accepted_as` is the registry's answer.** `registry.accepted_as(T)` is every id in that vocabulary whose `accepts` admits `T`, its own included, a series judged by its element. `_admits` is gone, so a bug in a type's `accepts` surfaces instead of dropping the type from every answer.
- **The palette is `registry.describe()`.** A `RegistryDescription` of every node's `NodeDescription` plus one `TypeDescription` per word — `id`, `title`, `accepted_as`. A field's dtype record is `{"id": ...}` (a series' `of` and a table's `columns` as before): where a value may land is a fact about a vocabulary, which a field's dump cannot know, so it is served once per type rather than on every field.

**Worth knowing when reviewing**

- The providers' `/nodes` and `palette_from_registry` still dump node records only, so an editor behind them has no `accepted_as`; both are on the surface-sweep PR's list.
- The test types keep their `<file>-test-` id prefixes; they no longer need them.
- Retargets to #25's successor when that merges.

**Tests**

759 pass, ruff clean, the six notebooks run.

author: tnunamak
body:
A personal-data server can return records successfully while ignoring the permissions its user approved. This adds an executable conformance harness for PDPP, the Personal Data Portability Protocol, that checks both permitted access and requests that must be refused, with results mapped to the [Core specification’s Section 9 checklist](https://github.com/PDP-Connect/pdpp/blob/main/spec-core.md#9-conformance). It changes no protocol requirements or certification rules.

Tests reach the target over HTTP. Adapters handle each implementation’s consent and token-issuance flow, allowing the same assertions to run against PDP-Connect’s reference server and Vana’s Personal Server, two distinct implementations that store personal data and enforce access permissions. Reports distinguish passes, failures, missing test cases and unavailable fixtures; incomplete coverage cannot produce a full-conformance result.

The harness tests itself against servers with deliberate defects. Positive controls prevent a server that denies every request from passing an access-control test. Coverage includes scoped records and metadata, pagination, authorization-code replay, revocation, expiry, and blob authorization. Blob checks compare returned bytes and headers before testing denial with the same token.

The script that prepares the Vana test target pins a published server commit, boots and seeds a local instance, and obtains tokens through its actual consent flow. A dedicated client with a short grant lifetime tests that the same token reads a known record before expiry and is refused afterward. Other clients retain their normal lifetime.

The latest Vana run exercises 23 of 36 applicable authorization-server/resource-server checklist items, with all 23 passing. This does not establish full normative conformance, Client-role conformance or deployed-product readiness. Remaining evidence gaps include blob fixtures, complete issued-grant inspection, cross-user access and reuse of a consumed single-use grant. Nine applicable checklist items still have no executable case.

author: ssowonny
body:
## TL;DR - Agents working over MCP can finally **link** the files they talk about — every tool that names a file hands back its hub page beside the path. - `list` / `glob` / `files_only` grep rows get a trailing link column; `read`, `write`, `move`, `restore` and `history` get a `url:` line. - Links carry the project **id** and percent-encode each segment: a formula the agent builds from the name-based paths these tools print can land on a different project, and dies on a space or a `#`. - Reading a past version links **that** version (`?v=`), not the live page, so the link matches the bytes the answer was written from. - Known gap: grep's match rows stay link-free (see below) — `files_only: true` is the grep mode whose rows carry links. ## Why emit the URL instead of describing it The CLI door has had a link convention for a while: `bdrive sync --hook` injects a formula as `additionalContext`, and agents append `` `path` [🔗](hub url) `` to synced paths they mention. The MCP door printed paths and nothing else, so the same agent working on a project it has *not* synced could only say "see `/wiki/docs/spec.md`" and leave the reader to find it. A formula would have been cheaper, and wrong twice over: 1. **The paths these tools print carry the project's NAME** (deliberately — a UUID in every row is unquotable). The viewer resolves a name only when it is unique among the projects the *browser user* can see, which is a larger set than the agent's grant — so a name unambiguous to the agent can be ambiguous to whoever receives the link, and it lands on a project list instead of the file. The id always resolves, for every reader. 2. **Percent-encoding**: a space or a `#` in a filename is a dead link, and the separators have to stay literal (same rule `router.ts` parses by). The origin comes off the request, the way `issuer()` does for the OAuth metadata — one hub answers on a tunnel, a LAN address and a public name, and a link pinned to one of them is dead in the other two. ## Where the links appear | Tool | Shape | | --- | --- | | `list`, `glob`, `grep files_only` | trailing tab-separated column (last, so every existing column keeps its position) | | `read` | `url:` line under the header — pinned with `?v=` when reading a past version | | `write`, `edit`, `move`, `restore`, `history` | `url:` line | | `read` of a binary / oversized image | the link, next to the existing "open it in the viewer" | | `delete` | none — the file is gone, a link would 404 | The session instructions now say what the `url:` lines are for, in the same `path` + emoji formula the CLI hook uses, so an agent behaves the same through either door. ## The gap: grep match rows A grep row is `path:N:text` and the only other lines grep prints are bracketed notes, so anything reading its output line by line can tell the two apart. A trailing `Links:` block is path-shaped lines *with no line number in them* — it broke the first reader that parsed it (`TestMCPGrepContextDoesNotDuplicate Lines` panicked on the link line), which is exactly what it would do to an agent reconstructing a file from grep output. So match mode has no links, and `files_only: true` — one row per file — carries them instead. Also skipped: the root listing's project rows. Its rows are addresses that must resolve back to the project they name, and that contract has its own test; a project-page link is a separate question from linking a file. ## Tests - `TestMCPOutputCarriesHubLinks` — every surface above, through the real MCP protocol, on a file named `notes/road map #2.md` so the encoding is asserted, written **by project name** while the link comes back **by id**. - `TestMCPReadOfOldVersionLinksThatVersion` — `?v=` pinning. - `TestMCPOutputPathsUseProjectNames` now strips links before asserting the output is UUID-free: the *paths* stay name-based, the links are id-based on purpose. - Full `go test ./...` green. ## Docs `README.md` and `web/docs/.../guides/mcp.md` both gained a short section — these are the same gated URLs `bdrive url` prints (sign-in + membership), not public share links. ## Architecture changes `architecture/webapp-server.md`: the MCP section gains one class, `fileURL` — the link builder that takes its origin off the request (`mcpBaseKey`) and renders `//` — and one relationship, `mcpTools ..> fileURL`. Nothing was removed or renamed. > ✅ added · ❌ removed (strikethrough) · unmarked = unchanged ```mermaid flowchart TB mcpTools["
mcpTools <<10 tools>>
list read glob grep
write edit delete move
history restore
"] internalClient["
internalClient <<mcp.go>>
re-enters Server.apiMux
memWriter captures the response
withGrant + withUser on the context
"] lockPath["
lockPath
<<sync.Map of per-path mutexes>>
"] recordAgentRead["
recordAgentRead
ReadKindAgent
actor mcp:<grantID>
"] fileURL["
fileURL <<mcp.go>>
origin off the request (mcpBaseKey)
/<project-ID>/<percent-encoded path>
"] mcpTools -- "every tool" --> internalClient mcpTools -- "edit, restore" --> lockPath mcpTools -- "read" --> recordAgentRead mcpTools -- "✅ link beside every named file" --> fileURL classDef added fill:#22c55e22,stroke:#22c55e,stroke-width:2px class fileURL added linkStyle 3 stroke:#22c55e,stroke-width:2px ``` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: mattdhill
body:
## Summary

`docs.start9.com` and `marketplace.start9.com` resolve to evelyn now, so the VPS halves of the deploys go:

- `deploy-brochure.yml` — SSH setup and rsync removed; the NextExplorer publish is the deploy.
- `docs-deploy.yml` — rsync, `book_versions.conf` generation and nginx reload removed; it publishes to Pages itself (`keep: 0.3.5.x`), through the action in the tree.
- `WEBSITE_DEPLOY_KEY` is no longer referenced anywhere; delete the secret once the `live-docs` copy of `docs-deploy.yml` has moved on (below).

The `docs-deploy.yml` on `master` reaches `live-docs` only with the next product tag, and until then the copy there still rsyncs to a box that is going away. So `deploy-docs-pages.yml` keeps publishing in the meantime, with two changes: it follows **every** `Build and deploy docs` run, not only successful ones — the VPS steps will start failing, and the publisher's own build is its gate — and it stands down by itself once it finds the `live-docs` copy of `docs-deploy.yml` publishing on its own. It can be deleted after that.

`versions.conf`'s header and the start-docs docs stop describing nginx maps; the routing they drove is what `build.sh` writes into the tree.

author: rasuvaeff
body:
Class A findings of the 2026-09-18 full-cycle review — each reproduced by a probe, each with a regression test. No API shape changes.

| Fix | Issue |
|---|---|
| `readOnly`/`writeOnly` properties are dropped under `additionalProperties` as they already were under `properties`, `items` and the composition keywords; a map of objects kept the other direction's property required and rejected a legal request. `not` is deliberately left alone. | Fixes #130 |
| `requireMatch()` prints the request path, not the URI, in its `UnknownOperation` message; `request.server.mismatch` renders scheme/host/port instead of the PSR-7 authority. Query strings and userinfo carry credentials, and `unmatchedResult()` already printed the path alone for that reason. | Fixes #131 |
| `schema: false` on a non-JSON response body is reported as `response.body.schema`, as the request side and the JSON branch already did; the opaque branch read it as "no schema declared" and passed the body. | Fixes #132 |

Checks: `composer build` (751 tests), `composer rector`, `git diff --check`; `make mutation` — 2407 mutants, Covered Code MSI 93% at gate 92, one new escape classified as equivalent in `AGENTS.md`; the generated-corpus differential is unchanged (435 cases).

author: ccoventry
body:
> **Stacked on #279.** Base is `feat/hide-scoreboard`, so this diff is just the two new features. Merge #279 first and GitHub retargets this to `dev` automatically.

Two more things that could only be fixed by editing game files, turned into settings.

## `dodtools_mute_voice_commands 1`

"Fire in the hole!" and the rest replay from a demo exactly as the player pressed them, over whatever the clip is actually about. The workaround was overwriting every `player/us*.wav`, `player/brit*.wav` and `player/ger*.wav` with a blank sound — destroying shipped game content for a per-take decision.

DoD plays them through exactly two client event callbacks:

```
pfnHookEvent("events/misc/usvoice.sc",  client+0xb3f0)   ; US *and* British
pfnHookEvent("events/misc/gervoice.sc", client+0xb5d0)   ; German
```

behind three contiguous 28-entry `const char*` tables:

| table | first entries |
|---|---|
| `+0x1c55c8` | `player/usattack.wav`, `player/ushold.wav`, … |
| `+0x1c5638` | `player/britattack.wav`, `player/brithold.wav`, … |
| `+0x1c56a8` | `player/gerattack.wav`, `player/gerhold.wav`, … |

Those being *exactly* the files the blank-wav trick overwrites is the evidence that this is the whole mechanism, not one path of several.

Each callback reaches `pEventAPI->EV_PlaySound` through `call dword ptr [ebx]`. **Those two calls become `90 90`.** The stack needs no other change: cleanup is caller-side and separate (`add esp, 0x20` and `add esp, 0x24`) and doesn't move.

**Patching the call rather than stubbing the callback is the whole point.** Everything after it still runs, and what it does is print the chat line — so this reproduces the blank-wav behaviour exactly. A `ret` at the top would have been simpler and would have taken the chat line with it, silently.

The tail, read rather than assumed: it gets the speaker and the local player, returns if they are not on the same team, **returns whenever the observer-mode global is non-zero — i.e. whenever you are spectating** — returns if the speaker is too far away, and only then formats `(PlayerName): Fire in the hole!` from the `#Voice_subtitle_*` table behind a `#VOICE` prefix.

So in practice: **in an HLTV demo the chat line never appears at all**, and this only ever removes the sound. In a POV demo the sound goes and the chat line stays, exactly as it did with blanked `.wav` files. Removing that too is a `ret` at the top of each callback — a second mode, not a different design, and not built because nothing has asked for it.

*(An earlier version of this description claimed the tail also draws "the voice icon over the speaker". That was never verified and is wrong: `sprites/voiceicon.spr` belongs to `CVoiceStatus`, the voice chat system, which has nothing to do with these callbacks.)*

Voice **commands** only — pain/death sounds are different events, and player voice chat is a separate system.

## `dodtools_crosshair 0`

The stock `crosshair` cvar **cannot** turn the crosshair off. `CHud::Redraw` silently forces the value back every frame — it's one of three cvars in that enforcement block, and the other two (`r_drawentities`, `cl_lw`) don't reset, they quit the game. So the gap isn't a missing setting; it's a setting that's overwritten before it takes effect.

`CHudDoDCrossHair::Draw` gets `33 C0 C2 04 00` over its first five bytes — `xor eax, eax; ret 4`, which is **byte-for-byte `CHudBase::Draw`**, the do-nothing base implementation every element inherits and most override. The element stays in the list, still gets called, and does what an element that draws nothing does. Reverting writes back the five bytes the signature already proved were there.

Patching the function rather than the vftable slot (#265's idea) avoids needing the vftable address at runtime. #265 is still worth having and isn't blocked by this.

## Shared machinery

`commands.rs` grows `poll_code_patch` — one loop for all three code-patch cvars, replacing the bespoke `poll_scoreboard` from #279.

All three are applied **every frame from the bytes**, not from a cached flag, because the engine reloads `client.dll` between demos and a reloaded module comes back stock. A cached belief would leave all three working for the first demo of a session and quietly stopping from the second onward.

## Verification

`tools/verify_voice_crosshair_offsets.py` checks eight things against a real `client.dll`, reading every constant out of the Rust:

```
  -- the US/British voice callback
  OK   the signature matches exactly once, at +0xb479
  OK   +0xb489 is `call dword ptr [ebx]` (EV_PlaySound)
  OK   inside the callback DoD registers for events/misc/usvoice.sc (+0xb3f0)
  OK   the caller cleans up itself: `add esp, 0x20` at +0xb48b
  OK   with the call NOPped, every later instruction still starts where it did
  -- the German voice callback
  ... same five, at +0xb64e / +0xb664 / +0xb5d0 / +0xb66d
== crosshair.rs ==
  OK   the signature matches exactly once, at +0x2cd20
  OK   it starts with the 5 bytes STOCK restores
  OK   the 5 overwritten bytes are whole instructions
  OK   +0x2cd20 is CHudDoDCrossHair's vftable slot 3 (Draw), resolved from RTTI
  OK   HIDDEN is byte-identical to CHudBase::Draw, present at +0x18c0 and 46 other places
SIGNATURES VERIFIED
```

The load-bearing checks resolve each target **independently of its signature** — the voice callbacks by the function pointer DoD hands `pfnHookEvent` next to each script name, the crosshair by RTTI.

`cargo test -p goldsrc-hooks --target i686-pc-windows-msvc` green (50, 10 new), clippy clean, release cross-build clean, `cargo test --workspace` green (480).

**Neither is live-tested.**

## Not included: the spectator bars

`docs/goldsrc_hud_suppression.md` §5 records where that stands. HLAE's `mirv_disable_specmenu` fails on DoD with `"Error: Hook not installed."` — its `TeamFortressViewport_UpdateSpecatorPanel` address exists for `tfc` and `valve`, not `dod`. DoD has all the classes, and the construction path is known (`+0x82df9` loads `Spectator.res`, constructor at `+0x1d9ec`), but **the per-frame function that re-shows the panel has not been found**, and that's what needs blocking. Likely shape is stubbing `PaintTraverse` on the panel's vgui2 vftable, which would take the bars, dropdowns and buttons in one dword — that needs the vgui2 `Panel` vtable layout for this build.

Lower priority than it looks: unlike the voice commands, the spectator bars already have a working `.res` workaround.

[XProf: trace viewer] Implement tree-like architecture for timeline groups

Migrates group hierarchy and relationships in Trace Viewer V2 to a tree-like architecture:
- Replaces index-based group lookups and linkages (`parent_index`, `child_indices`) with direct raw pointers (`parent`, `prev_sibling`, `next_sibling`, `first_child`, `last_child`).
- Updates group layout calculation, track rendering, event snapping, and scroll restoration to traverse groups using the tree hierarchy.
- Maintains zero-allocation performance on hot render paths and preserves existing track ordering and visibility behavior in helper functions.

author: tristan-stoltz-erc
frikkern
body:
## The defect

`:` is itself a pipeline, so running it on the right of `||` **replaces PIPESTATUS** before the next line reads it:

```
$ bash -c 'set -o pipefail; (exit 3) | cat >/dev/null || :; echo "${PIPESTATUS[0]}"'
0
```

So `cmd | tee f || :` followed by `rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}` reads **0 on every exit**. The capture is reachable and dead.

`scripts/workflow-errexit-capture-check.sh` *recommended* that idiom — `FIX: rc=0; <cmd> || rc=$?  (or `<cmd> | tee … || :` for a pipeline)` — and its arm A5 asserted "a trailing `|| :` clears the pipeline shape (rc 0)". Three steps took the advice.

## What it cost — three false greens, measured

| Site | What it published |
|---|---|
| `main-red-owner.yml` "Has a clean 24 h actually been OBSERVED?" | run **35276736665**: `NOT YET MEASURED: no anchor poll at or before now-86400s` then, on the next line, `TERMINAL: window verdict exit=0`. The step summary this writes labels exit 0 as **`0 CLEAN`**. The one instrument `task-0a48c7b64d5ab0f1` c0 is stamped from was publishing a clean 24 h day over an unmeasured ledger. |
| `main-red-owner.yml` "read main's tip and deliver ownership" | `exit "$rc"` on a dead capture — concluded SUCCESS on could-not-deliver codes 3/4/5, defeating the fail-closed guarantee the file's own header promises ("It fails closed both ways"). |
| `scheduled-arm-health.yml` | same shape, same `exit "$rc"` — SUCCESS on a red arm (1) and on cannot-measure (2), the script's only two interesting outcomes. The comment above it claimed `exit "$rc"` "still fails the step exactly as before". It did not, and had not since the `|| :` landed. |

`grip-suite.yml` and `research-coverage-suite.yml` were never affected: they use `set +e`, and nothing runs between their pipeline and their capture.

## The fix

All three sites now wrap the pipeline **and** its capture in `set +e` / `set -e` — the form the two unaffected workflows already use. `-e` still cannot steal the diagnosis, and nothing overwrites PIPESTATUS in between.

The guard gains the rule so the idiom cannot return: a `${PIPESTATUS[n]}` capture whose preceding executable line carries a top-level `||` is refused as a **DEAD PIPESTATUS capture**. `$?` captures are untouched — `cmd || rc=$?` remains the blessed remedy (arm A5c states that boundary).

## Two arms

**REVERT ARM** — restore the `|| :` on all three sites:

```
$ bash scripts/workflow-errexit-capture-check.sh .github/workflows
workflow-errexit-capture-check: 3 DEAD PIPESTATUS capture(s) — the `||` on the line above overwrote the array, so this reads 0 no matter what the pipeline did

  .github/workflows/main-red-owner.yml job `own-the-red` step[6] (name: "Has a clean 24 h actually been OBSERVED?")
      run-body line 28: rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
      the command above it: bash scripts/main-red-window.sh --verdict "$L" | tee "$RUNNER_TEMP/mrw.txt" || :
  .github/workflows/main-red-owner.yml job `own-the-red` step[8] (name: "read main's tip and deliver ownership")
  .github/workflows/scheduled-arm-health.yml job `sweep` step[1] (name: "read every declared cron against its real scheduled runs")

scanned 639 run-step(s), 25 status capture(s)
TERMINAL: exit 1
REVERT rc=1

$ bash scripts/workflow-errexit-capture-check.sh --selftest   # under the revert
  FAIL D5 live tree — a DEAD PIPESTATUS capture is live in .github/workflows
SELFTEST: 1 of 30 arm(s) FAILED
```

**QUIET ARM** — the shipped tree:

```
$ bash scripts/workflow-errexit-capture-check.sh .github/workflows
workflow-errexit-capture-check: OK — 25 status capture(s) across 639 run-step(s), every one either under `set +e` or guarded by `||`; and no unreachable reporter (51 `--selftest` preflight(s) walked, none of them shadowing a bare re-run of the same command)
TERMINAL: exit 0
rc=0

$ bash scripts/workflow-errexit-capture-check.sh --selftest
  ok   A5 dead PIPESTATUS — a trailing `|| :` before a ${PIPESTATUS[0]} capture REDS (rc 1)
  ok   A5b pipeline fixed — `set +e` around pipeline+capture clears it (rc 0)
  ok   A5c `$?` unaffected — `|| rc=$?` is not read as a dead capture (rc 2)
  ok   D0 fixture control — the exit-3 subject actually ran
  ok   D1 old idiom loses the status — `| tee … || :` then ${PIPESTATUS[0]} reads 0, not 3
  ok   D2 set +e keeps it — the shipped remedy reads the pipeline's own 3
  ok   D3 guarded compound keeps it — `{ …; rc=${PIPESTATUS[0]}; } || :` reads 3
  ok   D4 set +e step survives — `-e` does not abort on the pipeline's exit 3
  ok   D5 live tree — no DEAD PIPESTATUS capture under .github/workflows (rc 0)
SELFTEST: 30/30 arms pass
TERMINAL: exit 0

$ bash scripts/workflow-job-shape-check.sh
workflow-job-shape-check: OK — 78 file(s), 171 job(s), 931 step(s)
$ bash scripts/main-run-concurrency-check.sh | tail -1
main-run-concurrency gate OK — 56 main-triggered workflow(s) with a concurrency block discovered
```

**D0 is the arm that caught a real fault in this PR's own arms.** D1's expected value is `rc=0`, which is also what a fixture that never ran produces — and the first draft's fixtures did not run (`SUT_DIR` is `unset` after the B arms, and `set -u` exits 1). D1 passed on a fixture that had never executed the subject. D0 asserts the subject spoke before D1's 0 is read as evidence.

## Not fixed here, and why

Re-measured `bash scripts/main-red-predicate.sh` from a worktree cut fresh off `origin/main` (c53447e7c) at **2026-09-17T21:48Z**:

```
branch-driven push workflows = 57 · red 4 · green 53 · unread 0 · n/a 2
2H PREDICATE: FALSE -- 1 workflow(s) red for more than 2 hours
```

| Workflow | Age | Lane |
|---|---|---|
| `scaffy-catalog-drift.yml` | 4h57m **OVER-2H** — the sole predicate breaker | CLI |
| `cli-release-cadence.yml` | 0h06m | CLI |
| `doc-gates.yml` | 0h06m | STUDIO — PR #19130 open on `docs/cards/js-sdk.md 2605B/2400B` |
| `js-tests.yml` | 0h21m | STUDIO |

`release-artifact.yml` is gone from the red set, confirming #19139. None of the four names in the row's title (doc-gates 157:1, security evicted, gofmt drift, deploy) is still real; the doc-gates red that remains has a different cause. No red in this PR's fence.

The mutation runner deleted `find` for every entry and ignored the `replace` field that 28 entries carry. body: ## Описание проблемы После мержа PR #12 баг «Нет доступных целей» у лука **не был исправлен**. Причина в том, что данные уже были испорчены до попадания в боевую систему. ### Цепочка проблемы: 1. `GET /api/items` возвращает structured properties: `[{ type:"range", normal:150, long:600, text:"Дальность 150/600" }, ...]` 2. `mapItem.ts` извлекал **только строки текста**, выбрасывая `type`/`normal`/`long`: ```ts const texts = item.properties?.map((p) => p.text).filter(Boolean) properties: texts?.length ? texts : undefined ``` 3. `getWeaponsFromInventory` получал массив строк вместо объектов 4. Regex `/range\s*\((\d+)/i` **не матчил** русское `"Дальность 150/600"` 5. `useWeaponTargets`: нет range → `maxRange = 5` → гоблины на 30 ft отфильтрованы 6. Результат: «Нет доступных целей» у лука, кинжала и меча одинаково ## Исправления ### 1. Сохранение structured properties в mapItem `mapItem.ts` теперь сохраняет полные объекты properties вместо извлечения только текста: ```ts properties: item.properties?.length ? item.properties : undefined ``` ### 2. Обновление типа IInventoryItem ```ts export interface IItemProperty { type: "range" | "twoHanded" | string normal?: number long?: number text: string } export interface IInventoryItem { // ... properties?: (string | IItemProperty)[] } ``` ### 3. Обработка обоих форматов в getWeaponsFromInventory - Если property — объект: используем его напрямую - Если property — строка: парсим с fallback для русского языка ### 4. Fallback парсинг русских строк Добавлена функция `parseRangeFromString` которая матчит: - `"range (150/600)"` (английский) - `"Дальность 150/600"` (русский) - `"150/600"` (только числа) ### 5. Обновление UI компонентов `itemDetail.tsx` теперь корректно извлекает text из объектов: ```ts const text = typeof p === "string" ? p : p.text ``` ### 6. Debug логи Добавлены логи под флагом `localStorage.combatDebug = '1'`: - `getWeaponsFromInventory`: raw properties, parsed range - `useWeaponTargets`: range property, maxRange, combatants distances, filtered targets ## Результат ✅ Лук с `normal: 150` видит монстров до 150 ft ✅ Меч без range остается на дефолтных 5 ft ✅ Данные не теряются при прохождении через `mapItem` ✅ Поддержка русских и английских строк ✅ Обратная совместимость со строковыми properties ## Как тестировать 1. Включить debug: `localStorage.setItem('combatDebug', '1')` 2. Открыть консоль 3. Начать бой с врагами на разных дистанциях 4. Выбрать лук — должны быть видны враги до 150 ft 5. Выбрать меч — должны быть видны только враги до 5 ft
